Ready to make your mark? Discover Farmers' vibrant culture and explore career opportunities at www.Farmers.com/careers/corporate.

Job Summary

This position oversees actuarial functions with a focus on financial projections of U.S. product liability cashflows. The role focuses on model development, testing, governance and consistency among various model stakeholders. This position leverages in-depth actuarial knowledge and understanding of the business to solve more complex issues and deliver strategic recommendations that align with business objectives. The position performs work independently while receiving guidance from a direct people leader and guiding more junior staff.

Essential Job Functions

  • Collaborates with stakeholders, teams, and other departments to resolve more complex actuarial issues. Guides the preparation of financial projections to enable leadership to assess financial implications and overall impact of business decisions. Accountable for timely and accurate delivery of actuarial deliverables. Interprets data and formulas to extract valuable insights for management. Analyzes operational performance and presents findings and recommendations for optimization. May represent the actuarial department with external stakeholders.
  • Independently develops and implements solutions to more complex actuarial issues. Oversees project workflows, provides robust feedback to stakeholders and management, and ensures timely and effective completion of work. Delivers on plans and priorities while guiding projects and/or teams to achieve successful outcomes and business objectives.
  • Advocates for improvements to assumption formulas, procedures, and programs. Anticipates the impact of changes and ensures recommendations align with broader business objectives.
  • Oversees the integration of new and updated products into financial projection system. Ensures actuarial modeling systems comply with controls and standards including updates for IT, product, and regulatory changes.
  • Stays informed about industry trends, emerging actuarial practices, and regulatory changes to contribute effectively to work within team, department, or across departments. Acts as a subject matter specialist to mentor and train less experienced actuarial staff by providing guidance on fundamental actuarial principles and practices. Performs other duties as assigned.

Physical Actions

Physical Environment

Education Requirements

High School Diploma or equivalent is required. Bachelors degree is preferred but not required. Associate of the Society of Actuaries (ASA) or equivalent designation required. Two Fellow of the Society of Actuaries (FSA) courses preferred. Life insurance industry experience preferred. Experience with US statutory regulations or IFRS 17 preferred.

Experience Requirements

  • 6+ years of experience working in relevant roles
  • Advance experience working with actuarial projection software like MG-ALFA or equivalent (Axis or Profit)
  • Experience working with Python, R, SAS or similar
  • Strong understanding of actuarial modeling
  • Familiarity with U.S. Life/Annuity product designs and features.
  • Able to analyze complex data, interpret trends, and develop actuarial models and assumptions.
  • Deep understanding on Financial Modeling within Alpha database

Special Skill Requirement

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Boston, MA
  • Benefits: Health insurance, 401(k), paid time off, tuition assistance

About this job

Senior Insurance Defense Trial Attorney handling moderate to high complexity cases in Massachusetts for Farmers Insurance. Remote position with in-person appearances as required, managing cases from intake through trial or settlement.

Good fit if you have seven years of litigation experience, insurance defense background, jury trial experience, and are licensed to practice law in Massachusetts.

Full job description

We are Farmers – where ambition meets opportunity.

At Farmers, we're not just known for unforgettable jingle – we're a team with a passion for purpose and making a real difference in people's lives. We deliver peace of mind when it matters most. Our results-driven, high-performance culture thrives on creativity, accountability and bold solutions. Here, growth isn't just a goal – it's a way of life for both the organization and every individual on our team. We tackle challenges head-on, learn from every experience and measure our impact on the customers who trust us.

Join an award-winning, equal opportunity employer, where you'll find more than a job – you'll find a supportive community. Enjoy competitive benefits, take part in meaningful volunteer projects, and help shape the future alongside talented colleagues across all backgrounds. At Farmers, helping others is at the heart of what we do.

Ready to make your mark? Discover our vibrant culture and explore career opportunities at www.Farmers.com/careers/corporate. Connect with us on Instagram, LinkedIn and TikTok, and let's build something incredible together!

Workplace: Remote ( #LI-Remote )

We are seeking an experienced Trial Attorney with experience handling complex matters to join our Massachusetts staff counsel team and handle cases venued primarily in the Boston area and surrounding counties. Our attorneys work from home and handle in-person appearances and trials as required. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including annual bonus potential up to 20% of the salary, generous 401k, auto allowance, PTO, medical/dental/vision, paid parental leave, and much more all without the stress of billable hours!

Job Summary

This position is responsible for representing clients in all areas of insurance defense practice, handling cases that are primarily moderate to high complexity and exposure and/or involve unique insurance defense issues. Manages all phases of cases from intake to resolution.

Essential Job Functions

  • Litigates moderate to high complexity and exposure cases and/or cases involving unique legal or procedural issues and performs duties necessary from intake to trial and/or settlement.
  • This includes but is not limited to preparation of pleadings, motions, discovery, and briefs.
  • Acts as the lead attorney at hearings, conferences, interviews, mediations, arbitrations, and/or trials.
  • Develops strategies and arguments to thoroughly prepare for trial.
  • Utilizes knowledge of legal precedents to analyze the probable outcomes of a case.
  • Identifies the strengths and weaknesses of approaches to a case.
  • Performs or ensures completion of any other tasks or duties necessary for the proper representation of clients.
  • Consults with Claims Executive team and renders legal strategy recommendations regarding the legal aspects of the handling of personal injury claims.
  • Provides guidance to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and industry standards.
  • Interprets applicable industry laws, rulings and regulations.
  • Functionally supervises attorneys who are assisting in the handling of cases as development opportunities.
  • Provides guidance and mentorship with the autonomy to learn.

Physical Actions

Job is performed in-person at a Farmers office or virtually at an approved alternative work location. Job may include work performed at field locations. The physical work environment is indoors and climate-controlled with adequate lighting and ventilation. Normal and customary distractions include background noise produced by office equipment and chatter among people, as well as interruptions. Field work performed outdoors may include exposure to weather elements. Frequently sits or stands for prolonged periods of time, up to a full shift. Occasionally moves about the workplace including navigating stairs, ramps, and level or uneven surfaces. Occasionally moves, pushes, pulls, lifts, carries, and places objects or materials weighing up to 50 pounds without assistance. Frequently uses shoulders, arms, hands, and fingers to manipulate equipment, tools, and objects necessary to perform job duties. Frequently performs fine motor tasks such as typing, mousing, or writing, up to a full shift. Occasionally performs movements such as bending, stooping, crouching, kneeling, twisting, and reaching overhead or below the knees. Possesses clear vision, with or without correction, to visually read and verify information. Relies on depth perception and peripheral vision to navigate the work environment visually by identifying barriers, changes in terrain and locating objects. Possesses adequate hearing, with or without correction, to communicate with co-workers, respond promptly to auditory signals or alarms, and discern sounds essential for maintaining safety and productivity in the workplace. Jobs in this category may require regular travel between Farmers offices, alternative work locations, and/or field locations.

Physical Environment

Required job duties are normally performed in a climate- controlled office environment, with some exposure to uncontrollable outside environmental conditions and travel via automobile and/or commercial transportation.

Education Requirements

Bachelors degree preferred. Licensed to practice Law in applicable states required upon hire.

Experience Requirements

Seven years of litigation experience required. Insurance defense, personal injury, and/or jury trial experience required. First and second chair trial experience in bodily injury litigation strongly preferred. Multistate jurisdictional practice preferred.

Special Skill Requirement

Public speaking, ability to function and handle high case loads in adversarial or confrontational situations, driving.

Additional Qualification

Effective leadership skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to command the attention of an audience. Demonstrated problem solving skills. Possesses a genuine interest in the defense of Insurance regulations. Ability to represent the company with external constituents. Handles conflict effectively with the ability to quickly interpret and respond to new information. Demonstrates excellent judgment and decision making skills. Ability to work within tight timeframes and meet strict deadlines. Excellent time management and priority setting skills. Articulate and responsive to colleagues. Possesses strong technical aptitude. Adept and proficient at using technology to maximize efficiency in virtual, paperless environment.

Benefits

  • Farmers offers a competitive salary commensurate with experience, qualifications and location.

Job Summary

IAM Information Security Lead Specialist provides technical and strategic leadership for identity governance, access management, authentication, and IAM modernization initiatives. Collaborates with program sponsors, cross-functional teams, and assigned project managers to plan and develop scope, deliverables, required resources, work plan, budget, and timing for new security initiatives.

Essential Tasks & Leadership Philosophy

  • Lead the deployment, integration, and optimization of enterprise Identity and Access Management (IAM) solutions, ensuring alignment with business, security, and regulatory requirements.
  • Serve as a strategic IAM subject matter expert, identifying opportunities to enhance identity governance, access management, authentication, and authorization capabilities across the organization.
  • Drive the adoption of modern identity security practices, including Single Sign-On (SSO), Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), Privileged Access Management (PAM), and identity lifecycle management.
  • Develops expertise in insurance business operations in order to drive security innovations for a financial services organization.
  • Evaluate emerging IAM technologies and industry best practices to improve security, operational efficiency, and user experience.
  • Develops and implements innovative IAM programs, automation capabilities, and minimum viable products (MVPs) that support the organization's strategic security roadmap.
  • Partner with business leaders, technology teams, and security stakeholders to define IAM requirements, establish priorities, and deliver enterprise-wide identity initiatives.
  • Lead complex IAM projects and programs with broad scope, significant business impact, and cross-functional dependencies.
  • Coordinate activities across multiple IAM, cybersecurity, and technology initiatives to ensure alignment with organizational goals and security objectives.
  • Resolve complex identity, access, and authentication challenges by developing practical solutions that balance risk reduction with business enablement.
  • Develop metrics, dashboards, and executive reporting to communicate IAM program effectiveness, operational performance, compliance posture, and risk trends.
  • Builds and owns relationships that positively influence business outcomes.
  • Influence enterprise adoption of identity governance and access management best practices through effective communication, education, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Partners with business leaders to ensure information security risk findings are reviewed and solutions are implemented.
  • Effectively mentors, coaches and influences peers.

First Year Success Factors

  • Develop and Execute an Enterprise IAM Roadmap: Assess the current IAM, IGA, PAM, SSO, and MFA environment. Identify security gaps, compliance risks, and improvement opportunities. Create a prioritized roadmap aligned to business and security objectives.
  • Strengthen Identity Governance and Access Controls: Improve joiner, mover, and leaver processes. Enhance role-based access controls (RBAC).Implement or mature access certification and periodic access reviews. Reduce inappropriate or excessive access privileges.
  • Advance Identity Security Capabilities: Increase adoption of: Single Sign-On (SSO); Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA); Privileged Access Management (PAM); Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) and Improve authentication security while maintaining a positive user experience.
  • Deliver Major IAM Initiatives Successfully: Lead large-scale IAM projects across business and technology teams. Ensure implementations are delivered on time and within scope. Minimize disruption to business operations.

Education & Career Experience Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree required.
  • Relevant Information Security certification (CISSP, SCC, ISSAP and/or ISACA, etc.) required.
  • 7-10 years related experience in IT Security or identity access management, and Project Management, or comparable base of knowledge/expertise in the field.
  • Strong knowledge of Identity and Access Management principles, including authentication, authorization, identity governance, and access lifecycle management.
  • Deep expertise in Identity and Access Management, Identity Governance and Administration (IGA), authentication, authorization, and access lifecycle management.

Physical Actions

Sits or stands for extended periods of time, up to a full work shift. Occasionally reaches overhead and below the knees, including bending, twisting, pulling, and stooping. Occasionally moves, lifts, carries, and places objects and supplies weighing 0-10 pounds without assistance. Listens to, interprets, and differentiates auditory information (e.g. others speaking) at normal speaking levels with or without correction. Visually verifies and reads information. Visually locates material, resources and other objects. Ability to operate a computer for extended periods of time, up to a full work shift. Physical dexterity sufficient to use hands, arms, and shoulders repetitively to operate keyboard and other office equipment up to a full work shift.

Physical Environment

This position operates in an open office working environment which will include normal and customary distractions, noise, and interruptions.

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Insurance Sales Representative, Insurance Sales, Insurance Agent
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $18.00 an hour
  • Schedule: Full-time, includes weekends
  • Location: Louisville, KY
  • Education: High school diploma or GED
  • Benefits: Health insurance, 401(k), tuition assistance

About this job

Remote insurance sales role selling Allstate products to warm leads via phone, chat, and SMS. Base pay of $18/hour plus uncapped performance incentives, paid training from day one, and licensing support provided.

Good fit if you have 1+ year of sales or customer service experience and can obtain a Personal Lines or Property & Casualty Producer license.

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

Allstates sales organization is growing its virtual workforce, and we are looking for highly motivated individuals that thrive in a fast-paced sales environment and enjoy being rewarded for their efforts. At Allstate, we are committed to offering a reputable product suite that protects people from lifes uncertainties so they can realize their hopes and dreams.

As a full-time Insurance Sales Representative, you will:

  • Engage with active insurance shoppers via inbound/outbound calls, live chat, SMS, and more in a work from home call center environment.
  • Use your insurance expertise to uncover customer needs, identify coverage gaps, and recommend tailored solutions from Allstate products and products within the Allstate family of companies.
  • Convert warm leads into customers using a proven consultative sales strategy no cold calling required.
  • Work from home to drive sales growth while delivering an exceptional, customer-first experience.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Base Pay: $18/hour
  • Average Total Compensation: $52,730$76,480/year (base + uncapped performance-based incentives)
  • Incentives are productivity-based and governed by the applicable bonus plan, which is subject to change at Allstates discretion.


Full suite of employee benefits starting day one, including:

  • Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) with company match and pension plan
  • Tuition reimbursement and career development
  • Wellness programs

Additional Benefits

  • Paid training from day one (classroom and hands-on)
  • Licensing support: study materials, exam reimbursement, and assistance
  • Monthly internet reimbursement
  • Home office equipment provided by Allstate

Why Join Allstate

  • No Prospecting: Warm leads delivered directly to you
  • Career Growth: Develop your skills within a dynamic, supportive Fortune 100 company
  • Supportive Culture: Learn from best-in-class leaders and motivated teammates
  • Trusted Brand: Be part of a company with 90+ years of industry experience
  • Diverse & Reputable Product Suite: Sell from a wide portfolio that meets every customers needs

Requirements

  • At least 1 year of experience in sales or customer service (with a sales focus)
  • Active Personal Lines or Property & Casualty Producer license in your state of residence (preferred)
  • If unlicensed, ability to obtain a Personal Lines or Property & Casualty Producer license with Allstates support
  • Sales Representatives are required to obtain and maintain all required resident and non-resident Producer licenses necessary to sell insurance products in any state designated by Allstate. This includes obtaining non-resident Producer licenses in all states as required for the role.
  • If hired, Sales Representative must relinquish all non-Allstate insurance carrier appointments and may not hold active appointments with other carriers while employed in this role, in accordance with Allstate licensing and appointment policies.
  • High school diploma or GED required
  • Reliable high-speed internet with wired connection (Ethernet)
  • Dedicated, distraction-free home workspace (equipment provided)
  • Comfortable working evenings and weekends
  • Receptive to feedback and performance coaching
  • Strong communication, critical thinking, and multitasking skills
  • Competitive, highly self-motivated and enjoys being rewarded for your efforts
  • Able to work independently and hold yourself accountable for your performance
  • Ability to navigate multiple computer systems simultaneously


Essential Job Functions

  • Handle inbound and outbound customer calls as the primary method of customer engagement.
  • Maintain availability during assigned work hours to meet call volume and service expectations. This function is particularly crucial during an employees first 90 days of employment.
  • Deliver consultative sales conversations and complete transactions during live customer interactions.
  • Adhere to assigned schedules, including evenings and weekends, based on business coverage needs.
  • Meet established productivity, quality, and performance standards.
  • Navigate multiple computer systems simultaneously while actively engaged with customers.

This position is only available within theUS, but notcurrently available for Puerto Rico, California, New York, Alaska, Hawaii, or Washington state residents.

Candidates who reside in locations where the local minimum wage exceeds the base pay for this position are also not eligible for consideration. This is due to compliance with wage regulations and internal compensation practices.


Reasonable Accommodation Statement

Allstate provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities to enable them to perform the essential functions of their role. During the first 90 days of employment, reasonable accommodations generally do not include removing essential job functions, creating new positions, or lowering performance or productivity standards.

Job.JobTitle: Attack Surface Management Service Lead Consultant - Exposure Intelligence Team
Job.JobDescription:
At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

Role Scope: Attack Surface Management Service Lead Consultant Exposure Intelligence

Allstate Job Profile & Family: Lead Consultant- Threat & Incident Response


Team and overall work scope

  • The team operates within a newly established Exposure Management function in the broader cybersecurity organization, focused on modernizing how the enterprise identifies, prioritizes, and mitigates security vulnerabilities shifting from traditional patch approaches to a more strategic focus on true business risk and exploitability
  • Individual Contributor/ Lead Consultant roles are designed to bring in deep respective domain expertise (network, endpoint, cloud, identity, infrastructure, Databases & Data Stores, Applications, API's, Attack Surface Management etc.) to bridge the gap between security insights and practical remediation strategies
  • The Lead Consultant Attack Surface Management is the SME responsible for discovering, monitoring, and governing the enterprise's internet-facing attack surface, including unknown and unmanaged assets, external exposures, and third-party and subsidiary footprints. As the founding member of the capability, the role establishes ASM practices, applies CTEM principles to tie external findings to real attack paths, and partners with asset owners to drive remediation that measurably reduces exploitable exposure.

Success Measures

  • Expanded and validated coverage of the external attack surface, with fewer unknown or unowned internet-facing assets.
  • Reduced time from discovery of a new external exposure to an assigned owner and completed mitigation.
  • Higher signal quality in external findings, with fewer false positives and more accurate prioritization.

Key Responsibilities (Core + Domain)


Exposure Intelligence (Core)

  • Translate external attack surface findings into exposure intelligence and exploitability-based prioritization.
  • Identify attack paths that start from internet-facing assets, such as exposed services, misconfigurations, expired or weak certificates, and exposed admin interfaces.
  • Produce clear remediation guidance and partner with asset owners to validate closure.


Attack Surface Management (Domain)

  • Own SME coverage for external attack surface discovery and monitoring using EASM and scanning platforms (e.g., Censys, Qualys).
  • Establish asset governance practices, including attribution, ownership assignment, inventory reconciliation, and detection of shadow IT and orphaned assets.
  • Extend visibility to third-party, subsidiary, and cloud-hosted footprints, and partner with Penetration Testing, Product Security, and Exposure Response to operationalize findings.

Required Qualifications

  • 3+ years in attack surface management, vulnerability management, security operations, or exposure management.
  • Strong understanding of internet-facing infrastructure, including DNS, IP space, certificates, cloud hosting, and common external misconfigurations.
  • Ability to translate technical findings into business risk and practical remediation actions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Hands-on experience with Censys or comparable EASM platforms, and with Qualys or similar vulnerability scanning tools.
  • Familiarity with asset inventory/CMDB processes, cloud provider connectors, and third-party risk practices.
  • Ability to build a new capability from the ground up, including processes, metrics, and stakeholder buy-in, as the first person in the function.

Skills Attack Surface Management, External Attack Surface Management (EASM), Asset Discovery, Asset Inventory Management, Cloud Security, Network Security, Third-Party Risk Management, Vulnerability Management, Threat and Vulnerability Management

Skills

Asset Inventory Management, Attack Surface Analysis, Cyber Incident Response, Cyber Threat Hunting, IT Security Operations, Network Security, Penetration Testing, Stakeholder Management, Threat and Vulnerability Assessment, Threat and Vulnerability Management, Vulnerability Management

Compensation

Compensation offered for this role is 100,000.00 - 170,500.00 annually and is based on experience and qualifications.

The candidate(s) offered this position will be required to submit to a background investigation.

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. Compensation Overview

What Is the Opportunity?

This role is eligible for a sign-on bonus of up to $20,000.

As a Major Case Specialist, Auto Liability, you are responsible for investigating, evaluating, reserving, negotiating, and resolving the office and/or department's most complex, high-exposure, and highest-severity injury and/or property damage claims within appropriate authority and oversight. You will serve as an expert technical resource to claim professionals, business partners, customers, and other stakeholders.

What Will You Do?

  • Independently manage and oversee an active caseload of injury and/or property damage claims and litigation from first notice of loss through resolution within level of authority. Typically, handles high complexity injury and/or property damage claims which includes coverage disputes and contractual indemnity issues.
  • Conduct detailed investigations to gather evidence, assess liability and determine extent of damages and establish appropriate reserves.
  • Evaluate claim information and documentation to make informed decisions regarding coverage and resolutions.
  • Engage in negotiations with claimants, legal representatives, and other parties to achieve fair and equitable resolutions.
  • Develop and execute advanced resolution strategies and coordinate internal and external resources to conduct comprehensive claim investigations and evaluations.
  • Prepare and present detailed reports on claim status, trends and outcomes to senior management.
  • Work closely with legal, underwriting, and other departments to ensure coordinated claim handling.
  • Partner with Counsel to develop, direct, and execute litigation management strategies.
  • Maintain comprehensive and accurate records of all claim activities, communications, and decisions.
  • Identify areas in which we can improve or enhance current best practices and offer creative solutions.
  • Adapt to new technology implementations, system upgrades, and digital tool rollouts, particularly in the areas of AI while maintaining productivity and service quality.
  • Acquire and maintain relevant Insurance License(s) to comply with state and Travelers' requirements within three months of starting the job.
  • May require travel, including overnight stays, to attend mediations, trials, arbitration, etc.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's Degree.
  • Five plus years of complex, bodily injury claim and litigation experience.
  • Active adjuster license, where required by state law.
  • Experience with claims management and estimating software, with advanced skills in Microsoft Office and enterprise technology systems and platforms.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with the ability to understand, synthesize, interpret, and convey complex information in a simplified manner to multiple stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to make independent decisions and handle complex claims, evaluate severe losses, and negotiate settlements strategically.
  • Exceptional customer service skills; demonstrated ability to manage relationships with key stakeholders while delivering a consistently positive experience.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and organizational skills with the ability to manage a high-volume workload and prioritize effectively.
  • Expert-level negotiation and conflict resolution skills with the ability to apply strategic claim handling practices.
  • Ability to manage stress, navigate difficult situations, and maintain composure and professionalism under pressure while always taking accountability for decisions.
  • Expert level knowledge of insurance principles, policy language, exclusions, and ISO forms with thorough understanding of business line products.
  • Strong understanding of state and federal insurance regulations, fair claims practices legislation, and legal requirements, with the ability to apply this knowledge to complex claims.
  • Ability to quickly learn from experience and apply it to new situations with speed and flexibility.

What is a Must Have?

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • Four years of bodily injury liability, property damage liability, or comparable claim related experience.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

BASIC PURPOSE:

The Manager – Expense Planning & Analysis leads enterprise budgeting, forecasting, workforce planning, expense management, and financial analysis activities. This position serves as a strategic finance partner to business and executive leadership by translating financial and operational information into actionable insights, scenarios, and recommendations.  The manager develops FP&A talent, strengthens financial governance, and drives continuous improvement through advanced analytics, automation, generative AI, and modern planning technologies.

PRIMARY JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

Leadership and Team Development

  • Lead, coach, and develop Expense Management team members; establish priorities, allocate resources, manage performance, and build capabilities aligned with the evolving needs of the finance function.
  • Promote a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous learning, sound judgment, and constructive challenges.
  • Provide clear goals, timely feedback, meaningful development opportunities, and effective succession and workforce planning for the Expense Management team.

Enterprise Planning, Forecasting, and Performance Management

  • Own and continuously enhance enterprise processes for annual budgeting, rolling forecasts, workforce planning, capital planning, and multi-year strategic financial planning.
  • Develop driver-based forecasts and scenario analyses that connect financial outcomes to business volumes, operational assumptions, strategic initiatives, and external conditions.
  • Oversee consolidated expense and staffing forecasts, including salaries, employee benefits, discretionary expenses, capital expenditures, and other significant cost categories.
  • Monitor forecast accuracy, explain material variances, identify emerging risks and opportunities, and recommend actions to improve financial performance.
  • Serve as a trusted finance partner to officers, senior leaders, and department leaders by providing objective analysis, constructive challenges, and clear financial recommendations.
  • Lead or support business cases, cost-benefit analyses, investment evaluations, and post-implementation reviews for significant initiatives and projects.

Management Reporting and Financial Communication

  • Lead the preparation and delivery of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting that compares actual results with plan, forecast, prior year, and relevant operational measures.
  • Ensure financial analyses and presentations are accurate, reconciled, appropriately documented, and tailored to the needs of the intended audience.

Technology, Analytics, AI, and Process Transformation

  • Identify and implement opportunities to simplify, standardize, and automate expense processes while maintaining appropriate financial controls and auditability.
  • Identify, evaluate, and implement responsible uses of generative AI, automation, and agent-enabled workflows within forecasting, variance analysis, management reporting, scenario modeling, and financial narrative development.
  • Develop, test, and refine structured prompts and finance-focused AI agents that improve the efficiency, consistency, and scalability of work while maintaining human review, data security, documentation, and validation controls.

Financial Governance and Other Responsibilities

  • Promote compliance with corporate financial policies, expense procedures, internal controls, and applicable accounting and regulatory requirements.
  • Maintain strong working knowledge of company financial results, expense trends, strategic priorities, and relevant property and casualty insurance performance measures.
  • Lead and participate in cross-functional initiatives, ad hoc analyses, and other assignments in support of enterprise priorities.

QUALIFICATIONS:

      Required

  • Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, economics, business administration, data analytics, or a related analytical field.
  • Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in expense management, financial planning and analysis, corporate finance, financial analysis, management reporting, or a related field. .
  • Previous experience leading people, projects, or significant cross-functional financial processes.
  • Demonstrated proficiency in budgeting, forecasting, variance analysis, financial modeling, scenario analysis, and management reporting.
  • Strong understanding of financial statements, GAAP concepts, financial controls, and the relationship between operational drivers and financial results.
  • Advanced spreadsheet and financial modeling skills, with experience using enterprise planning, reporting, database, or business intelligence tools.
  • Ability to communicate complex financial information clearly and persuasively to business, executive, and board-level audiences.
  • Demonstrated ability to build partnerships, influence decisions, challenge assumptions constructively, and manage competing priorities in a changing environment.

Preferred

 

  • MBA, CPA, CMA, CFA, or another relevant advanced degree or professional designation.
  • Experience in property and casualty insurance, financial services, or another regulated and financially complex industry.
  • Familiarity with statutory accounting, insurance financial reporting, expense allocation, and insurance performance measures.
  • Experience with enterprise performance management or FP&A platforms, Power BI or comparable visualization tools, Power Query, SQL, Microsoft Fabric, or similar data technologies.
  • Experience applying generative AI, prompt design, automation, or agent-based solutions to financial planning, analysis, reporting, or workflow improvement.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

Professional office environment.

About this job

Supervise underwriting support staff for property and casualty insurance broker and specialty markets at Church Mutual Insurance in Merrill, Wisconsin. Responsibilities include managing premium development, policy quotes and issuance, staff recruitment and training, and broker relationship management.

Good fit if you have at least five years of property and casualty insurance experience, including large account quoting, and previous management experience.

Full job description

What you'll be doing:
Manage and provide leadership to the underwriting support staff to effectively develop premiums, prepare quotes, and issue and maintain policies for Broker/Specialty Markets.  Assist personnel at all levels to properly rate, quote, issue, and maintain policies in compliance with underwriting policy and regulatory requirements.  Provide policy information/special reports to executive management, others within Church Mutual, brokers, and insureds.  Establish priorities and adjust workloads to meet completion dates.  Build a strong working relationship with brokers and others outside and inside the company to attain corporate goals.  Recruit, hire, train, appraise, and conduct salary administration for direct reporting staff members.  Coach assigned personnel in setting and attaining professional development goals.  Annually assist in the development of broker/specialty markets underwriting goals and objectives and the supporting budget.
 
 
On any given day, you'll:
  • In compliance with company policies and regulatory filings, provide leadership and manage the underwriting support staff to effectively develop premium for the underwriter's review, prepare quotes, and issue policies to meet set target dates and performance and quality expectations.  Be responsible for providing various reports to executive management, brokers, insureds, and others on a timely basis.
  • Assist underwriting support personnel to maintain and develop technical knowledge and expertise on Church Mutual products and processing systems.  Be a resource within the department, share knowledge, and mentor and train others to recognize and resolve issues and concerns.
  • Review and evaluate rating and pricing processes specific to the large accounts market.  Make recommendations for enhancements and changes as appropriate.
  • Build a strong working relationship with brokers, sales associates, and others within the company to attain corporate goals and enhance excellent service through providing technical knowledge and expertise of processing guidelines, philosophies, and general directives.
  • Recruit, hire, train, appraise, and conduct salary administration for direct reporting staff members.  Coach assigned personnel in setting professional development goals and attaining these goals.
  • Work as a solid part of the broker/specialty markets underwriting management team, discussing underwriting issues, developing efficiencies, and identifying and assisting in resolving department needs.
  • Continue to develop leadership skills through internal and external publications, seminars, and conferences.  Share knowledge gained with peers.
  • Participate/lead assigned projects and special research projects as necessary.
  • Annually assist in developing broker/specialty markets underwriting goals and objectives and the supporting budget for Broker/Specialty Markets.
  • Travel as necessary to visit brokers and insureds to assist in new or renewal presentations or foster business relationships.
 
Here's what we expect:
  • At least five (5) years of property and casualty insurance-related experience with a proven record of favorable working relationships with brokers or direct agents.
  • A strong background in quoting and issuing large (excess of $50,000 annual premium) property and casualty accounts and reflecting increasing levels of responsibility.
  • Significant knowledge of the property and casualty industry demonstrated from experience in underwriting, claims, risk management, etc., is desirable.
  • Previous management experience is desirable.
  • A high school diploma or equivalent is required.
  • Bachelor's degree is preferred but may consider comparable industry experience.
  • A CPCU designation or evidence of continuing education in the insurance industry is highly desirable.
Necessary Knowledge and Abilities:
 
Proven ability to creatively quote large accounts.
Demonstrated superior knowledge of processing systems.  A high level knowledge of underwriting tools, such as loss development, trending, large deductible products, loss projections, etc., is desirable.
Ability to foster and maintain excellent relationships with brokers, direct agents, and senior living representatives.
Knowledge of the underwriting function, insurance coverages, and rate making.
Knowledge of religion practices and religious organizations.
Strong judgment, decision-making, organizational, and negotiation skills.
Ability to communicate effectively by enhancing information flow through active listening and sharing.
Coaching skills to assist others to grow and attain their personal goals.
Ability to deal with confrontation and work to a solid resolution.
Ability to work with others in a team environment.
Ability to work independently.
Strong leadership qualities to assist underwriting personnel, peers, and others within the company to attain corporate objectives.
Ability to recognize potential improvements (efficiencies) and be a change agent for the department.
Maintain confidentiality.

About this job

Senior Underwriter who independently evaluates and prices insurance policies, managing broker and agent relationships while focusing on complex and high-value accounts. Role involves data-driven decision-making, portfolio development, and cross-departmental collaboration at Liberty Mutual's Los Angeles office.

Good fit if you have 2.5+ years of underwriting experience, a business degree, analytical skills with quantitative tools, and a track record of profitable business development.

Full job description


Description

Works independently and autonomously on all but the most complex accounts/cases (subject to required process oversight). Underwrites policies within underwriting authority. Makes decisions on whether to accept business by making analytical, data-driven decisions based on data and information provided, including pricing the risk. In parts of North America more likely to underwrite complex/unusual policies - or those of high individual line size - policies assessed will focus on those of high complexity and/or larger size.


Responsibilities

Manages portfolio of brokers/agents & clients. Leverages market presence and expertise to develop and underwrite profitable business, acting as a representative for Liberty. Has relationships with senior/market-leading brokers and/or key agents. Maintains a strong market presence, including established relationships with agents and brokers. Looks to strengthen these relationships and develop new ones. Articulates key coverage differences with a high degree of detail. Provides significant input into the business and marketing planning process, including advanced data-driven insights from portfolio analysis. Participates in projects across departments designed to drive underwriting and process excellence (e.g., member of a working team). Models effective collaboration across teams, stakeholders and partners (e.g., UW Support, Claims, Actuarial, Directors of Underwriting in North America). Has strong knowledge of key legal cases, legislation and regulation impacting area(s) of underwriting expertise. Shares knowledge based on technical expertise, including providing external thought-leadership. Mentors, coaches, and trains other underwriters and internal partners.

Qualifications
  • Degree in Business or equivalent typically required
  • A minimum of 2.5 years, typically 3 or more years, of progressive underwriting experience and/or other related experience
  • CPCU or professional insurance designation preferred
  • Proven analytical ability to evaluate and judge underwriting risks within scope of responsibility that includes competence with all phases and aspects of the underwriting process, and proficiency in the use of qualitative and quantitative tools and techniques
  • Must demonstrate comprehension of complex technical underwriting issues and be capable of defining and implementing necessary underwriting and administrative processes/workflows to properly manage or administer those issues
  • Proven track record of developing and underwriting profitable business

Job.JobTitle: Claims Specialist II - Rideshare Commercial Auto - Attorney Represented Bodily Injury Claims Adjuster
Job.JobDescription:
Description

At Liberty, you'll thrive in a hybrid setting that fosters in-person collaboration, innovation and growth. This approach optimizes both remote and in-person interactions, enabling you to connect and ideate with your team and deepen valuable relationships across the company, while still enjoying the flexibility of remote work for focused tasks and projects.

The Claims Specialist works within a Claims Team, using the latest technology to manage an assigned caseload of routine to moderately complex claims from the investigation of the claim through resolution. This includes making decisions about liability/compensability, evaluating losses, and negotiating settlements. The role interacts with claimants, policyholders, appraisers, attorneys, and other third parties throughout the claims management process. The position offers training developed with an emphasis on enhancing skills needed to help provide exceptional service to our customers.

You will be required to go into the office twice a month if you reside within 50 miles of one of the following offices:Boston, MA; Westborough, MA; Hoffman Estates, IL;Weatogue, CT; Indianapolis, IN; Plano, TX;Suwanee, GA; orLake Oswego, OR; Las Vegas, NV; Chandler, AZ. (Please note this policy is subject to change.)

Responsibilities:

  • Manages an inventory of claims to evaluate compensability/liability.
  • Establishes action plan based on case facts, best practices, protocols, regulatory issues and available resources.
  • Plans and conduct investigations of claims to confirm coverage and to determine liability, compensability and damages.
  • Assesses policy coverage for submitted claims and notifies the insured of any issues; determines and establishes reserve requirements, adjusting reserves, as necessary, during the processing of the claim, refers claims to the subrogation group or Special Investigations Unit as appropriate.
  • Assesses actual damages associated with claims and conducts negotiations, within assigned authority limits, to settle claims.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.
Qualifications
  • BS/BA degree or equivalent work experience.
  • Minimum of 2 years' experience in claims adjustment, general insurance or formal claims training.
  • Required to obtain and maintain all applicable licenses.
  • Continuing education courses leading to industry certifications preferred (e.g., AEI, IIA, CPCU).
  • Knowledge of claims investigation techniques, medical terminology and legal aspects of claims.

As part of the application process, you'll complete an assessment related to the skills needed for this role please allow approximately 35 minutes, although there is no time limit

Job.JobDescription:
Description

At Liberty, you'll thrive in a hybrid setting that fosters in-person collaboration, innovation and growth. This approach optimizes both remote and in-person interactions, enabling you to connect and ideate with your team and deepen valuable relationships across the company, while still enjoying the flexibility of remote work for focused tasks and projects.

The Claims Specialist works within a Claims Team, using the latest technology to manage an assigned caseload of routine to moderately complex claims from the investigation of the claim through resolution. This includes making decisions about liability/compensability, evaluating losses, and negotiating settlements. The role interacts with claimants, policyholders, appraisers, attorneys, and other third parties throughout the claims management process. The position offers training developed with an emphasis on enhancing skills needed to help provide exceptional service to our customers.

You will be required to go into the office twice a month if you reside within 50 miles of one of the following offices:Boston, MA; Westborough, MA; Hoffman Estates, IL;Weatogue, CT; Indianapolis, IN; Plano, TX;Suwanee, GA; orLake Oswego, OR; Las Vegas, NV; Chandler, AZ. (Please note this policy is subject to change.)

Responsibilities:

  • Manages an inventory of claims to evaluate compensability/liability.
  • Establishes action plan based on case facts, best practices, protocols, regulatory issues and available resources.
  • Plans and conduct investigations of claims to confirm coverage and to determine liability, compensability and damages.
  • Assesses policy coverage for submitted claims and notifies the insured of any issues; determines and establishes reserve requirements, adjusting reserves, as necessary, during the processing of the claim, refers claims to the subrogation group or Special Investigations Unit as appropriate.
  • Assesses actual damages associated with claims and conducts negotiations, within assigned authority limits, to settle claims.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

  • Required to obtain and maintain all applicable licenses.
  • Continuing education courses leading to industry certifications preferred (e.g., AEI, IIA, CPCU).
  • Knowledge of claims investigation techniques, medical terminology and legal aspects of claims.

About this job

Liberty Mutual seeks an Executive Underwriter to manage a Major Accounts Property portfolio of complex monoline accounts with minimum TIVs of $100m in the Central Region. The role involves analyzing property exposures, determining terms and conditions, collaborating with Risk Engineering, and mentoring other underwriters.

Good fit if you have 5+ years of progressive property underwriting experience, strong analytical skills, and experience with risk engineering or property reinsurance.

Full job description


Description

We are seeking an Executive Underwriter to manage and maintain a significant portion of our Major Accounts Property portfolio in the Central Region. In this role, you will be responsible for handling complex monoline Property accounts with minimum TIVs of $100m, analyzing the customer's property exposures, hazards, financial information, requested coverages, loss history, pricing targets and desired program structure to select business and determine appropriate terms and conditions. Will work closely with Risk Engineering to produce and manage a profitable book of business and manage producer/customer relationships. Maintains the highest level of skills/knowledge in the large property space with average account annual premium of around $1m. Shares underwriting expertise with other underwriters and stakeholders across all levels.

Responsibilities

  • Manages portfolio of brokers/agents & clients. Leverages market presence and expertise to develop and underwrite profitable business, acting as a representative for Liberty.
  • Has relationships with senior/market-leading brokers and/or key agents. Maintains a strong market presence, including established relationships with agents and brokers.
  • Looks to strengthen these relationships and develop new ones.
  • Articulates key coverage differences with a high degree of detail. Provides significant input into the business and marketing planning process, including advanced data-driven insights from portfolio analysis.
  • Participates in projects across departments designed to drive underwriting and process excellence (e.g., member of a working team).
  • Models effective collaboration across teams, stakeholders and partners (e.g., UW Support, Claims, Actuarial, Directors of Underwriting in North America).
  • Has strong knowledge of key legal cases, legislation and regulation impacting area(s) of underwriting expertise. Shares knowledge based on technical expertise, including providing external thought-leadership.
  • Mentors, coaches, and trains other underwriters and internal partners.
Qualifications

Qualifications:

  • Prior single carrier property underwriting experience preferred.
  • Prior experience working with property risk engineering and/or loss prevention preferred.
  • Prior property facultative reinsurance or shared and layer property experience also will be considered.
  • Degree in Business or equivalent typically required
  • A minimum of 5 years expected, typically 7 years or more, of progressive underwriting experience and/or other related business experience
  • CPCU or professional insurance designation preferred
  • Proven analytical ability to evaluate and judge underwriting risks within scope of responsibility
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate complex analyses and information in understandable written and/or oral directives to other persons in the organization for underwriting or training purposes
  • Demonstrated effective communication and interpersonal skills in dealing with internal and external stakeholders
  • Must demonstrate comprehension of most complex technical underwriting issues and be capable of defining and implementing necessary underwriting and administrative processes/workflows to properly manage or administer those issues
  • Proven track record of developing and underwriting profitable business

Job.JobTitle: Senior Quantitative Analyst - Liberty Mutual Investments
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Boston, MA
  • Experience: 3+ years
  • Education: Bachelor's degree

About this job

Senior Quantitative Analyst role in Liberty Mutual Investments' Global Liquid Markets unit, applying quantitative methods and machine learning to fixed-income strategy development. Work with Portfolio Managers and Traders on portfolio construction, performance analysis, and systematic strategy development.

Good fit if you have 3+ years in portfolio analysis or systematic fixed-income investing, with hands-on Python and SQL experience.

Full job description


Description

Liberty Mutual Investments (LMI) manages Liberty Mutual Insurance Groups (LMIG) global financial assets across public and private markets to build capital and generate income. With over $100 billion in assets under management and a team of more than 300 investment, finance, and operations professionals based in Boston, MA, LMI offers the best of both worlds: the entrepreneurial spirit of a boutique investment firm backed by the reputation and financial strength of a global leader.

LMI is on a transformational journey to foster innovation, build on our deep expertise, and further scale returns on our long-term capital through a one firm, one portfolio, one team approach. Our operating model is built on three pillars: centralized portfolio construction, asset management, and investment-enabling services. Teams are organized into Investment Business Units (IBUs): Strategy & Asset Allocation, Risk Management, Global Fixed Income, Global Private Investments, and Global Investment Solutions. Our portfolio spans a wide range of asset classes, and we are committed to expanding our capabilities and toolkit to deliver on our mission.

We are seeking a Senior Quantitative Analyst to join the Investment Innovation, Integration & Trading (I3T) team within the Global Liquid Markets (GLM) unit. In this role, you will apply advanced quantitative methods, data modeling, and emerging technologies to enhance investment decision-making across various fixed-income strategies. You will collaborate with team members, Portfolio Managers, and Traders to tackle high-profile projects involving portfolio construction, performance assessment, and the development of new systematic fixed income strategies. This position is pivotal in advancing our teams expertise and helping LMI thrive in the constantly evolving global financial landscape. #LMI #LM-LMI

Responsibilities

  • Quantitative Model Development Systematic Alpha Research
    Design and implement quantitative methods and tools for portfolio construction, performance & attribution, and investment strategies in collaboration with Portfolio Managers, Traders, and Risk Managers.
  • Analytics & Visualization
    Build and refine analytic models, develop robust data pipelines and interactive dashboards, leveraging advanced Python, SQL, Dash and Power BI to translate complex data sets into actionable insights.
  • Machine Learning & AI
    Employ statistical techniques, machine learning algorithms, and GPT-based solutions to improve market analysis, develop investment strategies, and enhance decision-making processes.
  • Innovation & Continuous Improvement
    Proactively identify opportunities to upgrade capabilities and stay at the forefront of fixed-income analytics. Monitor industry trends, market developments, and new analytical tools to maintain a competitive edge.
  • Project Coordination
    Oversee multiple projects simultaneously, ensuring timely delivery of high-quality results. Maintain meticulous attention to detail and effective communication throughout all stages of project execution.
Qualifications

Qualifications

Education

  • Numerate self-starter with a bachelors degree in finance, Economics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field ( Masters degree preferred, CFA a plus.

Experience & Technical Skills

  • 3+ years of experience in portfolio analysis or investment management, with a strong preference for systematic fixed-income experience.
  • Must have hands-on experience with Python, SQL and familiarity with BI/visualization tools (Dash, Power BI, Jupyter Notebooks).
  • Nice-to-have, Practical knowledge of machine learning and AI (including GPT-based models) and their applications in financial analysis.

Tools & Systems

  • Preferred experience with BlackRocks Aladdin, Bloomberg, and Macrobond for data extraction, portfolio monitoring, and analytics.

Soft Skills

  • Tenacious problem-solving abilities with a focus on efficiency and effectiveness.
  • Strong attention to detail and passion for learning.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated interest in investments and a desire to delve into the intricacies of fixed-income markets.

Description

Comparion Insurance Agency is hiring self-motivated, relationship-driven professionals for a rewarding outside sales career. This role offers autonomy and flexibility to build your career, grow your earnings, and make a meaningful impact by helping protect individuals and families with auto, home, life, small commercial auto, and specialty insurance.

Backed by a Fortune 100 company, you'll receive hands-on training, resources, and team support to help you succeed. No prior insurance experience required.

THIS POSITION HAS IN-OFFICE REQUIREMENTS. Must reside in the state of Illinois.

This is a full-time, field-based employee position. Applicants must be able to travel within their local community to meet with customers and build relationships. Reliable transportation, such as a valid driver's license or another means of travel, is preferred.

Pay Details

  • The typical training salary is $55k - $65k
  • Through a combination of base, bonuses, and uncapped commissions, typical total first year compensation ranges from $55k - $75k
  • Potential for top performers to earn over $100k in their first year

What you'll do:

  • Sell auto, home, life, small commercial auto, and related insurance products using a consultative, needs-based approach.
  • Build and maintain a book of business through referrals, networking, and community engagement as part of your outside sales efforts.
  • Identify prospective customers using established lead methodologies and relationship-driven outreach.
  • Accurately document customer interactions and handle sensitive information with integrity and confidentiality.
  • Use insurance sales technology, relationship management tools, and multi-carrier platforms to deliver tailored insurance solutions.
  • Participate in training, coaching, and performance incentives to continuously improve sales results.

Essential functions include: meeting with customers in the office and in the community, communicating by phone, email, and in person, traveling locally, and using a computer and sales software.

Qualifications

Day One Skills & Traits:

  • Self-motivated and accountable: you take ownership of your work and results.
  • Reliable and responsive: you follow through and do what you say you'll do.
  • Professional and trustworthy: you handle customer information with care and integrity.
  • Relationship-focused: you enjoy helping others and building long-term trust.
  • Strong communicator: you're comfortable talking with people and explaining options clearly.
  • Comfortable with technology: you can learn and use new software and digital tools with ease.
  • Composed and dependable: you stay organized and professional while managing multiple customer needs.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in customer-facing roles like retail, hospitality, service, operations, logistics, banking, account management, or sales.
  • Basic understanding of sales conversations, including handling common customer questions or objections.
  • Experience managing multiple accounts, clients, or priorities simultaneously.
  • Exposure to consultative selling, negotiation, or regulated industries.

Licensing:

You will be required to obtain relevant licenses upon being hired (P&C and Life).

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Insurance Sales Manager, Insurance Sales, Insurance Sales Representative
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Independence, OH

About this job

Lead a team of insurance sales agents across Northern Ohio at Comparion Insurance Agency. Drive sales growth, coach your team, and manage branch operations while earning based on team performance.

Good fit if you have a bachelor's degree, insurance sales experience, strong communication skills, and can obtain a state property and casualty license.

Full job description


Description

As a member of the Comparion Insurance Agency, you will lead a team of Insurance Sales Agents across Northern Ohio. This is a high-impact, high-visibility role, with the goal being to better meet the needs of our customers, help improve the sales process for our reps, and to support growth and profitability of the core business by influencing and mentoring sales representatives.

This position is responsible for providing strategic guidance and coaching support to drive the expansion and optimization of the agency, including the identification and evaluation of emerging opportunities for business growth. You determine how much you earn by how well you motivate and develop your team to sell and service customers.

This is a chance to play a key role in evolving the agency while developing and maintaining effective relationships with business partners and serving as a liaison between your branch and other business areas.

Responsibilities:

  • Drive sales team towards achieving/exceeding sales metrics.
  • Develop and coach the sales team.
  • Establish long-lasting relationships with customers in order to maintain high customer retention and satisfaction.
  • Oversee operational functions of the Branch.
  • Ensure exceptional customer satisfaction and high customer retention.
  • Generate strategic and innovative ideas in order to drive new business development.
  • Facilitate an engaging environment in which agents are inspired and feel supported.
  • Manage acquisition and service cost for Branch assignment.
Qualifications
  • Bachelor`s degree or equivalent experience required.
  • Demonstrated knowledge of personal lines products and services; proven success with prior sales or related experience required.
  • Must possess highly effective oral and written communication skills, including group and individual presentation, persuasion, negotiation and customer service skills.
  • Requires excellent organizational skills, effective time management, strong leadership, interpersonal and analytical skills.
  • Incumbents must have, or be able to secure, a current state license, in property, casualty and life insurance.
  • Prior supervisory experience helpful

About this job

Liability trial attorney at Travelers Insurance handling insurance defense litigation cases from inception through trial and appeal. Position involves case analysis, legal research and writing, court proceedings, and client counseling on predominantly low to moderate complexity matters.

Good fit if you have 3+ years of insurance defense litigation experience and an active law license, with ability to independently handle cases through trial.

Full job description

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$112,000.00 - $184,800.00

Target Openings

2

What Is the Opportunity?

Travelers offers the strength of a national legal organization committed to your professional development while maintaining a local focus, positioning you as a strong business partner and trusted advisor who delivers exceptional value through local expertise and outstanding client service. We handle litigation arising from claims asserted against policyholders or the company and take cases from inception through trial and appeal. As a Counsel with Travelers you will be responsible for high quality, proactive case handling and will have the opportunity to use your legal expertise and litigation skills to handle a caseload of predominantly low to moderate complexity and deliver optimal results for Travelers' insured customers.

What Will You Do?

  • In the handling of a caseload of predominantly low to moderate complexity, your responsibilities will include:
  • Develop and apply effective use of litigation skills and techniques to try cases to verdict or negotiate resolution.
  • Conduct legal research and demonstrate strong and persuasive legal writing and presentation skills.
  • Draft pleadings, motions, briefs, discovery and other documents.
  • Attend court events, depositions, and other appointments independently.
  • Provide case analysis and recommendations to insured clients and claim partners on file handling strategies.
  • Build and maintain strong internal and external client and business partner relationships.
  • Provide advice and training to Claim partners and clients.
  • Fully and effectively utilize available technology, case management system and automation.
  • Travel as required to meet business needs.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • 3+ years of insurance defense litigation experience as a practicing attorney.
  • Experience independently handling cases from inception through trial/hearing & appeal.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to present information on litigated matters to diverse audiences
  • Skilled in fostering collaborative relationships with colleagues, customers, and business partners to deliver exceptional customer service
  • Demonstrates persuasive legal writing skills and oral advocacy skills.
  • Strong legal research skills & ability to utilize technology.
  • Effectively manages multiple priorities with an attention to detail, sense of urgency & responsiveness.
  • Exercises sound decision making and possesses strong negotiation skills.
  • Possesses a flexible and agile mindset with a willingness to take on new challenges as needs evolve.

What is a Must Have?

  • Juris Doctorate or equivalent International legal degree; graduate of an accredited law school.
  • 2 years experience as a practicing attorney.
  • Active license in good standing to practice law in the state(s) in which representation is required.
  • Regularly handles hearings, trials, dispositive motion arguments, depositions, or other court proceedings and has the ability to transport to those meetings. Valid driver's license required depending on the location.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit http://careers.travelers.com/life-at-travelers/benefits/.

Good fit if you have six to eight years of construction loss sensitive underwriting experience and a CPCU designation.

Full job description

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$123,400.00 - $203,600.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

The Account Executive Officer (AEO), Construction Loss Sensitive will partner with agents and brokers to provide coverage for new and renewal business based on customers' needs. This role is seen as a technical resource. As an AEO, you are decisive, detail-oriented, and know how to build relationships internally and externally to drive results. Your ability to independently assess complex risk and sell our products in challenging markets will contribute to the profitability and success of Travelers.

What Will You Do?

  • Underwrite casualty programs for large construction projects including Wrap Ups, Joint Ventures and Project Specific placements.
  • Manage the profitability, growth, and retention of an assigned book of business.
  • Underwrite and skillfully negotiate complex customer accounts to minimize risk and maximize profitability.
  • Cultivate and maintain relationships with internal partners within the business unit and across the enterprise to create sales plans and identify cross-selling opportunities.
  • Foster and maintain relationships with external partners by regularly meeting in person with agents and brokers to market and sell Travelers products with a goal of writing and retaining accounts consistent with our risk appetite. Must be able to travel to such meetings.
  • Identify and capture new business opportunities using consultative marketing and sales skills.
  • Independently develop and execute agency sales plans and frequently partner with your Managing Director (MD) to develop region/group sales plans.
  • May assist in the training and mentoring of less experienced Account Executives.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's degree.
  • Six to eight years of relevant underwriting experience with experience in construction loss sensitive.
  • Deep knowledge of construction loss sensitive products, the regulatory environment, and the local insurance market.
  • Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to proactively identify underwriting, marketing, or financial challenges and analyze available information to make timely decisions in alignment with our risk appetite.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to successfully negotiate in difficult situations with agents and brokers.
  • CPCU designation.

What is a Must Have?

  • Four years of underwriting, claim, operations, risk assessment, actuarial, sales, product, or finance experience.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences.
