Job.JobTitle: Claim Professional Development Program Internship (CPDP Intern)
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $25.00 to $26.00 an hour
  • Schedule: Internship
  • Location: Diamond Bar, CA

About this job

Internship in insurance claims at Travelers in Diamond Bar, California. Gain hands-on training in claims investigation, damage estimation, and coverage determination through structured onboarding, mentorship, and ride-alongs with experienced claim professionals.

Good fit if you are pursuing or have a Bachelor's degree, prefer business-related studies, and are authorized to work in the U.S.

Full job description

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The hourly salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual hourly rate for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards. 

Salary Range

$25.00 - $26.00

Target Openings

2

What Is the Opportunity?

Applicants must be authorized to work for ANY employer in the U.S. now and in the future. The company does not sponsor/support H-1B petitions, TN, or Forms I-983/STEM OPT for this role. The Travelers Claim Intern program provides qualified candidates an excellent opportunity to gain first-hand business experience, receive valuable on-the-job training, contact clients, determine coverage, scoping of losses and completing damage estimates. We are seeking applicants who are interested about entering the insurance industry and who are excited about the prospect of making Claim their future career choice. Housing assistance is not provided.

Applications for this posting will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

What Will You Do?

  • Structured onboarding to Travelers systems and protocols.
  • Exposure to Personal and Business Insurance claims of basic to moderate complexity.
  • Learn and understand effective strategies for investigating, negotiating and resolving claims thoroughly, accurately and efficiently.
  • Develop knowledge of what happened, estimating damage, determining what coverages apply and helping our customers through the process through strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Observe the work of the Claim Professional through desk and 'ride-alongs' with experienced employees.
  • Work with a designated manager/mentor to develop knowledge of claims through core assignments.
  • Develop a strong foundation of customer service, analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Complete challenging and meaningful project work.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Preferred cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above.
  • Suggested college majors include Business Administration, Liberal Arts (with business focus preferred), Business Management, Risk Management and Insurance or a business-related discipline.
  • Knowledge of Microsoft Office.

What is a Must Have?

  • Obtained or pursuing a Bachelor's degree.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

We are committed to providing accommodation to persons with disabilities. If you require accommodation during the recruitment or interview process we will work with you to accommodate your needs.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit http://careers.travelers.com/life-at-travelers/benefits/.

Quick facts

  • Pay: $112,000 to $184,800 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Rancho Cordova, CA
  • Experience: 3+ years
  • License: Valid driver's license
  • Benefits: Health insurance, 401(k), paid time off

About this job

Litigation Counsel at Travelers Insurance handling insurance defense cases from inception through trial and appeal. You will manage a caseload of low to moderate complexity, conduct legal research, draft pleadings, attend court proceedings, and advise claim partners and clients on case strategy.

Good fit if you have 3+ years of insurance defense litigation experience, an active law license, and can independently handle cases through trial or appeal.

Full job description

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$112,000.00 - $184,800.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

Travelers offers the strength of a national legal organization committed to your professional development while maintaining a local focus, positioning you as a strong business partner and trusted advisor who delivers exceptional value through local expertise and outstanding client service. We handle litigation arising from claims asserted against policyholders or the company and take cases from inception through trial and appeal. As a Counsel with Travelers you will be responsible for high quality, proactive case handling and will have the opportunity to use your legal expertise and litigation skills to handle a caseload of predominantly low to moderate complexity and deliver optimal results for Travelers' insured customers.

What Will You Do?

  • In the handling of a caseload of predominantly low to moderate complexity, your responsibilities will include:
  • Develop and apply effective use of litigation skills and techniques to try cases to verdict or negotiate resolution.
  • Conduct legal research and demonstrate strong and persuasive legal writing and presentation skills.
  • Draft pleadings, motions, briefs, discovery and other documents.
  • Attend court events, depositions, and other appointments independently.
  • Provide case analysis and recommendations to insured clients and claim partners on file handling strategies.
  • Build and maintain strong internal and external client and business partner relationships.
  • Provide advice and training to Claim partners and clients.
  • Fully and effectively utilize available technology, case management system and automation.
  • Travel as required to meet business needs.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • 3+ years of insurance defense litigation experience as a practicing attorney.
  • Experience independently handling cases from inception through trial/hearing & appeal.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to present information on litigated matters to diverse audiences
  • Skilled in fostering collaborative relationships with colleagues, customers, and business partners to deliver exceptional customer service
  • Demonstrates persuasive legal writing skills and oral advocacy skills.
  • Strong legal research skills & ability to utilize technology.
  • Effectively manages multiple priorities with an attention to detail, sense of urgency & responsiveness.
  • Exercises sound decision making and possesses strong negotiation skills.
  • Possesses a flexible and agile mindset with a willingness to take on new challenges as needs evolve.

What is a Must Have?

  • Juris Doctorate or equivalent International legal degree; graduate of an accredited law school.
  • 2 years experience as a practicing attorney.
  • Active license in good standing to practice law in the state(s) in which representation is required.
  • Regularly handles hearings, trials, dispositive motion arguments, depositions, or other court proceedings and has the ability to transport to those meetings. Valid driver's license required depending on the location.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit http://careers.travelers.com/life-at-travelers/benefits/.

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Property Claims Adjuster, Claims, Claims Representative
Job.JobDescription:
Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$53,800.00 - $88,800.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

As an Associate Claim Rep, Outside Property, you will receive comprehensive training in claim handling, customer service, and policy interpretation while working alongside experienced claim professionals. This position focuses on developing your skills and knowledge to successfully manage 1st party property claims. This program is typically 9-12 months and upon successful completion of this program you will have the skills needed to handle claims independently and progress toward full claims handling responsibility. This position is based remotely with work at residential and commercial locations with a combination of mobile work, work from your primary residence, or the nearest Travelers office. This is a field position with a territory in the Hudson area of Massachusetts.

What Will You Do?

  • Actively participate in structured training classes covering insurance policies, specific claim processes, systems, and procedures, including virtual, classroom, and on-the-job training.
  • Review, investigate, and document 1st party property claims under close supervision.
  • Gather information from policyholders, claimants, witnesses, and third-party providers.
  • Learn to investigate and evaluate all relevant facts and information (including but not limited to analyzing leases, contracts, by-laws and other relevant documents which may have an impact). Determine and apply coverage for building damages per policy terms.
  • Establish accurate scope of damages for building and contents losses and utilizes as a basis for written estimates and/or computer assisted estimates.
  • Provide timely and professional communication to customers, claimants, and internal stakeholders.
  • Maintain accurate records of claim activity in claim management systems.
  • Demonstrate openness to continuous learning, particularly in AI and digital transformation.
  • Adapt to new technology implementations, system upgrades, and digital tool rollouts while maintaining productivity and service quality.
  • In order to perform the essential functions of this role, acquisition and maintenance of Insurance License(s) and/or a UAS Remote Pilot Certification may be required to comply with federal, state, and Travelers requirements. Generally, required Insurance License(s) must be obtained within three months of starting the role, and ongoing continuing education requirements must be maintained as mandated.
  • This position requires participation in our Catastrophe Response Program, which could include deployment to assist our customers in other states.
  • This position requires the individual to access and inspect all areas of a dwelling or structure, which is physically demanding requiring the ability to carry, set up and climb a ladder weighing approximately 38 to 49 pounds, walk on roofs, and enter tight spaces (such as attic staircases and entries, crawl spaces, etc.). While specific territory or day-to-day responsibilities may not require an individual to climb a ladder, the incumbent must be capable of safely climbing a ladder when deploying to a catastrophe which is a requirement of the position.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's Degree.
  • Previous internship or work experience in customer service or insurance.

What are the requirements needed for this position?

  • Must have strong verbal and written communication skills

What other skills/experience would be helpful to have?

Job.JobTitle: Summer 2027 Intern: Employee Relations & People Partner Intern
Job.JobDescription:
The Assurant Internship Program is a 12-week immersive experience where interns do not sit on the sidelines. You will gain real-world experience by tackling business challenges and helping drive meaningful outcomes. The program combines hands-on work with learning and development opportunities, mentorship, networking and engagement opportunities, and resources designed to support your professional growth.


Are you curious about what drives employee engagement, workplace culture, and organizational success?

At Assurant, our greatest asset is our people and our culture is a distinct competitive advantage. This is more than a traditional HR internship. You'll contribute to projects that strengthen business outcomes through influencing culture, improving employee experiences, and proactively identifying and mitigating organizational risks. Along the way, you'll develop valuable skills in employee relations, workforce analytics, problem solving, stakeholder management, and strategic thinking.


At Assurant, we're transforming the way work gets done by harnessing innovative thinking, the power of AI, automation, and data-driven insights while leveraging the unique skills of our people to deliver the greatest value in the moments that matter most.


As an intern, you'll have the opportunity to:

  • Work on meaningful projects focused on driving our culture and continually improving the support and experiences of our employees and leaders
  • Gain exposure to Employee Relations and HR People Partner teams
  • Analyze employee feedback and workforce data to uncover insights
  • Collaborate with experienced HR professionals and business leaders
  • Help improve processes, resources, and experiences
  • Explore emerging HR technologies, digital enablement, and AI-powered solutions
  • Present recommendations and ideas that can influence real business outcomes

You'll leave with practical experience, professional connections, and a deeper understanding of how leading organizations create great employee experiences while delivering business results.


What You'll Do

Employee Experience & Workforce Insights

  • Analyze engagement survey results, employee feedback, and workforce trends to identify themes, root causes, and opportunities.
  • Help develop presentations, dashboards, reports, and executive-ready summaries that communicate insights and recommendations.
  • Summarize survey comments and feedback trends to support People Partner priorities and action planning.
  • Research employee experience and workplace trends to inform team initiatives.

Special Projects & Stakeholder Collaboration

  • Partner with People Partners and cross-functional stakeholders on strategic and operational priorities.
  • Gather stakeholder feedback and analyze findings to identify opportunities for process improvement and stronger employee experiences.
  • Conduct research and benchmarking, then translate findings into practical recommendations.
  • Support presentations, communications, project materials, and leadership updates.
  • Bring a fresh perspective by challenging assumptions, identifying new ideas, and recommending innovative approaches.
  • Contribute to projects focused on employee relations, organizational effectiveness, digital enablement, employee experience, and continuous improvement.

Performance Management & Employee Relations Support

  • Support review of performance improvement and termination documentation for completeness, consistency, and alignment with company practices, while identifying items requiring additional People Partner review.
  • Help identify recurring documentation themes and opportunities to improve consistency and effectiveness.
  • Support maintenance of templates, resources, and job aids used by the People Partner team.
  • Summarize findings and insights related to performance management and employee relations activities to drive continual improvements.

Process Improvement & Digital Enablement

  • Support documentation and continuous improvement of People Partner processes, tools, and resources.
  • Assist with process mapping and identify opportunities to simplify workflows, reduce administrative effort, and improve efficiency.
  • Support development, testing, and implementation of tools, templates, and digital solutions that provide consistent guidance.
  • Help maintain centralized process documentation and knowledge resources.

Required Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Human Resources, Business, Psychology, Organizational Development, or a related field. Graduating between December 2027 - May 2028
  • Demonstrated interest in HR, employee experience, or process improvement.
  • Experience using Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, or similar tools.
  • Strong curiosity, a proactive learning mindset, and a problem-solving approach.
  • Analytical skills with attention to detail.
  • Ability to organize and simplify complex information.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to handle confidential and sensitive information with discretion.
  • A collaborative, team-oriented, and people-centered approach.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with process mapping tools, such as Visio.
  • Exposure to HR processes, employee relations, or employment practices.
  • Interest in HR technology, automation, or AI-driven solutions.
  • Experience summarizing data and creating visual insights.

The Role at a Glance

The VP, Legal Counsel M&A and Reinsurance will play a key role in advancing Lincoln's strategic priorities by providing legal counsel across mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, reinsurance transactions, and other strategic initiatives. This leader will guide transactions from structuring and due diligence through negotiation, execution, and integration, partnering closely with executive leadership, Finance, business leaders, and other key stakeholders. As a trusted advisor, they will help shape transaction strategy, navigate complex legal and regulatory considerations, mitigate risk, and deliver practical solutions that support business objectives.

This role is ideal for a highly experienced transactional attorney who brings strong business judgment, executive presence, and the ability to lead sophisticated negotiations while influencing decisions across the organization.

What you'll be doing

  • Responsible for all legal aspects of mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, joint ventures, and reinsurance transactions, including structuring, negotiation, due diligence, and execution.
  • Provides strategic legal counsel to executive leadership and other stakeholders on transaction risks, regulatory and compliance implications, negotiation strategy, and complex deal structures.
  • Leads complex negotiations with external counterparties, regulators, and partners, representing the company in high-impact transactions.
  • Partners cross-functionally with Finance, business unit leaders, and other SME(s) in developing and executing legal strategy.
  • Proactively evaluates evolving regulatory and competitive landscapes, as well as developments and trends in applicable practice areas, and adapts legal advice accordingly.
  • Advises on integration and separation activities, ensuring legal risks are identified, mitigated, and managed effectively.
  • Develops and maintains key external relationships, including external counsel and trade/industry groups.
  • Provides legal counsel as needed on enterprise contracts involving the acquisition of goods and services, including software-as-a-service and outsourcing

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $75,000 to $120,000 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Radnor, PA
  • Experience: 4+ years
  • Benefits: 401(k), paid time off, tuition assistance

About this job

Senior Associate Actuarial Analyst role in assumption governance at Lincoln Financial, part of the Actuarial Development Program with rotations across business areas. Reviews and documents Life business assumptions, partners with Pricing on model inputs, and develops process improvements.

Good fit if you have passed at least 4 actuarial exams, have 1 to 4+ years of actuarial experience, know MG-ALFA, and work well independently and across teams.

Full job description

Alternate Locations: Radnor, PA (Pennsylvania); Charlotte, NC (North Carolina); Fort Wayne, IN (Indiana); Greensboro, NC (North Carolina); Hartford, CT (Connecticut); Omaha, NE (Nebraska)

Relocation assistance: is not available for this opportunity.

The Role at a Glance

The Actuarial Development Program (ADP) at Lincoln Financial is an industry-leading program that demonstrates Lincoln Financial's commitment to creating highly qualified business leaders. As an ADP participant, you'll be able to explore your unique interests while developing the essential actuarial, technical, management, communication, and leadership skills you need to succeed. The Actuarial Development Program includes a series of rotations, typically every 18-24 months. For each rotation, roles are available in different business areas including Life and Annuities, Retirement and Group Protection. Experience gained will enable participants to become well-rounded actuaries with knowledge that may include Product Development, Pricing, Reinsurance, Inforce Management, Valuation, Financial Projections, Risk Management, Financial Planning & Analysis, Financial Strategy & Management, Appointed Actuary, Experience Studies, Modeling and Data Analytics & Actuarial Transformation.


ADP participants are expected to pass the Society of Actuaries' exams at a prescribed pace. The program is designed to support you as you work towards your FSA and provide the training and resources necessary to become a well-rounded actuarial leader.

Additional Program Highlights:

•Highly competitive compensation package with salary increases and bonuses upon successful exam completion
•Social and training opportunities to enhance skills, network with ADP participants and build long-lasting industry relationships
•Dedicated leaders and mentors to assist with career development
•Work with actuarial and data science software and technologies including MG-ALFA, Axis, Prophet, Dataiku, R, and Tableau
•Generous study time allowances for each exam session
•Payment and/or reimbursement of actuarial exam fees, materials, review courses, and seminars taken during the program


We're excited to bring on an Senior Associate Actuarial Analyst, Assumption Governance, to own the review and documentation of assumption proposals, approvals, implementations and impacts. This role offers a unique view into the assumptions that drive profitability across Life business, and it is a strong fit for someone who enjoys diving into the details of model inputs, taking on ad hoc projects, and collaborating across teams.

What you'll be doing

•Manage and maintain documentation of Life new business assumptions, including regular updates, version control, documentation of changes.
•Partner with the Pricing team to understand, review and refine model (MG-ALFA) input assumptions.
•Coordinate assumption updates with cross-functional teams and confirm that the latest approved assumptions are reflected in the assumptions
•Develop tools and process improvements to make assumption maintenance and validation more efficient and controlled
•Support ad hoc data analysis and projects as priorities evolve

What we're looking for

•Minimum of 4 actuarial exams passed
•1 to 4+ years of actuarial experience
•1 prior actuarial rotation
•Working knowledge of MG-ALFA
•Strong technical skills (Microsoft Office suite)
•Self-motivated with high level of integrity, strong problem-solving skills, and the capability of working independently
•Ability to quickly learn and apply new skills and information
•Collaborative, with the ability to build effective relationships across teams
•Strong written and verbal communication skills
•Experience with Tableau, SQL and Python is a plus

Job.JobTitle: Life Insurance Agency Development Manager (Life Sales Manager)
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Insurance Sales Manager, Insurance Sales, Insurance Sales Representative
Job.JobDescription:
*This range represents a national range and the actual salary will depend on several factors including the scope and complexity of the role and the skills, education, training, credentials, location (State) based on ERIE's geographical differences, and experience of an applicant, as well as level of role for which the successful candidate is hired. Position may be eligible for an annual bonus payment.

At Erie Insurance, you're not just part of a Fortune 500 company; you're also a valued member of a diverse and inclusive team that includes more than 6,000 employees and over 13,000 independent agencies. Our Employees work in the Home Office complex located in Erie, PA, and in our Field Offices that span 12 states and the District of Columbia.

Benefits That Go Beyond The Basics

We strive to be Above all in Service® to our customers—and to our employees. That's why Erie Insurance offers you an exceptional benefits package, including:

  • Premier health, prescription, dental, and vision benefits for you and your dependents. Coverage begins your first day of work.
  • Low contributions to medical and prescription premiums. We currently pay up to 97% of employees' monthly premium costs.
  • Pension. We are one of only 13 Fortune 500 companies to offer a traditional pension plan. Full-time employees are vested after five years of service.
  • 401(k) with up to 4% contribution match. The 401(k) is offered in addition to the pension.
  • Paid time off. Paid vacation, personal days, sick days, bereavement days and parental leave.
  • Career development. Including a tuition reimbursement program for higher education and industry designations.

Additional benefits that include company-paid basic life insurance; short-and long-term disability insurance; orthodontic coverage for children and adults; adoption assistance; fertility and infertility coverage; well-being programs; paid volunteer hours for service to your community; and dollar-for-dollar matching of your charitable gifts each year.

Position Summary

Life Sales Manager

ERIE Family Life is seeking a Life Sales Manager to drive life insurance and annuity growth across Central and Eastern Pennsylvania. In this highly visible field leadership role, you'll partner with independent ERIE Agents to expand life insurance production, identify cross-sell opportunities, develop agency growth strategies, and provide consultative sales coaching that helps agencies strengthen customer relationships and grow their business.

Success in This Role

Within the first year, successful Life Sales Managers will:

  • Build trusted relationships with agency partners throughout the territory
  • Increase life insurance and annuity production
  • Identify and execute agency growth opportunities
  • Conduct joint sales calls and field coaching sessions
  • Help agents develop sustainable life insurance sales strategies
  • Partner with branch leadership to drive territory performance and business growth

Territory

This territory-based position supports agencies throughout Central and Eastern Pennsylvania, including Harrisburg, Lancaster, Reading, Allentown, Bethlehem, Easton, and surrounding communities.

Candidates should reside within or near the Harrisburg or Lehigh Valley markets and be willing to travel throughout the assigned territory.

A company vehicle is provided.

Additional Opportunity

The hiring manager will also consider candidates for the Senior Life Sales Manager (F13) level. The level offered will be based on the selected candidate's experience, qualifications, and demonstrated success in life insurance sales leadership, agency development, and territory management.

Trains and guides Agents in a designated branch territory as well as additional assigned branch offices in the promotion and sale of life insurance and annuity products, providing assistance in the areas of production, product knowledge and application, underwriting, and agency management. Also assists Agents in examining and evaluating their current books of business for potential prospects and serves as company representative in maintaining favorable agency and Policyholder relationships. Scope: Life Sales Manager role is assigned to one branch. Sr Life Sales Manager is assigned to multiple branches.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Assists branch managers and district sales managers in establishing short- and long-range objectives related to life insurance and annuity sales, with emphasis on production, underwriting and Agent training.
  • Provides training and direction to ERIE Agents regarding the promotion and sale of life insurance and annuity products. Interacts with Agents as necessary, educating them regarding approved marketing and sales tools and techniques.
  • Educates Agents regarding the products available through Erie Family Life, including policy features and benefits. Assists Agents in reviewing their current books of business in order to identify cross selling opportunities for life insurance and annuity sales. Collaborates with Agents to identify prospecting opportunities.
  • Accompanies Agents on sales calls and assists with servicing existing customers and writing new business.
  • Serves as a liaison between the Home Office and the field. Clarifies and resolves issues, implements new programs and communicates program changes as necessary.
  • Represents the company in community relations activities as directed.
  • Develops marketing and prospecting programs to assist Agents in the sale of life insurance and annuity products.
  • Collaborates with Home Office and Branch Office marketing personnel regarding the design and promotion of incentive campaigns related to the sales of life insurance and annuity products.
  • Assists in the selection and training of newly appointed Agents, life producers and customer service representatives.
  • Handles Agency relationships and business, as a licensed life insurance Agent, according to company policy.
  • Advises appropriate Home Office personnel of competitive intelligence issues related to Agents and agency management.

The first 6 duties listed are the functions identified as essential to the job. Essential functions are those job duties that must be performed in order for the job to be accomplished.


This position description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the incumbent. Employees are required to follow any other job-related instruction and to perform any other duties as requested by their supervisor, or as become evident.

Capabilities

  • Values Diversity
  • Self-Development
  • Nimble Learning
  • Collaborates
  • Customer Focus
  • Cultivates Innovation
  • Instills Trust
  • Optimizes Work Processes (IC)
  • Ensures Accountability
  • Decision Quality

Qualifications

Minimum Educational Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in insurance, sales, marketing or related field and five years' experience in sales, investment and/or annuity products or in life insurance related experience is required; or
  • Associate's degree in insurance, sales, marketing or related field and seven years' experience in sales, investment and/or annuity products or in life insurance related experience is required; or
  • High School diploma or GED and nine years' experience in sales, investment and/or annuity products or in life insurance related experience is required; or

Additional Experience

  • A minimum of two years' experience in sales of life insurance.
  • The incumbent must live in the state assigned unless a change is approved by the company.
  • Frequent overnight travel required.

Designations and/or Licenses

  • Related designations, such as CIC, CFP, ChFC, or CLU, preferred.

Physical Requirements

  • Lifting/Moving 0-20 lbs; Occasional (<20%)
  • Lifting/Moving 20-50 lbs; Occasional (<20%)
  • Ability to move over 50 lbs using lifting aide equipment; Occasional (<20%)
  • Driving; Frequent (50-80%)
  • Pushing/Pulling/moving objects, equipment with wheels; Occasional (<20%)
  • Manual Keying/Data Entry/inputting information/computer use; Often (20-50%)
  • Climbing/accessing heights; Rarely

The Role at a Glance

We are excited to bring on a highly motivated Sr. Associate Long Term Disability Team Lead to staff our ever-growing claims organization.

As a Sr. Associate Long Term Disability Team Lead, you will perform and deliver on long-term disability (LTD) claims assignments/projects while simultaneously leveraging and applying knowledge. You will review, investigate, and make claim determinations regarding coverage, compensability, and appropriateness assigned claims. You will provide oversight, technical information, detailed guidance and supervise the daily activities for their assigned claims area. Additionally, they will oversee and ensure the daily fair, ethical, and timely management of all claims area(s).

What you'll be doing

  • You'll manage a caseload of complex Long Term Disability claims with varied eligibility types, policy provisions, and diagnoses.
  • You'll apply policies and engage internal and external resources to ensure fair, ethical, and timely claim decisions.
  • You'll make claim-related financial decisions within company guidelines.
  • You'll use sound judgment and claims expertise to decide based on the information available.
  • You'll explain policy details, the claims process, and determinations so customers understand the outcome.
  • You'll keep inventory stable through timely risk management and efficient processing.
  • You'll resolve escalated issues and elevate to management when needed.
  • You'll research questions from the Claims team, partnering with Underwriting, Actuarial, Compliance, Account Management, and others to find answers.
  • You'll provide technical guidance on claims adjudication and coach junior team members on medical terminology, duration, functionality documentation, and workflow.
  • You'll monitor individual and team performance and act to meet or exceed standards.
  • You'll analyze reports to spot trends, then propose and develop process improvements that enhance performance and the customer experience.
  • You'll advise on how proposed process changes affect operations and system compatibility.
  • You'll mentor others and model the behaviors that build claims knowledge and strong relationships.
  • You'll contribute to departmental projects and lead workstreams as needed.

What we're looking for

Must-have experience (Required):

  • 4 Year/Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience (4 years of experience in lieu of Bachelor's).
  • 1+ Years of Long Term Disability claims experience directly aligned to the specific responsibilities for this role.
  • Ability to communicate effectively (verbal/written).
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook).

Nice-to have experience (Preferred):

  • Strong mathematical skills for payment calculations.
  • Strong attention to detail.

Farmers believes in a culture of collaboration, creativity, and innovation, which thrives when we have the ability to work flexibly in a virtual setting as well as the opportunity to be together in person. Our hybrid work environment combines the best of both worlds with at least three (3) days in office and up to two (2) days virtual for employees who live within fifty (50) miles of a Farmers corporate office. Applicants beyond fifty (50) miles may still be considered.

Job Summary

Ready to change how a Life Insurance business uses data to grow? As Director, Business Intelligence & Analytics, you will lead a team of two analysts and serve as the go-to data and analytics partner across our Life Insurance organization. You will transform how the business accesses and uses data, turning insights from distribution and sales, new business, and customer and agent experience into decisions that drive profitable growth.

Your team will own a portfolio of field-facing and operational reports and dashboards, build statistical models, and provide the analytical horsepower behind high-visibility, cross-functional initiatives. You will influence data and analytics strategy, review and approve analytics initiatives, oversee the support and evolution of existing data products, and bring innovative ideas to business leadership, then lead them through to implementation. This is a highly visible role for a builder who wants to see their work move the needle.

Essential Job Functions

In this role, you will lead the analytics engine behind our Life Insurance business. You will develop advanced, value-driven analytics solutions, from statistical models that sharpen our understanding of the application funnel, policy placement, and persistency to Power BI dashboards that give agents, field leaders, and operations teams the insights they need to act. You will own and continuously evolve a portfolio of field-facing and operational reports and dashboards so they keep pace with changing business needs.

As a trusted partner to leaders across distribution and sales, customer and agent experience, and operations, you will identify the biggest opportunities to unlock business value, translate them into clear analytics requirements and business plans, and drive them to resolution. You will apply a deep understanding of the data elements, structures, and standards common in financial services and Life Insurance, including cloud-based data storage and sharing, to balance regulatory and compliance requirements with business needs. You will consult on UAT, technical specifications, strategic planning, contract design, testing, and training, and independently lead highly complex projects with little to no guidance.

As a people leader, you will supervise, coach, and manage the performance of two analysts, deliver regular feedback, and support their professional development, fostering a high-performance culture where excellence is standard and innovation is actively encouraged. You will craft strategic plans and turn them into action for your team and for partners across three or more business domains, communicating strategy in a way that resonates with audiences new to data and analytics and helping enable enterprise priorities.

Education Requirements

Bachelor's degree or equivalent required, preferably in Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Data Science, Computer Science, Information Systems, Actuarial Science, Finance, Business Analytics, or a related quantitative field. Master's degree in Analytics, Data Science, Statistics, Economics, or an MBA with a quantitative focus preferred. Relevant certifications, such as Microsoft Certified: Power BI Data Analyst Associate or insurance industry designations (e.g., LOMA FLMI), are a plus.

Experience Requirements

7-10 years of related work experience in business intelligence, analytics, or data science required, including:

  • Building and maintaining enterprise reporting and dashboards in Power BI (or a comparable BI tool) for business and front-line audiences, including data modeling and DAX

  • Applying statistical and predictive modeling techniques (e.g., regression, segmentation, propensity or retention modeling) to solve business problems and influence decisions

  • Hands-on proficiency with SQL and experience working with data warehouses, data marts, and cloud-based data platforms across multiple source systems

  • Partnering with senior business leaders to translate ambiguous questions into analytics requirements, prioritized roadmaps, and measurable business outcomes

  • Leading complex, cross-functional analytics initiatives with IT, data science, product, and vendor partners from concept through implementation

  • Establishing data quality, governance, and reporting standards, and resolving data issues across systems

  • Communicating insights and recommendations clearly to executive and non-technical audiences

Preferred experience:

  • Insurance or financial services industry experience, ideally in Life Insurance, with familiarity with new business, underwriting, policy administration, and distribution data

  • Experience analyzing sales and distribution performance, application funnel and throughput, placement, persistency, or agent and customer experience metrics

  • Experience in a people leader or management role, including coaching and developing analysts

  • Experience supporting field-facing or agent-facing reporting in a distribution-driven organization

  • Working knowledge of Python or R and of data privacy and regulatory considerations in insurance

Benefits

Required job duties are normally performed in a climate- controlled office environment, with some exposure to uncontrollable outside environmental conditions and travel via automobile and/or commercial transportation.

Bachelors degree preferred. Licensed to practice law in applicable states required upon hire.

Experience Requirements

Three years of insurance defense litigation and/or personal/bodily injury experience preferred. Second chair trial experience strongly preferred. Multistate jurisdictional practice preferred.

Public speaking, ability to function and handle high case loads in adversarial or confrontational situations, driving.

Strong verbal communication and listening skills. Excellent written communication skills. Effective negotiation skills. Demonstrated conflict management skills. Job Description

Director – Contracts - Reinsurance

This is a hybrid role with the flexibility to work both virtually and from our Chicago, IL or Bloomington, MN office

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we build decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

What the day will look like

Joining Aon's Reinsurance Solutions team, you will take charge of preparing, examining, and completing formal documentation that captures the terms and conditions related to treaty reinsurance arrangements. You will be motivated to continuously learn and stay current with industry expressions, conditions, trends, and regulatory changes.

Role Responsibilities

  • Support hiring, workforce planning, and talent development to ensure suitable staffing, technical knowledge, and capabilities within the department.
  • Prepare complex reinsurance contracts and review the work of supporting Contract Drafters, ensuring technical quality, accuracy, and consistency.
  • Manage and develop team of supporting Contract Drafters, offering technical mentorship, quality oversight, mentoring, feedback, and support for colleague development.
  • Participate in client, reinsurer, and broker meetings, providing wording expertise in the development and interpretation of contract language.
  • Apply deep understanding of reinsurance structures and intent to guide brokers and clients in developing and interpreting contract language covering complex coverage builds and potential loss scenarios.
  • Partner with brokers during placement negotiations to join client discussions regarding wording provisions addressing emerging risks and specific client concerns.
  • Support business growth and strengthen client advocacy through RFP participation, competitor wording reviews, and recommendations for coverage and contract improvements for new and existing clients.
  • Maintain a solid grasp of evolving insurance, reinsurance, and risk management market conditions and keep brokers and clients updated on pertinent developments.
  • Serve as a senior subject-matter expert on reinsurance contract wordings, offering mentorship and recommendations to brokers and clients.
  • Manage departmental projects and initiatives passionate about improving contract processes, capabilities, consistency, and client service.
  • Develop training materials and deliver internal technical training on reinsurance contract wording, market trends, and guidelines within the department.
  • Contribute to the Annual Global Client Training Summit by presenting to clients and preparing materials on reinsurance contract wording trends, market developments, and possible coverage or contract improvements.
  • Support multiline reinsurance business for Global and US clients.

Skills and experience that will lead to success

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Legal Studies, Risk Management, a related field, or equivalent years of industry experience.
  • A minimum of 8 years in insurance or reinsurance, working as a lawyer/attorney or contract/policy specialist, with preference for experience in reinsurance structures. Experience drafting and interpreting treaty wordings for domestic and global placements is preferred.

For positions in San Francisco and Los Angeles, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction record in accordance with local Fair Chance ordinances.

About this job

Principal Software Engineer role at Allstate's Technology Operations, Risk & Compliance division, building the Unified System of Controls platform for enterprise-scale risk management. Requires leading engineering team development, establishing engineering practices, and delivering secure, sustainable control and compliance capabilities across the organization.

Good fit if you have 12+ years leading enterprise-scale software delivery, building high-performing engineering teams, and translating strategy into technical execution.

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

Technology Operations, Risk & Compliance (TORC) is ACCs first-line operating system for controls, risk management and remediation, compliance, and resilience. TORC operates at the intersection of cybersecurity, technology operations, risk, controls, compliance, resilience, and enterprise transformation, turning ACC priorities and enterprise obligations into measurable controls, actionable intelligence, accountability, and sustained risk reduction.

TORC is entering the next phase of that evolution: engineering risk and control capabilities that operate at enterprise scale. A cornerstone of this work is the Unified System of Controls (USC), a strategic ACC product intended to provide a sustainable command-and-control capability for controls, bringing together control expectations, procedures, measurement, evidence, reporting, exceptions, ownership, and accountability.

The Principal Engineer will help build the engineering function required to make that ambition real.

Job Summary

The role will also establish close engineering partnerships with Product Security (ProdSec) and Security Operations (SecOps) across ACC, leveraging and integrating their capabilities into TORC products where appropriate and avoiding creation of parallel security engineering capabilities.


Key Responsibilities

Build and Lead the TORC Engineering Function

  • Build and mature TORC's engineering capability, including the talent, engineering practices, operating model, delivery discipline, and technical competencies necessary to deliver enterprise-scale products.
  • Establish an engineering culture centered on quality, automation, reliability, security, reuse, observability, and measurable outcomes.
  • Build and develop a high-performing engineering organization capable of solving complex technology, risk, and control problems.
  • Establish clear engineering accountability and decision rights while developing future technical leaders and strengthening engineering capability across the organization.
  • Create reusable engineering patterns and capabilities that enable TORC to scale beyond individual solutions.


Deliver the Unified System of Controls (USC)

  • Provide senior engineering leadership for the Unified System of Controls, translating its product direction and requirements into scalable, production-grade technology.
  • Lead engineering delivery of capabilities supporting control measurement, evidence, reporting, exceptions, workflow, integration, accountability, and decision-grade insight.
  • Enable the movement from point-in-time and manually intensive control processes toward sustainable capabilities supported by automation and continuous telemetry.
  • Ensure USC engineering is designed for enterprise scale, sustainability, interoperability, security, reliability, and reuse.
  • Establish an extensible engineering foundation that can support additional TORC and ACC strategic products over time.


Translate Strategy and Product Direction into Engineering Execution

  • Partner with Digital Product leadership to convert product vision, priorities, and outcomes into executable engineering roadmaps and delivery.
  • Apply sound engineering judgment to determine how capabilities should be implemented within established enterprise technology and architecture direction.
  • Bring an engineering perspective into product discovery, helping teams understand technical feasibility, complexity, dependencies, scalability, and implementation tradeoffs.
  • Maintain strong discipline between strategy ownership, product ownership, architecture accountability, and engineering execution.


What Success Looks Like

Success is not simply delivering a technology solution. It is establishing engineering as a durable capability within TORC.


The Principal Engineer will have:

  • Built a mature, high-performing TORC engineering function with clear accountability, strong talent, disciplined engineering practices, and an outcome-oriented culture.
  • Delivered significant engineering capabilities supporting the Unified System of Controls and demonstrated that USC can operate as a sustainable enterprise product.
  • Created strong working relationships across Platform Consulting, Digital Product, Architecture, Product Security, Security Operations, and other ACC engineering functions.
  • Established reusable engineering capabilities that can scale additional TORC and ACC strategic products.
  • Increased the use of automation, integration, telemetry, and continuous measurement within TORC products.
  • Demonstrated that complex risk and control challenges can increasingly be addressed through sustainable engineering rather than additional manual process.
  • Established TORC Engineering as a trusted, high-impact technology partner within ACC.


Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, or a related technical field required.
  • Master's degree or equivalent advanced technical experience preferred.


Experience

  • 12+ years of progressive technology and engineering experience preferred.
  • Significant experience leading enterprise-scale software, platform, or engineering capability.
  • Demonstrated experience building or materially transforming engineering teams and engineering practices.
  • Experience delivering secure, enterprise-scale applications or platforms.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead highly complex initiatives spanning multiple organizations and technology domains.
  • Experience translating strategy, product direction, and business requirements into engineering execution.
  • Demonstrated success operating with senior executives and influencing across organizational boundaries.


Leadership & Functional Capabilities

  • Exceptional engineering depth, with significant experience delivering secure, reliable, and scalable enterprise technology.
  • Strong knowledge of modern software engineering, APIs, data integration, automation, cloud, telemetry, observability, reliability, and secure engineering practices.
  • Ability to assess highly complex technical and business challenges, evaluate implementation options and tradeoffs, and make sound decisions in high-pressure or time-sensitive environments.
  • Strong product and business orientation, with the ability to translate strategy and desired outcomes into executable engineering roadmaps, standards, reusable patterns, and delivery disciplines.
  • Ability to communicate complex engineering concepts in clear business language and influence senior executives, engineering leaders, peers, and cross-functional partners without relying solely on positional authority.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead across highly matrixed and distributed environments, building alignment among product, platform, architecture, cybersecurity, risk, and engineering stakeholders.
  • Experience leading significant technology, engineering, or operating-model transformation and establishing the practices required to sustain change.
  • Strong talent and capability-building skills, including coaching, role clarity, accountability, upskilling, and development of future technical leaders.
  • Sound judgment regarding the application of modern technology, AI, and automation, including the ability to balance innovation, business value, security, and risk.
  • Ability to connect engineering decisions to measurable business outcomes through analytical rigor, technology fluency, and disciplined execution.


Why This Role Matters

TORC's next evolution depends on our ability to engineer solutions to risk and control problems that historically relieve process, manual intervention, and point-in-time visibility.


The Principal Engineer will be the senior engineering leader responsible for helping make that transition real.


This leader will build the engineering capability behind TORC, deliver foundational products such as the Unified System of Controls, and connect Product, Platform, Architecture, ProdSec, SecOps, and engineering execution to create sustainable technology solutions that improve how Allstate understands and manages control and technology risk.

Skills

Automation, Data Integration, Enterprise Architecture (EA), Executive Leadership, People Leadership, Software Engineering

Compensation

Compensation offered for this role is 199,000.00 - 274,000.00 annually and is based on experience and qualifications.

The candidate(s) offered this position will be required to submit to a background investigation.

Position is responsible for product/user integration with industry technology and comparative rating platforms within market and assigned agencies

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

A day in the life of a Field Property Adjuster, and what it takes to do the job!

As a Field Property Adjuster, you will be dedicated to providing exceptional service to our policyholders. Your primary responsibility will involve traveling to our customers' homes to conduct on-site inspections, investigate coverage, prepare estimates, and settle claims promptly and efficiently. Additionally, you will handle virtual claims countrywide, leveraging various platforms and software such as Xactimate and ClaimsX Video Collaboration. Your expertise will be particularly focused on water losses, ensuring our customers receive the highest level of support and resolution for these specific claims.

You'll wear a few hats that will require a level of experience:

  • Strong critical thinking and technical skills to assess damages accurately and expedite claims settlements.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to provide exceptional customer service.
  • Ability to travel to customers' homes and handle virtual claims countrywide effectively.

What Is the Opportunity?

Travelers Data Engineering team constructs pipelines that contextualize and provide easy access to data by the entire enterprise. As a Data Engineer, you will play a key role in growing and transforming our analytics landscape. In addition to your strong analytical mind, you will bring your inquisitive attitude and ability to translate the stories found in data. You will leverage your ability to design, build and deploy data solutions that capture, explore, transform, and utilize data to support Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and business intelligence/insights. Applicants must be authorized to work for ANY employer in the U.S. The company does not sponsor/support H-1B petitions, TN, or Forms I-983/STEM OPT, for this role.

What Will You Do?

  • Build and operationalize complex data solutions, correct problems, apply transformations, and recommend data cleansing/quality solutions.
  • Design data solutions.
  • Analyze sources to determine value and recommend data to include in analytical processes.
  • Incorporate core data management competencies including data governance, data security and data quality.
  • Collaborate within and across teams to support delivery and educate end users on data products/analytic environment.
  • Perform data and system analysis, assessment and resolution for defects and incidents of moderate complexity and correct as appropriate.
  • Test data movement, transformation code, and data components.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's Degree in STEM related field or equivalent.
  • Six years of related experience.
  • Hands-on Expertise with Databricks and AWS: you've built and shipped real solutions on these platforms and are comfortable working in the cloud.
  • Strong SQL Skills: you know how to turn complex data into clear, reliable answers.
  • Snowflake Experience is a Pus: bring your knowledge of modern data warehousing and help us push it further.
  • Curiosity about AI is a Plus: experience or exposure to artificial intelligence is welcome, and you'll have room to grow it here.
  • Fluent in the Modern Engineering Toolkit: you're proficient with cloud platforms and programming languages, and you apply sound software engineering practices to everything you build.
  • Technical Excellence and Problem Solving: Proficient with cloud platforms, programming languages, and software engineering practices, with proven domain expertise, in-depth knowledge of the systems you support, and strong debugging skills to resolve issues in unfamiliar code and recurring problems.
  • Delivery, Communication, and Leadership: Deliver work at a steady, predictable pace using small-batch releases, contribute to tradeoff and negotiation discussions, communicate clearly with team members and business partners, and show self-motivated leadership by pursuing your own growth.

What is a Must Have?

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, related STEM field, or its equivalent in education and/or work experience.
  • 2 additional years of software/data engineering experience.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

Job.JobDescription:
Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

$112,000.00 - $184,800.00

Target Openings

What Is the Opportunity?

Commercial Accounts offers a wide array of guaranteed-cost products to mid-size businesses. Total account solutions include General Liability, Property, Automobile, Workers' Compensation, and Lead Umbrella.

The Account Executive Officer (AEO), Commercial Accounts will partner with agents and brokers to provide property, general liability, commercial auto, and/or workers' compensation coverage for new and renewal business based on customers' needs. This role is seen as a technical resource.

As an AEO, you are decisive, detail-oriented, and know how to build relationships internally and externally to drive results. Your ability to independently assess complex risk and sell our products in challenging markets will contribute to the profitability and success of Travelers.

What Will You Do?

  • Manage the profitability, growth, and retention of an assigned book of business.
  • Underwrite and skillfully negotiate complex customer accounts to minimize risk and maximize profitability.
  • Cultivate and maintain relationships with internal partners within the business unit and across the enterprise to create sales plans and identify cross-selling opportunities.
  • Foster and maintain relationships with external partners by regularly meeting in person with agents and brokers to market and sell Travelers products with a goal of writing and retaining accounts consistent with our risk appetite. Must be able to travel to such meetings.
  • Identify and capture new business opportunities using consultative marketing and sales skills.
  • Independently develop and execute agency sales plans and frequently partner with your Managing Director (MD) to develop region/group sales plans.
  • May assist in the training and mentoring of less experienced Account Executives.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's degree.
  • Six to eight years of relevant underwriting experience with experience in commercial lines.
  • Deep knowledge of commercial lines products, the regulatory environment, and the local insurance market.
  • Strong critical thinking skills with the ability to proactively identify underwriting, marketing, or financial challenges and analyze available information to make timely decisions in alignment with our risk appetite.
  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to successfully negotiate in difficult situations with agents and brokers.
  • CPCU designation.

What is a Must Have?

  • Four years of underwriting, claim, operations, risk assessment, actuarial, sales, product, or finance experience.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences.

  • Location: Irvine, CA

About this job

Executive Consultant provides risk assessment and loss mitigation services to large, complex construction, energy, and marine accounts at Travelers Insurance. The role involves field presence with customers, technical evaluations of high-severity exposures, and collaborative work with underwriting and claims teams.

Good fit if you have 7+ years in safety, risk control, or related fields, hold relevant certifications like ASP or CSP, and can travel extensively.

Full job description

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. $112,000.00 - $184,800.00

What Is the Opportunity?

Provide the Underwriter with account knowledge as it relates to hazards, controls, and management. They will need to evaluate how a company identifies and manages their inherent risk factors. Additionally they are expected to differentiate the account from others in similar classes of business. In this role the consultant will be working with our largest, most complex and all lines accounts. This role reports to the Risk Control Field Director or Managing Risk Control Consultant. This job does not manage others.

What Will You Do?

  • Maintain a consistent field presence, spending approximately 20% - 50% of the time onsite with customers. Traveling to customers may entail long-distance, overnight travel, and/or multi-night trips depending on the needs of the business and alignment with territory and/or geography.
  • Partner and have joint ownership with Underwriting to select, retain, and grow a profitable book of business.
  • Build and maintain productive relationships with Underwriting, Claim, Risk Control Specialists, and Brokers to service customers as a unified team.
  • Complete all lines risk assessment evaluations for Construction industry related accounts with high complexity including challenging products liability exposures with potential for the most severe losses, largest multi-location companies, and largest fleet exposures.
  • Write technically detailed reports that communicate a clear assessment of risk and effectively articulate recommendations.
  • Discover and evaluate customer needs through loss analysis and customer readiness in order to provide Risk Control products and services to help control losses.
  • Identify uncontrolled exposures to influence the customer to make improvements and take corrective actions to mitigate the potential for loss.
  • Provide solutions to assist the customer in risk mitigation through the use of our extensive span of resources. Stay current with technical subject matters, regulatory environment and emerging issues.
  • Subject Matter Expert in specialty area(s) (in such disciplines as Fleet, Sprinkler Contractor, Inland Marine, Industrial Hygiene, Human Factors & Ergonomics) to support the broader team to conduct 'Level of Expertise' consults.
  • Stay current with technical subject matters, regulatory environment and emerging issues.
  • Create a valued customer experience through each assessment and service encounter.
  • Ability to maintain core Sr. RCC responsibilities while taking on higher level project work that impacts the RC organization or Travelers enterprise.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's or graduate degree in environmental health and safety, engineering, construction management, basic sciences and related technical fields.
  • Advanced level knowledge of insurance industry and business acumen.
  • Recognized relevant certifications (such as ASP, CSP, ARM, CFPS).
  • Technical aptitude, detail oriented.
  • Superior communication skills - both written and verbal.
  • Ability to quickly establish credibility and rapport with all others.
  • Experience working in a collaborative environment.
  • Critical thinking skills.
  • Influencing skills that effectively drive business needs.
  • Negotiating change to achieve optimal outcomes.
  • Ability to give and receive coaching and feedback.

What is a Must Have?

  • Seven years of experience in safety, risk control/management, or a related field, such as occupational/environmental health and safety, science, engineering, construction, manufacturing, or relevant military experience.
  • Valid driver's license.
  • Must have or be able to attain appropriate certification to meet state-specific requirements, where applicable.

What Is in It for You?

  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.

  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.
