Job.JobTitle: Claims Resolution Adjuster II - Remote - MST/PST
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Phoenix, AZ
  • Experience: 2+ years

About this job

Investigate automobile accident claims involving property damage and bodily injury, assessing coverage and liability while communicating with customers via phone, email, and text. Remote position in MST/PST time zones, Monday-Friday 8am-4:30pm with potential Saturday duty rotation.

Good fit if you have 2+ years of claims adjusting experience determining liability and strong phone communication skills.

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

As a Claims Resolution Adjuster II, your focus will be investigating automobile accidents involving single or multiple vehicles that result in property damage and/or bodily injury. In this role, you will assess coverage, liability, and damages while providing exceptional customer service. You will communicate with customers through voice calls, email, and text messages, and use innovative platforms and tools to negotiate fair injury settlements with all parties involved.

Candidates for this role must reside in the Pacific or Mountain time zones. This position is not available to residents of California, Washington, Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico.


At Allstate, responsibilities may vary from day to day. We are looking for adaptable professionals who thrive in a dynamic environment, bring care and sound judgment to each claim, and are excited to make an impact.


  • The Customer Service Expert Youll support customers by caring, empowering, and restoring throughout the claims process. You will do this by being compassionate, clear, and a committed partner in each Casualty claim. You lead with empathy, always.
  • The Investigator Youll confidently and independently investigate casualty claims by performing detailed reviews of damage and interpreting policies to determine coverage.
  • The Effective Communicator Youll use phone, email, and sometimes video chat to help customers through a fast, fair, and easy claims process. Youll also tailor your approach to claim handling by honoring the customers communication preferences and keeping them updated on claim progress.
  • The Negotiator You will evaluate and negotiate claim settlements with customers, vendors, third-party carriers, and claimants in accordance with legal and business standards. You will incorporate tactics for handling challenging and complex situations.
  • The Problem Solver Youll use multiple tools to get the job done in a fast-paced environment, including estimating tools, job aids, and additional settlement platforms, while applying strong critical thinking skills.
  • The Recorder Youll help protect the company financially by following applicable policies and keeping a clear record of your work in the claims system. Youll ensure timely and accurate documentation is completed as you work on each claim.

Work Location


This position is a remote home-based role. Your home office does not need to be near an Allstate office, but it does need to be in the United States within one of the listed time zones above.


When you work from home full time, youll need:

  • A dedicated workspace in your residence that is private and free from distractions.
  • A minimum internet bandwidth of 50 MB down/5 MB up.
  • Appropriate work surface and seating.


What will Allstate provide?

  • A technology bundle that includes all equipment needed to perform your work from home (laptop, monitors, headset, keyboard, mouse).
  • Connectivity reimbursement of $80 per month to offset some of the cost of internet.

Work Schedule

  • 8-hour shift Mon-Fri | 8:00am - 4:30pm with potential Saturday duty rotation.

Licensing Requirements

  • You may be required to obtain an adjuster and/or appraiser license as a condition of employment.
  • If required, licensing may include an additional Department of Insurance background check and must be completed within 60 days of hire.
  • If you currently hold an active insurance license, you must terminate all existing appointments before onboarding and must not hold any outside appointments during employment.
  • If you are seeking an adjuster role and hold a resident producer license, you must formally surrender that license when instructed by the licensing team.
  • The Hiring Manager and Centralized Licensing team will provide support if licensing is required. By proceeding with the application process, applicants acknowledge and agree to comply with these licensing requirements.

Sign-On Bonus Information

  • Candidates with the active license(s) required for this role may be eligible for a $1,000 Licensing Sign-On Bonus.
  • Eligible licenses may include a Home Resident Property & Casualty License, Designated Home State (DHS) Florida or Texas License, and/or applicable Appraiser License.
  • Current employees and candidates previously employed by Allstate or its family of companies are not eligible for this sign-on bonus.

Qualifications

  • 2+ years of claims adjusting experience determining liability.
  • Claims investigation and negotiation experience preferred.
  • Experience with liability investigations, coverage investigations, property damage coverage, method of inspection, rental, and liability resolution preferred.
  • Strong phone communication skills, with the ability to build rapport and assess claims accurately.
  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate and negotiate injury claims successfully.

Allstate Benefits

  • Day 1 benefits, including time off, healthcare, retirement, and more.
  • Competitive pay, plus support for ongoing development and career advancement.
  • Time off programs and resources that support work/life balance.
  • Initial and ongoing training to help you succeed in the role.
  • Additional benefits may include 401(k)/pension, education reimbursement, and programs that support life outside of work. Visit www.allstategoodlife.com to learn more.

Please Note

  • In our virtual environment, employees are expected to be on camera and actively participate during online meetings and training sessions.
  • This job description is not intended to include a complete list of all duties and responsibilities. Employees may be asked to perform other related duties as assigned.
  • Regular, predictable attendance is an essential function of this role.

The first approximately 8-12 of employment are dedicated to onboarding, licensing (if applicable), and role-specific training designed to prepare you for success in the role. Successful candidates must be able to attend required training sessions, actively participate in virtual learning activities, and successfully complete the training program.

National General is a part of The Allstate Corporation, which means we have the same innovative drive that keeps us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. We offer home, auto and accident and health insurance, as well as other specialty niche insurance products, through a large network of independent insurance agents, as well as directly to consumers.

The Direct Sales Agent Specialist is responsible for driving profitable growth by generating new business, cross-selling existing customers, and building lasting relationships. This role focuses on understanding customer needs, delivering tailored solutions, and maintaining a strong book of business.

This role sells to local customers both in person and over the phone, while driving growth through community involvement, relationship building, and outside marketing efforts.

If you are ready to start working in a fun & exciting environment while making a difference, then apply to join our team today!

  • Partner with leadership to support sales and local marketing initiatives
  • Stay informed on products, underwriting guidelines, and market competition

  • Pay: $123,400 to $203,600 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Baltimore, MD
  • Experience: 5+ years
  • License: Valid driver's license
  • Benefits: Health insurance, 401(k), paid time off

About this job

Associate Senior Counsel at Travelers Insurance handling insurance defense litigation matters from inception through trial and appeal in Baltimore, Maryland. Role involves managing moderate to high complexity cases, mentoring junior attorneys, and serving as trusted advisor to insured clients and internal partners.

Good fit if you have 5+ years of insurance defense litigation experience, proven jury trial success, and an active law license to practice in Maryland.

Full job description

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$123,400.00 - $203,600.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

Travelers offers the strength of a national legal organization committed to your professional development while maintaining a local focus, positioning you as a strong business partner and trusted advisor who delivers exceptional value through local expertise and outstanding client service. We handle litigation arising from claims asserted against policyholders or the company and take cases from inception through trial and appeal. As an Associate Senior Counsel with Travelers you will be responsible for high quality, proactive case handling and will have the opportunity to use your legal expertise and litigation skills to independently handle a caseload of predominatly moderate to higher complexity matters, which may include Major Case matters depending on line of business. You will deliver optimal results for Travelers' insured customers, and will mentor less experienced attorneys.

What Will You Do?

  • In the handling of a caseload of predominantly moderate and higher exposure cases, including Major Case litigation matters depending on line of business, your responsibilities will include:
  • Leverage pre-trial and trial experience to apply effective use of litigation skills and techniques to try cases to verdict or negotiate resolution.
  • Conduct proficient to advanced legal research and demonstrate strong and persuasive legal writing and presentation skills.
  • Draft substantive pleadings, motions, briefs, discovery and other legal documents.
  • Attend court events, depositions, and other appointments independently.
  • Provide in-depth, substantive case analysis and recommendations to insured clients and Claim partners on file handling strategies.
  • Collaborates with expert witnesses and consultants to develop case strategies, evaluate technical matters, and prepare compelling testimony for litigation.
  • Build and maintain strong internal and external client and business partner relationships, including accountability for managing client and business partner relationships.
  • Provide internal and external training, seminars and legal updates to insured clients and Claim partners.
  • Provide leadership through mentoring other attorneys and legal support staff.
  • Contributes to special projects and identifies other opportunities to support office goals/business needs.
  • Fully and effectively utilize available technology, case management system and automation.
  • Travel as required to meet business needs.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • 5+ years of insurance defense litigation experience as a practicing attorney.
  • Demonstrates an aptitude for trying cases to a jury; proven track record of preparing and/or litigating jury trials, with a history of successful courtroom outcomes.
  • Demonstrates strong technical knowledge in the practice area(s) and the ability to effectively communicate complex information on litigated matters to diverse audiences.
  • Proficient oral and written advocacy skills, with a demonstrated track record of summary judgment and/or appellate successs.
  • Possesses in-depth knowledge of the bench, bar, local jurisdictional practices, adversaries.
  • Capably fosters collaborative relationships with colleagues, customers, and business partners to deliver exceptional customer service.
  • Demonstrates leadership through mentoring and influencing skills.
  • Exercises sound decision making and possesses advanced negotiation skills.
  • Effectively manages multiple priorities with an attention to detail, sense of urgency and responsiveness.
  • Possesses a flexible and agile mindset with a willingness to take on new challenges as needs evolve.

What is a Must Have?

  • Juris Doctorate or equivalent International legal degree; graduate of an accredited law school.
  • 4 years experience as a practicing attorney.
  • Active license in good standing to practice law in the state(s) in which representation is required.
  • Regularly handles hearings, trials, dispositive motion arguments, depositions, or other court proceedings and has the ability to transport to those meetings. Valid driver's license required depending on the location.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit http://careers.travelers.com/life-at-travelers/benefits/.

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Property Claims Adjuster, Claims, Claims Representative
Job.JobDescription:
Claims Representative II - Property

Our preference is for this role to be HYBRID, working inoffice Tuesday–Thursday at our Merrill, WI location.

We will also consider fully remote candidates who are not within commuting distance to one of our offices in Milwaukee or Madison, WI.

What You'll Be Doing

In accordance with application of state and federal laws and company best practices, handle low-to-moderate value commercial property claims short in duration with lower indemnity which may include property damage, business personal property, and building damage. Gather and review claim information, determine coverage, and conduct thorough investigations. Initiate and maintain customer contact to provide updates and resolve any issues with the claim. Update information in the claim system to document claim handling activities. Determine/set reserves and make payments within level of authority. Investigate and refer identified claims to Loss Recovery Services, as applicable.

On Any Given Day, You'll

  • Perform claim tasks timely and document claim files appropriately. Proactively manage claim activities to ensure fair claim resolution. Handle all claims in accordance with state and federal laws.

  • Verify coverage by gathering adequate information necessary to make an informed decision in a fair, equitable, and ethical manner. Deny losses under limited supervision, providing detailed explanation, citing facts, and policy language.

  • Perform a thorough investigation based upon the type, complexity, and severity of the claim. Upon completion of the investigation, analyze and evaluate the potential exposure and damages, including potential full or partial liability and compensability denials. Formulate and document an action plan based on the covered damages and injuries.

  • Determine and set reserves based on the most probable outcome of the claim, within authority level. Evaluate and negotiate directly with insured or insured representative on all cases within authority level. Review claim facts and exposure with claims management, as appropriate, to guide claim strategy. Make complete, accurate, and timely payments within authority for covered losses. Refer claims above authority to management for review and potential reassignment.

  • Maintain a professional, courteous, and helpful approach when communicating in-person, on the phone, or through email and other correspondence with internal and external customers and business partners.

  • Recognize when vendor partners are required on a claim, including experts, independent adjustors, or other. Assign and direct vendors, as needed, to aid in the investigation and evaluation of the claim. Manage claim expenses by concluding vendor assignment when vendor is no longer adding value to the claim.

  • Investigate and refer identified claims to Loss Recovery Services, as applicable.

  • Completes all other assigned duties, as requested.

Here's What We Expect

  • Two to four years of claim handling and/or insurance-related experience is preferred.

Education

  • Bachelor's degree preferred. A combination of equivalent education and/or experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.

  • Additional training in insurance, construction, restoration, and/or building terminology knowledge is desirable.

  • Completion of courses in any one or more of the following designations, INS, AIC, or CPCU, is preferred.

Necessary Knowledge and Abilities

  • Ability to obtain and maintain state adjusting license requirements and complete continuing education requirements.

  • Evidence of ability to think independently, be detail oriented, and organized.

  • Strong listening, verbal, and written communication skills.

  • Knowledge of policy terminology and legal principles involving at least one or more of the following: insurance, automobile, medical, and property claims.

About this job

Lead business user acceptance testing for Guidewire PolicyCenter implementation supporting commercial property and casualty insurance operations. Coordinate between business and technology teams to ensure system functionality meets requirements, manage testing execution across policy lifecycle functions, and drive readiness for production deployment.

Good fit if you have five or more years in commercial P&C insurance, experience leading UAT for complex system implementations, and strong knowledge of policy administration and insurance operations.

Full job description

***This role can be FULLY REMOTE or HYBRID (in office days Tuesday-Thursday) if in close proximity to one of our office locations below***

  • Merrill, WI 
  • Milwaukee, WI
  • Mechanicsburg, PA
  • Madison, WI

ROLE:

Lead business user acceptance testing (UAT) activities supporting the implementation of Guidewire PolicyCenter and related systems for commercial property and casualty insurance operations. This role serves as the primary coordinator between business and technology teams to ensure system functionality aligns with approved business requirements and operational needs.

The Guidewire UAT Lead is responsible for establishing the structure, governance, processes, and reporting necessary to successfully execute UAT activities across multiple products and business functions. This position works closely with underwriting, insurance product, technology product, quality assurance, and implementation teams to define requirements, develop testing strategies, manage testing execution, facilitate issue resolution, and ensure business readiness prior to production deployment. The role provides leadership and influence across cross-functional teams without direct supervisory authority.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Lead UAT strategy, planning, preparation, execution, and completion for Guidewire PolicyCenter and related integrations supporting commercial property and casualty insurance products.
  • Partner with underwriting, insurance product, technology product, business analysis, quality assurance, development, and implementation teams to establish UAT scope, schedules, resource requirements, entry and exit criteria, and business sign-off expectations.
  • Facilitate working sessions with underwriting and product subject matter experts to define and refine business requirements, workflows, referrals, product rules, and expected system behavior.
  • Translate approved business requirements into acceptance criteria, end-to-end business scenarios, test cases, test scripts, expected outcomes, and reusable regression testing assets.
  • Establish and maintain a comprehensive UAT framework, including test inventories, traceability documentation, readiness assessments, tester assignments, schedules, execution tracking, and supporting documentation.
  • Coordinate and lead business subject matter experts and UAT participants by assigning work, clarifying expectations, monitoring progress, and addressing resource constraints, dependencies, and testing gaps.
  • Coordinate test environments, system access, test data, integrations, documentation, and other prerequisites required to support successful testing execution.
  • Lead testing activities across policy lifecycle functions including submission, quote, underwriting, referral, rating, bind, issue, endorsement, renewal, cancellation, reinstatement, and associated integrated systems.
  • Validate configured workflows, screens, rating logic, product rules, documents, integrations, and migrated data to ensure compliance with approved business and operational requirements.
  • Document, assess, prioritize, track, and communicate defects, requirement gaps, and testing issues while coordinating appropriate resolution activities with business and technology teams.
  • Coordinate corrective actions, retesting, regression testing, and issue closure to ensure successful implementation outcomes.
  • Develop and communicate testing status, defect trends, risk assessments, readiness evaluations, dependencies, and recommendations to project stakeholders and leadership.
  • Facilitate business review and acceptance activities and support final business sign-off decisions based on testing outcomes, acceptance criteria, and residual risk evaluation.
  • Drive continuous improvement of UAT methodologies, testing standards, documentation practices, and governance processes to support future technology implementations.
  • Support organizational readiness by identifying operational impacts, process changes, and training considerations associated with new system functionality.
  • Build collaborative relationships across business and technology teams and provide leadership through influence, coordination, and effective communication.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience required; degree emphasis in insurance, risk management, information technology, business, or a related discipline preferred.
  • Five or more years of commercial property and casualty insurance experience in policy administration, business analysis, quality assurance, user acceptance testing, or a related discipline. Experience spanning underwriting, insurance product management, and technology product functions is strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience leading business user acceptance testing efforts for complex enterprise system implementations, modernizations, or migrations.
  • Experience defining and documenting business requirements, workflows, acceptance criteria, business scenarios, test scripts, expected results, and regression testing materials.
  • Strong knowledge of commercial property and casualty insurance operations and policy lifecycle processes.
  • Ability to translate business requirements into structured testing methodologies and repeatable test conditions.
  • Strong organizational, analytical, problem-solving, and project coordination skills.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to effectively communicate across all organizational levels.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence outcomes and lead work across cross-functional teams without direct authority.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, dependencies, and competing business needs in a fast-paced transformation environment.
  • Guidewire PolicyCenter experience strongly preferred. Experience with policy administration platforms, testing tools, defect management systems, agile delivery methodologies, and related insurance industry designations is preferred.
  • Advanced computer skills and the ability to learn and apply new technologies and tools.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

  • Professional office environment.
  • Hybrid work arrangement with in-office days Tuesday through Thursday in Merrill, Madison, or Milwaukee.
  • Fully remote work may be considered for candidates outside commuting distance.
  • Occasional travel may be required to support project planning, testing activities, training, or implementation efforts.

Quick facts

  • Location: Merrill, WI
  • Experience: 3 to 5 years
  • Education: High school diploma or GED

About this job

Provides advanced underwriting support for renewal accounts, endorsements, and policy servicing while evaluating risk information and applying underwriting guidelines. Serves as a technical resource and mentor for underwriting support operations at Church Mutual Insurance in Merrill, Wisconsin.

Good fit if you have underwriting or insurance support experience and can mentor team members while managing complex accounts.

Full job description

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Senior Underwriting Support Specialist is responsible for providing advanced underwriting support underwriting activities, and servicing activities while serving as a technical resource for underwriting support operations. This role supports underwriters through risk review, renewal preparation, endorsement evaluation, account servicing, and the underwriting of designated accounts of increasing size, premium volume, and complexity within established authority through risk evaluation, coverage review, and application of underwriting guidelines while promoting operational quality and customer satisfaction

The Senior Underwriting Support Specialist provides leadership through technical expertise, mentoring, training, and process improvement initiatives. The primary accountability of this role is delivering advanced underwriting support while enhancing team capability, supporting underwriting operations, and developing expertise necessary for increasingly complex underwriting responsibilities. This role serves as an advanced underwriting support position that provides opportunities to develop underwriting knowledge, technical expertise, and advanced technical, leadership, and underwriting career opportunities.


Primary Job Responsibilities

Underwriting Support & Risk Review

  • Underwrite designated renewal accounts and routine underwriting transactions of increasing size and complexity within delegated authority by evaluating risk information and applying underwriting guidelines and standards.
  • Review risk information, account characteristics, and supporting documentation to assess exposures and determine appropriate underwriting actions or recommendations.
  • Apply underwriting guidelines, coverage analysis, and rating considerations when evaluating and processing assigned underwriting responsibilities.
  • Perform designated underwriting activities for assigned accounts and other risks within established authority and guidelines, including evaluating risk information, applying underwriting guidelines, analyzing coverage considerations, and completing underwriting actions within delegated authority and established procedures.
  • Provide advanced underwriting support for renewals, endorsements, and policy servicing activities.
  • Prepare and review renewal files and supporting documentation to facilitate underwriting evaluation and decision-making.
  • Conduct review of endorsements and policy transactions within established authority and procedures, evaluating risk characteristics, coverage considerations, and appropriate underwriting actions
  • Evaluate supporting documentation for completeness, accuracy, and underwriting readiness.
  • Support underwriters with increasingly complex underwriting support activities and account servicing needs.
  • Document underwriting actions, communications, and supporting information in accordance with departmental standards.

Customer Service & Collaboration

  • Build and maintain effective working relationships with producers, customers, underwriters, and internal business partners.
  • Provide timely, accurate, and professional service in support of retention, customer satisfaction, and business objectives.
  • Assist in resolving complex service issues and underwriting support concerns.
  • Collaborate with underwriters and business partners to support underwriting workflows, account servicing, and renewal processes.
  • Serve as a resource for underwriting support staff and assist with escalated questions or issues.
  • Communicate underwriting decisions, requirements, coverage considerations, and risk-related recommendations to producers, customers, underwriters, and internal business partners as appropriate.

Leadership, Mentoring & Training

  • Serve as a technical resource and experienced team member for underwriting support operations.
  • Mentor and support less experienced underwriting support staff through coaching, knowledge sharing, and guidance.
  • Assist with onboarding and training activities for new and existing team members.
  • Support development and maintenance of procedures, workflow documentation, and job aids.
  • Contribute to a positive culture of learning, development, and operational excellence.
  • Serve as a resource to team members regarding underwriting guidelines, risk evaluation, coverage analysis, and underwriting best practices

Compliance, Documentation & Quality

  • Ensure underwriting support activities comply with established guidelines, procedures, and company standards.
  • Support quality, audit, and process consistency initiatives across underwriting support operations.
  • Identify recurring issues, trends, and opportunities for quality improvement.
  • Maintain accurate and complete underwriting documentation and records.
  • Protect the confidentiality of customer and company information

Knowledge Development & Contribution

  • Maintain advanced knowledge of insurance products, policy forms, underwriting support processes, and underwriting workflows.
  • Apply and continue developing advanced underwriting knowledge, including risk evaluation, coverage analysis, underwriting guidelines, complex account review, and underwriting support operations.
  • Participate in projects, initiatives, and process improvement efforts designed to enhance service, quality, and operational effectiveness.
  • Provide recommendations to improve workflows, procedures, and underwriting support effectiveness.
  • Demonstrate a commitment to continuous learning and professional development.

Operational Excellence & Adaptability

  • Meet established service, productivity, quality, and timeliness expectations.
  • Effectively manage competing priorities and support departmental workload needs.
  • Promote consistency, professionalism, and accountability across underwriting support activities.
  • Demonstrate flexibility and adaptability in response to changing business needs, priorities, and processes.
  • Support process improvements and change initiatives that strengthen underwriting support operations.

..

 

SCOPE & DECISION-MAKING AUTHORITY

  • Account Scope: Advanced underwriting support activities, renewal preparation, endorsement review, policy servicing, and designated small-account underwriting activities.
  • Complexity: Advanced underwriting support responsibilities combined with underwriting responsibility for designated accounts and transactions of increasing size and complexity within delegated authority.
  • Authority: Expanded authority for designated underwriting support activities and underwriting responsibility for designated accounts and transactions of increasing size and complexity within delegated authority.
  • Decision-Making: Exercises judgment on assigned accounts, endorsements, and transactions within established guidelines and delegated authority while providing guidance to others and escalating higher-risk, more complex, or out-of-authority situations appropriately.
  • Supervision: Functions independently and provides mentoring, training, and technical support to team members without formal supervisory responsibility.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education & Experience

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Post-secondary education preferred.
  • Recognized insurance education or coursework is desirable.
  • Typically 3-5 years of insurance experience with demonstrated progression in underwriting support, policy administration, policy processing, underwriting operations, or related functions.
  • Demonstrated ability to mentor, train, and support the development of others.

Technical Knowledge

  • Advanced knowledge of insurance products, underwriting concepts, policy forms, underwriting support processes, and underwriting workflows.
  • Understanding of risk review, coverage considerations, and underwriting support activities.
  • Ability to review documentation, identify issues, and support underwriting decisions within established authority.
  • Proficiency with company systems, applications, and technology supporting underwriting operations

Skills & Abilities

  • Strong organizational and time-management skills.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong customer service and relationship-building skills.
  • Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to train, mentor, and support others.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and complex assignments.
  • Demonstrated leadership through influence and expertise.
  • Commitment to continuous learning, professionalism, and operational excellence.

WORK ENVIRONMENT & TRAVEL

  • Work is performed in a professional office or remote/hybrid environment, consistent with organizational policy.

This job description is not intended to be allinclusive. Employees may be asked to perform other duties as assigned. Duties and scope may vary by product line or Center of Excellence while maintaining core underwriting responsibilities.

Full job description


Description

Comparion Insurance Agency is hiring self-motivated, relationship-driven professionals for a rewarding outside sales career. This role offers autonomy and flexibility to build your career, grow your earnings, and make a meaningful impact by helping protect individuals and families with auto, home, life, small commercial auto, and specialty insurance.

Backed by a Fortune 100 company, you'll receive hands-on training, resources, and team support to help you succeed. No prior insurance experience required.

THIS POSITION HAS IN-OFFICE REQUIREMENTS. Must reside in the state of Indiana.

This is a full-time, field-based employee position. Applicants must be able to travel within their local community to meet with customers and build relationships. Reliable transportation, such as a valid driver's license or another means of travel, is preferred.

What you'll do:

  • Sell auto, home, life, small commercial auto, and related insurance products using a consultative, needs-based approach.
  • Build and maintain a book of business through referrals, networking, and community engagement as part of your outside sales efforts.
  • Identify prospective customers using established lead methodologies and relationship-driven outreach.
  • Accurately document customer interactions and handle sensitive information with integrity and confidentiality.
  • Use insurance sales technology, relationship management tools, and multi-carrier platforms to deliver tailored insurance solutions.
  • Participate in training, coaching, and performance incentives to continuously improve sales results.

Essential functions include: meeting with customers in the office and in the community, communicating by phone, email, and in person, traveling locally, and using a computer and sales software.

Qualifications

Day One Skills & Traits:

  • Self-motivated and accountable: you take ownership of your work and results.
  • Reliable and responsive: you follow through and do what you say you'll do.
  • Professional and trustworthy: you handle customer information with care and integrity.
  • Relationship-focused: you enjoy helping others and building long-term trust.
  • Strong communicator: you're comfortable talking with people and explaining options clearly.
  • Comfortable with technology: you can learn and use new software and digital tools with ease.
  • Composed and dependable: you stay organized and professional while managing multiple customer needs.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in customer-facing roles like retail, hospitality, service, operations, logistics, banking, account management, or sales.
  • Basic understanding of sales conversations, including handling common customer questions or objections.
  • Experience managing multiple accounts, clients, or priorities simultaneously.
  • Exposure to consultative selling, negotiation, or regulated industries.

Licensing:

You will be required to obtain relevant licenses upon being hired (P&C and Life).

About Us

Pay Philosophy: The typical starting salary range for this role is determined by a number of factors including skills, experience, education, certifications and location. The full salary range for this role reflects the competitive labor market value for all employees in these positions across the national market and provides an opportunity to progress as employees grow and develop within the role. Some roles at Liberty Mutual have a corresponding compensation plan which may include commission and/or bonus earnings at rates that vary based on multiple factors set forth in the compensation plan for the role.

In 2022, Comparion Insurance Agency was created to transition former Liberty Mutual exclusive agents to an agency that delivers a unique value proposition to carriers with over 2,000 agents in approximately 180 cities in 44 states. We offer customers 50 insurance companies with product breadth including auto, home, life, pet, renters, umbrella, jewelry and much more. We use our scale to deliver a first-rate customer experience through consultative insurance experts located in their communities.

Our Leadership team has over 200 years of cumulative insurance experience. At Comparion, we have a philosophy of staying close to our customers and agents, so sales leadership is located throughout the country in our larger storefronts. Comparion is owned and backed by Liberty Mutual Group, a Fortune 100 company, founded in 1912

Full job description


Description

We are looking for an Insurance Sales Associate to join our team in our Chandler office. This is not a remote position.

Were Hiring Immediately!

As an Insurance Sales Associate, you will work alongside with and support a Comparion Insurance Sales Agent in profitable growth through new business sales and customer retention. Your ability to listen and empathize are key in being the initial contact for our customers. Success in this role will require building a strong local network and in-person relationship in the community.

Working for Comparion Insurance Agency, a Liberty Mutual company, means working for a company thats committed to advancing an inclusive environment. We do that through leadership development programs aimed at advancing, engaging, and retaining under-represented talent and our Employee Resource Groups, which strengthen our inclusive workplace, enhance personal development, and provide ways for employees to connect, learn and engage.

Ready to find out what it means to work for an agency that is backed by Liberty Mutuala Fortune 100 company thats committed to putting people first, acting responsibly and making things better?

Responsibilities:

  • Utilize consultative sales techniques to prospect and initiate new business sales.
  • Assists in the processing of new business, including contacting customers to finalize sales and service transactions.
  • Identifies cross selling opportunities for Sales Agent.
  • Contributes to and executes a marketing plan with the Sales Agent.
  • Identifies mass marketing prospects through existing book of business and community prospecting opportunities.
  • Meet monthly goals for new business sales.
  • Completes follow-ups on new policies in order to keep retention level high and capitalize cross-selling opportunities.
  • Coordinates activities with other departments to ensure quality customer service
  • Acts as initial contact in addressing customer concerns regarding establishment of policies and new account status.
  • Unlicensed candidates will be enrolled in a new hire training class once they begin working for Comparion. The training includes a licensing training program in which Comparion covers the cost of training materials and exam fees.
Qualifications
  • High School Degree
  • 1-2 years of relevant sales experience preferred
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to handle common objections and educate customers in a consultative manner
  • Demonstrated self-starter, motivated to learn and grow in a professional sales organization
  • Professional business acumen, strong presence and confidence
  • Resourceful team player that can contribute and accept new ideas
  • A state insurance licenseor willingness to earn one with training and supportin Property & Casualty, and Life

Description

Comparion Insurance Agency is hiring self-motivated, relationship-driven professionals for a rewarding outside sales career. This role offers autonomy and flexibility to build your career, grow your earnings, and make a meaningful impact by helping protect individuals and families with auto, home, life, and specialty insurance.

Backed by a Fortune 100 company, youll receive hands-on training, resources, and team support to help you succeed no prior insurance experience required.

Description

What youll do:

  • Sell auto, home, life, and related insurance products using a consultative, needs-based approach.
  • Build and maintain a book of business through referrals, networking, and community engagement as part of your outside sales efforts.
  • Identify prospective customers using established lead methodologies and relationship-driven outreach.
  • Accurately document customer interactions and handle sensitive information with integrity and confidentiality.
  • Use insurance sales technology, relationship management tools, and multi-carrier platforms to deliver tailored insurance solutions.
  • Participate in training, coaching, and performance incentives to continuously improve sales results.

What We Offer:

  • Unlimited commission and renewal income potential for earnings growth over time.
  • Full-time employment with benefits from day one, including health insurance, generous 401(k) match, and paid time off.
  • Paid training, licensing support, and ongoing development.
  • Autonomy to embrace your entrepreneurial spirit and structure your time your way.
  • Flexible work structure (hybrid office, field, and remote based on what your day requires).
  • Supportive team culture with mentorship and long-term career paths.
Qualifications

Who Were Looking For:

Day One Skills & Traits

  • Self-motivated and accountable you take ownership of your work and results.
  • Reliable and responsive you follow through and do what you say youll do.
  • Professional and trustworthy you handle customer information with care and integrity.
  • Relationship-focused you enjoy helping others and building long-term trust.
  • Outgoing youre comfortable talking with people and explaining options clearly.
  • Tech savvy youre able to learn and use technology and digital tools with ease.
  • Calm under pressure you stay composed in a fast-paced, customer-focused environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in customer-facing roles like retail, hospitality, service, operations, logistics, banking, account management, or sales.
  • Basic understanding of sales conversations, including handling common customer questions or objections.
  • Experience managing multiple accounts, clients, or priorities simultaneously.
  • Exposure to consultative selling, negotiation, or regulated industries.

You will be required to obtain relevant licenses upon being hired.

Build a career for yourself, not by yourself. Launch a rewarding insurance sales career today.

About Us

Pay Philosophy: The typical starting salary range for this role is determined by a number of factors including skills, experience, education, certifications and location. The full salary range for this role reflects the competitive labor market value for all employees in these positions across the national market and provides an opportunity to progress as employees grow and develop within the role. Some roles at Liberty Mutual have a corresponding compensation plan which may include commission and/or bonus earnings at rates that vary based on multiple factors set forth in the compensation plan for the role.

In 2022, Comparion Insurance Agency was created to transition former Liberty Mutual exclusive agents to an agency that delivers a unique value proposition to carriers with over 2,000 agents in approximately 180 cities in 44 states. We offer customers 50 insurance companies with product breadth including auto, home, life, pet, renters, umbrella, jewelry and much more. We use our scale to deliver a first-rate customer experience through consultative insurance experts located in their communities.

Our Leadership team has over 200 years of cumulative insurance experience. At Comparion, we have a philosophy of staying close to our customers and agents, so sales leadership is located throughout the country in our larger storefronts. Comparion is owned and backed by Liberty Mutual Group, a Fortune 100 company, founded in 1912

Plus, youll enjoy:

  • Generous earning potential
  • Paid licensing and training opportunities
  • Comprehensive benefits
  • Flexible work arrangements
  • Strong work-life balance
  • And more!

Why Liberty Mutual?

Pay Details:

  • Starting base salary is $45K with opportunity for growth.
  • Average earnings range from $55K-$75K through a combination of base salary and generouscommission.
  • Top Performing Agents in their second year and onward, can earn up to $85k+.

We are currently hiring quality Inbound sales professionals in the following states:AR, AZ, FL, GA, IA, ID, IN, KS, LA, MA, MD, ME, MI, MN, MO, NC, NE, NH, NJ, NM, NV, NY, OH, OR, PA, SC, TX, UT, VA, WA, WI, andWV

Licensed only candidates based in ID, MT, WY, GA, TN, AL, OK, KS and KY. Applicants must reside within these specified locations to be considered for this role.

Positivity. Flexibility. Determination and a persuasive personality. Qualities like these cannot be taught. But they can be sharpened, strengthened, and appropriately compensated when you join Liberty Mutual Insurance as a part of our Contact Center Sales Organization. Bring your unique sales talent to our Fortune 100 company and receive paid-training, licensing in all 50 states, and a dynamic role that directs only warm leads your way (no cold calls) because we believe in supporting your success, not holding it back. Join our sales team and realize the rewards of a career with unlimited earning potential, generous commissions, and a portfolio of benefits that start on day one.

Job Details

As an Inside Sales Agent, you will be handling inbound calls and warm leads, consulting with customers on their insurance needs and match the correct coverages, products, and benefits to convert sales leads into policyholders.

Due to state licensing restrictions, employees must remain in their resident state for at least one year before relocating.

Youd be a great fit if you are:

A Passionate Seller:When a lead comes in, you skillfully pick up the phone and use your sales expertise to turn prospects into happy, confident Liberty Mutualpolicyholders.

A Front Lines Liaison:You rise to the role of representing the Liberty brand, you believe in what youre selling, and you enjoy connecting customers to the right products for their individual needs.

A Reliable Teammate:Whether you work at the office or from home, you adapt well to different environments, schedules, and the varying needs of ourpolicyholders.

A Customer-Centric Closer:While sales is in your title, integrity is in your nature. That means you sincerely care that our customers get exactly the quality products and services they need to embrace today and confidently pursue tomorrow.

Position Details:

From day one you will begin paid training in a remote work environment. All insurance representatives need to hold a Property & Casualty Insurance license. If you do not have one, no worries, paid training also includes licensing!

  • Training extends over a period of 16 weeks for licensed hires and 18 weeks for unlicensed hires.
  • Comprehensive medical benefits from Day 1.
  • No cold calls, all incoming warm leads.
  • Opportunities for rewards and recognition.

  • Must be available to work a schedule of 4 weekdays and 1 weekend day. Standard shift is 11:30-8 EST, 12:30-9 CST, or 8:30-5 PST.

  • All computer equipment is provided. Youmust be able to maintain department.Work at home (W@H) requirements whichinclude a professional workspace/room with adedicated desk and wired (cable, fiber of DSLservice) high-speed internet connection with aminimum 100 MBps download speed and 20MBps upload speed. Liberty Mutual does notsupport satellite and mobile internet services.
Qualifications
  • 2-3 years sales experience preferred. 2 yearsof sales/service-related work experiencerequired.
  • Strong, engaging interpersonal and persuasion skills needed to close sales
  • Ability to communicate well to both prospects and customers
  • Excellent analytical, decision-making and organizational skills
  • Strong typing capabilities and PC proficiency
  • Property and Casualty License required afterhire.

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Workers' Compensation Adjuster, Claims, Claims Representative
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Lake Oswego, OR
  • Experience: 5 to 7 years

About this job

Investigate and resolve complex workers compensation claims of high exposure and severity. Requires Oregon Workers Compensation Adjuster License and 5-7 years of claims experience, with 1-2 years in complex claims.

Good fit if you have an Oregon Workers Compensation Adjuster License and 5-7 years of claims experience with complex claims background

Full job description


Description

Under limited supervision and established practices, responsible for the investigation, evaluation, and disposition of Complex Workers Compensation cases of high exposure and severity. Applies established medical management strategies on high dollar complex claims. Has developed high level of knowledge of Workers Compensation claims handling techniques, a full knowledge of LMG claims procedures and is cognizant of new industry trends and claim handling techniques Uses available data to track claims trends and other claim related metrics.

Candidates should be based in Oregon with Oregon Workers Compensation Adjuster License.

The salary range posted reflects the range for the varying pay scale that encompasses each of the Liberty Mutual regions and the overall cost of living for that region.


Responsibilities

  • Investigates claims to determine whether coverage is provided, establish compensability and verify exposure.
  • Resolves claims within authority and makes recommendations regarding case value and resolution strategy to Branch Office Management and HO Examining on cases which exceed authority.
  • Participates in pricing, reserving and strategy discussions with HO Examining and Examining Management.
  • Works closely with staff and outside defense counsel in managing litigated files according to established litigation management protocols.
  • Identifies and appropriately handles suspicious claims and claims with the potential to develop adversely.
  • Identifies and appropriately handles claims with third party subrogation potential, SIF (Self-Insured Fund) and MSA (Medicare Set Aside) exposure.
  • Establishes and maintains accurate reserves on all assigned files.
  • Makes timely reserve recommendations to Branch Office Management and HO Examining on cases which exceed authority.
  • Prepares for and attends mediation sessions and/or settlement conferences and negotiates on behalf of LMG and LMG Insureds.
  • Demonstrates the ability to understand new and unique exposures and coverages.
  • Demonstrates the ability to understand key data elements and claims related data analysis.
  • Confers directly with policyholders on coverage and resolution strategy issues.
  • Coordinates and participates in training sessions for less experienced staff, including both Complex Non-Complex staff.
Qualifications
  • A bachelors degree or equivalent business experience is required
  • In addition, the candidate will generally possess 5-7 years of related claims experience with 1-2 years of experience in complex claims
  • Demonstrated proficiency in Excel, PowerPoint as well as excellent written and verbal communication skills required

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Insurance Operations Manager, Operations & Policy Administration
Job.JobDescription:
Description

Risk Financing sits at the center of how Liberty Mutual transfers risk to the reinsurance market, and its effectiveness depends on a large number of functions moving in step. This role exists to make that happen. As Reinsurance Operations Manager, you will be the connective tissue between Risk Financing and its key partner functions Enterprise Risk Management, RI Operations, RI Accounting, Legal, Tax, LM Re and the broker community ensuring that priorities are clearly set, actively managed and consistently executed across all of them.

This is a role for someone who is energized by turning recurring friction into durable process. You will own the definition of the treaty lifecycle and its implementation across the team, contribute to the standard operating procedures that allow placement teams to act with confidence, and take a leading role in renewal preparation and management including the treaty handover to downstream teams within agreed service levels. You will work across the full lifecycle, from market approval and reinsurer governance through binding, post-placement data delivery and in-force management.

Much of the work involves shaping the agenda of teams you do not manage, so the ability to build credibility, communicate with clarity in writing and in person, and hold a position under senior scrutiny is central to success.

What you'll do

  • Serve as a key operational point of contact between Risk Financing and its partner functions, establishing and maintaining a governed cadence with each
  • Own the treaty lifecycle definition end to end and drive its adoption across the Risk Financing team
  • Author, secure approval for and implement standard operating procedures and standardized templates that remove ambiguity and reduce duplication of work
  • Own operational renewal preparation and management for reinsurance cycles, including new process implementation, training, and monitoring of operational handovers to Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) and RI Operations withing tight SLAs
  • Partner with ERM on reinsurer governance, collateral requirements, approved market lists and concentration frameworks, and implement approved changes as business as usual
  • Support regulatory and control processes including SSAP62 risk transfer reviews, transfer pricing documentation and internal audit requests
  • Drive data quality and standardization initiatives with internal teams and external delivery partners
  • Identify and champion opportunities to simplify how the team delivers, including responsible adoption of GenAI tooling

At least 75% of time is spent on a combination of the following responsibilities:

  1. Operational excellence and SOP ownership: Own, maintain and continuously improve Risk Financing standard operating procedures across the treaty lifecycle, ensuring processes are clearly documented, scalable, audit ready and consistently applied globally.
  2. Process optimization and waste reduction: Identify inefficiencies, duplication and bottlenecks across Risk Financing operations, applying continuous improvement methods to simplify processes, reduce manual effort, minimize rework and shorten cycle times.
  3. Automation and simplification: Lead workflow simplification initiatives in partnership with Technology, Data and operational teams, translating strategic priorities into practical improvements.
  4. Data, reporting and insight: Improve data quality, lineage and usability across reinsurance systems and reporting outputs, using descriptive analytics, visualization tools, KPIs and operational metrics to support decision making and executive reporting.
  5. Stakeholder and partner connectivity: Act as a central coordinator between Risk Financing and partner functions including Finance, Claims, Actuarial, Legal, Tax, brokers and reinsurers, ensuring smooth handoffs, clear ownership and aligned timelines.
  6. Governance, controls and risk management: Support operational risk identification and remediation, ensuring controls, documentation and governance are in place to meet internal, audit and regulatory expectations.
  7. Operational performance management: Develop, update and analyze complex metrics used to assess operational performance, productivity, staffing needs, service levels and other measures valuable to Risk Financing leadership.
  8. Audit, review and senior forum support: Prepare materials, insights and recommendations for audits, reviews, governance meetings and senior forums
  9. Innovation and continuous improvement: Champion new tools, ways of working and data-driven practices across Risk Financing Operations, embedding continuous improvement into daily management.
  10. Mentoring and capability building: Provide guidance, coaching and mentoring to less experienced staff, helping embed consistent operational practices across the Risk Financing team.
Qualifications
  • Competencies typically acquired through a Bachelor`s degree or equivalent experience in addition to 8+ years of relevant experience to includereinsurance operations, process improvement, accounting or audit
  • Substantial experience in reinsurance operations, treaty administration or a closely related insurance operations discipline
  • Advanced degree preferred
  • Displays strong research, problem solving, analytical, and critical thinking skills
  • Advanced business operations knowledge to include understanding the function`s value chain and market conditions
  • Advanced influencing, relationship management & presentation skills
  • Highly skilled at supporting change and imparting value within an organization
  • Strong project management skills as part of implementing business process changes
  • Advanced knowledge of available data sources, strengths and shortcomings
  • May also be relevant based on the particular needs of the position: Advanced knowledge of Excel and strong knowledge of database software
  • Solid knowledge of business intelligence tools
  • A demonstrated record of cross-functional coordination in a complex organization, including influencing teams outside your reporting line
  • Strong process design and documentation capability the ability to take an undefined process, map it, and produce guidance others can follow without you present
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with the judgement to adapt the same material for operational, financial and risk-and-controls audiences
  • Sound working knowledge of treaty structures, reinsurer governance and regulatory requirements affecting reinsurance transactions
  • Comfort operating with autonomy and precision on long-horizon initiatives alongside a high volume of ad hoc requests
  • A collaborative, service-oriented approach and the credibility to become the person stakeholders bring problems to for quick resolution

What Is the Opportunity?

Travelers is seeking an Infrastructure Engineer II to join our organization as we grow and transform our Enterprise Technology Solutions organization.

The Infrastructure Engineers II focuses on administering and improving enterprise Microsoft 365 messaging and collaboration services. The position combines Exchange, Teams, automation, troubleshooting, security, compliance, and project delivery responsibilities.

What Will You Do?

  • Exchange platform ownership: The role manages Exchange Online and on-premises Exchange Server in a hybrid environment, including Azure AD Connect, mail flow, mailboxes, distribution groups, routing policies, server health, queues, retention, and archiving.
  • Teams and collaboration administration: Responsibilities include enterprise Teams policies, meetings, client updates, and Teams Phone System capabilities such as Direct Routing, dial plans, call queues, normalization rules, and E911 services. The role also maintains integrations with Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive.
  • Automation and operational support: PowerShell automation is used for onboarding and offboarding, license and mailbox setup, Teams configuration, batch changes, health reporting, usage analysis, monitoring, configuration management, patching, and backups. The engineer provides Tier 3 troubleshooting, performs root cause analysis, and manages escalations to Microsoft Support.
  • Upgrades and cross-team delivery: The position plans and executes Exchange updates, mailbox migrations, new Microsoft 365 feature deployments, and possible tenant-to-tenant migrations through testing and change-management processes. It also requires detailed documentation, runbooks, training, and collaboration with Network, Security, and Help Desk teams.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

Core Qualifications & Experience:

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, or its equivalent in work experience.
  • 5 years of relevant Infrastructure or Systems Engineering experience.
  • Substantial Exchange hybrid and Teams expertise, and experience with SharePoint Online and OneDrive for Business.
  • Required technical knowledge spans Exchange architecture, Teams policies and voice, Azure AD identity and security, Conditional Access, MFA, PowerShell, Windows Server, Active Directory, DNS, networking, and monitoring.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Microsoft certifications, advanced Microsoft 365 services, third-party administration tools, enterprise or regulated-industry experience, and leadership of migrations or upgrade projects are advantageous.

Work Environment & Availability:

  • This position offers a flexible hybrid work model.
  • Occasional off-hours maintenance or critical-incident response may be required. 

What is a Must Have?

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, related STEM field, or its equivalent in work experience plus 4 years of infrastructure engineering experience.

  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

35

At Travelers, our vision is to advance our ability to fuel analytic-driven business decisions by accelerating cross-enterprise collaboration and capabilities. The Business Insights & Analytics Leadership Development Program (BI&ALDP) internship is built for analytically driven students who are serious about launching a career in data and analytics. This is not a passive, observational internship - you will do real work, solve real business problems, and be evaluated like a professional from day one.

Over 10 weeks, you and your cohort of peers will be embedded in Travelers' data and analytics community, gaining hands-on experience in one or more of our core analytics disciplines while building the technical and professional skills that define a successful career.

Technical training is delivered to you by current full-time BI&ALDP participants - those who were recently in your position - giving you an authentic, peer-informed perspective on what it takes to grow here.

Housing: The internship program is based in Hartford, CT and St. Paul, MN. Positions are available in our business units and corporate departments. Subsidized apartments are available for students who live beyond a commutable distance from Hartford, CT or St. Paul, MN.

Positions are available from June through early August.

What Will You Do?

  • Real project work aligned to active business needs across Travelers' analytics functions.
  • Technical training taught by full-time BI&ALDP participants.
  • Formal performance reviews that give you honest, structured feedback on your growth.
  • Leadership exposure through company-wide events including the Intern Symposium and community outreach initiatives, where you will interact with leaders and a cohort across the enterprise.
  • A collaborative capstone presentation where you and your fellow interns develop and present solutions to relevant business and analytics challenges.
  • Leverage modern analytical and artificial intelligence (AI) tools/platforms with the ability to apply critical thinking to evaluate limitations related to quality and accuracy of AI-assisted outputs.
  • At the close of the internship, high performing interns are eligible to interview for a full-time offer to join the BI&ALDP - making these 10 weeks one of the most important career opportunities of your academic journey.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Cumulative GPA of 3.0 or greater preferred.
  • Pursuing or obtained a Bachelor's or Master's degree in a STEM related discipline (Science, Technology, Engineering, or Math).
  • Data warehouse and ETL understanding with Python, SQL, and/or Snowflake.
  • Knowledge of data lakes and/or experience with Databricks.
  • Exposure to dashboarding, scorecards or other descriptive reporting tools.
  • Knowledge of multidimensional data and open-source cloud-enabled analytical programming languages.
  • Familiarity with agile concepts & workflows.

What is a Must Have?

  • Pursuing or obtained a Bachelor's or Master's degree.

Employment Practices

About this job

12-week paid remote internship supporting underwriting teams with risk analysis, data reporting, and portfolio management. Work on real business challenges while developing skills in insurance underwriting and business analytics.

Full job description

We are seeking an Underwriting Intern to join our team!


The Assurant Internship Program is a 12-week immersive experience where interns do not sit on the sidelines. You will gain real-world experience by tackling business challenges and helping drive meaningful outcomes. The program combines hands-on work with learning and development opportunities, mentorship, networking and engagement opportunities, and resources designed to support your professional growth.


The Underwriting Intern will support the Underwriting team by assisting with risk analysis, portfolio management, reporting, and underwriting processes that help drive informed business decisions and profitable growth. This role offers an opportunity to gain hands-on experience in insurance underwriting, data analysis, and cross-functional collaboration while developing foundational skills for a career in underwriting and risk management.


Underwriting Analysis & Development (80%)

  • Assist the Underwriting team with data collection, analysis, and reporting of key underwriting and portfolio performance metrics.
  • Support the review and evaluation of underwriting results, trends, risk characteristics, and financial performance.
  • Assist in the preparation of underwriting reports, presentations, and business insights for internal stakeholders.
  • Conduct research and analysis to support underwriting strategies, pricing initiatives, and risk management decisions.
  • Help identify opportunities for process improvements and support the development of more efficient underwriting practices.
  • Utilize reporting and analytical tools to manage and interpret underwriting data in support of various projects.
  • Collaborate with underwriting, finance, product, and operations teams to support business objectives.

Project Management & Continuous Improvement (20%)

  • Participate in team meetings and brainstorming sessions to support underwriting initiatives and business solutions.
  • Assist in documenting underwriting processes, standard operating procedures, and work instructions.
  • Support special projects related to portfolio management, risk assessment, business analytics, and operational improvements.
  • Contribute to process mapping and workflow optimization efforts.

Learning & Development Opportunities

In this role, the intern will have the opportunity to gain experience, enhance skills, and develop competencies that prepare them for future underwriting and risk management roles, including:

  • Exposure to a corporate insurance and underwriting environment
  • Understanding of underwriting principles and risk evaluation
  • Critical thinking and analytical problem-solving skills
  • Advanced use of data analysis and reporting tools
  • Experience working with business performance metrics and portfolio analysis
  • Ability to develop business recommendations supported by data and research
  • Experience presenting findings and insights to stakeholders
  • Exposure to cross-functional collaboration and business decision-making

Basic Qualifications

  • Minimum of 2 years completed and currently enrolled in a 3rd or 4th year undergraduate program in Risk Management, Finance, Business Management, Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, Actuarial Science, Information Systems, or a related field. Master's degree candidates will also be considered.
  • Strong analytical and quantitative skills.
  • Experience with Microsoft Excel, including data analysis, reporting, and basic modeling.
  • Interest in insurance, underwriting, risk assessment, and business analytics.

Other Skills

  • Ability to work effectively in a team environment.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Detail-oriented with strong organizational and follow-up skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and adapt to changing business needs.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Professional demeanor and positive attitude.
  • Strong analytical and strategic thinking capabilities.
  • Ability to learn new systems and applications quickly.
  • Comfortable working with ambiguity and making sound recommendations based on available information.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Strong computer skills with proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint).
  • Experience using data visualization or analytical tools (Power BI, Tableau, SQL, or similar) is a plus.
  • Coursework in insurance, risk management, finance, statistics, or related disciplines preferred.

Remote Opportunity

End Date: 8/7/2027
