Job.JobTitle: Bodily Injury Adjuster - Attorney Represented - National General
Job.JobDescription:
National General is a part of The Allstate Corporation, which means we have the same innovative drive that keeps us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. We offer home, auto and accident and health insurance, as well as other specialty niche insurance products, through a large network of independent insurance agents, as well as directly to consumers.

Job Description

You know that resolving an attorney-represented bodily injury claim takes more than claims knowledge. It requires thoughtful investigation, strong evaluation skills, confident negotiation, and the ability to navigate complex conversations. As a Remote Attorney-Represented Bodily Injury Adjuster, youll take ownership of represented claims, analyzing coverage, liability, injuries, and damages to make informed decisions and negotiate appropriate resolutions within your authority. Youll bring together the details of each claim, communicate effectively with attorneys and other involved parties, and apply your experience to move claims toward resolution while balancing customer needs with sound claims practices.

This position supports a non-standard auto insurance book of business, requiring a strong understanding of liability investigations, injury evaluation, coverage analysis, and claims resolution strategies. Successful candidates are skilled at managing a high-volume caseload while delivering exceptional customer service and maintaining strong file quality. Candidates must be able to work 8am--5pm Pacific time zone hours.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Handles investigation regarding all aspects of bodily injury claims (coverage, damages, subrogation, litigation) with the exercise of discretion and independence within increased level of authority.
  • Applies intermediate understanding of insurance policies written by the company, the industry, and organizational relationships within the company and department.
  • Determines subrogation or fraud potential and how to handle.
  • Identifies customer needs and works to meet those needs using appropriate customer service skills.
  • Recognizes and identifies body parts of a vehicle and understanding of other potential property damage.
  • For claims involving fraud or subrogation, partners with assigned reps from those areas to achieve best outcome.
  • Supervisory Responsibilities:
  • This job does not have supervisory duties.

As a requirement of employment, individuals who currently hold an active insurance license must terminate all existing appointments prior to onboarding and must not hold any outside appointments at any point during employment. Applicants seeking an adjuster role who also hold a resident producer license must formally surrender that license when instructed to by the licensing team. By proceeding with the application process, applicants acknowledge and accept these licensing requirements and agree to comply.


Functional Skills

  • Customer service orientation.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong time management skills from a global case management and pending perspective (vs. transactional).
  • Effective problem solving and analytical skills; ability to detect differences and issue recognition from multiple sources.
  • Proficient in Word and Outlook.

Skills

Auto Insurance Claims, Bodily Injury Claims, Case Management, Casualty Insurance, Claims Resolution, Claims Review, Communication, Customer Service, Insurance Claims Investigations, Insurance Policies, Negotiation, Problem Solving, Time Management, Written Communication

Compensation

Pay Transparency:

Base compensation offered for this role is:

Adjuster Analyst III: $21.20 -- $34.69/hr
Adjuster Consultant I: $26.49 -- $40.99/hr
Adjuster Consultant II: $28.03 -- $43.70/hr
Adjuster Sr Consultant I: $35.82 -- $50.24/hr

And is based on experience and qualifications. Total compensation for this role is comprised of several factors, including the base compensation outlined above, plus incentive pay (i.e. commission, bonus, etc.) if applicable for the role.

Job.JobTitle: Senior Homeowner Liability Adjuster - Complex Bodily Injury Litigation - Remote
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Chicago, IL

About this job

Investigate and manage complex homeowner liability claims including bodily injury litigation, working remotely and independently. Handle higher-severity cases involving dog bites, slip-and-fall incidents, and third-party property damage while negotiating settlements with attorneys and other stakeholders.

Good fit if you have 3+ years of bodily injury claims handling experience with litigation and complex casualty claims background.

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

As an Adjuster, you will be responsible for investigating and managing complex homeowner liability claims, including dog bites, slip-and-fall incidents, and other claims involving third-party property damage and/or bodily injury. Working remotely from your home office, you will independently handle a litigation-focused caseload while delivering exceptional customer service throughout the claim lifecycle. In this role, you will evaluate coverage, liability, and damages, conduct thorough investigations, and work closely with customers, attorneys, and other claim stakeholders. Communication will occur through multiple channels, including phone, email, and text. Leveraging innovative claims platforms and tools, you will negotiate settlements, manage litigation exposures, and help drive fair and timely claim resolutions. This position is designed for an experienced litigation/complex claims adjuster who is comfortable handling higher-severity bodily injury claims and navigating the litigation process.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Negotiates and settles claims in accordance with business unit best practices.
  • Review policy language and analysis determine coverage.
  • Reviews of medical reports in preparation for claims settlement evaluation.
  • Coordinate the appraisal process for highly complex, disputed claims, ensuring adherence to policy provisions.
  • Determines and explains coverage limits in moderately complex and complex claims involving single or multiple claimants, also determines claim value.
  • Sets initial reserve, updates reserve, documents rationale and claim summary notes.
  • Act as the primary point of contact for policyholder attorneys, leading direct negotiations to resolve disputes efficiently.
  • Draft and respond to attorney correspondence, requests for information, and demands to maintain compliance and mitigate legal exposure.
  • Researches and responds to moderately complex and occasionally complex customer communications, concerns, conflicts or issues.
  • Summarizes documents and enters into claim system notes, documenting a claim file with notes, evaluations and decision-making process.

Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of bodily injury claims handling experience, including litigation and/or complex casualty claims.
  • Experience handling homeowner liability claims (dog bites, premises liability, etc.) preferred but not required.
  • Strong investigation, negotiation, and claim resolution skills.
  • Ability to effectively manage attorney-represented claims and complex liability exposures.
  • Candidates based on the West Coast are strongly preferred. Applicants in other locations may be considered if they can reliably work Pacific Time zone hours.

Training:

  • The first approximately 6-9 weeks of employment are dedicated to onboarding, licensing (if applicable), and role-specific training designed to prepare you for success in the role. Successful candidates must be able to attend required training sessions, actively participate in virtual learning activities, and successfully complete the training program.

Supervisory Responsibilities:

  • This job does not have supervisory duties.

Remote Home-Based Work:

  • This position is a permanent remote home-based role. Your home office does not need to be near an Allstate office, but it does need to be in the United States. This position is not available to Alaska, California, Hawaii or Washington residents.

When you work from home full time, youll need:

  • A home office a dedicated workspace in your residence that is private and free from distractions.
  • A minimum internet bandwidth of 50 MB down/5 MB up.
  • Appropriate work surface and seating.

What will Allstate provide?

  • A technology bundle that includes all equipment needed to perform your work from home (laptop, monitors, headset, keyboard, mouse).
  • Connectivity reimbursement of $80 per month to offset some of the cost of internet.

Certificates, Licenses, Registrations:

  • As a condition of employment, your office/area may require you to obtain an adjuster and/or an appraiser licensewhich includes passing an additional background check with the Department of Labor.If applicable, you will be required to secure license(s) within 60 days of hire.
  • If required, the Hiring Manager will work with you along with the Centralized Licensing team to ensure that you are properly licensed.

Notice of Licensing Requirement:

  • As a requirement of employment, individuals who currently hold an active insurance license must terminate all existing appointments prior to onboarding and must not hold any outside appointments at any point during employment.
  • Applicants seeking an adjuster role who also hold a resident producer license must formally surrender that license when instructed to by the licensing team. By proceeding with the application process, applicants acknowledge and accept these licensing requirements and agree to comply.

Sign-on Bonus:

  • You may be eligible for a $1,000 Licensing Sign on Bonus if you have the applicable active licenses needed for this role. This could include Home Resident Property & Casualty License, Designated Home State (DHS) Florida or Texas License, and/or applicable Appraiser License.
  • Current employees or candidates who have previously worked for Allstate, including its family of companies, are not eligible for this sign-on bonus.

Allstate Benefits:

  • Being a part of Allstate means you receive a benefits package from Day 1 of employment. This includes time off, healthcare, retirement, and more. That is why as an Allstater, youll enjoy a Total Rewards package that includes:
  • Competitive pay with needed support for continuous development and career advancement.
  • Flexibility in scheduling and a time off policy that helps support your work/life balance.
  • Initial and ongoing training to get you proficient in your new role.
  • Comprehensive benefits like a 401K/pension, education reimbursement, and programs to help you balance work with the rest of your life. Visit www.allstategoodlife.com to learn more.

#LI-YS1

Skills

Bodily Injury Claims, Business Communications, Complex Claims, Complex Litigation, Critical Thinking, General Liability Insurance, Homeowners Claims, Information Collection, Time Management

Compensation offered for this role is 65,600.00 - 110,075.00 annually and is based on experience and qualifications.

The candidate(s) offered this position will be required to submit to a background investigation.

Technical lead role focused on Kong AI Gateway, designing and implementing enterprise-grade AI Gateway solutions with LLM proxy development. Requires 8+ years in API Management and 3-5 years hands-on Kong Gateway experience.

This role will architect, design, build, test, and support modern digital products, while owning applications through production and driving their overall success against key performance goals.

  • API Management & API Lifecycle Management
  • AI Gateway / LLM Proxy Development
  • OpenAI / Azure OpenAI Integration

Job Description

The Architecture Compute, and Engineering (ACE) organization provides a transformative platform ecosystem with a comprehensive set of capabilities that empowers end users and digital product teams to innovate seamlessly and drive growth for Allstate through the Consumer Connected Cloud mission. This ecosystem aims to provide an absolute frictionless experience for our user community.

As a Digital Product Manager on the Network Connectivity team, you will operate at the crossroads of business and technology. You will partner closely with Network Connectivity Engineering and other stakeholders to design innovative solutions, pilot new capabilities, and deliver products that meet evolving business needs.

Key Responsibilities

  • Product Strategy and Vision: Develop, own, and communicate the vision and strategy for Network Connectivity capabilities.
  • Market Research: Conduct market and user research to identify trends, customer needs, and the competitive landscape. Stay ahead of industry shifts and emerging network communication technologies to uncover opportunities that drive innovation and deliver greater value to our customers.
  • Product Development: Collaborate with cross-functional teams to design, develop, and launch new digital products.
  • Roadmap Management: Create and continuously maintain a product roadmap that aligns with business goals and customer needs.
  • Ongoing Management: Work with the Digital Product team to write & groom stories, prioritize, and manage the backlog.
  • Performance Monitoring: Definite product performance metrics & monitor product performance using analytics tools and make data-driven decisions.
  • Stakeholder Communication: Communicate product progress and updates to internal stakeholders and external partners.
  • Budget Management: Manage product budgets and resources efficiently.
  • Customer Feedback: Gather and analyze customer feedback to continually improve the product.

Essential Criteria

  • Proven experience of 4+ years (Lead Consultant level) or 5+ years (Expert level) in digital product management, with ownership of product strategy, roadmap, and delivery outcomes.
  • Product management experience within Network Connectivity, Network Infrastructure, Cloud Networking, Telecommunications, or related enterprise technology domains.
  • Proven delivery across multiple Agile release cycles, with hands-on use of tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, or similar to manage backlogs, prioritisation, and delivery tracking.
  • Experience working with enterprise networking technologies, including evidence of supporting, delivering, or managing products related to LAN, WAN, WLAN, SD-WAN, Remote Office, VPN, SASE, or cloud networking solutions.
  • Experience partnering with Network Engineering, Cloud, Infrastructure, Security, Server, and Storage teams to define product requirements, influence stakeholders, and deliver technology products using customer, operational, or business performance metrics.

Additional Responsibilities for Expert level Digital Product Manager

  • Minimum 2 years' experience owning and executing product strategy independently, including prioritising investments and delivering outcomes across multiple release cycles.
  • Demonstrated experience mentoring Product Managers, Product Owners, or cross-functional teams and acting as a recognised subject matter expert within the organisation.

Desirable Experience

  • Experience with cloud networking technologies and platforms across AWS, Azure, GCP, or hybrid-cloud environments.
  • Experience with modern networking approaches such as SD-WAN, SASE, Zero Trust, Network Automation, or Network Observability.
  • Relevant industry certifications in Product Management, Agile, SAFe, Cisco (CCNA/CCNP), AWS, or Azure.
  • Experience working within large-scale, regulated enterprise environments.
  • Experience using customer research, market analysis, or technology trends to identify and validate new product opportunities.

Job.JobTitle: Homeowners Liability Bodily Injury Adjuster-Consultant II -Remote
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Chicago, IL

About this job

Investigate and settle moderately complex to complex homeowners liability bodily injury claims for Allstate. Remote position based in the US, requiring review of policies, medical reports, and negotiation with attorneys to resolve disputes.

Good fit if you have 2+ years of claims adjusting experience, hold an adjuster license, and have handled third-party bodily injury claims.

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

This role is responsible for investigating moderately complex and some complex comprehensive personal liability (CPL) claims, including unrepresentative moderate and CPL losses. Responsibilities include analyzing coverage, obtaining recorded statements, evaluating liability and damages, handling demands, issuing payments to appropriate parties, and negotiating settlements.

Key Responsibilities

  • Negotiates and settles claims in accordance with business unit best practices.
  • Review policy language and analysis determine coverage.
  • Reviews of medical reports in preparation for claims settlement evaluation.
  • Determines and explains coverage limits in moderately complex and some complex claims involving single or multiple claimants, also determines claim value.
  • Sets initial reserve, updates reserve, documents rationale and claim summary notes.
  • Act as the primary point of contact for policyholder attorneys, leading direct negotiations to resolve disputes efficiently.
  • Researches and responds to moderately complex and occasionally complex customer communications, concerns, conflicts or issues.
  • Summarizes documents and enters into claim system notes, documenting a claim file with notes, evaluations and decision-making process.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 2 or more years of experience.
  • Adjuster License.
  • Strong negotiating experience and policy interpretation experience.
  • Experience handling third-party bodily injury claims arising from homeowners, renters, landlord, ATV, boat, and golf cart insurance policies.

This position is not available to Alaska, California, Hawaii or Washington residents.

Supervisory Responsibilities

This job does not have supervisory duties.

Remote Home-Based Work:

This position is a permanent remote home-based role. Your home office does not need to be near an Allstate office, but it does need to be in the United States. This position is not available for California, Alaska, Hawaii, or Washington residents.

When you work from home full time, youll need:

  • A home office a dedicated workspace in your residence that is private and free from distractions.
  • A minimum internet bandwidth of 50 MB down/5 MB up.
  • Appropriate work surface and seating.

What will Allstate provide?

  • A technology bundle that includes all equipment needed to perform your work from home (laptop, monitors, headset, keyboard, mouse).
  • Connectivity reimbursement of $80 per month to offset some of the cost of internet.

Certificates, Licenses, Registrations:

  • As a condition of employment, your office/area may require you to obtain an adjuster and/or an appraiser licensewhich includes passing an additional background check with the Department of Labor.If applicable, you will be required to secure license(s) within 60 days of hire.
  • If required, the Hiring Manager will work with you along with the Centralized Licensing team to ensure that you are properly licensed.

Notice of Licensing Requirement:

  • As a requirement of employment, individuals who currently hold an active insurance license must terminate all existing appointments prior to onboarding and must not hold any outside appointments at any point during employment.
  • Applicants seeking an adjuster role who also hold a resident producer license must formally surrender that license when instructed to by the licensing team. By proceeding with the application process, applicants acknowledge and accept these licensing requirements and agree to comply.

Sign-on Bonus:

  • You may be eligible for a $1000 Licensing Sign on Bonus if you have the applicable active licenses needed for this role. This could include Home Resident Property & Casualty License, Designated Home State (DHS) Florida or Texas License, and/or applicable Appraiser License.
  • Current employees or candidates who have previously worked for Allstate, including its family of companies, are not eligible for this sign-on bonus.

Allstate Benefits:

  • Being a part of Allstate means you receive a benefits package from Day 1 of employment. This includes time off, healthcare, retirement, and more. That is why as an Allstater, youll enjoy a Total Rewards package that includes:
  • Competitive pay with needed support for continuous development and career advancement.
  • Flexibility in scheduling and a time off policy that helps support your work/life balance.
  • Initial and ongoing training to get you proficient in your new role.
  • Comprehensive benefits like a 401K/pension, education reimbursement, and programs to help you balance work with the rest of your life. Visit www.allstategoodlife.com to learn more.

Skills

Bodily Injury Claims, Business Communications, Critical Thinking, General Liability Claims, Homeowners Claims, Information Collection, Time Management

Compensation

Compensation offered for this role is 53,500.00 - 84,625.00 annually and is based on experience and qualifications.

The candidate(s) offered this position will be required to submit to a background investigation.

About this job

Field Property Claims Adjuster managing property claims from inspection through resolution in the Worcester, Massachusetts area. Responsibilities include estimating damages, reviewing coverage, handling contents losses, and documenting claim activity.

Good fit if you have property claims experience, Xactimate proficiency, an active adjuster license or ability to obtain one, and strong customer service skills.

Full job description

National General is a part of The Allstate Corporation, which means we have the same innovative drive that keeps us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. We offer home, auto and accident and health insurance, as well as other specialty niche insurance products, through a large network of independent insurance agents, as well as directly to consumers.

Job Description

As a Field Property Claims Adjuster with National General, youll play an important role in helping customers navigate the claims process following a loss. Youll manage claims from initial investigation through resolution, conducting field inspections, evaluating damages, reviewing applicable coverage, developing repair estimates, and working with customers and other involved parties to reach timely and accurate claim outcomes. This role combines independent field work, critical thinking, technical expertise, and strong customer service. Youll manage an assigned territory and workload while documenting claim activity, communicating throughout the claims process, and making sound decisions in accordance with applicable policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.

We're hiring a Field Property Adjuster based near Worcester, Northborough or Natick, Massachusetts. You'll manage property claims from inspection through resolution, including estimating damage, reviewing supplements, handling contents losses, and supporting customers throughout the claims process.

The ideal candidate has property claims experience, strong customer service and organizational skills, proficiency in Xactimate, and an active adjuster license (or the ability to obtain one). Experience handling claims both in the field and virtually is preferred.


Key Responsibilities

  • Exhibits mastery estimating fundamentals in order to create estimates of damages on the most complex first party homeowner losses of all severities
  • Builds mastered relationships with both internal and external customers
  • Interprets regulatory compliance and fair claims practices
  • Negotiates settlements, makes settlement payments and documents all activities in the most complex of files
  • Applies mastered content in interpretations of all policy types written by the company and assists leadership in formal and ad hoc training
  • Recommends process improvements


Supervisory Responsibilities

  • This job does not have supervisory duties.

Sign On Bonus:

You may be eligible for a $1,000 Licensing Sign on Bonus if you have the applicable active licenses needed for this role. This could include Home Resident Property & Casualty License, Designated Home State (DHS) Florida or Texas License, and/or applicable Appraiser License.

*Current employees or candidates who have previously worked for Allstate, including its family of companies, are not eligible for this sign-on bonus.

Applicants seeking an adjuster role who also hold a resident producer license must formally surrender that license when instructed to by the licensing team. By proceeding with the application process, applicants acknowledge and accept these licensing requirements and agree to comply.

Job.JobDescription:
National General is a part of The Allstate Corporation, which means we have the same innovative drive that keeps us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. We offer home, auto and accident and health insurance, as well as other specialty niche insurance products, through a large network of independent insurance agents, as well as directly to consumers.

Job Description

The Territory Sales Manager is responsible for consistently exceeding agreed upon new business production, direct written premium, and loss ratio goals, and other KPIs on an annual basis by effectively managing the agents of an assigned market to increase company market share by driving profitable growth.

Key Responsibilities

Position is responsible for product/user integration with industry technology and comparative rating platforms within market and assigned agencies

Positions and promotes full suite of National General Insurance products into Independent Agency Partners to include, multiple personal auto products, homeowners, commercial vehicle, flood, and recreational vehicle & key focus on Household package coverages (based on state availability)

Develops and maintains the assigned markets new agency appointment pipeline, supports National Accounts & Alternative Distribution Initiatives to implement corporate agreements at the local market level with large Independent Agents driving package product growth & coach new Territory Sales Managers

Consults with IAs by having a strong knowledge of the independent agency channel, including industry competitors, major brokers and national industry associations to gather market intel to help promote and position National General products and/or make market enhancement to align with industry opportunity

Delivers on the business units annual execution plan (growth, profitability, agency engagement, new appointments) for their market with focus on Household package coverages under the guidance of a Regional Sales Manager and/or Director.

Role uses full suite of production data and reporting to identify trends, capitalize on opportunity and regularly address agency level performance including training / skill gap to execute on business plan, educating on package products to drive agency growth

Collaborates with IAs to assist with creation of agency-specific short term and long-term strategic business plans, periodically reviews and suggests adjustments as necessary to achieve results

Collaborates with Product, Pricing, Operations to perform stakeholder (agency) and risk analysis on market related issues

Territory Sales Manager handles increasing the quote and issuance flow of assigned market beyond the rate and Underwriting trends filed and implemented in the market

Key company liaison within assigned market to both independent agencies and industry associations and must be field facing 4 days per week, driving key business initiatives, maintaining accurate records of these sales activities, client interactions, and follow-ups in CRM software


Candidates must reside in the greater Salt Lake City/Provo, UT area.


Experience

5 or more years of experience (Preferred)


Supervisory Responsibilities

This job does not have supervisory duties.


Skills

Client Relationship Building, Insurance Products, Relationship Building, Strategic Collaboration, Territory Sales Management

Compensation

Base Salary: $95,000 - $104,000 plus incentives based on performance

About this job

Inside Auto Appraiser for Travelers Insurance in Charlotte, NC. Conduct virtual inspections of damaged vehicles, estimate repair costs, and settle total loss claims using industry-standard software while working with repair partners and customers.

Good fit if you have two years of auto physical damage appraisal experience, an active adjuster license, and proficiency with claims management and estimating software.

Full job description

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$65,400.00 - $108,000.00

Target Openings

2

What Is the Opportunity?

As an Inside Auto Appraiser, you are responsible for virtually inspecting damaged vehicles, estimating repair costs, working with our direct repair partners to address vehicle owner damages, and determining and settling the actual cash value of total loss vehicles to ensure accurate and timely claim settlements. For this role, you will need to have a high level of technical expertise in vehicle damage assessment, strong customer service skills, and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment. This position will serve as a technical resource for auto claim staff and will provide advice and direction to claim professionals on claim damages to achieve optimal outcomes.

What Will You Do?

  • Review and assess vehicle damage resulting from accidents, weather events, or other covered losses by conducting thorough virtual inspections.
  • Prepare accurate repair estimates using industry-standard estimating software to determine the cost of parts, labor, and materials required to restore vehicles to pre-loss condition.
  • Evaluate and settle vehicle total losses by determining actual cash value (ACV) through market research, comparable vehicle analysis, and application of appropriate valuation tools and methodologies.
  • Negotiate repair costs and settlements with body shops, customers, and third-party claimants to reach fair and timely resolutions while maintaining quality repair standards.
  • Identify and document pre-existing damage, prior repairs, and potential fraud indicators to ensure accurate claim evaluation and protect company interests.
  • Collaborate with Direct Repair partners, claim representatives, body shops, and vendors to coordinate repairs, authorize supplements, and resolve coverage or repair-related issues.
  • Provide exceptional customer service by explaining the appraisal process, answering questions, and keeping vehicle owners informed throughout the claim lifecycle.
  • Adapt to new technology implementations, system upgrades, and digital tool rollouts, particularly in the areas of AI while maintaining productivity and service quality.
  • May deploy to on-site inspections and have the ability to transport to meet with customers.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's Degree.
  • Active adjuster license, where applicable.
  • Two years of auto physical damage appraisal experience.
  • Proficient in claims management and estimating software, with advanced skills in Microsoft Office and enterprise technology systems and platforms.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to convey information clearly and professionally.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgement and make effective decisions.
  • Exceptional customer service skills and commitment to providing a positive experience for customers throughout the claim process.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills; ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated conflict resolution skills; ability to facilitate productive discussions and reach equitable outcomes.
  • Ability to manage stress, navigate difficult situations, and maintain composure and professionalism under pressure while always taking accountability for decisions.
  • Basic understanding of insurance principles and terminology, state insurance regulations and claim handling requirements.
  • Ability to quickly learn from experience and apply it to new situations with speed and flexibility.

What is a Must Have?

  • High School Diploma or GED required.
  • One year of auto physical damage appraisal or comparable claim related experience or successful completion of required Travelers Claim Representative training program.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit http://careers.travelers.com/life-at-travelers/benefits/.

Description

Comparion Insurance Agency is hiring self-motivated, relationship-driven professionals for a rewarding outside sales career. This role offers autonomy and flexibility to build your career, grow your earnings, and make a meaningful impact by helping protect individuals and families with auto, home, life, and specialty insurance.

Backed by a Fortune 100 company, youll receive hands-on training, resources, and team support to help you succeed no prior insurance experience required.

Description

What youll do:

  • Sell auto, home, life, and related insurance products using a consultative, needs-based approach.
  • Build and maintain a book of business through referrals, networking, and community engagement as part of your outside sales efforts.
  • Identify prospective customers using established lead methodologies and relationship-driven outreach.
  • Accurately document customer interactions and handle sensitive information with integrity and confidentiality.
  • Use insurance sales technology, relationship management tools, and multi-carrier platforms to deliver tailored insurance solutions.
  • Participate in training, coaching, and performance incentives to continuously improve sales results.

What We Offer:

  • Unlimited commission and renewal income potential for earnings growth over time.
  • Full-time employment with benefits from day one, including health insurance, generous 401(k) match, and paid time off.
  • Paid training, licensing support, and ongoing development.
  • Autonomy to embrace your entrepreneurial spirit and structure your time your way.
  • Flexible work structure (hybrid office, field, and remote based on what your day requires).
  • Supportive team culture with mentorship and long-term career paths.
Qualifications

Who Were Looking For:

Day One Skills & Traits

  • Self-motivated and accountable you take ownership of your work and results.
  • Reliable and responsive you follow through and do what you say youll do.
  • Professional and trustworthy you handle customer information with care and integrity.
  • Relationship-focused you enjoy helping others and building long-term trust.
  • Outgoing youre comfortable talking with people and explaining options clearly.
  • Tech savvy youre able to learn and use technology and digital tools with ease.
  • Calm under pressure you stay composed in a fast-paced, customer-focused environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in customer-facing roles like retail, hospitality, service, operations, logistics, banking, account management, or sales.
  • Basic understanding of sales conversations, including handling common customer questions or objections.
  • Experience managing multiple accounts, clients, or priorities simultaneously.
  • Exposure to consultative selling, negotiation, or regulated industries.

You will be required to obtain relevant licenses upon being hired.

Build a career for yourself, not by yourself. Launch a rewarding insurance sales career today.

Description

Comparion Insurance Agency is hiring self-motivated, relationship-driven professionals for a rewarding outside sales career. This role offers autonomy and flexibility to build your career, grow your earnings, and make a meaningful impact by helping protect individuals and families with auto, home, life, and specialty insurance.

Backed by a Fortune 100 company, youll receive hands-on training, resources, and team support to help you succeed no prior insurance experience required.

Description

What youll do:

  • Sell auto, home, life, and related insurance products using a consultative, needs-based approach.
  • Build and maintain a book of business through referrals, networking, and community engagement as part of your outside sales efforts.
  • Identify prospective customers using established lead methodologies and relationship-driven outreach.
  • Accurately document customer interactions and handle sensitive information with integrity and confidentiality.
  • Use insurance sales technology, relationship management tools, and multi-carrier platforms to deliver tailored insurance solutions.
  • Participate in training, coaching, and performance incentives to continuously improve sales results.

What We Offer:

  • Unlimited commission and renewal income potential for earnings growth over time.
  • Full-time employment with benefits from day one, including health insurance, generous 401(k) match, and paid time off.
  • Paid training, licensing support, and ongoing development.
  • Autonomy to embrace your entrepreneurial spirit and structure your time your way.
  • Flexible work structure (hybrid office, field, and remote based on what your day requires).
  • Supportive team culture with mentorship and long-term career paths.
Qualifications

Who Were Looking For:

Day One Skills & Traits

  • Self-motivated and accountable you take ownership of your work and results.
  • Reliable and responsive you follow through and do what you say youll do.
  • Professional and trustworthy you handle customer information with care and integrity.
  • Relationship-focused you enjoy helping others and building long-term trust.
  • Outgoing youre comfortable talking with people and explaining options clearly.
  • Tech savvy youre able to learn and use technology and digital tools with ease.
  • Calm under pressure you stay composed in a fast-paced, customer-focused environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in customer-facing roles like retail, hospitality, service, operations, logistics, banking, account management, or sales.
  • Basic understanding of sales conversations, including handling common customer questions or objections.
  • Experience managing multiple accounts, clients, or priorities simultaneously.
  • Exposure to consultative selling, negotiation, or regulated industries.

You will be required to obtain relevant licenses upon being hired.

Job Details

As an Inside Sales Agent you will be handling inbound calls and warm leads, consulting with customers on their insurance needs and match the correct coverages, products, and benefits to convert sales leads into policyholders.

Due to state licensing restrictions, employees must remain in their resident state for at least one year before relocating.

Youd be a great fit if you are:

A Passionate Seller:When a lead comes in, you skillfully pick up the phone and use your sales expertise to turn prospects into happy, confident Liberty Mutualpolicyholders.

A Front Lines Liaison:You rise to the role of representing the Liberty brand, you believe in what youre selling, and you enjoy connecting customers to the right products for their individual needs.

A Reliable Teammate:Whether you work at the office or from home, you adapt well to different environments, schedules, and the varying needs of ourpolicyholders.

A Customer-Centric Closer:While sales is in your title, integrity is in your nature. That means you sincerely care that our customers get exactly the quality products and services they need to embrace today and confidently pursue tomorrow.

Position Details:

From day one you will begin paid training in a remote work environment. All insurance representatives need to hold a Property & Casualty Insurance license. If you do not have one, no worries, paid training also includes licensing!

  • Training extends over a period of 16 weeks for licensed hires and 18 weeks for unlicensed hires.

  • Must be available to work a schedule of 4 weekdays and 1 weekend day. Standard shift is 11:30-8 EST, 12:30-9 CST, or 8:30-5 PST.

  • All computer equipment is provided. Youmust be able to maintain department.Work at home (W@H) requirements whichinclude a professional workspace/room with adedicated desk and wired (cable, fiber of DSLservice) high-speed internet connection with aminimum 100 MBps download speed and 20MBps upload speed. Liberty Mutual does notsupport satellite and mobile internet services.

  • 2-3 years sales experience preferred. 2 yearsof sales/service-related work experiencerequired.
  • Strong, engaging interpersonal and persuasion skills needed to close sales.
  • Ability to communicate well to both prospects and customers.
  • Excellent analytical, decision-making and organizational skills.
  • Strong typing capabilities and PC proficiency.

Why Liberty Mutual?

Pay Details:

  • Starting base salary is $45K with opportunity for growth.
  • Average earnings range from $55K-$75K through a combination of base salary and generouscommission.

We are currently hiring quality Inbound sales professionals in the following states:AR, AZ, FL, GA, IA, ID, IN, KS, LA, MA, MD, ME, MI, MN, MO, NC, NE, NH, NJ, NM, NV, NY, OH, OR, PA, SC, TX, UT, VA, WA, WI, andWV

Licensed only candidates based in ID, MT, WY, GA, TN, AL, OK, KS and KY Applicants must reside within these specified locations to be considered for this role.

Positivity. Flexibility. Determination and a persuasive personality. Qualities like these cannot be taught. But they can be sharpened, strengthened, and appropriately compensated when you join Liberty Mutual Insurance as a part of our Contact Center Sales Organization. Bring your unique sales talent to our Fortune 100 company and receive paid-training, licensing in all 50 states, and a dynamic role that directs only warm leads your way (no cold calls) because we believe in supporting your success, not holding it back. Join our sales team and realize the rewards of a career with unlimited earning potential, generous commissions, and a portfolio of benefits that start on day one.

Job Details

As an Inside Sales Agent you will be handling inbound calls and warm leads, consulting with customers on their insurance needs and match the correct coverages, products, and benefits to convert sales leads into policyholders.

Due to state licensing restrictions, employees must remain in their resident state for at least one year before relocating.

Youd be a great fit if you are:

A Passionate Seller:When a lead comes in, you skillfully pick up the phone and use your sales expertise to turn prospects into happy, confident Liberty Mutualpolicyholders.

A Front Lines Liaison:You rise to the role of representing the Liberty brand, you believe in what youre selling, and you enjoy connecting customers to the right products for their individual needs.

A Reliable Teammate:Whether you work at the office or from home, you adapt well to different environments, schedules, and the varying needs of ourpolicyholders.

A Customer-Centric Closer:While sales is in your title, integrity is in your nature. That means you sincerely care that our customers get exactly the quality products and services they need to embrace today and confidently pursue tomorrow.

Position Details:

From day one you will begin paid training in a remote work environment. All insurance representatives need to hold a Property & Casualty Insurance license. If you do not have one, no worries, paid training also includes licensing!

  • Training extends over a period of 16 weeks for licensed hires and 18 weeks for unlicensed hires.
  • Comprehensive medical benefits from Day 1.
  • No cold calls, all incoming warm leads.
  • Opportunities for rewards and recognition.

  • Must be available to work a schedule of 4 weekdays and 1 weekend day. Standard shift is 11:30-8 EST, 12:30-9 CST, or 8:30-5 PST.

  • All computer equipment is provided. Youmust be able to maintain department.Work at home (W@H) requirements whichinclude a professional workspace/room with adedicated desk and wired (cable, fiber of DSLservice) high-speed internet connection with aminimum 100 MBps download speed and 20MBps upload speed. Liberty Mutual does notsupport satellite and mobile internet services.
Qualifications
  • 2-3 years sales experience preferred. 2 yearsof sales/service-related work experiencerequired.
  • Strong, engaging interpersonal and persuasion skills needed to close sales.
  • Ability to communicate well to both prospects and customers.
  • Excellent analytical, decision-making and organizational skills.
  • Strong typing capabilities and PC proficiency.
  • Property and Casualty License required afterhire.

Job Details

As an Inside Sales Agent you will be handling inbound calls and warm leads, consulting with customers on their insurance needs and match the correct coverages, products, and benefits to convert sales leads into policyholders.

Due to state licensing restrictions, employees must remain in their resident state for at least one year before relocating.

Youd be a great fit if you are:

A Passionate Seller:When a lead comes in, you skillfully pick up the phone and use your sales expertise to turn prospects into happy, confident Liberty Mutualpolicyholders.

A Front Lines Liaison:You rise to the role of representing the Liberty brand, you believe in what youre selling, and you enjoy connecting customers to the right products for their individual needs.

A Reliable Teammate:Whether you work at the office or from home, you adapt well to different environments, schedules, and the varying needs of ourpolicyholders.

A Customer-Centric Closer:While sales is in your title, integrity is in your nature. That means you sincerely care that our customers get exactly the quality products and services they need to embrace today and confidently pursue tomorrow.

Position Details:

From day one you will begin paid training in a remote work environment. All insurance representatives need to hold a Property & Casualty Insurance license. If you do not have one, no worries, paid training also includes licensing!

  • Training extends over a period of 16 weeks for licensed hires and 18 weeks for unlicensed hires.
  • Comprehensive medical benefits from Day 1.
  • No cold calls, all incoming warm leads.
  • Opportunities for rewards and recognition.

  • Must be available to work a schedule of 4 weekdays and 1 weekend day. Standard shift is 11:30-8 EST, 12:30-9 CST, or 8:30-5 PST.

  • All computer equipment is provided. Youmust be able to maintain department.Work at home (W@H) requirements whichinclude a professional workspace/room with adedicated desk and wired (cable, fiber of DSLservice) high-speed internet connection with aminimum 100 MBps download speed and 20MBps upload speed. Liberty Mutual does notsupport satellite and mobile internet services.
Qualifications
  • 2-3 years sales experience preferred. 2 yearsof sales/service-related work experiencerequired.
  • Strong, engaging interpersonal and persuasion skills needed to close sales.
  • Ability to communicate well to both prospects and customers.
  • Excellent analytical, decision-making and organizational skills.
  • Strong typing capabilities and PC proficiency.
  • Property and Casualty Insurance License. Training will be provided if you do not currently hold a license.

A Reliable Teammate:Whether you work at the office or from home, you adapt well to different environments, schedules, and the varying needs of ourpolicyholders.

A Customer-Centric Closer:While sales is in your title, integrity is in your nature. That means you sincerely care that our customers get exactly the quality products and services they need to embrace today and confidently pursue tomorrow.

From day one you will begin paid training in a remote work environment. All insurance representatives need to hold a Property & Casualty Insurance license. If you do not have one, no worries, paid training also includes licensing!

Job.JobTitle: Actuary, Auto Analytics, State Deep Dive
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Boston, MA
  • Experience: 5 to 7 years
  • Education: Bachelor's degree

About this job

Actuary supporting state leadership in Liberty Mutual's largest personal auto markets by analyzing segment performance, building growth and profitability projections, and identifying pricing and underwriting opportunities. Reports to the Auto Analytics State Deep Dive Team Manager in Boston.

Good fit if you have 5-7 years of relevant actuarial experience and ACAS/FCAS or ASA/FSA designation, with strong Excel and SAS skills.

Full job description


Description

The Auto Analytics State Deep Dive team is the analytical partner to state leadership in Liberty Mutuals largest and most complex Personal Auto markets. In this role you will work directly with the Directors of State Operations (DSOs) on the questions that shape each states direction.

You will analyze segment-level performance to identify targeted pricing and underwriting changes, and partner with Tactical Pricing and Underwriting teams to implement them. You will build the growth and profitability projections behind state planning and key strategic decisions, such as rating program launches, distribution strategy and responses to competitive moves. You will also monitor marketplace, operational and claims trends to catch emerging opportunities and risks early, and turn those insights into tactical actions with partners across Risk Analytics and the business.

You will join a team of three actuaries and report to the Auto Analytics State Deep Dive Team Manager. Your work will directly shape state strategy and support Libertys goal of top-quartile profitability.

**Applicants that live within 50 miles of the following Liberty Mutual offices will have a 2 day/week hybrid requirement: Boston, MA; Portsmouth, NH; Columbus, OH; Seattle, WA; and Plano, TX.**

Responsibilities

  • Turn segmentation insight into pricing and underwriting change. Identify underwriting rules and segment-level opportunities in rating variables, coverage limits and discounts. Partner with Tactical Pricing, Underwriting and Product teams to move recommendations into implementation.
  • Inform state strategy and planning. Build policies in force (PIF), retention and loss ratio projections for annual planning, long-range growth targets, program launches and rate changes. Quantify the growth and profitability trade-offs behind major strategic decisions.
  • Monitor performance and drive tactical action. Track marketplace, operational and claims trends. Discover what is driving the changes and proactively identify opportunities for tactical actions.
  • Evaluate program launches and initiatives. Measure how new rating programs, underwriting models and state initiatives perform against expectations, including retention, renewal dislocation, mix and loss ratio. Recommend course corrections.
  • Be a trusted partner to your DSOs. Bring forward-looking insights and recommendations, answer time-sensitive business questions quickly, and frame findings around decisions, impact and trade-offs.
  • Become the expert on your states. Build deep knowledge of each states product and program history, regulatory environment, competitive landscape and market dynamics. Use competitor filings and industry developments to anticipate change.
  • Collaborate across the organization. Work with Countrywide Analytics, Indications, Tactical Pricing, Product, Underwriting, Modeling, Claims, Reserving, Finance and Distribution so that cross-team work reflects state-specific needs.
  • Work smarter. Leverage and enhance the teams analytical tools, automation and AI to spend less time on routine work and more on interpretation and partner engagement.
  • Contribute to the team culture. Share findings, methods and state knowledge openly, and help build an inclusive, high-performing team.
Qualifications
  • Bachelor's degree required; Masters degree preferred.
  • Associateship or Fellowship in the Casualty Actuarial Society (ACAS/FCAS) or in Society of Actuaries (ASA/FSA) designation preferred or comparable education/designation with relevant experience.
  • Minimum 5-7 years relevant experience required.
  • Sound knowledge of actuarial techniques and standards, as well as other business operations including financial, underwriting, legal, statistics, claims, sales, etc.
  • Advanced communication and interpersonal skills and ability to build relationships and interact effectively with others within and outside the organization.
  • Ability to motivate and mentor peers and motivate and train subordinates.
  • Advanced computing skills (MS Office Excel, SAS, etc.) with ability to build complex models.
About Us

Pay Philosophy: The typical starting salary range for this role is determined by a number of factors including skills, experience, education, certifications and location. The full salary range for this role reflects the competitive labor market value for all employees in these positions across the national market and provides an opportunity to progress as employees grow and develop within the role. Some roles at Liberty Mutual have a corresponding compensation plan which may include commission and/or bonus earnings at rates that vary based on multiple factors set forth in the compensation plan for the role.

Quick facts

  • Location: Denver, CO
  • Experience: 8+ years

About this job

Senior Attorney role at Liberty Mutual managing complex civil litigation matters with exposures typically exceeding $50,000. Primarily remote in Colorado, involving legal strategy, trial management, mentorship of junior attorneys, and client advisory work.

Good fit if you have 8+ years of trial experience, Colorado bar admission, insurance law expertise, and proven ability managing high-stakes litigation cases.

Full job description


Description

This role is primarily remote in the state of Colorado except for required appearances.

At Liberty Mutual, were committed to delivering exceptional legal services to our customers around the world, working to uphold and protect our policyholders rights and positively impacting our business. As a Senior Attorney at Liberty Mutual, youll join a diverse team that values a healthy work/life balance and enjoy benefits that include eligible performance bonuses, 20 days of flexible time off each year, personal holidays, and a 401(k) plan with matching contributions. If youre looking for a place to build a long-term career while making a positive difference, consider joining our legal team where youll represent Liberty Mutual and our policyholders in moderately complex civil litigation matters involving claims for monetary damages or compensation for personal injuries or property damage of moderate value.

Liberty Mutual is seeking a highly experienced Senior Attorney to lead the management of complex litigation matters involving substantial legal and financial exposure. This role requires mastery of advanced legal principles, regulatory expertise, strategic litigation management, budget oversight, and client relationship leadership. The Senior Attorney will leverage cutting-edge technology, mentor junior attorneys, and collaborate extensively with Claims Representatives, insured clients, and external partners to deliver favorable outcomes while minimizing risk and cost. This position plays a critical role in driving continuous improvement and upholding the highest standards of legal ethics and compliance.

Responsibilities:

  • Legal Strategy Development: Craft, implement, and continuously refine sophisticated legal strategies for complex litigation matters by applying advanced legal principles and comprehensive knowledge of the regulatory environment.
  • Litigation Execution & Management: Independently oversee all phases of complex litigation, including discovery, hearings, trials, and settlement negotiations, ensuring meticulous preparation and execution of legal documents and motions. Manage and co-chair trials with exposure typically exceeding $50,000, leading negotiation efforts to achieve optimal resolutions that safeguard client interests.
  • Technology Utilization: Champion the use of state-of-the-art e-discovery tools and case management technologies to enhance legal workflows, operational efficiency, and remote collaboration across teams.
  • Client Advisory and Relationship Management: Serve as a trusted legal advisor providing clear, authoritative opinions and strategic counsel to Claims Representatives and insured clients.
  • Risk Evaluation and Mitigation: Proactively identify, assess, and mitigate potential legal risks associated with complex cases.
  • Budget and Resource Management: Oversee litigation expenses, trial budgets, and case timelines to balance high-quality legal representation with fiscal responsibility.
  • Training, Mentorship, and Leadership: Design and lead comprehensive training programs for Legal, Claims, and other departments to enhance team competencies and legal knowledge. Provide mentorship, guidance, and support to junior and mid-level attorneys, paralegals, and law clerks, fostering professional development and a collaborative work environment.
  • Continuous Legal Knowledge Enhancement: Stay current on evolving legal developments, industry trends, and relevant medical, scientific, or engineering issues affecting cases.

Senior Attorney role managing complex civil litigation for Liberty Mutual Insurance, primarily remote in Colorado. Lead litigation strategy, oversee trials with exposure exceeding $50,000, mentor junior attorneys, and advise Claims Representatives and insured clients.

Good fit if you have 8+ years of trial experience in insurance law and complex civil litigation with Colorado bar admission.

Full job description


Description

This role is primarily remote in the state of Colorado except for required appearances.

At Liberty Mutual, were committed to delivering exceptional legal services to our customers around the world, working to uphold and protect our policyholders rights and positively impacting our business. As a Senior Attorney at Liberty Mutual, youll join a diverse team that values a healthy work/life balance and enjoy benefits that include eligible performance bonuses, 20 days of flexible time off each year, personal holidays, and a 401(k) plan with matching contributions. If youre looking for a place to build a long-term career while making a positive difference, consider joining our legal team where youll represent Liberty Mutual and our policyholders in moderately complex civil litigation matters involving claims for monetary damages or compensation for personal injuries or property damage of moderate value.

Liberty Mutual is seeking a highly experienced Senior Attorney to lead the management of complex litigation matters involving substantial legal and financial exposure. This role requires mastery of advanced legal principles, regulatory expertise, strategic litigation management, budget oversight, and client relationship leadership. The Senior Attorney will leverage cutting-edge technology, mentor junior attorneys, and collaborate extensively with Claims Representatives, insured clients, and external partners to deliver favorable outcomes while minimizing risk and cost. This position plays a critical role in driving continuous improvement and upholding the highest standards of legal ethics and compliance.

Responsibilities:

  • Legal Strategy Development: Craft, implement, and continuously refine sophisticated legal strategies for complex litigation matters by applying advanced legal principles and comprehensive knowledge of the regulatory environment.
  • Litigation Execution & Management: Independently oversee all phases of complex litigation, including discovery, hearings, trials, and settlement negotiations, ensuring meticulous preparation and execution of legal documents and motions. Manage and co-chair trials with exposure typically exceeding $50,000, leading negotiation efforts to achieve optimal resolutions that safeguard client interests.
  • Technology Utilization: Champion the use of state-of-the-art e-discovery tools and case management technologies to enhance legal workflows, operational efficiency, and remote collaboration across teams.
  • Client Advisory and Relationship Management: Serve as a trusted legal advisor providing clear, authoritative opinions and strategic counsel to Claims Representatives and insured clients.
  • Risk Evaluation and Mitigation: Proactively identify, assess, and mitigate potential legal risks associated with complex cases.
  • Budget and Resource Management: Oversee litigation expenses, trial budgets, and case timelines to balance high-quality legal representation with fiscal responsibility.
  • Training, Mentorship, and Leadership: Design and lead comprehensive training programs for Legal, Claims, and other departments to enhance team competencies and legal knowledge. Provide mentorship, guidance, and support to junior and mid-level attorneys, paralegals, and law clerks, fostering professional development and a collaborative work environment.
  • Continuous Legal Knowledge Enhancement: Stay current on evolving legal developments, industry trends, and relevant medical, scientific, or engineering issues affecting cases.
  • Organizational Improvement & Collaboration: Actively contribute to initiatives that improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the Staff Legal and Global Legal & Compliance organizations.
  • Ethical Compliance Adherence: Uphold and promote the highest standards of legal ethics and professional conduct in all activities. Manage complex ethical issues and guide junior attorneys in compliance with the Model Rules of Professional Conduct (MRPC).
Qualifications
  • Juris Doctor (JD) or LLB degree from an accredited law school.
  • Admission to the bar in Colorado and in good standing; additional licensure for specialized courts or boards may be required.
  • Minimum of 8 years of successful trial attorney experience, with a focus on insurance law and complex civil litigation and as necessary, workers compensation and/or No Fault law. Construction Defect and Personal Injury experience preferred.
  • Proven expertise managing high-stakes, complex litigation with substantial exposure (trials exceeding $50,000).
  • In-depth knowledge of insurance law, regulatory frameworks, and client business operations.
  • Exceptional legal research, writing, negotiation, and analytical skills.
  • Proficiency with advanced e-discovery platforms, case management software, and remote collaboration tools.
  • Demonstrated leadership and mentorship experience within a legal team.
  • Superior communication, interpersonal, and client relationship management skills.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple complex cases concurrently.
  • Commitment to ethical legal practice and regulatory compliance.

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Premium Auditor, Accounting / Finance, Internal Auditor
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: East Syracuse, NY

About this job

Examine policyholders' accounting and financial records to ensure accurate premium calculation and insurance compliance. Work from home with travel to policyholder locations to audit smaller, less complex risks.

Good fit if you have experience reviewing financial records and can travel to client locations regularly.

Full job description


Description

Our professional auditors are integral to our company's mission by ensuring the financial integrity of premium development. In this role, you will examine policyholders' operations and financial records to ensure exposures (such as payroll, sales, fixed assets) are accurately calculated within strict insurance guidelines and communicate audit findings through detailed formal reports. As a Premium Auditor, you will work out of your home, when not traveling to policyholders' locations.

Responsibilities:

  • Perform examination of policyholders' accounting and financial records to ensure accurate calculation of earned premium for smaller, less complex risks.
  • Ensure that audited exposures (payroll, sales, fixed assets, etc.) are accurately calculated within strict insurance guidelines.
  • Communicate audit findings through detailed formal reports supported by audit workpapers.
Qualifications
  • Review appropriate audit documentation and/or company policy systems, to determine auditable exposures and coverages provided by the policy and plan audit strategy.
  • Investigate policyholder operations to obtain actual exposures, verify classifications as they apply to the policy and ensure conformity to various state laws and insurance regulations for the appropriate audit period.
  • Prepare detailed work papers and written correspondence in support of audit findings.
  • Identify issues to be communicated and socialize the audit information to appropriate stakeholders (i.e., Central Processing, Distribution, Underwriting, Agent/Broker, etc.) to elaborate on current risk conditions or initiate necessary changes to the policy contract. Exhibit effective workload management skills through efficient time utilization. This includes scheduling audit appointments taking into account priority and location of assignments within assigned territory managing work-in-process and documenting progress for appropriate stakeholders/management.
  • Perform routine administrative tasks such as: Time Tracking, Expense Reports, Mileage Reports, etc.
  • As assigned, coordinate assignment of multi-location audits for large risks review location audits to ensure quality and accuracy. Consolidate in proper format for rating purposes. As requested, assist with complex audits, Special Investigative Unit (SIU) related accounts, and/or special projects, including mentoring, presentations, etc.

About this job

Senior Retirement Benefits Consultant at Liberty Mutual Insurance overseeing U.S. defined contribution and defined benefit plans, plus Puerto Rico and Canadian programs. Manages plan compliance, committee support, vendor relationships, and complex benefits projects across a large organization.

Good fit if you have 7-10 years of retirement plan experience, strong ERISA and IRS knowledge, and have managed large recordkeeping platforms and complex plan implementations.

Full job description


Description

Candidates who live within 50 miles of Boston, MA; Portsmouth, NH; Seattle, WA; Indianapolis, IN; Columbus, OH; or Plano, TX will follow a hybrid schedule, coming into the office two days per week. Otherwise, this role is remote.

Position Summary

Liberty Mutuals Total Rewards Benefits team is seeking a Sr. Retirement Consultant to provide operational oversight of the companys retirement programs, with primary responsibility for U.S. defined contribution and defined benefit plans and additional responsibility for Puerto Rico and Canadian retirement plans. This senior individual contributor partners with vendors and team members to plan, develop, and administer employee retirement and health and welfare programs, ensuring accurate, efficient, and compliant plan administration in accordance with plan provisions and regulatory requirements.

Reporting to the Director, Retirement Strategies, the Sr. Retirement Consultant serves as a retirement operations subject matter expert and supports preparation for Retirement Committee and Investment Committee meetings. The role partners closely with recordkeepers, actuaries, trustees, financial advisors, and other external partners, as well as Legal, Payroll, Finance, HR, IT, and Benefits, and leads complex benefits projects from planning through implementation.

Job Responsibilities

Plan Operations, Compliance & Controls

  • Lead operational oversight of the companys retirement plans, ensuring effective execution of recurring activities, compliance requirements, controls, deadlines, and annual deliverables.
  • Oversee retirement plan compliance and testing, including nondiscrimination and coverage testing, contribution and compensation limits, regulatory filings, and other annual requirements, partnering with recordkeepers, actuaries, Legal, Payroll, and consultants to ensure timely, accurate completion.
  • Ensure plans, programs, and processes comply with applicable governmental laws and regulations, including ERISA and IRS requirements, across a wide range of benefits disciplines.
  • Monitor legislative and regulatory developments, such as SECURE 2.0 and IRS and DOL guidance, and assess their impact on plan operations, administration, and participant communications.
  • Lead resolution of complex operational issues, participant claims, and plan corrections, including root-cause analysis, participant impact assessment, and corrective action.
  • Oversee retirement plan data integrity and operational controls, using data and analytics to identify exceptions, trends, and risks, and partner with Payroll, IT, and vendors on interfaces, file feeds, reconciliations, testing, and data validation.

Governance & Committee Support

  • Support and assist in preparing for Retirement Committee and Investment Committee meetings, including materials, plan reporting, data, analysis, and operational updates, and track follow-through on committee actions.
  • Partner with Legal to maintain plan documents, amendments, summary plan descriptions, and required participant notices, ensuring plan operations align with plan terms.
  • Support retirement plan audits, regulatory filings, and governance activities, providing plan reporting, data, analysis, and operational expertise to the Director and other stakeholders.

Vendor Management & Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Serve as the primary operational relationship manager for retirement recordkeepers, actuaries, trustees/custodians, and other key vendors, setting clear service expectations, monitoring performance and deliverables, and holding partners accountable for timely, accurate execution.
  • Partner with vendors and team members to plan, develop, and administer employee health and welfare and retirement programs.
  • Serve as a senior retirement subject matter expert and trusted advisor to the Director, independently managing multiple complex priorities and collaborating across the Benefits team, Legal, Payroll, Finance, IT, and HR to deliver timely, compliant results.

Plan Design, Projects & Continuous Improvement

  • Evaluate benefits offerings and recommend enhancements that align with enterprise goals, providing operational expertise on retirement strategy, plan design changes, and program enhancements, including operational impacts and vendor capabilities.
  • Lead the planning and implementation of complex benefits projects and initiatives, including plan changes, regulatory requirements, vendor transitions, and system enhancements, by defining requirements, coordinating testing, and ensuring successful delivery.
  • Support defined benefit plan initiatives, including actuarial valuations, funding and benefit calculation reviews, and pension risk transfer or annuity purchase projects.
  • Lead stakeholder meetings and develop change management communications that explain complex retirement and benefits changes to different audiences.
  • Identify and lead continuous improvement opportunities that strengthen processes, procedures, controls, automation, vendor performance, and overall program delivery.
Qualifications

Preparation, Training & Experience

  • 7 10 years of progressive retirement plan experience, including support for large or complex employer-sponsored retirement programs.
  • Strong knowledge of defined contribution and defined benefit plans, including operations, regulatory requirements, compliance testing, annual processes, and operational corrections.
  • Strong working knowledge of ERISA, IRS requirements, and qualified retirement plan regulations, with experience identifying and resolving operational and compliance issues.
  • Demonstrated experience with large retirement recordkeeping platforms, actuaries, and other retirement vendors, including managing vendor performance and driving issues to resolution.
  • Experience supporting plan design changes, implementations, system enhancements, vendor transitions, and complex retirement projects, with strong cross-functional partnership across Legal, Payroll, and IT.
  • Experience preparing materials for, or supporting, Retirement and Investment Committees, with an understanding of fiduciary responsibilities and plan governance.
  • Strong analytical and data skills, including advanced Microsoft Excel capabilities and experience analyzing retirement plan data, reconciliations, exceptions, and operational controls.
  • Strong project management, problem-solving, and communication skills, including leading stakeholder meetings and developing change management communications, with the ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and explain complex retirement issues to different audiences.
  • Working knowledge of health and welfare benefit programs and how they integrate with retirement programs.
  • Familiarity with financial well-being programs, participant education, and retirement readiness metrics.
  • Familiarity with Puerto Rico and Canadian retirement plan requirements is a plus.
  • Retirement or benefits professional designations, such as CEBS, QKA, QPA, or ERPA, are a plus.
  • Bachelors degree or equivalent relevant experience required.
