Job.JobTitle: Business Insurance Underwriting Professional Development Program (BI UPDP) Internship
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $25.00 to $26.00 an hour
  • Schedule: Internship
  • Location: Hartford, CT
  • Education: Bachelor's degree

About this job

Ten-week summer internship in business insurance underwriting at Travelers in Hartford, Connecticut. Program includes core training, project work, exposure to AI tools, and networking events, with potential pathway to full-time underwriting professional development program.

Good fit if you are pursuing a bachelor's degree in business, finance, economics, risk management, insurance, or related field and are interested in commercial insurance underwriting.

Full job description

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The hourly salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual hourly rate for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards. 

Salary Range

$25.00 - $26.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

Applications for this posting will be reviewed on a rolling basis beginning in October. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. now and in the future. The company does not sponsor/support H-1B petitions, TN, or Forms I-983/STEM OPT, for this role. Applications for this posting will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Are you curious by nature? Do you enjoy managing relationships and employing your critical thinking skills? Underwriters perform the critical function of evaluating the acceptability of risk and determining appropriate pricing for insurance products. The Business Insurance (BI) Underwriting Professional Development Internship Program provides students with an amazing opportunity to gain exposure to this critical function at Travelers. The 10-week program (running from early June to mid-August) provides qualified interns with an excellent opportunity to gain first-hand commercial insurance underwriting experience, receive valuable on-the-job training, and learn more about the property and casualty insurance industry from industry professionals. Given that, we are seeking interns that are serious about entering the insurance industry and who are excited about the prospect of making underwriting their future career choice. This role is a potential pathway to our full-time Underwriting Professional Development Program (UPDP). Housing assistance is not provided.

What Will You Do?

  • Within your assigned business unit, each intern will be given a designated coach and be expected to:
  • Complete core assignments and training modules geared toward insurance and underwriting principles.
  • Participate and complete self-paced professional development courses in time management, presentation skills, and other key areas.
  • Complete challenging and meaningful project work over the course of this program at the discretion of your manager. You may work independently or with other interns and will be asked to present your findings to local leadership. Sample projects include a territorial risk assessment to determine profitability and underwriting opportunities as well as a business process analysis to determine underwriting gaps.
  • Learn to leverage modern analytical and artificial intelligence (AI) tools/platforms with the ability to apply critical thinking to evaluate limitations related to quality and accuracy of AI-assisted outputs.
  • Learn about other areas at Travelers such as Risk Control, Claims, and related corporate functions. Interns may also engage in agency visits with Account Executives.
  • Participate in the Enterprise Internship experience which includes Executive Speaker Series, Networking events, and Rising Senior Intern Symposium.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Preferred cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above.
  • Obtained or pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Economics, Finance, Liberal Arts (with business focus preferred), Management, Marketing, Risk Management and Insurance.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office.

What is a Must Have?

  • Pursuing or obtained a Bachelor's degree.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

We are committed to providing accommodation to persons with disabilities. If you require accommodation during the recruitment or interview process we will work with you to accommodate your needs.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit http://careers.travelers.com/life-at-travelers/benefits/.

Job.JobDescription:
Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$136,100.00 - $224,500.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

The Sourcing and Supplier Management (S&SM) team drives enterprise-wide sourcing strategy, supplier governance, and supplier risk management across Travelers' technology and operations supplier portfolio. This multi-disciplinary team manages Travelers' global sourcing and supplier relationships, and is accountable for implementing strategic sourcing models that optimize supplier relationships and deliver measurable business outcomes.

This Senior Director leads S&SM's Sourcing Risk & Operations function, managing a team responsible for supplier risk reviews, business continuity and disaster recovery (BC/DR) planning, offshore development center (ODC) management, site audits, and various other supplier operations and governance functions. The Risk & Operations team is shifting from a reactive, process-facilitation model to a proactive, portfolio-based approach to supplier risk management - this role is accountable for leading that transition and for building the frameworks, cadence, and team capability needed to deliver a holistic, enterprise view and approach to risk management for these suppliers.

Additionally, this role will play a key role in expanding Sourcing and Supplier Management's strategic partnership role with Tech & Ops platform and product partners, enhancing governance frameworks and relationship management protocols. Additionally, the role encompasses developing and maintaining executive briefing materials that provide leadership visibility into strategic vendor partnerships and performance outcomes.

This senior director role is also a key member of the extended S&SM leadership team, which is responsible for developing and executing Tech & Ops sourcing strategies that align supplier selection, relationship management, and strategic sourcing models with enterprise objectives. The position partners closely with Line of Business Technology & Operations leadership and cross-functional stakeholders - including SLT/ELT, Procurement, Legal, and Workforce Management. Leveraging Travelers' scale and strategic positioning, this role partners with technology and business leaders on managed services models, sourcing strategies, and supplier selection aligned to workforce planning initiatives.

This position manages a team.

What Will You Do?

  • Supplier Risk Program Leadership & Proactive Risk Monitoring: Own end-to-end supplier risk management for the Tech&Ops strategic supplier portfolio - including risk reviews, due diligence, and ongoing monitoring. Lead the team's transition from reactive, case-by-case process facilitation to proactive, portfolio-based oversight that gives S&SM and Tech & Ops leadership a holistic, enterprise view of supplier risk exposure. Drive continuous improvement to how the work is completed, emphasizing value-add activities and approaches while reducing reactive, manual work wherever possible.
  • Portfolio Design and Management: Develop a portfolio-based approach to Tech&Ops strategic supplier population, including a framework for determining which suppliers are in-scope, how suppliers align to portfolios, what level of governance/operational support are required for each supplier, and how to align portfolios to team members. Lead the growth of the team's role in ongoing supplier governance - identifying opportunities to add value, deepen the team's knowledge of the supplier's footprint, and partner to help business stakeholders drive the most value from each supplier relationship. Leverage S&SM's mature professional services sourcing (GSO) program to drive the development of a strategic, substantive approach to Tech&Ops non-GSO strategic providers.
  • Executive Briefings: Lead the development, maintenance and continued improvement of briefing materials for senior executives within Tech&Ops, in partnership with stakeholders across the organization, ranging from the supplier's executive sponsor to leaders responsible for day-to-day operations with the supplier, to procurement, finance and legal. Ensure materials are comprehensive, provide a holistic view of the total supplier footprint, and include timely, actionable information; additionally, prepare distilled talking points as required to summarize key aspects of each supplier relationship to support senior executive meetings.
  • BC/DR and Incident Management: Manage business continuity and disaster recovery planning and readiness across S&SM's strategic suppliers, including partnering with BC/DR stakeholders to plan and facilitate annual tabletop testing, drafting/disseminating communications to strategic suppliers in connection with incident management/DR events, and identify opportunities to improve BC/DR preparedness.
  • ODC Management, Site Audits & Other Operational Controls: Oversee oversight of Travelers' offshore development center footprint, evaluating site changes - capacity shifts, technology updates, operational control changes - for risk and operational impact, and directing site audits toward the areas of greatest control exposure. Own SOC review outcomes for strategic professional services partners, assessing findings for substantive risk and driving suppliers to remediate gaps rather than simply tracking review completion.
  • Team Leadership: Lead and manage the Sourcing Risk & Operations team, setting direction, priorities, and performance expectations. Build team capability - through coaching, role clarity, and tooling - to support the shift to portfolio-based risk management.
  • Maintain substantive, current knowledge of strategic suppliers' delivery capabilities, fit within our priorities and roadmaps and competitive positioning.
  • Serve as a credible, technically substantive counterpart to supplier leadership and delivery teams - able to engage directly rather than operating solely through account managers or relationship cadence.
  • Partner cross-functionally with Procurement, Legal, Workforce Management, and Tech & Ops leadership to align supplier risk and governance frameworks to enterprise objectives.
  • Participate in the Enterprise Supplier Management Steering Committee and represent Risk & Operations in enterprise governance forums.
  • Define and consult on risk measurement strategies, scorecards, and reporting cadence across the organization.
  • Maintain awareness of supplier risk indicators and emerging industry/regulatory trends, surfacing anomalies and risks proactively to senior leadership rather than waiting for escalation.
  • Support ad hoc analytical requests and special projects aligned to S&SM's strategic priorities.
  • Serve as the point of resolution for supplier risk issues, audit findings, or governance gaps prior to leadership review.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Typically 9+ years of Finance, Audit, Procurement or Sales/Servicing related experience.
  • Master's or other advanced degree.
  • Thorough knowledge of project management processes.
  • Thorough knowledge of business law, legal contracts and various financial issues including cash flow and working capital.
  • Intermediate to advanced proficiency of eSourcing and Ariba procurement applications.
  • Intermediate to advanced proficiency of MS Access, Excel, PowerPoint and Word.

What is a Must Have?

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience.
  • 8 years of supplier management or related experience.
  • Advanced communication skills, advanced computer literacy and ability to analyze and resolve complex issues.
  • Ability to successfully operate in a team and in a fast-paced environment.
  • Requires a demonstrated record of initiative, problem solving, and change management.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences.

Manage the end-to-end salvage process for total loss vehicles at Travelers Insurance, coordinating with vendors and claim handlers to handle title work, maximize asset recovery, and ensure regulatory compliance.

Good fit if you have an associate's or bachelor's degree, one or more years of work or customer service experience, and strong attention to detail with organizational skills.

Full job description

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. What Is the Opportunity?

As an Auto Salvage Coordinator, you will play a critical role in managing the end-to-end salvage process, ensuring timely and compliant disposal of total loss vehicles while maximizing asset recovery value. In this role, you will collaborate closely with salvage vendors, appraisers, and claim handlers to coordinate title work, manage vendor expenses, and uphold state titling laws and regulations. Your attention to detail and organizational expertise will directly contribute to accurate claim file management and outstanding customer outcomes.

What Will You Do?

  • Prepare and process title documentation and required paperwork for timely submission to the appropriate salvage vendor.
  • Evaluate and determine the most appropriate disposal method for salvage assets in accordance with applicable state titling laws and regulations. Establish follow-up activities to ensure prompt and efficient sale of the asset.
  • Review and audit vendor invoices to ensure accurate and appropriate expense management. Proactively review invoices for billing discrepancies, and engage the salvage vendor, Appraiser or Claim Handler to assist in negotiation to achieve fair and reasonable outcomes.
  • Review credit and debit transactions posted to the claim file to ensure accuracy.
  • Verify proper execution of inbound titling documents, and appropriately process payments for customers. Resolve improperly executed title documents and proactively contact relevant parties to obtain missing or incomplete transferable ownership documentation, including keys, to successfully resolve the salvage.
  • Establish minimum bids utilizing the salvage vendor pricing system, entering accurate data to ensure reliable pricing results. Provide counter bids as appropriate and re-list vehicles in accordance with established office guidelines to maximize recovery value.
  • Review auto sale listings to verify accuracy of sale data including loss type, area of damage, vehicle year, make, model, and percentage of damages. Evaluate vehicle photos for image quality, OEM or aftermarket parts, missing equipment, inconsistencies with accident facts or auto appraisal, and odometer readings where applicable.
  • Perform sale price audits by monitoring internet auto auctions to validate sale prices against gross proceeds and ensure competitive asset returns.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date salvage capture screens throughout the claims process and document all claim file activity not captured within the system, ensuring current and precise data integrity at all times.
  • Manage left-with-owner (LWO) vehicle dispositions and resolve associated title issues in accordance with local office workflows and procedures.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Associate's Degree or Bachelor's Degree with 2 years of work and/or customer service related experience.
  • Basic understanding of insurance principles and terminology.
  • Ability to thrive in a high-volume, fast-paced environment while effectively analyzing situations, exercising sound judgement, and making effective decisions.

  • Proficiency in technology tools including Microsoft Word, Excel, email, web-enabled applications, and database software.

What Is the Opportunity?

Member of the Sourcing and Supplier Management team within Tech & Ops Finance responsible for enterprise-wide sourcing and supplier strategies, governance, performance management, risk and operational processes for Travelers' global sourcing and supplier relationships.

As a Manager, Sourcing Strategy, Management and Governance, you will play a critical role in executing work order processes across assigned business lines and area-specific strategic sourcing strategies, including sourcing model design, supplier selection, and alignment of suppliers to business needs across our professional services and outsourcing partner portfolio. You will serve as a key point of contact on execution of sourcing strategy, workforce demand, and supplier performance across assigned lines, partnering closely with business stakeholders to track activity, resolve issues, and identify opportunities to improve how the team operates. This position does not manage others.

What Will You Do?

  • Work Order/Vendor Management and Sourcing Strategy: Manage a defined set of supplier work orders or portfolio activities across multiple assigned lines, including intake, modifications, closures, data-driven analysis, and process and tool optimization. Serve as a proactive sourcing advisor to LOB stakeholders, providing counsel on sourcing model selection, supplier performance, and workforce demand planning. Apply enterprise sourcing models and rate card structures to work being requested, advising stakeholders on right model, right supplier, right rate.
  • Onboarding and Team Support: Oversee resource onboarding and monitor engaged resources for quality, progress, and team dynamics. Own resource onboarding end-to-end, including understanding the skills required for the work being engaged, validating skill requirements with LOB stakeholders, and driving Technical Assessments. Cultivate ongoing, trusted relationships with the owners of the work, including engagement managers and LOB stakeholders, staying close enough to the business to anticipate needs, flag risks early, and bring forward solutions before issues escalate. Partner with Circle Leads on resource and team alignment needs.
  • Proactivity and Risk Management: Monitor assigned vendor performance data and flag early indicators of risk or control gaps, addressing delivery issues as they arise and escalating when appropriate. Analyze work order data, supplier capability changes, and sourcing market conditions to identify business continuity risks, surface insights, and deliver proactive recommendations to leadership. Maintain deep understanding of assigned business lines to anticipate workforce needs, monitor internal demands, and inform sourcing strategy.
  • Internal and External Stakeholder Engagement: Build and sustain trusted relationships with business stakeholders, finance partners, and assigned supplier contacts to surface risks, resolve delivery concerns and budget variances, and support governance interactions, performance discussions, and sourcing process coordination. Provide data and updates supporting ELT visibility for assigned lines on execution of sourcing strategy, workforce demand, and supplier performance.
  • Work Transition and Migration: Own the operational execution of work transitions when sourcing decisions result in a change of supplier, sourcing model, or workforce composition. This includes coordinating the migration of work from internal resources to external suppliers, managing supplier transitions, supporting onboarding of new supplier teams, and ensuring continuity of delivery throughout the transition period. Partner closely with LOB stakeholders, DFRs, and the S&SM Strategy team to sequence and execute transitions in alignment with enterprise sourcing strategy and workforce plans.
  • Process Optimization: Identify and implement process improvements and automation opportunities, including AI-enabled workflow enhancements. Optimize like work across assigned lines, standardizing repeatable processes, eliminating redundancy, and driving consistency across the Sourcing Delivery and Execution team. Champion the use of Travelers' AI tooling to streamline reporting, automate recurring workflows, and improve the quality and speed of work.
  • Rate Card Adherence: Ensure compliance with established enterprise sourcing models and rate card structures. Partner with the S&SM Strategy team to validate that work being requested aligns to the appropriate rate card, role designation, and sourcing model, and assist stakeholders in understanding and adhering to rate card guidelines.
  • Track and report on sourcing footprint, role utilization, team composition, and premium role usage across assigned lines.
  • Manage sourcing activity across multiple assigned lines or areas. Bring cross-line perspective to sourcing decisions, identify patterns and efficiencies across the portfolio, and ensure consistent application of enterprise sourcing strategy regardless of line-specific variation.
  • Monitor work order alignment to budget; proactively flag variances and partner with DFRs to resolve.
  • Contribute to the preparation of Business Review materials and Monthly Operating Review (MOR) data for assigned lines, supporting leadership visibility into supplier performance, workforce trends, and sourcing activity across the portfolio.
  • Partner cross-functionally with LOB stakeholders, DFRs, and Procurement to support sourcing and contracting activity, ensure alignment on budget and resource plans, and facilitate resolution of issues that span organizational boundaries.
  • Engage with and learn Travelers' AI tooling, applying these capabilities to improve the speed and quality of recurring work such as reporting, data analysis, and workflow management.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience required.   
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in sourcing, workforce strategy, supplier management, or a related field.
  • Experience with Fieldglass, ACS, and workforce planning tools strongly preferred.
  • Experience supporting or managing work transitions, supplier migrations, or sourcing model changes preferred.
  • Familiarity with rate card structures, role modernization concepts, and supplier performance principles.
  • Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships with senior LOB or technology leaders.
  • Experience identifying and implementing process improvements or automation opportunities.
  • Familiarity with AI-powered tools and large language models (e.g., Claude); demonstrated ability or willingness to integrate AI capabilities into day-to-day work processes preferred.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite, including Excel and PowerPoint.
  • Strong working knowledge of sourcing models: managed services, staff augmentation, GSO, POD/catalog models, and rate card structures.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage complex, ambiguous situations and drive to resolution with senior stakeholders.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to evaluate sourcing data, identify trends, and translate findings into actionable recommendations for business partners.
  • Process improvement and automation orientation, with experience identifying and implementing operational efficiencies.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills, comfortable engaging with senior LOB leaders and building trusted advisor relationships.
  • Demonstrated initiative in identifying and adopting tools, technology, and process improvements that increase team efficiency and output quality, including AI-enabled solutions.
  • Demonstrated proficiency or willingness to actively develop proficiency with AI-powered tools, including large language models such as Claude; ability to apply these tools to sourcing workflows, reporting, and operational tasks to improve efficiency and output quality.
  • Ability to operate effectively through change and ambiguity, adapting approaches as the function evolves.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to present information clearly to stakeholders at all levels.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and in a team environment.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities, multiple workstreams, and deadlines simultaneously in a fast-moving environment.

What is a Must Have?

  • Three years of experience Supplier Management, Finance, Audit, Procurement, or a related field.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

About this job

Lead operational execution and continuous improvement of Lincoln Financial's enterprise AI Governance program. Manage governance processes, coordinate cross-functional activities, oversee reporting and forums, and translate strategic objectives into scalable operating practices.

Good fit if you have 5+ years in governance, risk management, compliance, or program management, with strong executive communication and data-driven decision skills.

Full job description

Alternate Locations: Radnor, PA (Pennsylvania); Charlotte, NC (North Carolina); Fort Wayne, IN (Indiana); Greensboro, NC (North Carolina)

Work Arrangement:

Hybrid : Employee will work 3 days a week in a Lincoln office

Relocation assistance: is not available for this opportunity.

Requisition #: 76737

The Role at a Glance

This position leads the operational execution and continuous improvement of the enterprise AI Governance program. The role manages governance processes, coordinates cross-functional activities, oversees program reporting and governance forums, and helps ensure effective execution of governance priorities across the organization. This position translates strategic objectives into scalable operating practices, drives transparency through metrics and reporting, and improves governance effectiveness through process optimization and stakeholder engagement.

What you'll be doing

  • Leads the development, maintenance, and execution of the AI Governance operating roadmap, translating strategic priorities into actionable plans, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
  • Oversees the end-to-end AI Governance review lifecycle, including intake, tiering, prioritization, review coordination, issue tracking, escalation management, and stakeholder communications to support timely and effective governance execution.
  • Serves as the primary coordination point between AI Governance and adjacent functions to promote alignment and reduce duplication of effort.
  • Translates complex technical, operational, and regulatory AI risk concepts into clear, actionable communications for business, technology, and risk stakeholders.
  • Establishes and tracks key performance indicators, operational metrics, and program health measures to evaluate governance effectiveness, identify trends, and inform priorities and decisions. Identifies operational bottlenecks, workflow inefficiencies, and governance process gaps, and leads improvements that increase throughput, scalability, stakeholder experience, and program maturity.
  • Owns AI Governance operating model, both internal stand-ups and regular cross-functional sessions, to surface blockers and align on next steps.
  • Synthesizes governance activities, program performance, emerging risks, and key decisions into executive- and board-ready reports, dashboards, presentations, and updates.
  • Establishes and maintains governance records, action plans, decision logs, and audit-ready documentation practices that support transparency, regulatory readiness, institutional knowledge, and operational continuity. Supports governance portfolio planning, resource forecasting, capacity management, and prioritization to balance reviews, projects, and ad hoc requests against available resources.
  • Partners with AIDA leadership to implement strategic initiatives, monitor progress against objectives, and drive execution of enterprise governance priorities.
  • Leads cross-functional efforts to enhance the governance operating model, strengthen stakeholder engagement, and promote consistent adoption of governance processes throughout the AI lifecycle.

What we're looking for

Must Haves:

  • 4 Year/Bachelor's degree (or equivalent)
  • 5+ years of experience in governance, risk management, compliance, audit, program management, AI governance, or a related discipline

Full job description

The Role at a Glance

The position is for a Lead Identity Infrastructure Engineer with experience designing, managing, securing, monitoring and supporting enterprise identity infrastructure, with primary emphasis on Active Directory, Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), Entra ID Application Registrations and related Domain Services technologies.

Responsibilities of this role include Active Directory architecture and lifecycle management; forest, domain and trust management; Certificate Services and Keyfactor integrations; operational monitoring and alerting; resilience, recovery and security hardening; and expert recommendations and guidance for Microsoft Entra ID application registrations and authentication strategies.

This role partners with Security, Enterprise Architecture, infrastructure teams and application owners to deliver compliant authentication and directory solutions. The role also supports, automation, high severity incident resolution, modern authentication patterns such as SAML and OAuth, and secure support for legacy authentication where required.

What you'll be doing

  • Serve as a technical expert for the architecture, engineering, administration and operational health of enterprise Active Directory and Domain Services.
  • Provide subject matter expertise and strategy recommendations for projects involving Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID application registrations, covering both legacy and modern authentication methods.
  • Demonstrate deep technical expertise in Public Key Infrastructure, including Keyfactor PKIaaS, certificate templates, enrollment services, certificate lifecycle processes and Keyfactor integrations.
  • Bring an AI agentic mindset to automation, continuous improvement and modernization opportunities that enhance the Domain Services service portfolio.
  • Design, manage and secure Active Directory forests, domains, trusts, sites and services, replication, DNS dependencies and domain controller lifecycle activities.
  • Build and improve monitoring, alerting, health checks and operational dashboards for Active Directory, authentication services and PKI using tools such as Splunk and enterprise monitoring platforms.
  • Contribute to Active Directory security hardening, identity threat detection and response, privileged access controls, disaster recovery planning and recovery exercises.
  • Lead troubleshooting and incident resolution for complex, high severity Active Directory, EntraID authentication and PKI incidents, including root cause analysis and corrective actions.
  • Working knowledge of PowerShell Desired State Configuration (DSC) and GitLab for infrastructure configuration, source control, and automation.
  • Work closely with Security and Enterprise Architecture to design enterprise compliant, resilient and supportable identity solutions.
  • Develop and implement PowerShell based automation to improve security, consistency, monitoring and operational efficiency.
  • Partner and guide cross functional teams, application owners and Managed Service Providers to integrate and support authentication and directory services.
  • Provide advanced support for Microsoft Entra application registrations, enterprise applications, OAuth, OpenID Connect and SAML integrations as needed.
  • Create and maintain architecture, operational and recovery documentation and share knowledge with the team.
  • Build\Present engineered solutions to Architecture and Peer Review Boards.

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years of experience managing and supporting enterprise identity services, with deep hands-on experience in Active Directory, PKI, and Entra ID Application Registrations.
  • Advanced knowledge of Active Directory architecture, including forests, domains, trusts, organizational units, replication, sites and services, DNS dependencies and Group Policy.

About this job

Lead research and due diligence for investment options across Lincoln's variable life, annuity, and retirement products, with focus on fixed income and international equity strategies. Role involves fund evaluation, manager oversight, and analytical support for internal stakeholders and investment committees.

Good fit if you have 5+ years of manager/fund research experience, expertise with tools like Morningstar Direct, and strong Excel and PowerPoint skills.

The Role at a Glance

This role will provide research & due diligence across Lincoln's manager-of-managers platform, with an emphasis on fixed income and international equity strategies. They will provide investment expertise and insight regarding the selection, oversight and placement of asset management solutions across Lincoln's product lines.

What you'll be doing

•Functions as a key resource in the selection and oversight of new and existing investment options offered in Lincoln variable life, variable annuity and retirement products.
•Oversees the screening and ongoing evaluation process for new and existing investment options.
•Presents research findings and performance results to internal stakeholders and potentially a broader group of constituents, such as the LVIP Board of Trustees.
•Collaborates with portfolio management teams to provide insight/analysis on the optimal use of multi-asset class investment options within broadly diversified portfolios.
•Conducts regular on-site due diligence visits with investment managers, usually alongside Portfolio Managers, in the selection and ongoing evaluation process to ensure that funds are managed in accordance with the stated investment policies.
•Recommends changes and/or actions, as appropriate, to further the objectives of investment committee(s) and Lincoln's product lines.
•Provides competitive intelligence, including performing complex analysis and comparisons on an ongoing basis.
•Provides investment research subject matter expertise to various thought leadership research projects.
•Supports relationships with external consultants, asset allocation providers and research firms (e.g. Morningstar, eVestment, etc.).
•Provides consultative services to support sales efforts and training for investment products through regular interaction with sales teams, investment teams, and other internal clients.
•Leads the day-to-day usage of the core analytical tools, both internal and external (e.g. Morningstar), that are used by the Research and Portfolio Management teams.
•Designs and maintains analytics, risk reports, attribution, stress testing, etc. for managed funds in partnership with key internal stakeholders.
•Works closely with portfolio managers, external managers and analytic teams to understand investment portfolios, exposures and risks.
•Key contributor to risk management process across Lincoln's investment business including analyzing fund attribution & fund exposures, derivative exposures & risk, and potential impacts to the variable annuity hedge program, product pricing impacts.
•Contributes to the risk management process, including fund attribution and factor exposures, derivatives exposures and risks, and the potential impacts to Lincoln's variable annuity hedge program.
•Participates in the relationship management of external asset/investment managers, including optimally leveraging their investment expertise, intellectual capital & best ideas while understanding Lincoln's overall mission & the feasibility of strategies

What we're looking for

Must haves:


•4 Year/Bachelor's degree (or equivalent) (Minimum Required).
•5+ Years of experience in manager/fund research & analysis in fixed income, global/international equities, or US equities.
•Experience in mutual funds.
•Demonstrated expertise in fund industry research and analytical tools (Morningstar Direct, eVestment, or other similar tools).
•Expertise in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint with ability to illustrate complicated information succinctly in slides and charts for the benefit of senior management.
•Demonstrated strength in written and oral communication. Ability to communicate investment concepts to a variety of audiences.
•Strong analytical and critical thinking skills.
•Demonstrates excellent organizational skills with the ability to prioritize workload and multi-task while maintaining strict attention to detail.
•Demonstrate strong relationship management skills with internal and external stakeholders (e.g. senior management, peers, and business lines).

Nice-to-haves:

•CFA or Progress towards CFA or other professional designations, or willingness to pursue professional designations.
•Familiarity with portfolio construction, asset allocation, modern portfolio theory, risk management and hedging.
•Strong knowledge of capital markets and industry trends.
•Ability to solve problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists.
•A demonstrated track record of consistently meeting and/or exceeding performance expectations. Work hard and strive for excellence.
•Familiar with AI tools (Copilot / Claude).

The Role at a Glance

This position will assist in the design, implementation and maintenance of new and existing technology solutions for the life production valuation team. The ideal candidate will aid in developing data & analytics requirements for solutions to improve data warehousing, financial reporting, reserve analytics, and various automation efforts. They will also develop a detailed understanding of the various administration systems, modelling systems and reporting tools to help design a long-term solution for all valuation data needs. This position provides a broad range of experiences and responsibilities, allowing for growth.

What you'll be doing

•Gain in-depth knowledge of monthly, quarterly and annual valuation production duties for GAAP, Stat and Tax for all Life products, including business valued under PBR Stat requirements and LDTI GAAP accounting standards

•Maintain existing reporting processes as new requirements arise due to financial transactions, reinsurance deals or changes in regulatory requirements
•Review existing processes looking for improvements or corrections and evaluate efficient remediation.
•Demonstrate new capabilities for improvements with proof-of-concept builds
•Partner with stakeholders including valuation and modeling actuaries and developers including IT and consulting resources to implement more efficient/robust data solutions
•Help reduce manual deliverables by transitioning to more automated solutions
•Increase transparency, efficiency, and governance of processes by maintaining robust process and production documentation
•Upskill team members with emerging technology tools

What we're looking for

•FSA designation or ASA designation with additional years of actuarial experience.
•Undergraduate degree in Actuarial Science, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, Data Science or Data Analytics or other quantitative major
•5-7+ Years' experience that aligns with the specific responsibilities for this position.
•Ideal candidate has strong SQL Server skills.

Nice-to-haves:
•Demonstrates strong interpersonal skills with a collaborative style
•Curiosity and demonstrated capability to quickly learn new concepts
•Self-starter, Innovative, Problem Solver
•Experience with Dataiku, Tableau, SAS, Python, MSAccess, MSExcel, ALFA/Integrate

About this job

Negotiates purchase of complex equipment and strategic services, manages supplier relationships and cost optimization. Coaches junior buyers and leads special procurement projects requiring RFP process expertise.

Full job description

The Senior Buyer negotiates the purchase of complex equipment and strategic services within authorized limits, processes purchase requisitions and purchase orders using system software, looks for optimization, cost reduction, improved lead-times and product quality. The Senior Buyer coaches and mentors any Associate Buyer and Buyer. The Senior Buyer must have advanced knowledge of purchasing contract terms, RFP process, bid analysis and must be able to lead complex customer-focused special projects.

  • Purchase goods and services by utilizing the Procurement operation processes and technology across Assurant enterprise to meet the needs of the customers.
  • Review purchase requisitions for completeness and accuracy.
  • Develop, implement and follow established Procurement policies, procedures and organization structure.
  • Manage suppliers, internal costs, quality and delivery performance.
  • Drive continuous improvement on end-to-end aspects of the procurement process.
  • Maintain and promote sound relationships with suppliers and the business community.
  • Maintain positive relationships and communication with internal customers.
  • Demonstrate understanding of market trends and conditions for product changes.

  • 5 years buying and procurement related experience

Gemini Transportation Underwriters is a leading provider of excess liability insurance for companies in the transportation industry. We offer excess liability coverage for all types of vehicles and excess liability and railroad protection for freight and passenger railroads and public transit systems.

As part of W. R. Berkley Corporation, one of the nation's premiere commercial lines property casualty insurance providers, we combine the resources of a Fortune 500 company with the underwriting expertise and personalized service of a specialty carrier.

We are pleased to underwrite and issue policies on behalf of Gemini Insurance Company*, also a W.R. Berkley member company, which carries an A. M. Best Financial Strength Rating of A+ (Superior) and a Financial Size Category of XV.

Company URL: https://www.geminiunderwriters.com/

The company is an equal opportunity employee

Responsibilities

The Claims Specialist handles high-exposure transportation claims (trucking, public transit, rail) throughout the United States.

Key Functions/Duties of Position: Describe the overall job responsibilities (including any decision-making authority) for this position.

  • Determine whether Gemini has a present or potential future defense obligation or indemnity obligation on assigned claims and position claims accordingly.
  • Handle assigned claims for which Gemini has a present or potential future defense obligation or indemnity obligation
    • Actively monitor and evaluate handling of such claims by insureds within self-insured retentions or underlying carriers and gather all information, documentation and advice necessary to evaluate and manage the exposure to the insured and Gemini.
    • Participate in the defense of such claims with insureds or underlying carriers to the extent necessary to protect the interests of the insured and Gemini or assume control of the defense as may be required by policy language, law or circumstances.
    • Retain, lead and supervise monitoring counsel or defense counsel in representing the interests of the insured or Gemini or both.
    • Establish expense and loss reserves up to designated authority levels and recommend reserving above such levels to Claims Unit Manager, Senior Vice President of Claims and President of Gemini as needed.
    • Review, evaluate and, if necessary, respond in a reasonable and timely fashion to demands seeking payment of an insured's total applicable limits of liability, time-limited demands, offers of judgment, demands that Gemini settle a claim within its limits of liability and similar types of demands or offers.
    • Retain, lead and direct coverage counsel in providing advice and guidance to Gemini as needed.
    • Represent Gemini at settlement conferences, mediations and any court room or trial appearances as may be required.
    • Ensure that claims are being handled (by the insured, an underlying carrier or by Gemini) in a manner such that the insured and counsel retained to defend the insured are prepared and ready try a case to verdict if a reasonable negotiated resolution cannot be achieved.
    • Negotiation the settlement of claims on behalf of Gemini up to designated authority levels and request authority above such levels to Claims Unit Manager, Senior Vice President of Claims and President of Gemini as necessary.
  • Report on a regular basis to the Claims Unit Manager, Senior Vice President of Claims, Vice President of Underwriting, and President of Gemini due to nature of claims being handled.

  • Experience handling claims involving public transit systems (busses, subways, etc.) and railroads preferred.

  • Ability to assess priorities and manage deadlines effectively.

Farmers believes in a culture of collaboration, creativity, and innovation, which thrives when we have the ability to work flexibly in a virtual setting as well as the opportunity to be together in person. Our hybrid work environment combines the best of both worlds with at least three (3) days in office and up to two (2) days virtual for employees who live within fifty (50) miles of a Farmers corporate office. Applicants beyond fifty (50) miles may still be considered.

Job Summary

At Farmers, data powers better decisions. As a Sr. Associate Decision Scientist, you'll help transform complex business questions into actionable analytical solutions that shape strategy across our Direct & Strategic Partnerships organization.

In this role, you'll leverage advanced analytics, statistical modeling, and data visualization to uncover insights, identify opportunities, and influence critical business decisions. Working closely with business leaders and cross-functional partners, you'll apply tools such as Python, SQL, Excel, and Power BI to analyze large datasets, develop predictive models, and deliver recommendations that drive growth, improve customer outcomes, and optimize business performance.

Success in this role requires a blend of technical expertise, intellectual curiosity, and business acumen. The ideal candidate thrives in solving ambiguous problems, translating data into compelling stories, and turning analytical insights into measurable business impact.

Essential Tasks & Leadership Philosophy

  • Apply moderately advanced statistical, mathematical, and analytical techniques to solve medium-to-large-scale business problems impacting current and future business strategies.
  • Build descriptive and explanatory models or leverage outputs from predictive and machine learning models developed by others.
  • Analyze large and complex datasets to identify trends, patterns, risks, and business opportunities.
  • Utilize data visualization tools and advanced analytical methods, including: Distribution analysis, Correlation analysis, Outlier detection, Multivariate analysis, Time-series analysis, Machine learning techniques.
  • Conduct exploratory data analysis (EDA), test hypotheses, and validate findings with business stakeholders.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to understand business objectives and develop data-driven solutions.
  • Collect, integrate, and transform data from multiple sources into cohesive datasets for analysis.
  • Evaluate data quality and apply data governance and hygiene practices to ensure reliability and accuracy.
  • Perform quality-control checks, document processes, and collaborate with peers on data validation efforts.
  • Work closely with IT, Data Engineering, Data Science, and other technical teams to optimize data pipelines and resolve data quality issues.
  • Support the deployment, monitoring, and maintenance of predictive models within business workflows.
  • Translate complex analyses into clear, actionable insights and recommendations for business leaders.
  • Utilize effective storytelling and visualization techniques to make analytical findings accessible and impactful.
  • Stay current on emerging data science methodologies, technologies, and industry best practices.
  • Contribute to a culture of continuous learning and knowledge sharing.
  • Provide informal coaching or mentorship to less experienced team members as needed.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

First Year Success Factors

Within the first 12 months, a successful candidate can expect to have achieved the following:

  • Establish strong partnerships with business leaders and become a trusted advisor for data-driven decision-making across Direct & Strategic Partnerships.
  • Deliver actionable insights through advanced analytics, statistical modeling, and predictive techniques that solve complex business challenges and influence strategic outcomes.
  • Lead high-impact analytical projects from problem definition through implementation, driving measurable improvements in growth, customer experience, operational performance, and profitability.
  • Develop, validate, and deploy analytical models that identify key business drivers, improve forecasting capabilities, and support informed decision-making.
  • Leverage Python, SQL, Power BI, and other analytical tools to transform complex datasets into scalable analytical solutions and executive-ready insights.
  • Translate complex analytical findings into clear, actionable recommendations that influence leadership decisions and advance business objectives.

Education & Career Experience Requirements

Candidates would ideally reflect the following professional qualifications and experiences:

  • Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Business Analytics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative discipline. Equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
  • Three or more years of experience applying advanced analytics, statistical modeling, predictive analytics, or quantitative problem-solving to support business decision-making. Experience in insurance, financial services, or other data-driven industries is preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate complex or ambiguous business questions into analytical approaches, actionable insights, and measurable business outcomes.
  • Strong technical proficiency with Python, SQL, Excel, Power BI, and other analytical tools used for data exploration, statistical analysis, modeling, and visualization.
  • Experience developing, validating, and deploying analytical models, including forecasting, segmentation, driver analysis, optimization, predictive modeling, and performance measurement.
  • Solid foundation in statistical methods and analytical techniques, including hypothesis testing, regression analysis, experimental design, forecasting, and trend analysis.
  • Proven ability to communicate complex analytical findings to both technical and non-technical audiences, translating data into clear recommendations that influence business strategy and decision-making.

From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

A day in the life of a Represented Bodily Injury Adjuster Moderate, and what it takes to do the job!


As a Represented Bodily Injury Adjuster, your main focus will be investigating automobile accidents involving single or multiple vehicles, which result in property damage and/or bodily injury with attorney/litigation involved. You will have the convenience of working remotely from your home while efficiently handling your responsibilities. You will assess coverage, liability, and damages while providing exceptional customer service throughout your day. Customer and attorney communication will take place through different channels, including voice calls, email, and text messages. Through the utilization of innovative platforms and tools, you will engage in negotiation processes to reach fair and timely injury settlements with all parties involved.


***The ideal candidate will be able to handle a high-volume of pending cases and have experience with not only third-party casualty adjusting, but also first-party collision and third-party property damage claims.***


Candidates for this role must reside in the Eastern or Central Time Zones.


Claims experience in Ohio or Connecticut highly preferred


Qualifications

  • Prior represented third-party casualty claim handling experience is required
  • 2-5 years of moderate Bodily Injury claim handling experience is preferred
  • Proficient communication skills, especially over the phone, to establish rapport and assess claims accurately.
  • Ability to work independently and remotely, while managing time efficiently.
  • Proficient knowledge of insurance policies, coverage, and liability determination and state regulations.
  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills to evaluate and negotiate injury claims successfully.
  • Knowledge of innovative tools and platforms for effective claims evaluation.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite a plus


Youll wear a few hats to fill a few roles throughout your day that all require a level of experience:

  • The Customer Service Expert youll live into Allstates Claims Culture by caring, empowering, and restoring, and you will accomplish that by being compassionate, clear, and a committed partner in each casualty claim. You lead with empathy, always.
  • The Investigator youll confidently and independently investigate casualty claims by performing detailed reviews of damage and interpreting policies to determine coverage.
  • The Effective Communicator youll use phone, emails and sometimes even video chat with customers to help them through a fast, fair, and easy claims process. Youll also incorporate a specific approach to claim handling to offer the customer their preference of communication to efficiently discuss their claim needs and keep them updated on the claim progress.
  • The Negotiator You will evaluate and negotiate claims settlements with customers, vendors, third party carriers and claimants, in accordance with all legal and business standard methodologies. With negotiations, you will incorporate tactics in handling challenging and complex situations.
  • The Problem Solver youll utilize multiple tools to get the job done in a fast-paced environment, including estimate tools, job aids, and additional settlement platforms, all while using your sharp critical thinking skills.
  • The Recorder youll protect the company financially by executing policies along policy agreements, and you keep a clear record of your work in a claims system that you will be trained on. Youll accomplish this by ensuring timely and accurate documentation is completed as you work on each claim.

Notice of Licensing Requirement

  • As a condition of employment, your office/area may require you to obtain an adjuster and/or an appraiser license which includes passing an additional background check with the Department of Labor. If applicable, you will be required to secure license(s) within 60 days of hire.
  • If required, the Hiring Manager will work with you along with the Centralized Licensing team to ensure that you are properly licensed.

Sign On Bonus:

You may be eligible for a $1000 Licensing Sign on Bonus if you have the applicable active licenses needed for this role. This could include Home Resident Property & Casualty License, Designated Home State (DHS) Florida or Texas License, and/or applicable Appraiser License.*


**Candidates who have previously worked for and are seeking to be rehired at Allstate and its family of companies are not eligible for this sign-on bonus.


This position is not available to residents of California, Washington, Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico.


The first approximately 6-9 weeks of employment are dedicated to onboarding, licensing (if applicable), and role-specific training designed to prepare you for success in the role. Successful candidates must be able to attend required training sessions, actively participate in virtual learning activities, and successfully complete the training program.


Allstate Benefits

  • Being a part of Allstate means you receive a benefits package from Day 1 of employment. This includes time off, healthcare, retirement, and more. That is why as an Allstater, youll enjoy a Total Rewards package that includes:
  • Competitive pay with needed support for continuous development and career advancement.
  • Flexibility in scheduling and a time off policy that helps support your work/life balance.
  • Initial and ongoing training to get you proficient in your new role
  • Comprehensive benefits like a 401K/pension, education reimbursement, and programs to help you balance work with the rest of your life. Visit https://www.allstategoodlife.com to learn more.

Skills

Business Communications, Critical Thinking, Fraud Investigations, Information Collection, Time Management

Compensation

Compensation offered for this role is 56,000.00 - 92,000.00 annually and is based on experience and qualifications.

The candidate(s) offered this position will be required to submit to a background investigation.

Within established binding authority and company underwriting guidelines, analyze complex insurance submissions, recognize exposures, provide coverage alternatives, offer risk management suggestions, and adequately price insurance coverage on risks. Manage assigned underwriting book of business that involves highly complex accounts. Provide recommendations related to company underwriting guidelines, products, pricing strategies, and general directives. Achieve corporate goals by developing strategies to improve the book of business. Provide leadership and serve as an overall underwriting expert, providing input and consultation on unique situations and sharing underwriting knowledge and expertise through training programs and mentoring.

PRIMARY JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

* Within established binding authority and in compliance with filings, effectively write and retain business to meet corporate objectives.
* Using various sources of information, analyze, evaluate, make, and document decisions to achieve desired underwriting results on a highly complex assigned book of business. Recognize exposures to loss, identify coverage alternatives, develop risk management recommendations, and adequately price to an expected profitability level. Negotiate solutions, keeping the customer in mind. Decline/nonrenew business not meeting standards.
* Thoroughly understand the reinsurance function, calculations, and administration per company guidelines.
* Communicate with supervisor on issues exceeding binding authority and territory issues.
* Maintain an effective business relationship with and be a mentor to the sales force. Explain and help develop an understanding of coverages, forms, guidelines, and underwriting philosophies. Proactively research, gather, and disseminate information to help service customers and offer suggestions on options and alternative approaches to coverage, pricing, and risk management.
* Maintain underwriting expertise through an awareness of changes within the Underwriting Department, understanding CM Group, insurance industry coverages, policy forms, and operations specific to our niches. Professional knowledge development using external and internal opportunities.
* Maintain an advanced level of knowledge regarding insurance issues, products, trends in the market, and pricing principles. Maintain a program of self-development to strengthen underwriting knowledge and personal skills.
* Take a leadership role in achieving customer expectations through meeting department timeliness expectations, assisting in territories as needed, and positive interactions with all customers (including Sales, Technical Support, and other departments).
* Be a resource to the Underwriting Department through enhancing the knowledge of others, acting as a subject matter expert for the department and others in CM Group, assisting underwriting personnel with accounts above their binding authority or beyond their knowledge level, and assisting the department in special projects.
* Be a leader within the Underwriting Department through acting as role model, being engaged in changes, being energetic to recognize and resolve issues, assisting others to work in a team environment, assuming responsibility for decisions and actions, and developing trust within the department.

QUALIFICATIONS:

* Bachelor's degree is strongly preferred. Associate in Underwriting (AU) designation or successful completion of two Chartered Property Casualty Underwriter (CPCU) courses may be considered in lieu of a degree.
* Typically requires 10+ years of relevant experience, preferably with a property and casualty insurance company underwriting for nonprofit/human services entities.
* Ability and initiative to be self-directed.
* Recognize and be receptive to change opportunities to improve efficiency and effectiveness.
* Expertise of the underwriting functions, insurance coverages, and principles to handle highly complex insurance transactions, including reinsurance application and administration.
* Operate as a subject matter expert and leader for commercial underwriting.
* Demonstrated success in the ability to effectively identify and analyze exposures, recognize areas of concern, and develop appropriate solutions.
* Superior ability to make decisions outside parameter-based situations but within binding authority.
* Superior ability to explain decisions to others and negotiate appropriate solutions.
* Solid organizational skills.
* Work closely with management to provide leadership through knowledge, confidence, and integrity.
* Demonstrated desire and commitment to learn, accept new challenges, and strive for personal improvement/growth.
* Support others by sharing knowledge.
* Develop and maintain positive working relationships throughout the company. Work closely with management to achieve corporate objectives.
* Advanced ability to effectively communicate with others professionally, respectfully, and timely.
* Effectively use CM Group computer systems and stay current with changes.
* Ability to provide leadership in a team environment.
* Responsible, dedicated behavior to accomplish workload expectations and to assist others when necessary.
* Ability to travel as necessary and/or required.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

Professional office environment.

About this job

Hybrid role managing vendor relationships and procurement for Church Mutual Insurance. Responsibilities include vendor onboarding, contract evaluation, performance tracking, purchase order management, and serving as subject matter expert for procurement systems across assigned business units.

Good fit if you have at least three years of purchasing or vendor management experience and strong skills in procurement systems and Excel.

Full job description

This is a HYBRID position that requires in office days Tuesday-Thursday to be based at one of our office locations below:

  • Merrill, WI (preferred location)
  • Milwaukee, WI
  • Madison, WI

What you'll be doing:
Act as a liaison between the procurement department and business units for vendor management and purchasing responsibilities. Facilitate the vendor onboarding process, including the evaluation and approval workflow of vendor contracts. Track and evaluate vendor performance and compliance. Procure goods and services from vendors at the best possible price and level of service. Research alternative vendors and products. Serve as a subject matter expert for procurement owned systems and processes.

On any given day, you'll:

  • Facilitate the vendor onboarding process for assigned business units using the vendor management system.
  • Evaluate vendor contracts terms, make recommendations, and review for savings potential.
  • Facilitate the resolution of contract terms between the vendor, legal department, and the business unit.
  • Follow-up with vendors to ensure documentation is received to complete the vendor onboarding process.
  • Ensure vendor performance and compliance is evaluated in advance of contract renewal for assigned business units.
  • Initiate the purchase of goods and services from vendors.
  • Research alternative vendors, products, or services to drive organizational savings.
  • Facilitate the process of obtaining required documentation to initiate vendor payment. Review for goods or services delivered but not receipted in the procurement system.
  • Assist with creating and administering supplier request for proposals (RFPs).
  • Complete the reconciliation of corporate purchasing card transactions and Amazon account purchases and provide supporting documentation to Accounting, including general ledger coding for G/L upload. 
  • Support and administer procurement systems, including purchase order management, vendor onboarding, supplier data maintenance, reporting, and user support.
  • Assist employees with procurement processes, roles, and responsibilities.

Here's what we expect:

  • Minimum of three years' experience in purchasing or working with vendors is required.
  • Prior experience in the insurance industry is preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience supporting procurement technology, purchase order workflows, invoice matching, receiving processes, and supplier data management is preferred.
  • Experience utilizing procurement and purchase order systems is required; experience with Unit4 is preferred.
  • Bachelor's degree is required. Equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered in lieu of degree.
  • Effective interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to deal effectively with internal and external customers.
  • Ability to investigate and resolve issues.
  • Must be detail-oriented.
  • Ability to use good judgment and make appropriate decisions.
  • Ability to interact with multiple departments and employees at all levels of the organization.
  • Ability to work with limited supervision and meet necessary deadlines.
  • Strong Microsoft Word and Excel capabilities.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with frequent changes.
  • Ability to collaborate with all team members.
  • Ability to treat others with dignity and respect.
  • Ability to influence, negotiate, collaborate, and achieve consensus key stakeholders.
  • Ability to work effectively and cultivate strong relationships across all levels of the organization and with external parties.
  • Significant experience collaborating across organizational boundaries and building partnerships across various functions.
  • Ability to work independently and in a team environment and meet necessary deadlines.

About this job

Manages and resolves personal property insurance claims, including damage inventory assessment and policyholder communication. Role requires on-site inspections at least 50% of the time and coordination with vendors and adjusters.

Good fit if you have strong written and oral communication skills, customer service experience, and knowledge of homeowner insurance coverage or relevant retail experience.

Full job description


Description

Training is a critical component to your success and that success starts with reliable attendance. Attendance and active engagement during training is mandatory

  • Manages, investigates and resolves assigned Property Contents claims under limited supervision.
  • Compiles and values inventory of damaged/lost contents associated with property claims.
  • Provides policyholders with quality customer service.
  • May assist Claims Representatives with in-person inspection/policyholder contact where necessary.
  • Responsible for claims handling personal property losses to include large loss.
  • Works in concert with large loss adjuster for scheduling, inventorying, adjustment and relocation assistance.
  • Performs on-site inventory inspection and specific detail capture (50% minimum on-site) to provide to policyholder for pricing.
  • Develops expert list/websites for various product categories. Utilizes internet VIA/Insurer's World/vendors for pricing and/or validation. Documents the file accordingly.
  • Provides quality customer service. Provides insured with policy information to include coverage, limitations, replacement or ACV options.
  • Works with and may coordinate a number of vendor services such as contractors, emergency repair, cleaning services and various replacement services.
  • May assist on files handled by Claims Reps with in-person inspection/policyholder contact when needed.
  • Attends product seminars/shows to build personal property expertise.
  • May be called upon for catastrophe duty
Qualifications
  • Strong written and oral communications skills required.
  • Good interpersonal, analytical and negotiation skills required.
  • Customer service experience preferred.
  • Knowledge of coverages provided within various homeowner policies.
  • Experience in interior design, electronics, appliances, antique-collectibles, clothing and furniture retail preferred.
  • Bachelors degree or equivalent experience and 18-24 months of directly related experience.
  • Ability to obtain proper licensing as required.
