Description

This role will be based in our Boston, MA headquarters office working a hybrid schedule.

About the Team

The Corporate Strategy & Research (CS&R) group is an award-winning ~40-person enterprise strategy and internal strategy consulting team within Liberty Mutual Insurance, a Fortune 100 company with 40,000 employees operating in 28 countries and economies worldwide. The group serves as trusted strategic advisers to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team and drives transformational change by taking an enterprise-wide, customer-centric perspective.

Established in 1972, CS&R has an outstanding track record of developing future leaders and serving as a top talent feeder to the organization by creating an environment that fosters intellectual curiosity, professional development, and personal fulfillment. Alumni of the group include our current Chairman & CEO, Chief Insights & Solutions Officer, EVP & General Manager of Sales and Service, SVP & Head of BU Strategy, VP & Managing Director of Corporate Development, and Vice President of Product Strategy. This is a great opportunity for an energetic individual to join a vibrant, high performance and tight-knit team environment that will be front and center in driving change across the enterprise.

The Details

Were in search of intellectually curious, creative, driven individuals who have a strong desire to expand their management consulting toolkit as part of an energetic and high-impact team.

As a Senior Consultant, youll oversee a workstream within a tight-knit consulting team led by a Managing Director that will collectively advise Liberty Mutuals senior executives in making key strategic decisions. Projects are typically in the areas of strategy development, growth strategy, organizational design & operating model, innovation, or business transformation, and typically run for 2-5 months.

Youll develop key relationships with leaders and executives across the organization and communicate with senior leadership to influence and galvanize the organization into action.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Deciphering strategic issues faced by Liberty Mutual stakeholders, and determining how best to address them
  • Designing work plans for your workstream, and collecting data from various internal and external sources (e.g., executive interviews and workshops, customer surveys)
  • Crafting compelling storylines that clearly articulate findings, insights, and recommendations
  • Building and owning relationships with key client stakeholders
  • Directing team and client stakeholders towards consensus points and gaining buy-in
  • Communicating with senior leadership to influence and drive the organization to action
  • Supporting the development and coaching of Associate Consultants and Senior Associate Consultants
  • Contributing to CS&R initiatives such as recruiting, talent development, culture building and engagement, or alumni engagement

Your compensation will include:

    • Base salary plus an annual short term incentive bonus target: 17.5%
Qualifications

The group is looking for intellectually curious, creative, and driven individuals with an interest in developing the management consulting toolkit.

Candidates should, at minimum, possess the following:

  • MBA with a demonstrated record of success or equivalent business and analytical background
  • 3+ years of experience with a MBA or 5+ years of work experience with a Bachelors

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Loss Control Consultant, Risk Management / Loss Control
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: New York, NY

About this job

Senior Risk Engineer supporting Liberty Mutual's US Energy team across conventional and renewable power generation. You'll conduct on-site and desktop risk assessments for operating plants and construction projects, translating technical findings into underwriting decisions.

Good fit if you have a technical degree, five years in power generation or related industries, and experience in operations, maintenance, or loss prevention.

Full job description


Description

Risk Engineer, US Energy

Are you ready to sit at the intersection of engineering, insurance, and the energy transition? Join our US Energy team and help shape how we understand and underwrite Property risk across conventional power generation and the fast-growing renewable energy sector from operating plants to major construction projects.

We're looking for a technically sharp, commercially minded professional to bring deep risk engineering expertise to the table. You'll conduct on-site and desktop assessments, partner closely with Underwriting and Claims, and help turn complex technical exposures into clear, confident decisions. This is a role where your judgment directly shapes outcomes for our business and for the clients we protect.

What you'll do:

  • Conduct on-site risk engineering surveys and desktop reviews spanning conventional power and renewable energy risks
  • Evaluate operational plants and construction projects, including large and complex exposures
  • Translate technical findings into clear, actionable risk assessments that drive accurate, profitable underwriting decisions
  • Serve as a trusted technical resource for US Underwriters, Claims teams, and insureds
  • Analyze risk quality, pinpoint loss drivers, and recommend practical mitigation strategies
  • Support claims analysis and identify risk improvement opportunities across the portfolio

What you'll bring:

  • Experience in risk engineering, power generation, renewable energy, or a related technical discipline
  • Solid understanding of conventional power and/or renewable energy operations and construction risk
  • The ability to break down complex technical exposures and explain them clearly to business partners
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving instincts
  • A collaborative mindset and genuine enjoyment of working closely with underwriting and claims professionals

Why this role: This is your chance to work in one of the most dynamic corners of the insurance industry where traditional power meets the energy transition, and where your technical insight has real influence on underwriting strategy. You'll build expertise across a diverse and growing portfolio, work alongside experienced underwriting and claims professionals, and have genuine ownership over the accounts you manage.

Responsibilities:

  • Assess operational conventional and renewable power generation facilities, as well as construction projects
  • Plan, organize, and perform desk-based risk appraisals for assigned lines of business, delivering risk analysis to Underwriters
  • Prepare plant/process/product descriptions and assess design, hazards, mitigation adequacy, management systems, plant protection, and loss estimates
  • Conduct on-site risk engineering surveys for existing and prospective clients, producing internal summaries or detailed marketing survey reports per Liberty Mutual guidelines
  • Own allocated accounts attending surveys, following up on key recommendations, and keeping risk engineering files current
  • Provide technical input on claims, including reviewing loss adjuster reports and conducting site visits to identify claims mitigation opportunities,lessons learned, sharing insights with fellow Engineers and Underwriters to inform future loss prevention work
  • Maintain strong professional credibility through consistent technical expertise and sound judgment
  • Stay current on process technology, loss prevention, construction practices, and other developments relevant to your lines of business
  • Pursue ongoing professional development to deepen and broaden your expertise
  • Participate in business development and marketing activities for assigned lines of business
  • Travel regularly as part of the role
Qualifications
  • Bachelor of Science or Engineering degree in a technical discipline, such as Chemical, Process, Mechanical Engineering or equivalent.
  • The job holder will be expected to possess at least five years experience in relevant process industries and should have a background in at least one of the following areas in a managerial, technical or consultancy role; Operations, Operations Support, Maintenance, Inspection, Loss Prevention, or Process Safety
  • Previous Insurance experience is not a requirement of this role, but beneficial/desired
  • Demonstrated strong communication and listening skills in order to develop and maintain relationships with Underwriters, Risk Engineers, Claims teams, other Liberty Mutual Staff and Clients.
  • Demonstrated ability to effectively use required software applications, such as Microsoft Office Suite
  • Should be able to create/modify documents and complex spreadsheets

The details:

Do you love telling stories with data? Are you looking to jump into the broad world of analytics? Are you looking to jumpstart your career with a global Fortune 100 company?

Heres a fantastic opportunity to hone your strategic, technical, and analytical skills while learning the ins and outs of the fast-paced insurance industry.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Boston, MA
  • Experience: 10+ years

About this job

Director role leading energy and infrastructure equity investments at Liberty Mutual Investments, a $100B+ investment firm. Responsibilities include sourcing, executing, and managing complex transactions across power, utilities, digital infrastructure, and energy transition, with oversight of deal teams and junior staff.

Good fit if you have 10+ years in private equity infrastructure investments, a proven deal track record across sectors, and an extensive network in the infrastructure landscape.

Full job description


Description

The Company

Liberty Mutual Investments (LMI) is the investment firm for Liberty Mutual Group (Liberty). With deep expertise in fixed income, equity, and alternative strategies, LMI invests more than $100B of long-term capital globally, and has a team of nearly 300 investment, finance, and operations professionals located in Boston, MA, and New York, NY. LMI has a clear purpose: drive economic growth, build enduring businesses side-by-side with our partners, and generate superior risk-adjusted returns that secure Libertys promises.

LMI offers the best of both worlds the look and feel of a boutique investment firm with the reputation and financial strength of a global leader. As the investment firm of a mutual with long-term capital, LMI has a single client mandate. This gives us the freedom to focus on what we do best.

Our portfolio spans a broad spectrum of public and private investments, and we are committed to expanding our capabilities and our toolkit in support of our mission. We invest across diverse asset classes, financial structures, and industries, including real estate, digital infrastructure, healthcare, renewable energy, and technologywith the aim of creating value and powering innovation. We pride ourselves on our extensive network of mutually beneficial partnerships, and we use our substantial influence, capital, and energy to drive towards a better future. #LMI

The Position

The Energy & Infrastructure (E&I) strategy invests holistically across the infrastructure landscape including real asset, services, and technology opportunities spanning power, midstream, energy transition, digital, transportation, utilities, and products. The team's mandate is to deliver compelling, risk-adjusted returns with strong downside protection and significant upside potential. E&I leverages subject matter expertise, ability to underwrite complexity, speed to execute, and a peer-oriented go-to-market strategy to establish itself as a differentiated partner of choice. This hire will be a deal captain leading sourcing, execution and portfolio management across a variety of transaction types with responsibility as a senior member of the team to drive E&Is future growth and investment strategy.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead value-add infrastructure equity transactions with a focus on directs and co-investments as well as fund and platform opportunities
  • Lead all aspects of deal execution including sourcing, underwriting, due diligence, structuring, management of the investment committee process, legal documentation, and asset management
  • Manage multiples projects at a time
  • Work with external partners as well as LMIs legal, asset allocation, risk, and accounting & operations teams to develop customized investment opportunities and strategic partnerships
  • Engage with external counterparties and market participants to enhance E&Is presence in the space
  • Drive robust relative value discussions across the organization and seek to generate optimal risk-adjusted returns for the overall portfolio
  • Promote a culture of collaboration and be willing to work cross-functionally to add value across the organization
  • Pursue the development of technology, data, and analytics needed to support the role
  • Develop and train junior team members who are mostly based in Boston.
Qualifications

Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of experience in private equity infrastructure investments, including sourcing, structuring, execution, and management of complex transactions
  • Deep experience underwriting investments with an ability to identify risks, opportunities, and mitigation strategies
  • Proven investment track record with experience leading and overseeing a range of investments across sectors
  • Experience in managing deal teams and external constituents
  • Extensive network of investors, management teams, and advisors across the infrastructure landscape
  • Experience working from initial business plan review through execution
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to work collaboratively across teams and business units
  • Possess exceptional communication, presentation, and interpersonal skills
  • High-performing team player with a willingness to be flexible and take on additional responsibilities depending on the needs of the business
  • The expectation that the Director will be present in the office 3 days a week. Candidates must have a willingness and ability to travel as needed to support business demands if they are not Boston based.

At Liberty Mutual, our goal is to create a workplace where everyone feels valued, supported, and can thrive. We build an environment that welcomes a wide range of perspectives and experiences, with inclusion embedded in every aspect of our culture and reflected in everyday interactions. This comes to life through comprehensive benefits, workplace flexibility, professional development opportunities, and a host of opportunities provided through our Employee Resource Groups. Each employee plays a role in creating our inclusive culture, which supports every individual to do their best work. Together, we cultivate a community where everyone can make a meaningful impactforour business, our customers, and the communities we serve.

About this job

Full job description


Description

Comparion Insurance Agency is hiring self-motivated, relationship-driven professionals for a rewarding outside sales career. This role offers autonomy and flexibility to build your career, grow your earnings, and make a meaningful impact by helping protect individuals and families with auto, home, life, small commercial auto, and specialty insurance.

Backed by a Fortune 100 company, you'll receive hands-on training, resources, and team support to help you succeed. No prior insurance experience required.

THIS POSITION HAS IN-OFFICE REQUIREMENTS.

This is a full-time, field-based employee position. Applicants must be able to travel within their local community to meet with customers and build relationships. Reliable transportation, such as a valid driver's license or another means of travel, is preferred.

Licensing Requirement:
Candidates are welcome to apply even if you do not currently hold your Property & Casualty and Life insurance licenses; however, you must obtain both licenses before your scheduled start date. Whether you already hold your licenses or obtain them before your start date, youll receive a $1,000 professional start bonus to support your transition into your new role!

What you'll do:

  • Sell auto, home, life, small commercial auto, and related insurance products using a consultative, needs-based approach.
  • Build and maintain a book of business through referrals, networking, and community engagement as part of your outside sales efforts.
  • Identify prospective customers using established lead methodologies and relationship-driven outreach.
  • Accurately document customer interactions and handle sensitive information with integrity and confidentiality.
  • Use insurance sales technology, relationship management tools, and multi-carrier platforms to deliver tailored insurance solutions.
  • Participate in training, coaching, and performance incentives to continuously improve sales results.

Essential functions include: meeting with customers in the office and in the community, communicating by phone, email, and in person, traveling locally, and using a computer and sales software.

Qualifications

Day One Skills & Traits:

  • Self-motivated and accountable: you take ownership of your work and results.
  • Reliable and responsive: you follow through and do what you say you'll do.
  • Professional and trustworthy: you handle customer information with care and integrity.
  • Relationship-focused: you enjoy helping others and building long-term trust.
  • Strong communicator: you're comfortable talking with people and explaining options clearly.
  • Comfortable with technology: you can learn and use new software and digital tools with ease.
  • Composed and dependable: you stay organized and professional while managing multiple customer needs.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in customer-facing roles like retail, hospitality, service, operations, logistics, banking, account management, or sales.
  • Basic understanding of sales conversations, including handling common customer questions or objections.
  • Experience managing multiple accounts, clients, or priorities simultaneously.
  • Exposure to consultative selling, negotiation, or regulated industries.

Pay Philosophy: The typical starting salary range for this role is determined by a number of factors including skills, experience, education, certifications and location. The full salary range for this role reflects the competitive labor market value for all employees in these positions across the national market and provides an opportunity to progress as employees grow and develop within the role. Were Hiring Immediately!

  • Utilize consultative sales techniques to prospect and initiate new business sales.

  • Identifies mass marketing prospects through existing book of business and community prospecting opportunities.

  • Completes follow-ups on new policies in order to keep retention level high and capitalize cross-selling opportunities.

  • Acts as initial contact in addressing customer concerns regarding establishment of policies and new account status.

  • Resourceful team player that can contribute and accept new ideas

Description

Comparion Insurance Agency is hiring self-motivated, relationship-driven professionals for a rewarding outside sales career. This role offers autonomy and flexibility to build your career, grow your earnings, and make a meaningful impact by helping protect individuals and families with auto, home, life, small commercial auto, and specialty insurance.

Backed by a Fortune 100 company, you'll receive hands-on training, resources, and team support to help you succeed. No prior insurance experience required.

THIS POSITION HAS IN-OFFICE REQUIREMENTS.

This is a full-time, field-based employee position. Applicants must be able to travel within their local community to meet with customers and build relationships. Reliable transportation, such as a valid driver's license or another means of travel, is preferred.

What you'll do:

  • Sell auto, home, life, small commercial auto, and related insurance products using a consultative, needs-based approach.
  • Build and maintain a book of business through referrals, networking, and community engagement as part of your outside sales efforts.
  • Identify prospective customers using established lead methodologies and relationship-driven outreach.
  • Accurately document customer interactions and handle sensitive information with integrity and confidentiality.
  • Use insurance sales technology, relationship management tools, and multi-carrier platforms to deliver tailored insurance solutions.
  • Participate in training, coaching, and performance incentives to continuously improve sales results.

Essential functions include: meeting with customers in the office and in the community, communicating by phone, email, and in person, traveling locally, and using a computer and sales software.

Qualifications

Day One Skills & Traits:

  • Self-motivated and accountable: you take ownership of your work and results.
  • Reliable and responsive: you follow through and do what you say you'll do.
  • Professional and trustworthy: you handle customer information with care and integrity.
  • Relationship-focused: you enjoy helping others and building long-term trust.
  • Strong communicator: you're comfortable talking with people and explaining options clearly.
  • Comfortable with technology: you can learn and use new software and digital tools with ease.
  • Composed and dependable: you stay organized and professional while managing multiple customer needs.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in customer-facing roles like retail, hospitality, service, operations, logistics, banking, account management, or sales.
  • Basic understanding of sales conversations, including handling common customer questions or objections.
  • Experience managing multiple accounts, clients, or priorities simultaneously.
  • Exposure to consultative selling, negotiation, or regulated industries.

Licensing:

You will be required to obtain relevant licenses upon being hired (P&C and Life).

Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$157,500.00 - $259,900.00

Target Openings

1

What Is the Opportunity?

Travelers is seeking a Circle Lead Engineer (CLE) to join our organization as we grow and transform our Personal Insurance Technology landscape. Individual will complete expert end to end engineering tasks as well as manage and lead the development and work products of software engineers. Individual will also plan and execute at a strategic level, lead and influence resources and outcomes, lead the design, development and implementation of significantly complex, unscoped problems that extend beyond the confines of a team, and establish software engineering best practices and standards.

What Will You Do?

  • The CLE is accountable for the set of technical product solutions in the circle, ensuring they are well bounded and composable, all while growing and nurturing the circle's engineering team's skillsets. This includes:

  • Technical Guidance: Provide technical guidance and leadership to Team Lead Engineers though helping them understand how their team's technical solutions fit together to accelerate the Circle's mission.
  • Solution Architecture and Design: Collaborate with the Team Lead Engineers to define the solution architectures and design of the technical components to ensure boundaries are maintained. Partners with and defers to architecture when an architecturally significant change is needed for a design that spans teams.
  • Best Practices and Quality Assurance: Ensures teams are producing systems that meets all non-functional requirements, is well-bounded, composable, and adheres to Software Engineering best practices. Provides feedback to Team Lead Engineers to help them improve their system building skills.
  • Collaboration with Circle Leadership: Works closely with the Circle leaders to ensure the Circle's mission, vision, and objectives and KPIs are satisfied by the systems being maintained and built by the teams. Provides oversight to ensure capabilities are properly bounded.
  • Estimation and Planning: Participate in increment planning sessions to assist with and provide oversight over the estimation of the technical effort required for implementing features, user stories and tasks. Help the teams, where necessary, break down work into smaller, actionable tasks.
  • Technical Integrations: Own technical interdependencies of systems within the Circle and ensure an adequate interaction model across teams to support these.
  • Problem Solving: Help the Team Lead Engineers overcome technical challenges and roadblocks by offering expertise, brainstorming solutions, and providing support as needed.
  • Continuous Improvement: Foster a culture of continuous improvement within the Circle, encouraging experimentation, learning, and the adoption of new technologies and practices.
  • Lead by example, mentor, and coach: Lead by example, demonstrating professionalism, integrity, and a commitment to quality in all aspects of the work. Mentor Team Lead Engineers, helping them develop their technical skills and grow as engineers and leaders. Provide coaching on topics such as soft skills, coding practices, design patterns, and system architecture
  • Perform other responsibilities as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • 7+years in programming and software development.
  • Proven track record of empowering and guiding multiple teams simultaneously.
  • Tech Stack: Proficiency in Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, and React.
  • Cloud & Infrastructure: Expertise with AWS (specifically CDK), Terraform, and Jenkins.
  • Modern Tools: Strong background in API Development, GitHub, and integrating AI/GenAI solutions.
  • Delivery: Advanced delivery skills including the ability to examine and assess the effectiveness of software design strategies and methodologies across an organization, the ability to devise, apply, and share ways to ensure the quality, production readiness, and continued health of complex computer systems, the ability to incorporate awareness and understanding of work happening outside of the team, and the ability to develop widely used technical metrics that enable engineers to better understand and deliver their work.
  • Domain Expertise: Demonstrated track record of domain expertise including the ability to leverage expertise to improve company level capabilities within domain, consult on business priorities and optimize value by identifying business aligned solutions and thoughtfully and practically introduce concepts and technologies from the industry.
  • Problem Solving: Strong problem solver who creates architecture that is particularly robust against single points of failure, both in terms of systems and people and looks ahead 6-12 months to identify areas of need and turns this into action.
  • Communication: Strong communicator who possesses the ability to describe technology concepts in ways the business can understand, document effectively so that systems/architectures can be maintained or built upon, collaborate across disparate groups, helping to identify common goals and gain consensus, adapt language to meet the needs of various levels of technical and non-technical audiences and model and assist others in the practice of mindful communication, active listening, and messaging.
  • Leadership:2+ years of technical leadership experience. Advanced leadership skills including the ability to leverage internal networks across engineering and engage with other leaders to solve problems and develop strong credibility throughout the company as well as choose the most critical engineering challenges and work to improve the entire engineering organization by teaching others and sharing knowledge while creating opportunities for others to showcase and develop skills.

What is a Must Have?

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, related STEM field, or its equivalent in education and/or work experience.
  • 7 additional years of software engineering experience.
  • 2 years of technical leadership experience.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

The Account Executive Officer (AEO), Commercial Accounts will partner with agents and brokers to provide property, general liability, commercial auto, and/or workers' compensation coverage for new and renewal business based on customers' needs. This role is seen as a technical resource. As an AEO, you are decisive, detail-oriented, and know how to build relationships internally and externally to drive results. Your ability to independently assess complex risk and sell our products in challenging markets will contribute to the profitability and success of Travelers.

What Will You Do?

  • Manage the profitability, growth, and retention of an assigned book of business.
  • Underwrite and skillfully negotiate complex customer accounts to minimize risk and maximize profitability.
  • Cultivate and maintain relationships with internal partners within the business unit and across the enterprise to create sales plans and identify cross-selling opportunities.
  • Foster and maintain relationships with external partners by regularly meeting in person with agents and brokers to market and sell Travelers products with a goal of writing and retaining accounts consistent with our risk appetite. Must be able to travel to such meetings.
  • Identify and capture new business opportunities using consultative marketing and sales skills.
  • Independently develop and execute agency sales plans and frequently partner with your Managing Director (MD) to develop region/group sales plans.

  • Excellent communication skills with the ability to successfully negotiate in difficult situations with agents and brokers.
  • CPCU designation.

What is a Must Have?

What Is the Opportunity?

This position services Insureds/Agents in and around Prescott, AZ. The selected candidate must reside in or be willing to relocate at their own expense to the assigned territory.

As an Associate Claim Rep, Outside Property, you will receive comprehensive training in claim handling, customer service, and policy interpretation while working alongside experienced claim professionals. This position focuses on developing your skills and knowledge to successfully manage 1st party property claims.

This program is typically 9-12 months and upon successful completion of this program you will have the skills needed to handle claims independently and progress toward full claims handling responsibility.

This position is based remotely with work at residential and commercial locations with a combination of mobile work, work from your primary residence, or the nearest Travelers office.

What Will You Do?

  • Actively participate in structured training classes covering insurance policies, specific claim processes, systems, and procedures, including virtual, classroom, and on-the-job training.
  • Review, investigate, and document 1st party property claims under direct supervision.
  • Gather information from policyholders, claimants, witnesses, and third-party providers.
  • Learn to investigate and evaluate all relevant facts and information (including but not limited to analyzing leases, contracts, by-laws and other relevant documents which may have an impact). Determine and apply coverage for building damages per policy terms.
  • Establish accurate scope of damages for building and contents losses and utilizes as a basis for written estimates and/or computer assisted estimates.
  • Provide timely and professional communication to customers, claimants, and internal stakeholders.
  • Maintain accurate records of claim activity in claim management systems.
  • Demonstrate openness to continuous learning, particularly in AI and digital transformation.
  • Adapt to new technology implementations, system upgrades, and digital tool rollouts while maintaining productivity and service quality.
  • Acquire and maintain relevant Insurance License(s) and/or a UAS Remote Pilot Certification to comply with federal, state, and Travelers requirements within three months of starting the job.
  • Assess and inspect all areas of a dwelling or structure, including roofs, attics, crawl spaces, and other confined areas. Ability to carry, set up, and climb ladders weighing approximately 38-49 pounds.
  • May require extensive travel, including overnight stays, to support customers across multiple locations.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's Degree.
  • Previous internship or work experience in customer service or insurance.
  • Willingness to obtain an active adjuster license where required by state law.

  • Ability to exercise sound judgement and make effective decisions within established authority.
  • Exceptional customer service skills and commitment to providing a positive experience for insureds and claimants.
  • Attention to detail and organizational skills; ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritize effectively.
  • Basic conflict resolution skills; willingness to learn techniques for facilitating productive discussions and negotiations.

What is a Must Have?

What Is the Opportunity?

As a Sr Technical Specialist, General Liability, you will be responsible for managing and investigating complex and higher-severity injury and/or property damage claims including customer contact, determining coverage, evaluating liability, assessing damages, establishing timely reserves, and issue timely and accurate payments within appropriate authority and oversight. In this senior technical role, you will leverage advanced expertise in claims management, investigative techniques, coverage evaluation, and settlement negotiation to ensure timely and fair resolution. You will foster positive, professional relationships with customers and key stakeholders on matters involving significant litigation and extended resolution timelines. You will actively mentor and coach Claim Professionals, including providing higher-severity claims mentoring to enhance higher-level skill sets.

What Will You Do?

  • Independently manage an active caseload of injury and/or property damage claims and litigation from first notice of loss through resolution within level of authority. Typically, handles personal and/or business insurance high complexity liability claims with coverage disputes and contractual indemnity issues.
  • Gather and thoroughly investigate information by contacting all relevant parties to determine coverage, evaluate liability exposure, assess bodily injury and/or property damage which may include personal and advertising injury claims, and establish appropriate reserves in accordance with policy terms and management guidance.
  • Provide timely and professional communication to customers, representatives, opposing counsel, third-party vendors, and internal stakeholders.
  • Develop and execute advanced resolution strategies and coordinate internal and external resources to conduct comprehensive claim investigations and evaluations.
  • Partner with Counsel to develop, direct, and execute litigation management strategies.
  • Manage multi-party negotiations with key stakeholders to achieve optimal claim resolutions within delegated authority limits.
  • Maintain accurate records of claim activity in claim management systems.
  • Identify areas in which we can improve or enhance current best practices and offer creative solutions.
  • Adapt to new technology implementations, system upgrades, and digital tool rollouts, particularly in the areas of AI while maintaining productivity and service quality.
  • Acquire and maintain relevant Insurance License(s) to comply with state and Travelers' requirements within three months of starting the job.
  • May require travel, including overnight stays, to attend mediations, trials, arbitration, etc.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's Degree.
  • Four years of bodily injury claim and litigation experience.
  • Active adjuster license, where required by state law.
  • Experience with claims management systems, with advanced skills in Microsoft Office and enterprise technology systems and platforms.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to comprehend, synthesize, and clearly articulate complex information to multiple stakeholders.
  • Ability to analyze complex situations, exercise sound judgement, and make effective decisions independently.
  • Exceptional customer service skills; ability to proactively manage customer expectations, resolve escalated issues, and maintain trust throughout complex claims.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills with the ability to manage a high-volume workload and prioritize effectively.
  • Advanced conflict resolution and negotiation skills; ability to manage disputed high-value claims, negotiate settlements, and coordinate with legal counsel.
  • Ability to manage stress, navigate difficult situations, and maintain composure and professionalism under pressure while always taking accountability for decisions.
  • Strong understanding of insurance principles and terminology, state and federal insurance regulations, fair claims practices legislation, and legal requirements.
  • Demonstrated ability to interpret, apply, and clearly articulate complex policy language, endorsements, exclusions to assess coverage and claim eligibility.
  • Ability to quickly learn from experience and apply it to new situations with speed and flexibility.

What is a Must Have?

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • Three years of bodily injury liability, property damage liability, or comparable claim related experience.

What Is the Opportunity?

Travelers is seeking a Director, Technical Product Owner to work with the teams in the AI & Engineering Enablement circle within Claim Technology's Engineering Enablement group. The circle exists to build an AI-native software delivery system for Claim. It reshapes how engineers work alongside AI, automates the toil around delivery, codifies reusable patterns and standards, and gives clear insight into delivery health.
Your customers are Claim's engineers, engineering leaders and enterprise technology groups. You will help intake and prioritize work from these groups, managing relationships and staying true to the Engineering Enablement pillars. You will partner with the Enablement Lead and Circle Leads to set strategy and priorities, then own execution with the teams. You will focus on outcomes, like shorter lead time and real adoption, rather than how the work gets done. You will prioritize time-boxed initiatives that benefit many teams, test ideas quickly, and hand off capabilities teams can sustain on their own.

  • Partner with key leaders and peers across to determine resources required to achieve defined business outcomes.
  • Share best practices across teams to ensure alignment and consistency in ways of working within a value stream.

Overview of Position


Reporting to the AVP, Connected Living Compliance, this position is responsible for leading Assurant's global trade compliance program and ensuring compliance with all applicable import, export, sanctions, and customs regulations. In addition to enterprise related trade activities, this role actively supports the movement of mobile devices, device components, service parts, accessories, and related technologies across global markets while enabling efficient customer, carrier, OEM, repair, refurbishment, and logistics operations.


The Director serves as a strategic advisor to Connected Living leadership and business stakeholders, balancing compliance obligations with customer commitments, operational efficiency, and commercial objectives.


This role will also partner, coordinate, and align global trade compliance activities and strategies with the Director, Global Supply Chain Compliance.


What will my duties and responsibilities be in this job?


Global Trade Compliance Leadership (45%)


  • Develop, implement, and continuously improve Assurant's global trade compliance program.
  • Establish governance, policies, procedures, and internal controls covering import, export, sanctions, and customs compliance.
  • Ensure compliance with:
    • U.S. Export Administration Regulations (EAR)
    • OFAC sanctions requirements
    • U.S. Customs regulations
    • International customs laws and regulations
    • Foreign trade regulations in countries where Assurant operates
  • Provide strategic guidance to executive leadership on global trade risks and opportunities.
  • Identify and implement value-creation opportunities, including duty drawback, free trade agreements, foreign trade zones, tariff engineering, and other lawful duty mitigation strategies.

Import Compliance and Customs Management (20%)


  • Oversee global customs compliance for mobile devices, service parts, accessories, and technology.
  • Ensure accurate:
    • HTS classifications
    • Country-of-origin determinations
    • Customs valuation
    • Duty assessment
  • Manage customs brokers and trade service providers.
    • Identify and implement duty savings strategies and opportunities.
  • Support optimization of global supply chain costs and customs efficiency.

Export Controls and Sanctions Compliance (20%)


  • Oversee export classification activities for devices, components, software, and technology.
  • Ensure compliance with export controls.
  • Lead restricted-party screening and sanctions compliance programs.
  • Provide guidance regarding cross-border shipments, technology transfers, and international business transactions.
  • Manage export licensing requirements and government authorizations when required.
  • Drive global alignment for HTS classification, country of origin, customs valuation, and Export Control Classification Number (ECCN) determinations.
  • Maintain awareness of export-controlled technology, software, encryption, and restricted-access information requirements applicable to Assurant operations.
  • Assess and manage export control risks involving restricted destinations, restricted parties, military end users, military end uses, and controlled technologies, software, or technical data; develop procedures for end-use/end-user due diligence, escalation, licensing analysis, and transaction holds where required.

Risk Management and Compliance Governance (10%)


  • Conduct enterprise-wide trade compliance risk assessments.
  • Develop and maintain trade compliance controls and monitoring programs.
  • Lead internal audits and compliance reviews.
  • Establish compliance metrics, dashboards, and executive reporting.
  • Investigate compliance incidents and manage corrective actions.
  • Lead government audits, inquiries, disclosures, and remediation activities.
  • Assists in remediating trade compliance issues as necessary, including but not limited to putting together project plans, connecting resources to find solutions, documenting resolutions, and documenting remediation plans.
  • Supports internal compliance audits and assists with managing external audits or inquiries from government agencies Maintains accurate data and recordkeeping to include collecting and retaining records in response to third-party inquiries relating to Assurant compliance practices and business activities.

Training and Culture (5%)


  • Develop and deliver trade compliance training and awareness programs.
  • Ensure employees understand their responsibilities related to international trade activities.
  • Maintain training records and support audit readiness.

Experience

  • At least 5 years of leadership experience.
  • Experience supporting multinational import/export operations.
  • Experience managing customs and export compliance programs.
  • Experience supporting technology, telecommunications, consumer electronics, mobile device, repair/refurbishment, or logistics industries preferred.

Education & Certifications

Preferred Certifications

Leadership Competencies

The candidate will be able to provide examples of successfully demonstrating the following leadership competencies:

  • Sound and independent judgment, and demonstrated prudence and maturity

Job.JobTitle: Senior Manager, TPA Claims Strategy & Governance
Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity


We are looking for an experienced claims leader to lead the strategy, governance, and performance of our third-party administrator (TPA) claim programs across multiple products, business segments, and jurisdictions.

This is a highly visible leadership role with responsibility for ensuring our TPA partners deliver fair, timely, accurate, and compliant claim outcomes while meeting our expectations for customer experience, financial performance, and operational quality.


You will serve as the senior business owner for key TPA relationships, lead a team of claims and vendor oversight professionals, partner closely with senior leaders across the organization, and influence how we manage outsourced claims operations at an enterprise level.


This role is ideal for a strategic P&C claims leader who knows how to balance technical claims expertise, vendor accountability, financial discipline, and strong relationships to drive results.


What You'll Do


Lead TPA strategy and governance

  • Set the strategy, operating model, and governance framework for TPA claim programs across products, programs, jurisdictions, and business segments.
  • Establish and continuously improve service-level agreements, performance scorecards, claim-handling guidelines, authority levels, escalation protocols, and reporting standards.
  • Lead TPA selection, onboarding, implementation, renewal, transition, and termination activities while protecting claim continuity and customer service.

Own TPA performance and relationships

  • Serve as the senior relationship owner with TPA leadership, leading business reviews, performance discussions, escalations, and negotiations.
  • Hold partners accountable for claim inventories, cycle time, customer experience, claim quality, reserve adequacy, settlement accuracy, leakage, litigation activity, regulatory compliance, and contractual commitments.
  • Assess TPA capacity, staffing, training, licensing, business continuity, data security, and catastrophe readiness, and drive action plans when risks emerge.

Provide senior claims leadership

  • Provide strategic direction on complex, high-exposure, litigated, escalated, or disputed claims, including coverage, reserves, litigation strategy, and settlement approach within delegated authority.
  • Lead the audit, calibration, and quality assurance framework for TPA claim handling.
  • Identify performance trends and root causes and ensure corrective actions deliver sustainable improvement.

Lead and develop a high-performing team

  • Lead, coach, and develop managers, claim consultants, relationship managers, and vendor oversight professionals.
  • Build leadership capability and bench strength while creating a culture of accountability, sound judgment, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Set clear goals and expectations and ensure the team has the tools, resources, and direction needed to deliver results.

Drive enterprise partnership and improvement

  • Partner with Legal, Compliance, Finance, Actuarial, Underwriting, Procurement, Operations, Technology, and business leaders on contracts, controls, data, reporting, systems, and service delivery.
  • Develop and present performance dashboards, trend analysis, risk assessments, and strategic recommendations to senior and executive leadership.
  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives across TPA processes, controls, technology, training, and operating models.

Manage financial performance

  • Oversee department expenses as well as TPA fees, loss adjustment expenses, claim payments, reserves, vendor charges, and audit-related costs within delegated authority.
  • Identify leakage and adverse financial trends, validate contractual billing and service outcomes, and drive corrective action.
  • Establish financial performance targets and communicate results, trends, and risks to senior leadership.

What You'll Bring


Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • 10+ years of claims or related P&C insurance experience, including experience with TPA, vendor, program, or outsourced claims oversight.
  • 5+ years of progressive leadership experience, including leading managers or multiple teams.
  • Adjuster licenses for applicable states, with the ability to obtain and maintain additional licenses as needed.
  • Deep knowledge of claim investigation, policy interpretation, coverage analysis, reserving, litigation management, settlement practices, fraud indicators, regulatory requirements, and claims financial controls.
  • Demonstrated experience establishing governance models, service levels, vendor performance standards, claims audit programs, and corrective action plans.
  • Experience interpreting and negotiating contracts, statements of work, authority levels, fee structures, reporting obligations, and governance requirements.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior internal stakeholders and external business partners and drive accountability without direct authority.
  • Experience managing budgets and using operational and financial data to identify trends, determine root causes, and drive measurable action plans.
  • Strong executive communication, presentation, negotiation, relationship management, and change leadership skills.

We'd Especially Like to See

  • Bachelor's degree in business, insurance, risk management, finance, or a related field.
  • Experience leading multiple TPAs, outsourced claim programs, complex vendor relationships, or multi-state claims operations.
  • Experience with procurement, contract negotiation, vendor risk management, implementations, conversions, or TPA transitions.
  • Professional insurance designation such as AIC, CPCU, or SCLA .
  • Experience with claims analytics, dashboards, quality assurance programs, process improvement, or enterprise change initiatives.
  • Experience presenting to senior and executive leadership and contributing to broader claims strategy.


What Success Looks Like


In this role, success means building a TPA operating model that delivers:

  • Consistent, high-quality claim outcomes
  • Strong regulatory and contractual compliance
  • Improved cycle time and customer experience
  • Appropriate reserves and settlement outcomes
  • Reduced leakage and unnecessary expense
  • Clear accountability across TPA partners
  • Strong visibility into performance, risk, and financial results
  • Continuous improvement in claims controls, technology, and operational effectiveness

Work Environment & Travel


This role operates in a fast-paced, highly regulated environment and involves managing multiple external partners, competing priorities, confidential claim information, and significant financial and operational accountability.

Travel may be required for TPA site visits, business reviews, audits, implementation meetings, and leadership sessions. Occasional schedule flexibility may also be necessary to support urgent claims issues, catastrophe events, regulatory deadlines, or other critical operational needs.


Pay Range

$103,800.00 - $173,300.00

Job.JobDescription:
Alternate Locations: Greensboro, NC (North Carolina); Charlotte, NC (North Carolina); Fort Wayne, IN (Indiana); Radnor, PA (Pennsylvania)

Work Arrangement:

Hybrid : Employee will work 3 days a week in a Lincoln office

Relocation assistance: is not available for this opportunity.

Requisition #: 76880

The Role at a Glance

As the Lead Unified Communications & Collaboration (UCC) Systems Engineer, you will be an individual-contributor technical lead responsible for the architecture, engineering, security, reliability, and continuous improvement of Lincoln's enterprise communications and collaboration environment. In this role leadership is demonstrated through hands-on expertise, technical direction, mentoring, and influence. You will combine deep expertise in Microsoft Teams, Exchange Online, Teams Phone, and enterprise telephony with broad knowledge of Microsoft 365 collaboration services, conference room and audiovisual technologies, SharePoint, OneDrive, Microsoft Copilot, and emerging collaboration technologies. You will guide architecture and engineering decisions, mentor engineers through complex work, and partner across technology teams to deliver secure, resilient, scalable, and user-focused solutions.

What you'll be doing

Technical Leadership and Engineering

  • Own technical direction for Lincoln's UCC and Microsoft 365 environment, including architecture reviews, reference architectures, engineering standards, configuration baselines, and solution designs.
  • Lead complex implementations, migrations, integrations, lifecycle initiatives, and platform modernization from design through operational readiness.
  • Provide technical direction and hands-on mentoring to engineers, strengthening troubleshooting, design, and delivery capabilities without direct people-management responsibility.
  • Drive automation, standardization, platform simplification, and continuous improvement while reducing technical debt and manual effort.
  • Evaluate emerging technologies and translate Microsoft product roadmaps, industry trends, and artificial intelligence capabilities into prioritized platform roadmaps and investment recommendations.

Platform and Operational Excellence

  • Serve as an escalation point for complex incidents and problem investigations, lead root-cause analysis, and drive sustainable corrective actions.
  • Support effective incident, problem, change, and service-health management practices.
  • Prepare solutions for architecture review and change governance, ensuring security, scalability, reliability, supportability, rollback planning, and operational ownership are addressed.
  • Maintain technical documentation, runbooks, and knowledge that support platform operation, troubleshooting, and knowledge transfer.

Communication, Collaboration, and Influence

  • Lead technical discussions and communicate risks, options, recommendations, and service outcomes clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences.
  • Partner routinely with the Director of UCC/AV Engineering and leaders across Infrastructure, Network, Cybersecurity, Identity and Access Management, Enterprise Architecture, Artificial Intelligence, End-User Technology, Service Management, and Business Technology teams.
  • Build consensus across internal stakeholders, technology partners, and vendors while promoting accountability, knowledge sharing, and disciplined follow-through.

Leadership at Lincoln

This is an individual-contributor technical lead role with no direct reports. Leadership is demonstrated through expertise, sound judgment, accountability, mentoring, and influence. You will help engineers succeed on complex work, shape cross-team decisions, and model Lincoln's expectation that employees demonstrate leadership within their respective roles.

Why Join Us

Join a team modernizing enterprise communications at scale. You will influence platform strategy and product roadmaps, help simplify and strengthen critical services, and shape how emerging capabilities including automation, Microsoft Copilot, and artificial intelligence are introduced securely and responsibly.

What we're looking for

Must-Haves:

  • Extensive experience in engineering and supporting enterprise-scale Unified Communications, Microsoft 365, collaboration, or Digital Workplace technologies.
  • Expert-level capability in the architecture, engineering, administration, and troubleshooting of:
    • Microsoft Teams and Microsoft 365 collaboration services
    • Exchange Online
    • Teams Phone, enterprise voice, and telephony
    • PowerShell-based administration and automation
  • Working knowledge of adjacent technologies and control domains, including SharePoint and OneDrive, Microsoft Copilot, identity and access management, collaboration governance, networking, security and compliance, monitoring, endpoint integration, and conference room and audiovisual technologies.
  • Experience designing, implementing, and supporting highly available enterprise services.
  • Experience leading complex implementations, migrations, integrations, and modernization initiatives.
  • Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving capabilities.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex technical topics to different audiences.
  • Demonstrated ability to provide technical leadership, mentor others, influence decisions, and build consensus.
  • Ability to balance architecture and long-term technical direction with hands-on engineering and operational priorities.

Nice-to-Haves:

  • Experience automating Microsoft 365 or UCC services using PowerShell, Microsoft Graph, APIs, or comparable engineering tools.
  • Experience integrating collaboration platforms with identity, security, compliance, networking, monitoring, and endpoint technologies.
  • Experience providing technical leadership across organizationally or geographically distributed teams.
  • Experience working in a regulated, security-sensitive, or large enterprise environment.
  • Relevant Microsoft, cloud, networking, security, audiovisual, or collaboration certifications.

Application Deadline

Applications for this position will be accepted through 1/31/27, subject to close earlier.

What's it like to work here?

At Lincoln Financial, we love what we do. We make meaningful contributions each and every day to empower our customers to take charge of their lives. Working alongside dedicated and talented colleagues, we build fulfilling careers and stronger communities through a company that values our unique perspectives, insights and contributions and invests in programs that empower each of us to take charge of our own future.

What's in it for you:

  • Clearly defined career tracks and job levels, along with associated behaviors for each of Lincoln's core values and leadership attributes

  • Leadership development and virtual training opportunities

  • PTO/parental leave

  • Competitive 401K and employee benefits

  • Free financial counseling, health coaching and employee assistance program

  • Tuition assistance program

  • Work arrangements that work for you

  • Effective productivity/technology tools and training

The pay range for this position is $106,875 - $171,000 with anticipated pay for new hires between the minimum and midpoint of the range and could vary above and below the listed range as permitted by applicable law. Pay is based on non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to work experience, education, location, licensure requirements, proficiency and qualifications required for the role. The base pay is just one component of Lincoln's total rewards package for employees. About The Company

Lincoln Financial (NYSE: LNC) helps people to confidently plan for their version of a successful future. We focus on identifying a clear path to financial security, with products including annuities, life insurance, group protection, and retirement plan services.

With our 120-year track record of expertise and integrity, millions of customers trust our solutions and service to help put their goals in reach.

Be Aware of Fraudulent Recruiting Activities

If you are interested in a career at Lincoln, we encourage you to review our current openings and apply on our website. Lincoln values the privacy and security of every applicant and urges all applicants to diligently protect their sensitive personal information from scams targeting job seekers. Job.CustomJobTypeName: Risk Manager, Risk Management / Loss Control
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $120,375 to $192,600 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Radnor, PA
  • Experience: 7+ years
  • Education: Bachelor's degree
  • Benefits: 401(k), paid time off, tuition assistance

About this job

Lead Risk Management Analyst role within Enterprise Financial Risk at Lincoln Financial Group, providing independent oversight of market risk across annuity and life insurance products. Based in Radnor, PA (or five other locations) with hybrid work, 3 days per week in office.

Good fit if you have 5-7+ years market risk management experience, strong quantitative skills, knowledge of derivatives and annuity products, and proficiency in Python, VBA, or SQL.

Full job description

Alternate Locations: Radnor, PA (Pennsylvania); Charlotte, NC (North Carolina); Fort Wayne, IN (Indiana); Greensboro, NC (North Carolina); Hartford, CT (Connecticut); Omaha, NE (Nebraska)

Work Arrangement:

Hybrid : Employee will work 3 days a week in a Lincoln office

Relocation assistance: is not available for this opportunity.

Requisition #: 76881

The Role at a Glance

We are seeking a Lead Risk Management Analyst to join the Market Risk Governance team within Enterprise Financial Risk, part of the Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) organization in Lincoln's Chief Risk and Actuarial Office. This team provides independent second-line oversight of Lincoln's market risk. That includes product-driven exposures in our Variable Annuities (VAs), Registered Index-Linked Annuities (RILAs), Fixed Indexed Annuities (FIAs), Guaranteed Variable Universal Life (GVUL), and Indexed Universal Life (IUL), as well as market risk that comes from General Account investment strategy. Some of these risks are managed through hedge programs, others through reinsurance or other risk transfer, and the mix changes over time. We give leadership an independent read on whether the risk mitigation is working as intended, challenge strategy and methodology, and raise concerns early when results diverge from expectations. The team also leads enterprise scenario governance.


You will partner with first-line hedging, actuarial, investments, and other risk teams. The ideal candidate will have strong quantitative skills, hands-on experience with derivatives and financial instruments, and the judgment to turn complex analysis into a clear point of view for senior stakeholders.

What you'll be doing

•Build out independent market risk reporting such as liability attribution, performance attribution of hedge programs and other risk mitigation, hedge trading activity, and risk profile.
•Review proposed changes to risk mitigation strategy (hedging, reinsurance, and other approaches), methodology, and parameters. Help prepare risk opinions that give leadership an independent view before decisions are made.
•Analyze market risk across equity, interest rate, and volatility exposures, and provide insights to management on residual and emerging risks, performance metrics, and any deviations from established risk limits.
•Help keep the market risk policy, limits, and governance documents current.
•Prepare analysis and materials for market risk committees, framed to support decisions.
•Work with other ERM teams where market risk meets liquidity, counterparty capacity, capital, and ALM.
•Provide thought leadership on whether current risk mitigation approaches still fit as products, markets, and capital rules change.

What we're looking for

•Bachelor's degree in Finance, Mathematics, Actuarial Science, or a related field.
•Master's degree or relevant professional certifications (e.g., CFA, FRM, FSA, CQF) is a plus.
•5-7+ years of experience in market risk management, financial analysis, or a related field, preferably within the financial services or investment banking industry. Experience working in a second line market risk oversight role is a plus.
•Solid understanding of capital markets, derivatives, and annuity and life insurance products.
•Excellent quantitative and analytical skills with the ability to translate complex data into actionable insights.
•Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex risk information to senior stakeholders.
•High level of attention to detail, with the ability to identify and assess risks accurately and promptly.
•Strong programming skills (Python, VBA, SQL, etc.)
•Working knowledge of visualization software such as Tableau, PowerBI, etc.
•Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook).
•Familiarity with statutory capital frameworks (e.g., RBC, VM-21) is a plus.
•Ability to read, analyze and interpret both internal and external documents such as general media/publications, professional journals, technical procedures, governmental regulations, policies, proposals, and standard operating procedures.
•Ability to work collaboratively in cross-functional teams and manage multiple priorities.

The Role at a Glance

This Financial Planning & Analysis Specialist will perform and deliver on routine assignments and projects while leveraging and applying knowledge of FP&A principles to support Lincoln Financial Distributors (LFD). The individual will prepare, analyze, forecast, and report on financial information that helps business leaders make informed decisions regarding budgets, expenses, headcount planning, and business investments. This role partners with leaders across multiple business lines to provide financial insights, evaluate business performance, identify trends and variances, and support strategic and operational planning initiatives. The position also contributes to annual budgeting, forecasting, long-range planning, and ad hoc analyses that support business growth and profitability.

What you'll be doing

  • Prepare, analyze, and report on financial results and key business metrics for assigned LFD business areas.
  • Support the annual budget, forecast, and long-range planning processes, including expense, revenue, and headcount planning.
  • Perform budget-to-actual, forecast-to-actual, and variance analysis to identify trends, risks, and opportunities and communicate findings to leadership.
  • Partner with business leaders to provide financial guidance and decision support related to operational initiatives, strategic investments, and resource planning.
  • Develop financial models and analyses to evaluate business opportunities, including new products, pricing strategies, sales growth initiatives, and workforce planning scenarios.
  • Collect, compile, and evaluate financial information to develop and deliver both standard and ad hoc financial analyses.
  • Assist in the preparation and maintenance of financial forecasts, management reporting, and executive presentations.
  • Support monthly and quarterly close activities, including reconciliations and financial performance reviews.
  • Communicate financial insights, trends, and emerging issues to management and recommend actions where appropriate.
  • Collaborate with team members and cross-functional partners to improve financial processes, reporting capabilities, and decision-making tools.

What we're looking for

Must-Haves

  • 4 Year/Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience (4 years of experience in lieu of Bachelor's) (Minimum Required)
  • 1+ Years experience in financial planning & analysis
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills with the ability to interpret financial data and communicate insights effectively.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and financial modeling techniques.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to partner effectively with business leaders and stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated proficiency with AI tools (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, Claude, or similar platforms) to support data analysis, process efficiency, financial insights, and business decision-making.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft PowerPoint with experience developing clear and concise presentations that communicate financial results, forecasts, strategic recommendations, and key business insights to stakeholders.

Nice-to-haves

  • Experience with financial planning and reporting tools such as SmartView, Hyperion, Essbase, and/or Anaplan.
  • Experience supporting budgeting, forecasting, headcount planning, and ad hoc business analysis.
  • Experience presenting financial results and recommendations to business partners and leadership.

What's it like to work here?

At Lincoln Financial, we love what we do. We make meaningful contributions each and every day to empower our customers to take charge of their lives. Working alongside dedicated and talented colleagues, we build fulfilling careers and stronger communities through a company that values our unique perspectives, insights and contributions and invests in programs that empower each of us to take charge of our own future.

Pay is based on non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to work experience, education, location, licensure requirements, proficiency and qualifications required for the role. About this job

Inspect, refurbish, test, and repair mobile phones and wireless devices using diagnostic equipment like oscilloscopes and spectrum analyzers. Work independently at your station in a production environment with team collaboration, Monday through Thursday, 6am to 4:30pm in Irving, Texas.

Good fit if you have two years of small electronics assembly or component testing experience and strong soldering skills.

Full job description

As a Wireless Technician , you will inspect, refurbish, test, program, tune, troubleshoot and repair complex radio frequency electro-mechanical devices such as mobile phones. You will work from complex schematics and diagrams, and utilize Multi-meters, Oscilloscopes, RF Signal Generators, Spectrum Analyzers and Communication Test Sets to troubleshoot faults to the component level.

Additionally, you will work independently at your station but will also have the opportunity to work in a friendly, team-oriented environment. This is a production environment with productivity requirements and quality standards. If you enjoy working with your hands and want to work with the latest in wireless technology, this may be the perfect career opportunity for you!

This role is based at our Irving, TX location with a schedule of Monday - Thursday from 6am to 4:30pm

This job posting is part of our ongoing efforts to build a strong talent network for current and future opportunities. We invite you to apply, and qualified candidates will be contacted as roles become available.

What will be my duties and responsibilities in this job?

  • Conduct root case failure analysis and troubleshooting on suspected defective equipment

  • Perform repetitive electromechanical assembly using hand and electric tools

  • Must be able to perform component level and board repairs

  • Identify and report root cause deficiencies

  • Identify and report routine process deficiencies

  • Test, repair and program equipment

  • Perform soldering and de-soldering using handheld soldering equipment

  • Work with care and urgency in order to meet production goals

  • Participate in continuous improvement and team building activities

  • Refer to and follow Standard Operating Procedures to perform the job duties

  • Physically move material as needed

  • Perform other duties as assigned

What are the requirements needed for this position?

  • High school diploma or GED

  • Two years skill-related experience such as working with components, testing requirements and/or assembly of small electronics

  • Demonstrated high-level proficiency with soldering and de-soldering

  • Basic computer skills and the ability to enter data on multiple screens

  • Strong attention to detail

  • Ability to handle multiple priorities simultaneously

  • Ability to work independently and in a team environment

  • Ability to interact effectively and positively with all levels of company personnel

What other skills/experience would be helpful to have?

  • Associates degree in electronics or technical degree in a related field

  • One year of previous experience working in a manufacturing environment

  • Knowledgeable in analog, digital and RF disciplines

What are the working conditions and physical requirements of this job?

  • Must be able to lift and/or move up to 30 pounds

  • Must be able to work overtime and on Saturdays as needed

  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and the ability to adjust focus

  • Must be able to talk and hear

  • Required to use hands and fingers, handle, or feel objects, tools or controls. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions

  • The noise level in the work environment is low, and it is an Electro Static Discharge (ESD) safe area; wrist strap and smocks must be worn at all times

Quick facts
