Job.JobTitle: Inside Auto Claims Adjuster - Scottsdale, AZ (Hybrid)
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Scottsdale, AZ
  • Experience: 2+ years
  • Benefits: Health insurance, 401(k), paid time off, tuition assistance

About this job

Inside Auto Claims Adjuster investigating minor to moderately complex auto insurance claims in Scottsdale. Hybrid role with 3 days in office and 2 days remote, requiring adjuster's license within 60 days of hire.

Good fit if you have 2+ years of claim handling experience and strong communication skills

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

The Inside Auto Claims Adjuster is responsible for investigating basic and occasionally moderately complex auto insurance claims. This role may handle non-represented claims and requires evaluating coverage, determining liability, and negotiating settlements. The adjuster works directly with claimants, insureds, and other involved parties to ensure timely, accurate, and customer-focused claim resolution.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Ensure compliance with all regulatory requirements and company standards throughout the claim lifecycle.
  • Investigate minor to moderately complex auto accidents and prepare clear, concise claim summaries.
  • Conduct recorded statements with claimants, insureds, and witnesses.
  • Evaluate auto claims to determine coverage, liability, and damages.
  • Negotiate and settle claims in alignment with established guidelines and best practices.
  • Maintain detailed and well-documented claim files, including notes, summaries, and decision rationale.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to support efficient and customer-centric claim handling.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 2+ years of prior claim handling experience preferred.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with a demonstrated commitment to excellent customer service.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks, prioritize effectively, and operate in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong attention to detail with solid critical-thinking and decision-making skills.
  • Comfortable using technology and learning claims-related software and tools.
  • This position is not available for California, Alaska, Washington, and Hawaii residents.

Notice of Licensing Requirement:

  • As a condition of employment, you may be expected to obtain an adjusters license in multiple markets.
  • All required licenses must be obtained within 60 days of hire.
  • You must maintain all licensing required for your role. This includes any continuing education and/or other state-affiliated requirements for licensing renewal.
  • This role offers a $1,000 sign on bonus if you have an active adjuster license in TX, FL, or your resident state.
  • Current employees and former employees seeking rehire at Allstate or its affiliated companies are not eligible for this sign-on bonus.

Work Location and Schedule:

During Training

  • Hours: MondayFriday 8:00 AM 5:00 PM
  • Work Arrangement: Full-time, In-Person for Training

After Training

  • Hours: MondayFriday hours between 8:00 AM 5:30 PM AZ Time with occasional Saturday
  • Work Arrangement: Hybrid schedule 3 days in the office (Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday), 2 days remote (Thursday, Friday)

What You Need:

  • A dedicated workspace in your residence that is private and free from distractions.
  • A minimum internet bandwidth of 50 MB down/5 MB up.
  • Appropriate work surface and seating.

What Allstate Provides:

  • A technology bundle that includes all equipment needed to perform your work from home (laptop, monitor, headset, keyboard, mouse).
  • Connectivity reimbursement of $80 per month to offset a portion of your internet costs.

Allstate Benefits:

Allstate cares about you and your wellbeing. We offer a comprehensive total rewards package that includes pay, benefits, and programs to help you balance work with the rest of your life. You can choose whatever benefits are most important you. Here are some of our benefits:

  • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Allstate pension plan and 401(k) savings plan
  • Ayco financial coaching
  • Spring Health mental and emotional wellbeing resources
  • Paid parental leave
  • Adoption reimbursement
  • Paid time off
  • Tuition reimbursement
  • Wellness incentives
  • Allstate Foundation donation match and grant opportunities

Skills

Auto Insurance Claims, Critical Thinking, Customer Service, Multitasking

Compensation

Basecompensationoffered for this role is $50,000-$60,000 annually and is based on experience and qualifications.

The candidate(s) offered this position will be required to submit to a background investigation.

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Property Claims Adjuster, Claims, Claims Adjuster
Job.JobDescription:
At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

A day in the life of a Field Property Adjuster, and what it takes to do the job!Montgomery, AL

As a Field Property Adjuster, you willprovideexceptional service to our policyholders. Your primary responsibility will involve traveling to our customers' homes to conduct on-site inspections, investigate coverage, prepare estimates, and settle claims promptly and efficiently. Additionally, you will handle virtual claims countrywide,leveragingvarious platforms and software such as Xactimate andClaimsXVideo Collaboration. Yourexpertisewill be particularly focused on water losses, ensuring our customers receive the highest level of support and resolution for these specific claims.

You'llwear a few hats that will require a level of experience:

  • The Customer Service Expertyoulllive into Allstates Claims Culture by caring, empowering, and restoring, and you willaccomplishthat by being compassionate, clear, and a committed partner in each claim. You lead with empathy, always.
  • The Investigator youllconfidently and independently investigate property claims by performing detailed reviews of damage and interpreting policies todeterminecoverage.
  • The Effective Communicatoryoulluse phone, emails and sometimes even video chat with customers to help them through a fast, fair, and easy claims process.Youllalso incorporate a specific approach to claim handling to offer the customer their preference of communication to efficiently discuss their claim needs and keep them updated on theclaimprogress.
  • The Negotiator You will evaluate and negotiate claims settlements with customers, vendors, third party carriers and claimants,in accordance withall legal and business standard methodologies. With negotiations, you will incorporate tactics in handling challenging and complex situations.
  • The Problem Solveryoullutilizemultiple tools to get the job done in a fast-paced environment, including estimate tools, job aids, andadditionalsettlement platforms, all while using your sharp critical thinking skills.
  • The Recorderyoullprotect the company financially by executing policies along policy agreements, and you keep a clear record of your work in a claims system that you will be trainedin.Youllaccomplishthis by ensuringtimelyandaccuratedocumentation is completed as you work on each claim.

Qualifications:

  • 2years'previousexperience as an outside adjuster is highly desired.
  • Previousexperience as an outside adjuster is highly desired.
  • Proficiencyin using Xactimate and other relevant software for estimating.
  • Strong critical thinking and technical skills to assess damages accurately andexpediteclaimssettlements.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to provide exceptional customer service.
  • Ability to travel to customers' homes and handle virtual claims countrywide effectively.
  • Detail-oriented and organized, with a focus on delivering high-quality work.
  • This position is not available for California, Alaska,Hawaiior Puerto Rico residents.

Required Qualifications:

  • Residency within the posted location is mandatory for this role.
  • Are willing and able to carry a 50-pound ladder and access up to a 6/12 pitch onaone to two-story roof.
  • Valid driver's license and willingness to travel as part of the job requirements.

Youreprovided with comprehensive training:

  • The training program is designed to help you build a claims foundation and understand the systems and processes in yourday-to-daywork.
  • Ongoing training opportunities for continuous improvement happen regularly on the job.
  • You willbe requiredto attend approximately 2 weeks of training that will take place in Dallas, TX.

Notice of Licensing Requirement:

  • As a condition of employment, your office/area may require you to obtain an adjuster and/or an appraiser licensewhich includes passing anadditionalbackground check with the Department of Labor.If applicable, you willbe requiredto secure license(s) within60 daysof hire.
  • If required, the Hiring Manager will work with you along with the Centralized Licensing team to ensure that you are properly licensed.

Sign On Bonus:

You may be eligible for a $1,000 Licensing Sign on Bonus if you have the applicable active licenses needed for this role. This could include Home Resident Property & Casualty License, Designated Home State (DHS) Florida or Texas License, and/orapplicableAppraiser License.


*Current employees or candidates who have previously worked for Allstate, including its family of companies, are not eligible for this sign-onbonus.

Company Car:

Based on our Company Car Guidelines, this role may qualify for a company car. Our leadership teamdeterminesthis based on annual work mileage for this location. You maybe requiredto use your personal vehicle until these guidelines are met. We offer mileage reimbursements for personal vehicle usage during work.

Allstate Benefits:

Being a part of Allstate means you receive a benefits package from Day 1 of employment. This includes time off, healthcare, retirement, and more. That is why as anAllstater,youllenjoy a Total Rewards package that includes:

  • Competitive pay with needed support for continuous development and career advancement.
  • Flexibility in scheduling and a time off policy that helps support your work/life balance.
  • Initial and ongoing training to get you proficient in your new role.
  • Comprehensive benefits like a 401K/pension, education reimbursement, and programs to help you balance work with the rest of your life. Visit www.allstategoodlife.com to learn more.

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Property Claims Adjuster, Claims, Claims Adjuster
Job.JobDescription:
At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

A day in the life of a Field Property Adjuster, and what it takes to do the job!


As a Field Property Adjuster, you will be dedicated to providing exceptional service to our policyholders. Your primary responsibility will involve traveling to our customers' homes to conduct on-site inspections, investigate coverage, prepare estimates, and settle claims promptly and efficiently. Additionally, you will handle virtual claims countrywide, leveraging various platforms and software such as Xactimate and ClaimsX Video Collaboration. Your expertise will be particularly focused on water losses, ensuring our customers receive the highest level of support and resolution for these specific claims.

You'll wear a few hats that will require a level of experience:


  • The Customer Service Expert youll live into Allstates Claims Culture by caring, empowering, and restoring, and you will accomplish that by being compassionate, clear, and a committed partner in each claim. You lead with empathy, always.
  • The Investigator youll confidently and independently investigate property claims by performing detailed reviews of damage and interpreting policies to determine coverage.
  • The Effective Communicator youll use phone, emails and sometimes even video chat with customers to help them through a fast, fair, and easy claims process. Youll also incorporate a specific approach to claim handling to offer the customer their preference of communication to efficiently discuss their claim needs and keep them updated on the claim progress.
  • The Negotiator You will evaluate and negotiate claims settlements with customers, vendors, third party carriers and claimants, in accordance with all legal and business standard methodologies. With negotiations, you will incorporate tactics in handling challenging and complex situations.
  • The Problem Solver youll utilize multiple tools to get the job done in a fast-paced environment, including estimate tools, job aids, and additional settlement platforms, all while using your sharp critical thinking skills.
  • The Recorder youll protect the company financially by executing policies along policy agreements, and you keep a clear record of your work in a claims system that you will be trained on. Youll accomplish this by ensuring timely and accurate documentation is completed as you work on each claim.

Preferred Qualifications:


  • Reside on Nassau County, NY.
  • 1-3 years prior experience as an outside adjuster is highly desired.
  • Proficiency in using Xactimate and other relevant software for estimating.
  • Strong critical thinking and technical skills to assess damages accurately and expedite claims settlements.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to provide exceptional customer service.
  • Ability to travel to customers' homes and handle virtual claims countrywide effectively.
  • Detail-oriented and organized, with a focus on delivering high-quality work.
  • This position is not available for California, Alaska, Hawaii or Puerto Rico residents.

Required qualification:


  • Valid driver's license and willingness to travel as part of the job requirements.
  • Are willing and able to carry a 50-pound ladder and access up to a 6/12 pitch on a one-to-two-story roof.

Youre provided with comprehensive training:


  • The training program is designed to help you build a claims foundation and understand the systems and processes in your day-to-day work
  • Ongoing training opportunities for continuous improvement happen regularly on the job

** Please note, you will be required to attend 2-weeks of training that will take place in Dallas, TX **

Notice of Licensing Requirement:


  • As a condition of employment, your office/area may require you to obtain an adjuster and/or an appraiser licensewhich includes passing an additional background check with the Department of Labor.If applicable, you will be required to secure license(s) within 60 days of hire.
  • If required, the Hiring Manager will work with you along with the Centralized Licensing team to ensure that you are properly licensed.

Sign On Bonus:


  • You may be eligible for a $1000 Licensing Sign on Bonus if you have the applicable active licenses needed for this role. This could include Home Resident Property & Casualty License, Designated Home State (DHS) Florida or Texas License, and/or applicable Appraiser License.

**Current employees or candidates who have previously worked for Allstate, including its family of companies, are not eligible for this sign-on bonus.

Company Car:


Based on our Company Car Guidelines, this role may qualify for a company car. Our leadership team determines this based on annual work mileage for this location. You may be required to use your personal vehicle until these guidelines are met. We offer mileage reimbursements for personal vehicle usage during work.

Allstate Benefits:


Being a part of Allstate means you receive a benefits package from Day 1 of employment. This includes time off, healthcare, retirement, and more. That is why as an Allstater, youll enjoy a Total Rewards package that includes:

  • Competitive pay with needed support for continuous development and career advancement.
  • Flexibility in scheduling and a time off policy that helps support your work/life balance.
  • Initial and ongoing training to get you proficient in your new role.
  • Comprehensive benefits like a 401K/pension, education reimbursement, and programs to help you balance work with the rest of your life. Visit www.allstategoodlife.com to learn more.

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

Why This Role?

This is a meaningful leadership role within the enterprise P&C actuarial reserving organization, designed for a senior actuarial manager who wants to sit close to complex reserve analysis, business decision-making, and the continued modernization of reserving practices.

You will lead actuarial reserving work for Homeowners, catastrophe and runoff exposures across the Allstate brand and National General, partnering with reserving senior leadership and key business partners to develop, evaluate, and communicate reserve indications, methodologies, and insights. The role requires a strong blend of technical actuarial judgment, analytical discipline, people leadership, and the ability to translate complex results into clear recommendations that support business decisions.

As a Senior Actuarial Manager, you will not only execute core reserving responsibilities, you will help strengthen the craft of reserving through improved methodology, data quality, documentation, tool utilization, and team development. This is a role for someone who can operate independently on complex analyses, guide analysts through high-quality execution, and contribute to the ongoing evolution of a modern reserving function.

What Youll Do

  • Lead complex reserving analyses. Own reserving analyses for Homeowners, catastrophe and runoff exposures, using accepted actuarial and statistical standards, with a focus on high-quality analysis, sound judgment, and clear business implications.
  • Strengthen reserve decision support. Partner with senior reserving leaders and business stakeholders to develop and execute reserving strategies that support high-complexity reserve analyses and informed decision-making.
  • Ensure data quality and analytical rigor. Select, review, and challenge the data, assumptions, methods, and tools used in highly complex actuarial analyses, ensuring outputs are reliable, well-supported, and fit for purpose.
  • Translate technical work into clear insights. Review, evaluate, and communicate actuarial results, modeling techniques, and reserve indications in a way that is understandable, actionable, and relevant for leadership and external groups.
  • Guide work across projects and priorities. Plan, manage, and contribute to high-complexity projects that may span multiple disciplines, balancing technical quality, timelines, stakeholder needs, and execution discipline.
  • Develop analysts and build team capability. Lead a team by setting expectations, coaching technical development, reviewing work, and providing input on talent management, development, and team effectiveness.
  • Advance the reserving craft. Contribute technical and thought leadership through improvements to reserving methods, processes, tools, documentation, and analytical approaches, often serving as a subject-matter expert within the team.
  • Apply business and regulatory context. Use knowledge of insurance products, market dynamics, claims trends, and the regulatory environment to inform reserving conclusions and influence appropriate business decisions.

Impact & Exposure

This role sits at an important intersection of actuarial analysis, business partnership, and team leadership. Your work will support reserve estimates and explanations used by senior reserving leadership and key business partners, and your ability to communicate clearly will help shape how complex reserve movements, methods, and assumptions are understood.

It is a highly visible senior manager role that requires independent judgment, strong execution, and the ability to influence through technical credibility, clarity, and partnership.

Qualifications

Required

  • Fellow of the Casualty Actuarial Society (FCAS).
  • Ten or more years of actuarial experience.
  • Experience leading complex actuarial analyses and applying actuarial judgment to support business decisions.
  • Experience partnering with leaders and cross-functional business stakeholders.
  • Experience managing and developing actuarial talent.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Preferred

  • Property and casualty reserving experience.

Supervisory Responsibilities

This role has supervisory responsibility for a team that includes actuarial managers or team leads and analysts, and includes coaching, work direction, review, and input into talent management.

Job Description

The Senior Consultant II is responsible for granting settlement authority on highly complex claims valued in excess of Market Claim Office (MCO) and Regional Claim Office (RCO) limits, providing recommendations on requests to go to trial on cases where the gross exposure is in excess of MCO authority, and general oversight of all large losses for a specific CSA or CSAs. The individual may also provide discretionary referrals on coverage issues, opinions and research. In addition, the Sr Cons II may provide approval on Closed Without Payment (CWP) requests where liability is disputed, and the value is in excess of Field authority.

We are seeking Large Loss Adjusters to join our growing team! This team manages complex, high exposure claims and may include rejected tenders and extra-contractual exposures claims. Claims often involve severe injuries, such as catastrophic impairments, amputations, comas, and fatalities. The ideal candidate will have prior experience handling large loss claims, navigating complex liability issues, and managing litigation through resolution. Strong investigative, negotiation, and risk assessment skills are essential for success in this role.





Key Responsibilities

Performs file reviews for various complex projects or for cases in litigation, analyzes data, and reports findings

May review cases to determine if CWP is appropriate given gross tort value exposure

Supports the Field with discretionary referrals on complex coverage issues and engages Home Office Claim litigation for involvement and direction as needed

Reviews coverage, liability, and/or damages on highly complex cases referred for authorization and collaborates with Field leadership on addition steps to be taken and other feedback and direction

Collaborates with Frontline Performance Experts (FPEs), Frontline Performance Leaders (FPLS), and Claim Process Specialists (CPSs) to share experience and trends identified in referred cases

Works with Product, Protection, Law, and Claims on new products introduced to the Field and the sales force, and develops Claim Bulletins to provide new forms and/or endorsements that impact claim handling practices



Supervisory Responsibilities

This job does not have supervisory duties.

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Workers' Compensation Adjuster, Claims, Claims Representative
Job.JobDescription:
Who Are We?

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Compensation Overview

The annual base salary range provided for this position is a nationwide market range and represents a broad range of salaries for this role across the country. The actual salary for this position will be determined by a number of factors, including the scope, complexity and location of the role; the skills, education, training, credentials and experience of the candidate; and other conditions of employment. As part of our comprehensive compensation and benefits program, employees are also eligible for performance-based cash incentive awards.

Salary Range

$53,800.00 - $88,800.00

Target Openings

3

What Is the Opportunity?

As an Associate Claim Rep, Workers Compensation, you will receive comprehensive training in claim handling, customer service, and policy interpretation while working alongside experienced claim professionals. This position focuses on developing your skills and knowledge to successfully manage workers compensation claims. This program can typically last up to 12 months and upon successful completion of this program you will have the skills needed to handle claims independently and progress toward full claims handling responsibility.

What Will You Do?

  • Actively participate in structured training classes covering insurance policies, specific claim processes, systems, and procedures, including virtual, classroom, and on-the-job training.
  • Assist in reviewing, investigating, and documenting Workers Compensation claims under close supervision.
  • Investigate, develop, and evaluate action plans for claim resolution. Assess coverage and determine if a claim is compensable under Workers Compensation including evaluating claims for potential fraud.
  • Participate in Telephonic and/or onsite File Reviews.
  • Learn how to determine coverage, compensability, and exposure based on policy terms and claim facts.
  • Gather information from policyholders, claimants, witnesses, and third-party providers.
  • Communicate and apprise all parties regarding claim status which may include our business customers, injured employees, medical providers, and legal counsel.
  • Maintain accurate records of claim activity in claim management systems.
  • Achieve a positive result by returning an injured party to work when appropriate. This may include coordinating medical treatment in collaboration with internal or external resources.
  • Demonstrate openness to continuous learning, particularly in AI and digital transformation.
  • Acquire and maintain relevant Insurance License(s) to comply with state and Travelers' requirements within three months of starting the job.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's Degree.
  • Previous internship or work experience in customer service or insurance.
  • Willingness to obtain an active adjuster license where required by state law.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook); willingness to learn claims management.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to convey information clearly and professionally.
  • Ability to exercise sound judgement and make effective decisions within established authority.
  • Exceptional customer service skills and commitment to providing a positive experience for insureds and claimants.
  • Attention to detail and organizational skills; ability to manage multiple tasks and prioritize effectively.
  • Basic conflict resolution skills; willingness to learn techniques for facilitating productive discussions and negotiations.
  • Demonstrated openness to continuous learning.

What is a Must Have?

  • High School Diploma or GED and one year of customer service experience.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit http://careers.travelers.com/life-at-travelers/benefits/.

What Is the Opportunity?

The Sales Executive Team is dedicated to navigating and managing a high performing sales culture in-person and/or virtually which contributes to the overall success of the Select business. The team executes on industry-leading sales strategies aligned with business objectives, builds effective relationships with customers, distribution partners and fellow employees, and creates tactical sales plans for profitable growth through extensive product knowledge and state of the art sales and influencing tactics. The team also uses digitally advanced strategies to move the business forward, leads the relationships with our aggregator/networking groups, and partners with the agent to imbed into higher producing revenue streams. As Sales Director, Select, you will lead a team of sales professionals within your agency assignments/territories to optimize growth within defined new business, retention and profitability goals and deliver success within Travelers' framework of Corporate values. You will have primary responsibility for sales strategy and business development within your agency assignments or territories and will act as a brand ambassador to sell the Travelers value proposition to distribution partners. You will be out in the field attending meetings and building relationships with agents who are in need of support while also supporting the SE and Sr SEs who are assigned to the territory. This position is an outside sales position where assigned distribution relationships within the geographic territory tend to be best served through an in-person sales strategy.

What Will You Do?

  • Select, train and manage a team of Sales Executives to develop long-term and short-term plans aligned with business objectives, achieve and exceed sales targets, and operate within Travelers' Vision and Values.
  • Coordinate sales planning and quarterly performance reviews.
  • Create an environment that fosters high performance, continuous learning, and proactive initative.
  • Oversee and influence a team responsible for developing and implementing advanced sales strategies to expand and manage territory, with the objective of driving profitable growth.
  • Own assigned territory, including development of business strategy, leveraging performance metrics to create annual plans and managing territorial performance.
  • Conduct high-level agency diagnostics to identify growth opportunities, facilitate strategic appointments, and nurture long-term relationships.
  • Proactively manage measures of point-of-sale success, sales plan effectiveness and customer satisfaction.
  • Ensure the prospecting, onboarding and establishment of performance goals for new agencies, while providing training and support.
  • Oversee in-person office visits to strengthen key partnerships.
  • Influence key agency partners through exceptional communication, negotiation, and leadership skills.
  • Collaborate with internal teams, such as, Product, Underwriting, and Operations to ensure alignment of sales strategies with broader business objectives.
  • Demonstrate the ability to build partnerships with other business groups to identify and initiate multiple product solutions at the account level.
  • Leverage expertise in competitor products and market trends to enhance organizational learning and identify opportunities, serving as a significant resource for competitive intelligence and distribution channel insights in the region.
  • Represent region or territory at agency council meetings and supports corporate agency management in handling strategic distribution relationships with key brokers and cross-enterprise resources.
  • Utilize thorough knowledge of Travelers' systems, platforms, and sophisticated data and analytics to guide strategic sales decisions, measure performance metrics and identify opportunities for additional products and services to maintain a balanced portfolio.
  • Analyze market, distribution channel and product offerings, identify gaps and strategic opportunities, and work with business partners to develop plan to increase market share and drive profitable growth.
  • Ensure team leverages AI technologies to optimize industry processes, enhance decision-making, and drive innovation, while continuously learning and adapting to emerging AI trends and tools.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Bachelor's degree in sales, marketing, business or related field.
  • Eight or more years of insurance marketing and sales or related experience in managing and growing a high-value book of business, developing and executing successful sales strategies, conducting comprehensive agency diagnostics, and utilizing advanced data and analytics proficiently.
  • Four or more years of experience in leadership and management of other employees.
  • Certified Insurance Counselor (CIC) (or willingness to pursue).
  • Expert knowledge of Travelers products and general Property & Casualty marketplace.
  • Exceptional influencing, communication, and negotiation skills.
  • Proven ability to collaboratively build and maintain relationships with a diverse range of stakeholders both internally and externally.
  • Advanced skills in agency appointment.
  • Ability to set clear direction by defining goals and priorities and energize others to meet these goals in a timely manner.
  • Expert organizational skills to manage complex tasks and priorities.
  • Goal-oriented mindset with a focus on achieving sales targets and business objectives.

What is a Must Have?

  • Five years of professional sales experience within the Insurance Industry.
  • Two or more years of experience in leadership and management of other employees.
  • Must live in the territory that they manage and have the ability to travel up to 50% of the time.

What Is in It for You?

  • Health Insurance: Employees and their eligible family members - including spouses, domestic partners, and children - are eligible for coverage from the first day of employment.
  • Retirement: Travelers matches your 401(k) contributions dollar-for-dollar up to your first 5% of eligible pay, subject to an annual maximum. If you have student loan debt, you can enroll in the Paying it Forward Savings Program. When you make a payment toward your student loan, Travelers will make an annual contribution into your 401(k) account. You are also eligible for a Pension Plan that is 100% funded by Travelers.
  • Paid Time Off: Start your career at Travelers with a minimum of 20 days Paid Time Off annually, plus nine paid company Holidays.
  • Wellness Program: The Travelers wellness program is comprised of tools, discounts and resources that empower you to achieve your wellness goals and caregiving needs. In addition, our mental health program provides access to free professional counseling services, health coaching and other resources to support your daily life needs.
  • Volunteer Encouragement: We have a deep commitment to the communities we serve and encourage our employees to get involved. Travelers has a Matching Gift and Volunteer Rewards program that enables you to give back to the charity of your choice.

Employment Practices

Travelers is an equal opportunity employer. We value the unique abilities and talents each individual brings to our organization and recognize that we benefit in numerous ways from our differences. 

In accordance with local law, candidates seeking employment in Colorado are not required to disclose dates of attendance at or graduation from educational institutions.

If you are a candidate and have specific questions regarding the physical requirements of this role, please send us an email so we may assist you.

Travelers reserves the right to fill this position at a level above or below the level included in this posting.

To learn more about our comprehensive benefit programs please visit http://careers.travelers.com/life-at-travelers/benefits/.

Taking care of our customers, our communities and each other. That's the Travelers Promise. By honoring this commitment, we have maintained our reputation as one of the best property casualty insurers in the industry for over 170 years. Join us to discover a culture that is rooted in innovation and thrives on collaboration. Imagine loving what you do and where you do it.

Job.JobTitle: Medical-Only Workers' Compensation Claims Technician - California
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Workers' Compensation Adjuster, Claims, Claims Representative
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Rocklin, CA
  • Experience: 1 to 3 years
  • Education: High school diploma or GED

About this job

Process routine workers' compensation claims with ongoing medical management for medical-only cases. Conduct investigations, verify information, arrange medical exams, and authorize medical payments. Remote work available with twice-monthly office visits if within 50 miles of an office.

Good fit if you have a high school diploma, 1-3 years of customer service or insurance experience, and strong writing and telephone skills.

Full job description


Description

Are you looking for an opportunity to join a claims team with a fast-growing company that has consistently outpaced the industry in year over year growth? Liberty Mutual Insurance has an excellent claims opportunity available for a Workers Compensation Claims Technician. Claims Technicians obtain essential information in order to process routine workers' compensation claims with on-going medical management for medical pension claims. Provides injured workers and customers with accurate, timely information and quality service. Claims Technicians also identify potential problems and make claim referral decisions.

GRS North America Claims is excited to announce our go forward strategy to provide employees with the flexibility to include an option to work from home full-time. Candidates who are selected for this position will be trained remotely.

You will be required to go into the office twice a month if you reside within 50 miles of one a specified office. Please note this policy is subject to change.

Responsibilities:

  • Conduct investigation to secure essential facts from injured worker, employer and providers regarding workers' compensations through telephone or written reports. Verifies information from claimants, physicians, and medical providers to assess compensability and/or causal relation of medical treatment and make evaluations for cases with claim specific on-going medical management.
  • Provides on-going medical case management for assigned claims. Initiates calls to injured worker and medical provider if projected disability exceeds maximum triage model projection or to resolve medical treatment issues as needed. Maintains contact with injured worker, provider and employer to ensure understanding of protocols and claims processing and medical treatment.
  • Continually assesses claim status to determine if problem cases or those exceeding protocols should be referred to Claims Service Team and/or would benefit from, MP RN review or other medical /claims resources. Arranges Independent Medical Exam and Peer Review as necessary.
  • Maintains accurate records and handles administrative responsibilities associated with processing and payment of claims. Records and updates status notes; documents result of contacts, relevant medical reports, and duration information per file posting standards including making appropriate medical information viewable to customers in Electronic Document Management (EDM). Generates form letters following set guidelines (i.e., letters to physicians projecting disability, letters confirming medical treatment and disability and letters outlining expected outcome to employers).
  • Authorizes payment of medical payments and/or medical treatment.
  • Recognizes potential subrogation cases, prepares cases for subrogation and refers these cases to the Subrogation Units.
Qualifications
  • High school diploma plus 1-3 years' of related customer service experience or applicable insurance knowledge.
  • Licensing may be required in some jurisdictions
  • Effective written skills to compose clear, succinct descriptions when posting files and drafting correspondence.
  • Good telephone and typing skills required
  • Ability to learn when to make proper use of medical management resources, know when to use them and follow through with medical management information received.
About Us

Pay Philosophy: The typical starting salary range for this role is determined by a number of factors including skills, experience, education, certifications and location. The full salary range for this role reflects the competitive labor market value for all employees in these positions across the national market and provides an opportunity to progress as employees grow and develop within the role. Some roles at Liberty Mutual have a corresponding compensation plan which may include commission and/or bonus earnings at rates that vary based on multiple factors set forth in the compensation plan for the role.

At Liberty Mutual, our goal is to create a workplace where everyone feels valued, supported, and can thrive. We build an environment that welcomes a wide range of perspectives and experiences, with inclusion embedded in every aspect of our culture and reflected in everyday interactions. This comes to life through comprehensive benefits, workplace flexibility, professional development opportunities, and a host of opportunities provided through our Employee Resource Groups. Each employee plays a role in creating our inclusive culture, which supports every individual to do their best work. Together, we cultivate a community where everyone can make a meaningful impact for our business, our customers, and the communities we serve.

We value your hard work, integrity and commitment to make things better, and we put people first by offering you benefits that support your life and well-being. To learn more about our benefit offerings please visit: https://www.libertymutualgroup.com/about-lm/careers/benefits

Liberty Mutual is an equal opportunity employer. We will not tolerate discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, age, disability, veteran's status, pregnancy, genetic information or on any basis prohibited by federal, state or local law.

Fair Chance Notices

  • California
  • Los Angeles Incorporated
  • Los Angeles Unincorporated
  • Philadelphia
  • San Francisco

Initiates calls to injured worker and medical provider if projected disability exceeds maximum triage model projection or to resolve medical treatment issues as needed. Maintains contact with injured worker, provider and employer to ensure understanding of protocols and claims processing and medical treatment.
  • Continually assesses claim status to determine if problem cases or those exceeding protocols should be referred to Claims Service Team and/or would benefit from, MP RN review or other medical /claims resources. Arranges Independent Medical Exam and Peer Review as necessary.
  • Maintains accurate records and handles administrative responsibilities associated with processing and payment of claims. Records and updates status notes; documents result of contacts, relevant medical reports, and duration information per file posting standards including making appropriate medical information viewable to customers in Electronic Document Management (EDM). Generates form letters following set guidelines (i.e., letters to physicians projecting disability, letters confirming medical treatment and disability and letters outlining expected outcome to employers).
  • Authorizes payment of medical payments and/or medical treatment.
  • Recognizes potential subrogation cases, prepares cases for subrogation and refers these cases to the Subrogation Units.
Qualifications
  • High school diploma plus 1-3 years' of related customer service experience or applicable insurance knowledge.
  • Licensing may be required in some jurisdictions
  • Effective written skills to compose clear, succinct descriptions when posting files and drafting correspondence.
  • Good telephone and typing skills required
  • Ability to learn when to make proper use of medical management resources, know when to use them and follow through with medical management information received.

Job.JobTitle: Vice President, Insurance Investment Solutions - Liberty Mutual Investments
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Boston, MA
  • Experience: 15+ years
  • Education: Bachelor's degree

About this job

Vice President role at Liberty Mutual Investments' Boston office focusing on insurance investment solutions. You will advise investment teams on how investments function within insurance balance sheets, monitor regulatory and accounting trends, and shape portfolio strategy across statutory accounting, regulatory capital, and rating agency frameworks.

Good fit if you have deep knowledge of insurance statutory accounting, NAIC reporting, regulatory capital frameworks, and experience translating complex regulations into investment strategy.

Full job description


Description

The Company

Liberty Mutual Investments (LMI) is the investment firm for Liberty Mutual Group (Liberty) andis responsible forpowering Libertys strategy amid profound change in global capital markets. With deep expertise in fixed income, equity, and alternative strategies,LMI invests $120+ billion (as of 12/31/2025) of capital globally,taking a long-term approach across its integrated platform and has a team of over 350 investment, finance, and operations professionals located in Boston, MA, and New York, NY.

LMI has a clear purpose: build enduring businesses side-by-side with our partners, drive economic growth, and generate superior risk-adjusted returns that power Libertys strategy and secure its promises.Weoffer the best of both worlds the look and feel of a boutique investment firm with the reputation and financial strength of a global leader. As the investment firm of a mutual with long-term capital, LMI has a single client mandate. This gives us the freedom to focus on what we do best.

Our portfolio spans a broad spectrum of public and private investments, and we are committed to expanding our capabilities and our toolkit in support of our mission. We invest across diverse asset classes, financial structures, and industries, including real estate, digital infrastructure, healthcare, renewable energy, and technologywith the aim of creating value and powering innovation. We pride ourselves on our extensive network of mutually beneficial partnerships, and we use our substantial influence, capital, and energy to drive towards a better future.#LMI #LI-LMI

The Position

As Vice President, you will serve as LMI's authority on how investments behave inside an insurance balance sheet. You will work with investment teams to propose structuring guidance, and work with Liberty's regulatory and accounting teams to bring a business perspective to interpretation, ensuring commercial objectives and technical prudence are weighed together. You will monitor regulatory, accounting, and industry trends, events, activities, and emerging structures, both to identify new opportunities for Liberty and to flag changes that may affect existing investments and current asset allocation. Working with the regulatory, accounting, and legal teams to understand the issues, you will be responsible for management actions that address needed changes in the current portfolio and for proposing emerging investment opportunities. While the regulatory, accounting, legal, and capital teams hold responsibility for final interpretations, it is this position's role to bring all relevant aspects together, in partnership with Portfolio Managers, to craft the business case for management actions on the existing portfolio and the business case for new opportunities. This role offers significant visibility with senior leaders and a unique opportunity to shape investment strategy at enterprise scale, which is critical to LMI's success given today's rapidly evolving insurance regulatory, accounting, and investment landscape.

Responsibilities

Insurance Statutory Accounting & Regulatory Frameworks

  • Serve as GSCA's subject-matter expert on statutory accounting (SAP/SSAP), NAIC reporting, RBC treatment, SVO filings, and rating agency capital frameworks as they apply to investments.
  • Work with Liberty's regulatory and accounting teams to bring a business perspective to interpretation, ensuring commercial objectives and technical prudence are weighed together, and provide a strategic investment lens to total company portfolio design and to the assessment of new investment opportunities and structures.
  • Assess and communicate the statutory accounting, regulatory capital, and rating agency treatment of new and existing investments across the General Account, in partnership with regulatory and accounting teams, recognizing that final interpretations rest with the regulatory, accounting, legal, and capital teams.
  • Monitor U.S. insurance regulatory developments, NAIC initiatives, statutory accounting changes, and rating agency criteria; translate them into actionable recommendations for portfolio design and legal entity strategy.
  • Partner with Investment, Risk, Operations, Compliance, Legal, and Financial Reporting teams to embed insurance regulatory and accounting considerations into new products, asset classes, and portfolio strategies. Lead cross-functional initiatives.

Industry Investment Strategies & Trends

  • Monitor regulatory, accounting, and industry trends, events, activities, and emerging structures to identify new opportunities for Liberty and to flag changes that may affect existing investments and current asset allocation.
  • Monitor broad insurance industry investment strategies, asset allocation trends, and market developments, producing executive-ready insights for the CIO, GSCA, and Liberty Group Finance.
  • Identify emerging industry investment trends (new asset classes, structures, and capital solutions gaining adoption across insurance general accounts) and assess their relevance for Liberty.
  • Deliver industry insight as a direct input into capital allocation decisions and investment risk posture.

New Investment Structures, Opportunities & Management Actions

  • Work with investment teams to propose structuring guidance for new investment opportunities, ensuring insurance treatment is considered from inception.
  • Evaluate new and emerging investment structures and opportunities for capital efficiency and fit within Liberty's insurance balance sheets, spanning regulatory, solvency, statutory accounting, and rating agency dimensions.
  • Work with the regulatory, accounting, and legal teams to understand emerging issues; take responsibility for management actions to address changes needed in the current portfolio, including adapting existing investment structures to maintain long-term portfolio viability.
  • Bring all relevant aspects together (regulatory, accounting, legal, capital, and investment) in partnership with Portfolio Managers to craft the business case for management actions on the existing portfolio and the business case for new and emerging investment opportunities.
  • Support GSCA initiatives with research and analytical depth related to regulatory, accounting, or market shifts.

AI, Automation, and Tool-Building

  • Direct the development of AI-driven tools leveraging LLMs, APIs, and modern data platforms to scale insight generation, judgment leverage, scenario analysis, and regulatory and industry trend monitoring, and further expand efficiency.
Qualifications

Domain & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, economics, mathematics, or related field; advanced degree, CPA, or CFA a plus.
  • 1015 years of experience in insurance investments, insurance finance, regulatory or statutory accounting, banking, consulting, or related fields, with meaningful exposure to regulated financial institutions.
  • Deep expertise in insurance statutory accounting (SAP/SSAP), NAIC reporting and RBC frameworks, and rating agency capital models; direct insurance company or insurance-focused experience strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated fluency across regulatory regimes relevant to a global insurer (e.g., NAIC/RBC, Solvency II, Bermuda BSCR) and their implications for investment strategy.
  • Strong understanding of asset allocation, general account portfolio management, and both traditional and alternative asset classes.

Analytical & Investment Skills

  • Experience evaluating investment structures (e.g., rated feeder notes, CLOs, CFOs, asset-backed finance) for insurance balance sheet fit a plus; the emphasis is on regulatory, accounting, and capital treatment rather than deal structuring.
  • Exceptional analytical skills, strategic thinking, and problem-solving capability.

Technology & Tools

  • Familiarity with LLMs (e.g., ChatGPT), Python, Excel, and PowerPoint; familiarity with modern data architectures (e.g., Snowflake). Direct experience is a plus.
  • Familiarity with Bloomberg, BlackRock Aladdin, Power BI, VBA, or other financial and analytical tools is a plus.

Leadership & Communication

  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and communicate complex regulatory and accounting topics clearly to senior stakeholders.
  • Outstanding business acumen, organizational skills, and the ability to manage multiple high-priority projects under tight timelines.
  • Superior communication and listening skills; able to translate complex issues into clear, actionable narratives to influence and persuade a broad range of partners.
About Us

We build an environment that welcomes a wide range of perspectives and experiences, with inclusion embedded in every aspect of our culture and reflected in everyday interactions. This comes to life through comprehensive benefits, workplace flexibility, professional development opportunities, and a host of opportunities provided through our Employee Resource Groups. Each employee plays a role in creating our inclusive culture, which supports every individual to do their best work. Together, we cultivate a community where everyone can make a meaningful impactforour business, our customers, and the communities we serve.

We value your hard work,integrityand commitment to make things better, and we put people first by offering you benefits that support your life and well-being. To learn more about our benefit offerings please visit:https://www.libertymutualgroup.com/about-lm/careers/benefits

At Liberty Mutual, were committed to delivering exceptional legal services to our customers around the world, working to uphold and protect our policyholders rights and positively impacting our business.

As an attorney at Liberty Mutual, youll join a diverse team that values a healthy work/life balance and enjoy benefits that include eligible performance bonuses, 20 days of flexible time off each year, personal holidays, a 401(k) plan with matching contributions. If youre looking for a place to build a long-term career while making a positive difference, consider joining our legal team where youll represent Liberty Mutual and our policyholders.

We have an exciting opportunity for a Workers' Compensation Attorney admitted and residing in Nevada. You will be handling a caseload of workers compensation matters, conduct depositions, and represent Liberty Mutual and its policyholders at WC hearings. You will also interact with Liberty Mutuals Workers Compensation claims organization.

Responsibilities:

  • Use Litigation Protocols to develop and revise appropriate legal strategy for discovery, investigation, handling and trial/hearing of cases or matters.
  • Responsible for appearances before the Workers Compensation Board, conducting depositions, drafting, and filing summations, appeals and rebuttals.

  • Advise, communicate and confer with Claims Representatives and Insured Clients, rendering clear, unambiguous legal opinions and advice.Personally meet with and maintain good relations and communications with Claims Representatives and Insured Clients as required.

  • Provide daily direction and guidance to junior attorneys.
  • Understand and creatively use technology; apply technology to the process of law to improve quality and reduce cost.
  • Act as a team or group leader for an assigned group handling workers compensation cases.
  • Interface with Home Office Legal department.

  • Admission to the bar in Nevadaand in good standing; special licenses to practice before particular boards or federal courts may be required.
  • Minimum of 5 years of successful attorney experience,Workers Compensation experience required.
  • Must have experience with settlement conferences, expedited hearings and conducting depositions; trial experience preferred.
  • Proven experience managing moderately complex litigation with demonstrated success in achieving favorable outcomes.
  • General knowledge of insurance law, and as necessary, workers compensation and/or No Fault law.

Full job description


Description

We are looking for an Insurance Sales Associate to join our team in our Buffalo, NY office. This position has IN OFFICE requirement.

Were Hiring Immediately!

As an Insurance Sales Associate, you will work alongside with and support a Comparion Insurance Sales Agent in profitable growth through new business sales and customer retention. Your ability to listen and empathize are key in being the initial contact for our customers. Success in this role will require building a strong local network and in-person relationship in the community.

Working for Comparion Insurance Agency, a Liberty Mutual company, means working for a company thats committed to advancing an inclusive environment. We do that through leadership development programs aimed at advancing, engaging, and retaining under-represented talent and our Employee Resource Groups, which strengthen our inclusive workplace, enhance personal development, and provide ways for employees to connect, learn and engage.

Ready to find out what it means to work for an agency that is backed by Liberty Mutuala Fortune 100 company thats committed to putting people first, acting responsibly and making things better?

Responsibilities:

  • Utilize consultative sales techniques to prospect and initiate new business sales.
  • Assists in the processing of new business, including contacting customers to finalize sales and service transactions.
  • Identifies cross selling opportunities for Sales Agent.
  • Contributes to and executes a marketing plan with the Sales Agent.
  • Identifies mass marketing prospects through existing book of business and community prospecting opportunities.
  • Meet monthly goals for new business sales.
  • Completes follow-ups on new policies in order to keep retention level high and capitalize cross-selling opportunities.
  • Coordinates activities with other departments to ensure quality customer service
  • Acts as initial contact in addressing customer concerns regarding establishment of policies and new account status.
  • Unlicensed candidates will be enrolled in a new hire training class once they begin working for Comparion. The training includes a licensing training program in which Comparion covers the cost of training materials and exam fees.
Qualifications
  • High School Degree
  • 1-2 years of relevant sales experience preferred
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to handle common objections and educate customers in a consultative manner
  • Demonstrated self-starter, motivated to learn and grow in a professional sales organization
  • Professional business acumen, strong presence and confidence
  • Resourceful team player that can contribute and accept new ideas
  • A state insurance licenseor willingness to earn one with training and supportin Property & Casualty, and Life

Description

Join our team as a SeniorCommercial Lines Specialist, helping small businesses find the right coverage through consultative sales and tailored insurance solutions. In this fast-paced role, youll prospect new opportunities, build lasting client and referral relationships, and work with multiple carriers to deliver quality coverage and service.

Hiring locations: We are seeking candidates based in Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Connecticut, Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, New York, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Maryland, Delaware, and Washington, D.C.

Responsible for prospecting, generating, developing, and managing a book of small commercial insurance business. Counsels and advises prospects and policyholders on matters of protection and coverage. Is responsible for a specific volume of quality new business quoted and written within company guidelines. This role combines prospecting and new-business production with consultative sales, quoting through multiple carriers, and coordinating policy placement and renewals.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Source and develop new small commercial accounts (typically business accounts with revenues under $10M) through prospecting, referrals, networking, and inbound leads.
  • Utilizes coverage knowledge to counsel and advise prospects and existing policyholders on matters of protection and coverage based on a needs and exposure assessment by obtaining data and relative information concerning their business. Recommend appropriate insurance solutions (BOP, general liability, property, commercial auto, workers compensation, cyber, umbrella and surety/bonds).
  • Conducts front-line underwriting risk evaluation in accordance with established rules and guidelines. Prepare and present quotes and proposals by obtaining/comparing quotes from multiple carriers using agency management systems, CRM and carrier panel rating platforms.
  • Meets goals for volume of quality new business and cross sell opportunities quoted and written within company guidelines.
  • Works collaboratively with internal and agency partners to deliver a best-in-class customer experience.
  • Build relationships and trust with referring agents within the region to build COI/lead generation streams
  • Provide timely service for endorsements, cancellations, audits, and claims liaison as needed.
  • Stay current on carrier appetite, new products, underwriting guidelines, and industry trends.
Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with common small commercial products: BOP, general liability, property, commercial auto, workers compensation, cyber, umbrella and surety/bonds
  • Experience with networking, prospecting for new business and driving top of funnel leads from various sources
  • Experience using agency management systems, comparative raters
  • Strong verbal and written communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills
  • Property & Casualty license (or progress toward them. You will be required to obtain relevant licenses upon being hired.)

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience selling small commercial lines in an independent agency or carrier distribution channel
  • Proven track record of meeting production targets; demonstrated book of business or established referral sources

Skills & Competencies:

  • Consultative sales approach and client-focused problem solving.
  • Demonstrated analytical skills to understand complex coverage details and underwriting guidelines clearly to small-business owners
  • Collaborative mindset and comfortable working in a high-volume agency environment.
  • Highly effective verbal and written communication, persuasion and negotiation skills.
  • Ability to build a sphere of influence in the community and participate in community networking activities
  • Effective time management and ability to work well independently in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to navigate numerous computerized data entry systems or other relevant applications simultaneously while advising customers
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent business background plus a minimum of 1-3 years of insurance or sales/service-related work experience.

In this fast-paced role, youll prospect new opportunities, build lasting client and referral relationships, and work with multiple carriers to deliver quality coverage and service.

Hiring locations: We are seeking candidates based in Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Connecticut, Maine, New Hampshire, Vermont, New York, Pennsylvania, New Jersey, Maryland, Delaware, and Washington, D.C.

Responsible for prospecting, generating, developing, and managing a book of small commercial insurance business. Counsels and advises prospects and policyholders on matters of protection and coverage. Is responsible for a specific volume of quality new business quoted and written within company guidelines. This role combines prospecting and new-business production with consultative sales, quoting through multiple carriers, and coordinating policy placement and renewals.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Source and develop new small commercial accounts (typically business accounts with revenues under $10M) through prospecting, referrals, networking, and inbound leads.
  • Utilizes coverage knowledge to counsel and advise prospects and existing policyholders on matters of protection and coverage based on a needs and exposure assessment by obtaining data and relative information concerning their business. Recommend appropriate insurance solutions (BOP, general liability, property, commercial auto, workers compensation, cyber, umbrella and surety/bonds).
  • Conducts front-line underwriting risk evaluation in accordance with established rules and guidelines. Prepare and present quotes and proposals by obtaining/comparing quotes from multiple carriers using agency management systems, CRM and carrier panel rating platforms.
  • Meets goals for volume of quality new business and cross sell opportunities quoted and written within company guidelines.
  • Works collaboratively with internal and agency partners to deliver a best-in-class customer experience.
  • Build relationships and trust with referring agents within the region to build COI/lead generation streams
  • Provide timely service for endorsements, cancellations, audits, and claims liaison as needed.
  • Stay current on carrier appetite, new products, underwriting guidelines, and industry trends.
Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with common small commercial products: BOP, general liability, property, commercial auto, workers compensation, cyber, umbrella and surety/bonds
  • Experience with networking, prospecting for new business and driving top of funnel leads from various sources
  • Experience using agency management systems, comparative raters
  • Strong verbal and written communication, negotiation, and relationship-building skills
  • Property & Casualty license (or progress toward them. You will be required to obtain relevant licenses upon being hired.)

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience selling small commercial lines in an independent agency or carrier distribution channel
  • Proven track record of meeting production targets; demonstrated book of business or established referral sources

Skills & Competencies:

  • Consultative sales approach and client-focused problem solving.
  • Demonstrated analytical skills to understand complex coverage details and underwriting guidelines clearly to small-business owners
  • Collaborative mindset and comfortable working in a high-volume agency environment.
  • Highly effective verbal and written communication, persuasion and negotiation skills.
  • Ability to build a sphere of influence in the community and participate in community networking activities
  • Effective time management and ability to work well independently in a fast-paced environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to navigate numerous computerized data entry systems or other relevant applications simultaneously while advising customers
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent business background plus a minimum of 1-3 years of insurance or sales/service-related work experience.
About Us

Pay Philosophy: The typical starting salary range for this role is determined by a number of factors including skills, experience, education, certifications and location. The full salary range for this role reflects the competitive labor market value for all employees in these positions across the national market and provides an opportunity to progress as employees grow and develop within the role. Some roles at Liberty Mutual have a corresponding compensation plan which may include commission and/or bonus earnings at rates that vary based on multiple factors set forth in the compensation plan for the role.

In 2022, Comparion Insurance Agency was created to transition former Liberty Mutual exclusive agents to an agency that delivers a unique value proposition to carriers with over 2,000 agents in approximately 180 cities in 44 states. We offer customers 50 insurance companies with product breadth including auto, home, life, pet, renters, umbrella, jewelry and much more. We use our scale to deliver a first-rate customer experience through consultative insurance experts located in their communities.

Our Leadership team has over 200 years of cumulative insurance experience. At Comparion, we have a philosophy of staying close to our customers and agents, so sales leadership is located throughout the country in our larger storefronts. Comparion is owned and backed by Liberty Mutual Group, a Fortune 100 company, founded in 1912

Liberty Mutual is an equal opportunity employer. We will not tolerate discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, age, disability, veteran's status, pregnancy, genetic information or on any basis prohibited by federal, state or local law.

About this job

Senior Commercial Lines Specialist at Comparion selling small commercial insurance (under $10M revenue) through consultative sales and multiple carriers. Role combines prospecting, quoting, and policy placement with relationship building across New England, Mid-Atlantic, and D.C. regions.

Good fit if you have P&C license, 1-3 years insurance or sales experience, and knowledge of commercial products like BOP, liability, and workers compensation.

Position Summary

Under minimal supervision, settles claims within limits of authority.

  • Work location: The selected candidate will report to the Knowledge Park Office.
  • There are multiple positions available.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Processes first party automobile, third party clear liability automobile and low severity property claims within limits of authority. The Role at a Glance

As a Compliance Consultant, you will conduct in-person and remote inspections of broker-dealer offices to examine procedures and activities of registered representatives, managers, and broker-dealer personnel for compliance with company and industry rules.

You will also assist with managing and maintaining the Audit Management System, including audit scheduling, workflow monitoring, issue tracking, and documentation to support regulatory and internal compliance requirements.

What you'll be doing

• Scheduling, planning, and preparing pre-inspection materials.
• Reviewing representative activities including non-cash compensation, social media, and outside business activities.
• Conducting inspections of wholesaling practices, recordkeeping, and compliance procedures.
• Interviewing representatives, managers, and administrative personnel.
• Preparing inspection reports and follow-up actions.
• Responding to compliance inquiries.
• Remaining familiar with FINRA and state regulatory developments.
• Interacting with audit resource vendors.
• Completing expense reports and paperwork.
• Administering and supporting the Audit Management System.
• Working on additional special projects as assigned.
• Traveling regularly (about 15%).

What we're looking for

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience.
• 3-5 years of securities and/or insurance experience.
• Basic knowledge of SEC, FINRA, and state insurance regulations.
• Intermediate compliance risk management knowledge.
• Basic knowledge of variable annuities, variable life insurance, and defined contribution programs.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and AI tools.
• Strong relationship management skills.
• Process improvement experience.
• Strong organizational skills.
• Sound judgment with confidential information.

Certifications
• FINRA Series 6 or Series 7 required within 90 days of hire.

The Role at a Glance

The Lead Software Engineer provides technical leadership for Lincoln Financial Data Strategy and Delivery team. This role designs, builds, and maintains scalable data pipelines and optimizes data systems, with deep experience in Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon Redshift and strong knowledge of AWS services including Glue, Lambda, S3, Athena, and EC2. The role leads a team of data engineers, owns delivery, sets technical vision, and partners with business, IT, and analytics stakeholders to deliver secure, governed, high-quality data that enables advanced analytics and reporting across Lincoln.

What you'll be doing

  • Lead and prioritize work, own delivery, set standards and a clear technical vision, review code, mentor engineers, and grow future leaders.
  • Design, build, and maintain robust batch and streaming data pipelines (including change data capture, for example AWS DMS) to support business intelligence and analytics.
  • Integrate structured and unstructured data from internal and external sources.
  • Develop ETL workflows using AWS Glue, Lambda, custom Python, PySpark, and SQL-based scripts.
  • Analyze database workloads and optimize queries, indexing, partitioning, and storage in Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon Redshift for integrity, performance, and cost.
  • Build S3-based data lake and warehouse layers (Glue Data Catalog, Athena, Parquet) with fine-grained access controls.
  • Own end-to-end data flows from source to consumption; trace and resolve issues across the full chain.
  • Apply data modeling standards (normal form, star, snowflake) and data quality practices; create technical designs from business requirements.
  • Orchestrate and schedule workflows (Stonebranch, Step Functions, Airflow / MWAA) and monitor them with CloudWatch and automated data quality checks.
  • Ensure data security, governance, and compliance; monitor, troubleshoot, and optimize data workflows.
  • Integrate with upstream and downstream applications and collaborate with data scientists, analysts, and business stakeholders to deliver high-quality datasets; help shape data infrastructure strategy on AWS.

What we're looking for

Must-haves:

  • Bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field.
  • 7+ years in AWS data engineering or a similar role (confirm years for Lead level).
  • Proven leadership: leading a team, owning delivery of complex projects, and communicating clearly with stakeholders; a strong vision and drive to develop as a leader.
  • Strong expertise in Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon Redshift, including database analysis, query optimization, advanced SQL, execution plans, indexing, distribution and sort keys, and workload tuning.
  • Holistic view of end-to-end data processing, from source to consumption, including dependencies, bottlenecks, and downstream impact.
  • Data and application integration with upstream source systems and downstream consumers (APIs, files, messaging, reporting).
  • Hands-on AWS experience: Glue, Lambda, S3, Athena, EC2, and IAM.
  • Python / PySpark and SQL development for ETL and integration in Agile, SDLC-based environments.
  • DevOps and scheduling: Git, CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, CloudFormation or similar, and Stonebranch scheduling knowledge (or a similar scheduler such as Autosys).
  • Hands-on use of approved AI development tools (GitHub Copilot or Claude Code), validating AI output and following Lincoln data privacy and responsible AI requirements.

Nice-to-haves:

  • AWS certification (Data Engineer – Associate, Solutions Architect, or specialty); EMR, Kinesis, Lake Formation, DynamoDB, or Apache Iceberg experience.
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot and Claude Cowork experience; coaching teams on safe AI use.
  • RAG data preparation, embeddings, vector stores, and AWS AI services (Bedrock, SageMaker, Amazon Q).
  • Salesforce CRM and MuleSoft (API-led integration) as upstream or downstream systems; MicroStrategy and Tableau reporting and BI background.
  • Financial data experience is a plus, especially insurance, annuities, or retirement (401k/403b).
