What Is the Opportunity?

Product Development teams play a critical role in the development and achievement of Travelers financial objectives (growth, profit & retention) for one or more insurance products through the development, implementation and monitoring of product strategies and corresponding actions.

As a Dir, Product Development, Northfield Excess and Surplus Lines, you lead policy coverage form development for Northfield, Travelers' non-admitted program written in all 50 states and DC.

You will have responsibility for crafting E&S coverage forms, rules and guidelines behind Northfield's lines of business including General Liability, Property, Excess, and other misc. lines such as Inland Marine. Northfield's policies sold through appointed wholesalers in the Binding and Brokerage Solutions channels. This position may coach, provide feedback and/or oversee a team.

What Will You Do?

  • Lead coverage form development for Northfield E&S to achieve business objectives including growth, profit and retention objectives, influencing key stakeholders to gain consensus on recommendations.
  • Own proprietary and manuscript coverage form and endorsements that support unique E&S terms and conditions, partnering with BI Product Development on drafting, PDCA review and other teams for NorthLink implementation.
  • Influence and communicate strategies and associated action plans with key stakeholders and related initiatives to gain consensus for recommendations.
  • Oversee and execute market, competitor, and consumer research analysis to identify and recommend new products, markets and services or enhance existing ones.
  • Proactively develop solutions to product challenges and gain buy-in from key stakeholders to adopt recommendations.
  • Manage the design, development, and implementation of system and process solutions that align with the product's strategy.
  • Identify and test new products, markets or partnership opportunities or enhance existing ones by collaborating with stakeholders and other entities and vendors.
  • Lead and guide a team for product enhancement work including launch and rollout plans related to product strategies and action plans.
  • Ensure strategies and plans address compliance needs and regulatory requirements.
  • Oversee development of communication, training, and marketing materials in support of new or enhanced products and initiatives.
  • Manage monitoring and measurement mechanisms for product strategies and initiatives in support of outlined strategic success criteria and present findings and recommendations to leadership.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

  • Bachelor's Degree.
  • Six years of product development experience, preferably in Excess and Surplus Lines or commercial insurance.
  • One year people management experience.
  • Expert understanding of non-admitted products, underwriting, coverage, rules, forms, and the insurance regulatory environment across GL, Property, Excess Casualty, Inland Marine and Auto Liability.
  • Familiarity with wholesale distribution, including binding authority and brokerage models.
  • Able to interpret business specific translations and solutions.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills with the ability to interact and influence management.
  • Proven innovation skills including thinking critically about multiple perspectives and approaches to solving problems.

  • Excellent analytical skills with the ability to evaluate and understand current data and systems, find deficiencies/opportunities, recommend changes, and translate into business impacts.

What Is the Opportunity?

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. now and in the future. The company does not sponsor/support H-1B petitions, TN, or Forms I-983/STEM OPT, for this role. Applications for this posting will be reviewed on a rolling basis. We encourage you to apply as soon as possible. Are you curious by nature? Do you enjoy managing relationships and employing your critical thinking skills? Underwriters perform the critical function of evaluating the acceptability of risk and determining appropriate pricing for insurance products. The Business Insurance (BI) Underwriting Professional Development Internship Program provides students with an amazing opportunity to gain exposure to this critical function at Travelers. The 10-week program (running from early June to mid-August) provides qualified interns with an excellent opportunity to gain first-hand commercial insurance underwriting experience, receive valuable on-the-job training, and learn more about the property and casualty insurance industry from industry professionals. Given that, we are seeking interns that are serious about entering the insurance industry and who are excited about the prospect of making underwriting their future career choice. This role is a potential pathway to our full-time Underwriting Professional Development Program (UPDP). Housing assistance is not provided.

What Will You Do?

  • Within your assigned business unit, each intern will be given a designated coach and be expected to:
  • Complete core assignments and training modules geared toward insurance and underwriting principles.
  • Participate and complete self-paced professional development courses in time management, presentation skills, and other key areas.
  • Complete challenging and meaningful project work over the course of this program at the discretion of your manager. You may work independently or with other interns and will be asked to present your findings to local leadership. Sample projects include a territorial risk assessment to determine profitability and underwriting opportunities as well as a business process analysis to determine underwriting gaps.
  • Learn to leverage modern analytical and artificial intelligence (AI) tools/platforms with the ability to apply critical thinking to evaluate limitations related to quality and accuracy of AI-assisted outputs.
  • Learn about other areas at Travelers such as Risk Control, Claims, and related corporate functions. Interns may also engage in agency visits with Account Executives.
  • Participate in the Enterprise Internship experience which includes Executive Speaker Series, Networking events, and Rising Senior Intern Symposium.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What Will Our Ideal Candidate Have?

  • Preferred cumulative GPA of 3.0 or above.
  • Obtained or pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Economics, Finance, Liberal Arts (with business focus preferred), Management, Marketing, Risk Management and Insurance.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Office.

What is a Must Have?

  • Pursuing or obtained a Bachelor's degree.

Travelers is seeking a Sr. Director, Engineering and Operations Effectiveness, to join Business Insurance (BI) Technology as we transform engineering and technology operations. Engineering Excellence and Operations (EXO) leads engineering transformation and modernization across BI Technology.

In this role you will lead the function that connects EXO's three functional areas, Engineering Transformation, Portfolio Modernization, and Technology Operations, to every partner that depends on them. That includes Value Streams, Operations, Planning & Execution, and various enterprise partners.

In that capacity, you are accountable for EXO's engagement model, emerging demand pipeline, vendor and contract strategy, operational metrics our leadership team makes decisions from, and a team of Delivery Leads embedded across the portfolio. Since this is a change catalyst role, you are expected to drive delivery effectiveness, leverage and infuse AI throughout our delivery practices, and ensure a unified stakeholder engagement model.

This role plans at a strategic level and manages the effective use of resources. Directs assigned staff to implement and/or maintain systems and/or assigned project(s). Moderate to broad scope of responsibility as defined by such things as span of control, number of systems/projects, and/or complexity of systems/projects. Provides talent management to team members.

What Will You Do?

  • Own EXO's Unified Engagement Model across its core stakeholder groups and full functional portfolio including engineering transformation, application modernization, vendor provisioned Managed Services, and production operations.
  • Own emerging demand end to end. Be the single source of truth for demand coming into EXO from the enterprise and the value streams. Run the intake and demand forums, drive prioritization with the functional leads and other stakeholders, and manage demand from intake through readiness and implementation.
  • Own EXO vendor and technology contract management. Be the single point of accountability for contracts, vendor management, and cost. Rationalize the portfolio, drive equivalent terms and cost reduction across vendors, and reshape vendor scope and pricing as AI changes expectations.
  • Build and lead the EXO delivery center of excellence. Transform delivery practice from separate functional interpretations into one repeatable standard, with the playbooks, cadences, and assessments to sustain it.
  • Own EXO metrics and reporting for EXO's partners and stakeholders. Define the reporting requirements, govern the underlying data and engineering health indicators, and produce reporting that drives decisions.
  • Lead the Delivery Lead team. The Delivery Leads report to you and are matrixed into the functional areas. You set the standard for what a Delivery Lead does here: planning rigor, execution discipline, dependency management, impediment removal, and insights leaders can act on.   • Directs assigned staff to implement and/or maintain systems of high complexity and/or projects of major business unit significance.

About this job

Senior Insights Analyst role at Assurant in Miami focused on converting complex data into actionable recommendations for leaders and clients. Position combines hands-on analytics with project leadership, mentoring, and modernizing reporting capabilities using tools like Azure, Python, SQL, and Power BI.

Good fit if you have 7+ years in data analysis, advanced SQL and Power BI skills, experience with predictive modeling, and can lead analytical projects independently.

Full job description

We are looking for a Senior Insights Analyst to turn complex data into clear, actionable recommendations for senior leaders, internal business partners, and external client audiences. This is a hands-on individual contributor role for someone who can work independently across the full analytics lifecycle, shape ambiguous business questions, mentor fellow analysts, and deliver trusted insights that influence decisions.


What will be my duties and responsibilities in this job?

You will lead analytical projects and own high-visibility insight deliverables that support business performance, client relationships, operational strategy, and executive-level decision-making. You will balance hands-on analysis and modeling with project leadership, peer mentoring, and the continued modernization of the team's reporting and insight capabilities.


Create value through data

  • Produce clear, insightful, understandable work products, including presentations, visualizations, and dashboards, that outline business opportunities and actionable recommendations.
  • Transform data into insights using internal and external tools such as Azure, Python, SQL, Excel, and Power BI to identify and quantify opportunities.
  • Build studies that add substantial value to the decision-making process through proactive data analysis and research.

Deliver predictive insights

  • Translate business challenges into predictive modeling opportunities and collaborate with stakeholders to define forward-looking questions.
  • Build and validate ad-hoc predictive models using techniques such as regression, time series forecasting, and classification.

Lead projects and mentor teammates

  • Lead projects and assist in the development of project plans, conducting analysis and modeling, testing hypotheses, presenting complex information to various audiences in simplified terms, and identifying next steps and future opportunities.
  • Mentor team members in technical proficiency, code reviews, and business acumen.
  • Collaborate with team members to prioritize requests that require multiple resources so projects are completed thoroughly and within stated timelines.

Support data strategy and governance

  • Participate in and help drive data modeling and governance best practices across Power BI, Microsoft Fabric, and related analytics environments.
  • Proactively engage internal and external teams to discover areas of analytical need before they arrive as requests.
  • Advance company-wide understanding and implementation of AI and machine learning, and help mature the team's practices and procedures by leveraging learnings from existing implementations.

Communicate insights

  • Leverage data to present compelling business cases that optimize investments and operations.
  • Communicate with and educate both technical and non-technical employees on analytics and data-driven decision making.

Lead analytics products

  • Work cross-functionally with business owners to develop innovative advanced analytics products that improve customer experience, capitalize on growth opportunities, deliver competitive advantage, and improve decision making.

What will success look like in this role?

In your first 90 days

  • You understand the team, the business partners, the reporting portfolio, the data estate, and the highest-value decision points your work supports.
  • You are working independently on assigned projects and delivering analysis that is accurate, reproducible, and clearly communicated.
  • You have built working relationships with key business partners and understand how requests are prioritized.

By six months

  • You are leading analytical projects from scoping through delivery and presenting insights and recommendations to senior leaders or client audiences with confidence.
  • You have identified recurring reporting and manual processes that should be automated, consolidated, or moved into governed self-service.
  • Your code reviews and feedback are helping teammates raise the quality of their analysis and documentation.

By twelve months

  • You are a trusted partner to business stakeholders and are engaged early in decisions, helping shape the question rather than only responding after the request is fully defined.
  • You have delivered at least one predictive or advanced analytics product that is adopted and used in decision making.
  • You have contributed to more standardized, governed, and better-documented Power BI and Fabric assets that stakeholders find easier to trust and use.
  • At least one teammate has grown into more complex work through your mentoring.

What are the requirements needed for this position?

  • Master's degree in Business Analytics, Statistics, Economics, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, Information Management, or a related quantitative field; equivalent work experience may be considered.
  • 7+ years of experience in business analysis, research, statistics, applied mathematics, data management, business intelligence, or a related field.
  • 7+ years of experience with data science tools (e.g., R, Python, SQL, Advanced Excel, Power BI) and relational database software.
  • 7+ years of experience in data analysis that includes translating insights into recommendations.
  • 5+ years of experience leading analytical projects.
  • Experience performing statistical analyses, such as predictive modeling, time series analysis, exploratory data analysis, segmentation and cluster analysis, and retention analysis.

Technical requirements

  • Advanced SQL skills, including complex joins, window functions, CTEs, data validation, and the ability to work directly with enterprise data warehouses.
  • Strong Power BI experience, including data modeling, DAX, semantic model development, and governed self-service analytics.
  • Working knowledge of cloud technologies such as Azure (Databricks, Azure ML, Cognitive Services), or Microsoft Fabric.
  • Advanced Excel skills and comfort using modern analytics, automation, and AI-assisted tools to improve productivity and documentation.

Communication and data storytelling

  • Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively at all levels of the organization.
  • Strong data storytelling skills, including the ability to distill complex information into understandable ideas, business implications, and recommended actions.
  • Strong analytical and research skills, with an innovative approach to problem solving and a track record to demonstrate it.
  • Ability to work independently on all project types.
  • Travel potential of up to 10%.

What other skills/experience would be helpful to have?

  • Degree in statistics, applied mathematics, operations research, economics, engineering, computer science, or a related quantitative field.
  • Experience working in the insurance industry.
  • Experience with Databricks, Azure, Python, R, Copilot, or Claude.
  • Experience modernizing legacy reporting, consolidating dashboards, defining KPI frameworks, and improving semantic models.
  • Hands-on use of AI-assisted coding, documentation, or analytics tools to accelerate analysis and automate recurring work responsibly.
  • A track record of mentoring peers and creating a culture of curiosity, accountability, inclusion, and continuous improvement.

Job.JobDescription:
The Assurant Internship Program is a 12-week immersive experience where interns do not sit on the sidelines. You will gain real-world experience by tackling business challenges and helping drive meaningful outcomes. The program combines hands-on work with learning and development opportunities, mentorship, networking and engagement opportunities, and resources designed to support your professional growth. This program offers students meaningful, real-world experience while building foundational technical and business skills in a Fortune 500 organization.


The Marketing Operations Project Analyst Intern is responsible for strengthening project intake, prioritization, workflow governance, reporting, and process discipline across Marketing Services. This role partners with stakeholders and delivery teams to ensure requests are clearly scoped, appropriately prioritized, consistently managed, and executed through standardized processes. The position uses project management expertise, workflow analytics, and AI-enabled tools to identify efficiencies, reduce manual effort, improve visibility, and support faster, more predictable delivery.


Project Management and Delivery Oversight 60%

  • Serve as the primary project management partner for Marketing Services workstreams, ensuring project scope, requirements, timelines, owners, dependencies, and risks are clearly documented and actively managed.
  • Lead intake review and project planning activities to confirm requests are complete, appropriate for the team, aligned with business priorities, and ready for execution.
  • Maintain project plans, task lists, milestones, and status updates within the project management platform to provide timely visibility to stakeholders and leadership.
  • Identify delivery risks, schedule conflicts, resource constraints, and scope changes; escalate issues and recommend mitigation plans to keep work on track.
  • Facilitate project meetings, status reviews, and post-project retrospectives to drive accountability, improve handoffs, and capture lessons learned.

Process Governance and Standardization 20%

  • Develop, document, and maintain standardized processes for project intake, prioritization, routing, workflow management, approvals, reporting, and closure.
  • Establish governance routines that promote consistent use of tools, templates, naming conventions, required fields, workflow steps, and project documentation.
  • Monitor process adherence and follow up with stakeholders when information, approvals, or deliverables are incomplete, delayed, or misaligned with established standards.
  • Analyze workflow trends, bottlenecks, and recurring issues to recommend process improvements that increase speed, quality, transparency, and operational consistency.
  • Partner with team leads and stakeholders to clarify decision rights, escalation paths, service expectations, and handoff responsibilities.

AI-Enabled Workflow Optimization and Reporting 20%

  • Use approved AI tools and automation capabilities to streamline project tracking, status reporting, meeting summaries, action item follow-up, workflow analysis, and process documentation.
  • Identify repeatable tasks and manual reporting steps that can be improved through AI-enabled prompts, templates, dashboards, or automation workflows.
  • Create clear, actionable reporting that translates project data into insights on volume, cycle time, bottlenecks, aging work, prioritization trends, and process compliance.

Apply responsible AI practices, including human review, data protection, prompt quality, and validation of AI-generated outputs before use in business communications or decision support.


Required Qualifications

  • Currently enrolled in an accredited college or university program with at least one academic semester remaining after the internship.
  • Ability to work 40 hours per week for the full Summer 2027 program.
  • Coursework or demonstrated interest in business, marketing, data analytics, communications, operations, project management, or a related field.
  • Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook, and Teams, or the ability to learn them quickly.
  • Ability to organize information, manage deadlines, follow written procedures, and produce accurate work.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills.

About this job

A 12-week summer internship supporting the Account Management team at Assurant's Atlanta office. You will handle account coordination tasks, analyze client performance data, and complete a structured business project with measurable deliverables.

Good fit if you are currently enrolled in college, available full-time in Summer 2027, and have working knowledge of Excel, PowerPoint, and Word.

Full job description

The Assurant Internship Program is a 12-week immersive experience where interns do not sit on the sidelines. You will gain real-world experience by tackling business challenges and helping drive meaningful outcomes. The program combines hands-on work with learning and development opportunities, mentorship, networking and engagement opportunities, and resources designed to support your professional growth. This program offers students meaningful, real-world experience while building foundational technical and business skills in a Fortune 500 organization.


The Account Management Intern will support the Account Management team with the behind-the-scenes work required to serve mortgage servicing clients effectively. This is a development role and is not responsible for owning client relationships, leading client meetings, negotiating commitments, or independently responding to client escalations. The intern will work with account managers, account executives, operational partners, and other internal teams to organize information, analyze performance, prepare materials, track follow-ups, and improve the tools and processes used to support assigned clients.


In addition to day-to-day account support, the intern will own a clearly scoped, meaningful project aligned with team priorities. The project will include defined goals, measurable deliverables, regular checkpoints, and a final capstone presentation describing the work completed, business impact, lessons learned, obstacles addressed, and key takeaways.


What You Will Do

Account Management Support - approximately 50%

· Support preparation for internal account reviews, client business reviews, operational meetings, claims reviews, audits, and other account activities by gathering and organizing approved materials.

· Maintain account support tools such as contact lists, organizational charts, action logs, issue trackers, meeting records, service-release information, acquisition-volume reports, and document repositories.

· Collect information from Operations and other internal partners to help account managers answer client questions and document next steps.

· Draft internal summaries, meeting notes, status updates, presentation content, and background materials for review by an account manager or account executive before use.

· Track open items, owners, target dates, dependencies, and completion status; identify missing information or overdue follow-ups for team review.

· Assist with documenting meeting takeaways, decisions, risks, and action items. The intern may observe selected client meetings for learning but will not serve as the client point of contact.

· Help coordinate logistics and materials for vendor-management reviews, onsite visits, audits, and other account events.

· Follow company requirements for confidentiality, information handling, documentation, and appropriate use of client data.


Reporting, Analysis, and Process Support - approximately 25%

· Compile and organize client performance, service-level, quality, complaint, claims, volume, and operational data from approved sources.

· Perform basic data validation and analysis to identify patterns, missing information, recurring issues, or potential opportunities for improvement.

· Help create clear charts, tables, scorecards, and summaries that enable the account team to explain performance and prepare recommendations.

· Compare information across reports and supporting records, document inconsistencies, and escalate questions to the assigned account manager.

· Research mortgage servicing, property insurance, lender-placed insurance, loss draft, and related industry topics using approved resources, then summarize findings in plain language.

· Suggest practical improvements to templates, trackers, shared files, workflows, and reporting methods based on observations during the internship.


Assigned Business Project - approximately 25%

· Own a structured 12-week project that addresses a real Account Management need and can be completed within the internship period.

· Develop a project plan with scope, objectives, stakeholders, milestones, risks, measures of success, and expected deliverables.

· Gather requirements and feedback from internal stakeholders; document findings and recommendations.

· Provide progress updates during regular manager check-ins and adjust the work based on coaching and business needs.

· Deliver a usable final work product, supporting documentation, and a capstone presentation to leaders and program participants.


Program Participation and Development

· Attend required internship meetings, training sessions, professional-development activities, peer networking events, and weekly one-on-one meetings.

· Participate in the FranklinCovey learning journey and apply the concepts to daily work and project planning.

· Build knowledge of Assurant, Global Housing, Account Management, mortgage servicing, and the products and services supported by the team.

· Ask for guidance, communicate schedule conflicts promptly, and use feedback to improve work quality and professional skills.

· Complete midpoint and final program evaluations and prepare for the final capstone presentation.

· Work the program schedule and accurately submit time in accordance with internship requirements.


Required Qualifications

· Currently enrolled in an accredited college or university program with at least one academic semester remaining after the internship.

· Ability to work 40 hours per week for the full Summer 2027 program.

· Coursework or demonstrated interest in business, finance, risk management, insurance, data analytics, communications, operations, project management, or a related field.

· Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook, and Teams, or the ability to learn them quickly.

· Ability to organize information, manage deadlines, follow written procedures, and produce accurate work.

· Clear written and verbal communication skills.

· Ability to handle confidential business and client information appropriately.


Preferred Qualifications

· Experience through coursework, student organizations, part-time work, or prior internships involving data analysis, reporting, research, presentations, project work, or business operations.

· Comfort working with spreadsheets, trackers, charts, and multiple sources of information.

· Interest in mortgage servicing, financial services, insurance, client management, or business operations.

· Curiosity, learning agility, problem-solving, attention to detail, collaboration, and willingness to ask thoughtful questions.

· Ability to explain findings and recommendations in clear, plain language.

The Role at a Glance

We are excited to bring on highly motivated Supplemental Health Appeals Associate to our team within Workplace Solutions.
As a Supplemental Health (SH) Appeals Associate you will be responsible for being a product subject matter expert to provide full, fair appeal reviews for multiple voluntary product lines. You will perform and complete full, fair reviews and adjudicating appeal decisions on Accident, Critical Illness, and Hospital Indemnity claims for our customers. You will analyze and manage a caseload of SH appeals claims. You will review, investigate, and make appeal determinations regarding coverage, compensability, and appropriateness of claims. You will provide technical information and detailed guidance to Claims management & teams regarding products, claims processes, regulations, and applicable systems for their assigned claims area. If you enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, then please read on!

What you'll be doing

  • You will be communicating with claimants, employers as needed to ensure complete submission of necessary information for appeal review.
  • You will be leveraging knowledge of coverage, certificate provisions, eligibility & benefits as well as other appropriate resources (e.g., other internal teams, practices/procedures, clinical etc.) to include as part of your appeal review.
  • You will be applying core knowledge of Supplemental Health/voluntary insurance products, claims processes and certificates to render appeal decisions
  • You will be identifying, interpreting, and resolving gaps in financial calculations when applicable, share technical knowledge and approach on financial calculations with claims.
  • You will be ensuring appeals processing is consistent with applicable policies, procedures, and department guidelines.
  • You will be researching questions and escalations as needed for complete appeal review; liaises with various stakeholders from across the business (Enrollments, Legal, Compliance, Account Management, etc.) to obtain needed information to clarify and address issues.

What we're looking for

Must-haves:

  • 2+ Years of experience in Supplemental Health Claims: Accident, Critical Illness, Hospital Indemnity. (Required).
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Excellent organizational skills with the ability to multi-task
  • 4 Year/Bachelor's degree (Strongly preferred)

The Role at a Glance

The Actuarial Development Program (ADP) at Lincoln Financial is an industry-leading program that demonstrates Lincoln Financial' s commitment to creating highly qualified business leaders. As an ADP participant, you'll be able to explore your unique interests while developing the essential actuarial, technical, management, communication, and leadership skills you need to succeed. The Actuarial Development Program includes a series of rotations, typically every 18-24 months. For each rotation, roles are available in different business areas including Life and Annuities, Retirement and Group Protection. Experience gained will enable participants to become well-rounded actuaries with knowledge that may include Product Development, Pricing, Valuation, Modeling, Risk Management, Asset Liability Management, Investments, Data Analytics, and Internal Audit.

ADP participants are expected to pass the Society of Actuaries' exams at a prescribed pace. The program is designed to support you as you work towards your FSA and provide the training and resources necessary to become a well-rounded actuarial leader.

Additional Program Highlights:
•Highly competitive compensation package with salary increases and bonuses upon successful exam completion
•Social and training opportunities to enhance skills, network with ADP participants and build long-lasting industry relationships
•Dedicated leaders and mentors to assist with career development
Work with actuarial and data science software and technologies including MG-ALFA, Axis, Prophet, Dataiku, R, and Tableau
•Generous study time allowances for each exam session
•Payment and/or reimbursement of actuarial exam fees, materials, review courses, and seminars taken during the program

We are seeking an Associate Actuary, Internal Audit to apply actuarial knowledge in support of Internal Audit engagements involving actuarial subject matter, including market risk, product development, pricing, reserving, and other actuarial functions. The role works closely with senior actuarial and audit team members to execute defined testing procedures, evaluate risks, controls, and processes, and support audit conclusions and recommendations.

This position is designed for an actuarial professional who has completed two rotations through the company's Actuarial Development Program and is interested in applying that experience in an Internal Audit setting. Prior Internal Audit experience is not required. With guidance, coaching, and regular review from experienced team members, you will support the evaluation of actuarial assumptions, models, and controls while building both technical actuarial depth and Internal Audit knowledge.

What you'll be doing

•Apply actuarial knowledge to support the assessment of the reasonableness of methodologies, assumptions, models, and results as part of audit engagements involving actuarial activities.
•Support audit planning activities by gathering information about actuarial processes, risks, and controls, and assist in developing actuarial testing procedures under the direction of senior team members.
•Perform defined technical actuarial testing, such as recalculations, data reconciliations, benchmarking, and reasonableness and sensitivity analysis, and support the evaluation of model governance, validation, and change management practices.
•Review assumption-setting documentation, experience studies, and supporting data, and raise questions or inconsistencies with senior team members for further evaluation.
•Support the evaluation of actuarial processes and controls, including data inputs, model and end-user computing controls, peer review, and the reporting of actuarial results to management.
•Document testing results and technical observations, and contribute to the preparation of audit observations and recommendations related to actuarial risks and controls.
•Communicate clearly with Internal Audit colleagues and business partners, and participate in client meetings and walkthroughs as directed.
•Seek and incorporate coaching and feedback from senior actuarial and audit team members, and share knowledge gained through Actuarial Development Program experience with the team.
•Remain informed of emerging actuarial risks, regulatory developments, and industry trends, and bring relevant considerations to the team.
•Learn and apply audit methodology, including risk assessment, audit execution, documentation, and reporting, in accordance with department policie and standards. Prepare work papers that clearly document actuarial testing performed, sources, results, and conclusions.
•Support tracking of remediation activities for actuarial-related issues, as directed by the audit lead.
•Build working relationships with Actuarial, Risk Management, Finance, and other first and second line partners, while maintaining independence and objectivity.
•Continue developing knowledge of actuarial standards of practice, industry regulations, and best practices, and of the company's products, operations, and regulatory obligations.
•Develop working knowledge of the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission framework and carry out duties in compliance with the Institute of Internal Auditors' Global Internal Audit Standards, state and federal regulations, and company policies and procedures.

What we're looking for

Must-haves:

•Successful completion of two rotations through the company's Actuarial Development Program (3+ years of experience).
•Bachelor's degree in Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Finance, Economics, or a related field.
•Working knowledge of actuarial concepts, methodologies, and models, and practical experience applying them in areas such as market risk, asset-liability management, product development, pricing, valuation, or reserving, gained through Actuarial Development Program rotations.
•Demonstrated ability to analyze data and actuarial information, apply sound judgment, and effectively communicate findings and questions.
•Strong written and oral communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts clearly.
•Ability to manage assigned work and multiple priorities in a deadline-driven environment, with appropriate guidance and supervision.
•Willingness to learn Internal Audit methodology and apply it in conjunction with actuarial expertise. Prior Internal Audit experience and audit certifications are not required.
•Proficiency with Microsoft Office suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook).
•Upon Hire Certifications/Licensures: (5-8 Actuarial Exams passed; typically has ASA designation, progressing toward FSA designation.

Nice-to-haves:


•Progress toward the Associate or Fellow of the Society of Actuaries designation.
•Exposure to model validation, peer review, or actuarial governance and controls.
•Experience with data analytics and programming tools and with actuarial modeling and valuation platforms.
•Familiarity with internal control frameworks, risk assessment, or audit concepts.
•Interest in emerging technologies, including AI, and how they may impact actuarial and business risk.

The Role at a Glance

We are seeking a Lead Actuary, Internal Audit to apply actuarial expertise in support of Internal Audit engagements involving actuarial subject matter, including market risk, product development, pricing, reserving, and other actuarial functions. The role partners closely with audit leaders and business stakeholders to evaluate risks, controls, methodologies, and processes and contributes to audit conclusions and recommendation.

This position is designed for a Fellow of the Society of Actuaries who is interested in leveraging actuarial expertise to contribute to complex Internal Audit engagements. Prior Internal Audit experience is not required. Working under established audit methodologies and in partnership with experienced auditors, you will evaluate actuarial risks, assumptions, models, and controls while developing Internal Audit knowledge and contributing to audit conclusions and recommendations.

What you'll be doing

•Apply actuarial knowledge and professional judgment to assess the reasonableness of methodologies, assumptions, models, and results as part of audit engagements involving actuarial activities.
•Support audit planning activities by identifying actuarial risks and control objectives, and recommend the scope, nature, and extent of actuarial testing procedures for complex and higher-risk audit topics.
•Design and perform technical actuarial testing, including independent recalculation, benchmarking, sensitivity and reasonableness analysis, and evaluation of model governance, validation, and change management practices.
•Evaluate assumption-setting processes, experience studies, and the use of expert judgment, and challenge conclusions where support is insufficient or inconsistent with actuarial standards of practice, regulatory requirements, or financial reporting requirements.
•Evaluate actuarial processes and controls, including data inputs, model and end-user computing controls, peer review, and the governance and reporting of actuarial results to management.
•Develop and document technical conclusions and contribute to the preparation of audit observations and recommendations related to actuarial risks and controls.
•Communicate complex actuarial concepts clearly to Internal Audit colleagues, business partners, and senior stakeholders, including in client meetings and closing discussions.
•Share actuarial knowledge and provide peer support to team members and co-source partners, as appropriate.
•Remain informed of emerging actuarial risks, regulatory developments, and industry trends and incorporate relevant considerations into audit activities.
•Learn and apply audit methodology, including risk assessment, audit execution, documentation, and reporting, in accordance with department policies and standards. Prepare work papers that clearly document actuarial testing performed, sources, results, and conclusions.
•Support monitoring and validation of remediation activities for actuarial-related issues, as directed by the audit lead.
•Partner with Actuarial, Risk Management, Finance, and other first and second line partners to establish strong working relationships, while maintaining independence and objectivity.
•Stay current on actuarial standards of practice, industry regulations, and best practices, while continuing to expand knowledge of the company's products, operations, and regulatory obligations.
•Apply the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission framework and carry out duties in compliance with the Institute of Internal Auditors' Global Internal Audit Standards, state and federal regulations, and company policies and procedures.

What we're looking for

Must-haves:
•Fellow of the Society of Actuaries (FSA) designation.
•Bachelor's degree in Actuarial Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Finance, Economics, or a related field.
•5+ years of experience in the insurance or financial services industry, including hands-on experience in one or more areas such as market risk, asset-liability management, product development, pricing, valuation, or reserving.
•Strong working knowledge of actuarial methodologies, models, and assumptions, and of applicable actuarial standards of practice, statutory and GAAP reporting, and regulatory requirements.
•Demonstrated ability to analyze complex actuarial issues, apply sound professional judgment, and effectively communicate findings and recommendations.

The Role at a Glance

We are excited to bring on a Sr. Associate, Actuarial Product Specifications to support the Life Product business in a hybrid environment. We are open to candidates in any of the Lincoln key cities with preferred locations in Hartford, CT or Greensboro, NC.

Background Details
As a Sr. Associate, Actuarial Product Specifications, you will help bring life insurance products, riders and enhancements from design through implementation. You'll serve as an important connection between product and pricing actuaries and business partners, translating actuarial, regulatory and business requirements into clear, accurate product specifications. You'll apply your knowledge of actuarial concepts and applicable regulations, including IRC Section 7702, to understand their impact on product features, calculations and specifications. Through collaboration with actuarial, legal, compliance, operations, administration and technology, you'll help ensure product intent and requirements are consistently understood and implemented. If you enjoy combining analytical thinking, technical detail and cross-functional collaboration to bring products to life, please read on!

What you'll be doing

  • You will serve as a bridge between the team and pricing/product actuaries, providing technical and actuarial support during product development and implementation initiatives.
  • You will develop and maintain product specifications using established standards and guidelines to support new products and changes to existing products.
  • You will review product specifications for completeness, consistency, accuracy, and alignment with actuarial intent and identify issues requiring further review or resolution.
  • You will advise stakeholders on product design decisions, calculation methodologies, and downstream impacts.
  • You will provide actuarial input to support the development of product specifications, contract language, and related product documentation.
  • You will develop an understanding of applicable regulatory requirements, including IRC Section 7702, and interpret and apply those requirements to life insurance product features and specifications.
  • You will apply established guidelines to address challenging but non-complex specification issues and escalate matters requiring additional expertise.
  • You will collaborate with actuarial, legal, compliance, operations, administration, and technology partners to support consistent interpretation of product requirements.
  • You will support the translation of actuarial and business requirements into clear product specifications for implementation by internal and external stakeholders.
  • You will assist with product development and implementation activities for life insurance products, riders, and product enhancements.
  • You will explain product specifications, requirements, and established practices to stakeholders to support understanding and consistent execution.

What we're looking for

  • 4 Year/Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience (4 years of experience in lieu of Bachelor's)
  • 1+ Years actuarial experience or has passed three (3) actuarial exams
  • Excellent organizational skills with the ability to prioritize workload and multitask while maintaining strict attention to detail

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Location: Radnor, PA
  • Experience: 12+ years

  • Benefits: 401(k), paid time off, tuition assistance

About this job

Senior Director role leading end-to-end architecture and delivery of an AI Native Intelligence platform on AWS that converts enterprise data into conversational, queryable insights. Hands-on builder-leader position owning technical vision, team scaling, and production deployment across call center, claims, policy, and underwriting data.

Good fit if you have 12+ years in data/ML engineering with 5+ years leading technical teams, deep AWS data and AI services expertise, and proven production RAG or agentic AI experience.

Full job description

Alternate Locations: Radnor, PA (Pennsylvania); Charlotte, NC (North Carolina); Fort Wayne, IN (Indiana); Greensboro, NC (North Carolina)

Work Arrangement:

Hybrid : Employee will work 3 days a week in a Lincoln office

Relocation assistance: is not available for this opportunity.

Requisition #: 76793

The Role at a Glance

Lincoln Financial Group is building an AI Native Intelligence platform that turns enterprise data — starting with call center audio and transcripts, and expanding to claims, policy, and underwriting data — into a conversational, agentic layer the business can query directly. Instead of static reports, the platform is designed to let business users ask natural-language questions and get grounded, cited answers, backed by a real semantic understanding of Lincoln's data.

We're looking for a Senior Director to own the architecture and technical delivery of this platform end to end. This is a hands-on, builder-leader role: someone who sets the technical vision and roadmap, but who is equally comfortable reviewing a Bedrock agent's tool-calling logic, debugging a Step Functions pipeline, or sketching a knowledge graph schema on a whiteboard. You'll build and lead the team that takes this from pilot to enterprise scale.

What you'll be doing

  • Own the end-to-end architecture for the AI Native Intelligence platform on AWS — ingestion, enrichment, the semantic/business ontology layer, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), knowledge graphs, and agentic orchestration (Amazon Bedrock, Bedrock AgentCore, Amazon Neptune, OpenSearch Serverless, AWS Glue, Amazon Transcribe/Comprehend, and related services).
  • Translate diverse enterprise datasets — call center transcripts and audio, policy administration, claims, underwriting — into a unified, governed data and semantic foundation that supports natural-language querying and analytics.
  • Design and evolve the business ontology, knowledge graph, and KPI/metrics glossary that ground the platform's AI in Lincoln's own business definitions, so answers are accurate and consistent with how the business already measures itself.
  • Lead build-vs-buy decisions across the AI/ML and data stack, and stay ahead of a fast-moving AWS AI landscape — model updates, agent frameworks, vector and graph databases, evaluation tooling.
  • Build, mentor, and scale a team of engineers, data scientists, and architects; set technical standards, run design/architecture reviews, and unblock hard technical problems.
  • Partner directly with business stakeholders — call center operations, claims, underwriting, compliance — to identify high-value insight use cases and translate them into technical requirements and delivery plans.
  • Establish guardrails, governance, and responsible-AI practices: PII handling and redaction, model evaluation, hallucination mitigation, human-in-the-loop review, and auditability.
  • Define and track success metrics for AI initiatives — retrieval/insight accuracy, adoption, time-to-insight, and cost-to-serve — and report progress to senior and executive leadership.
  • Stay technically hands-on: prototype new capabilities, review code and architecture, and work directly alongside the team rather than directing from a distance.

What we're looking for

  • 12+ years of experience in data engineering, ML/AI engineering, or applied data science, including 5+ years in a technical leadership role (Director, Senior Manager, or Principal Architect) building production data or AI platforms.
  • Deep, hands-on experience with AWS data and AI services: S3, Glue, Lambda, Step Functions, Amazon Bedrock (or an equivalent enterprise LLM platform), OpenSearch or another vector database, and a graph database such as Amazon Neptune.
  • Proven experience building or leading RAG, agentic AI, or conversational AI systems in production — not just proofs of concept.
  • Strong grasp of data modeling, semantic layers, business ontologies, and knowledge graphs, and how they ground LLM-based systems in accurate, consistent business meaning.
  • A track record of building, mentoring, and scaling high-performing technical teams. Excellent communication skills — able to explain architecture trade-offs to engineers and business impact to executives with equal clarity.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience; advanced degree a plus.

Preferred

  • Experience with speech-to-text and NLP pipelines (e.g., Amazon Transcribe, Amazon Comprehend), particularly for audio or call center data.
  • Experience in insurance, financial services, or another regulated industry, with a working understanding of data privacy, PII, and regulatory compliance.
  • Familiarity with call center analytics, claims processing, or policy administration data.
  • Experience establishing responsible-AI governance frameworks — bias mitigation, hallucination controls, model evaluation, and audit trails.
  • Contributions to open-source AI/data tooling, patents, or published technical work.

Application Deadline

Applications for this position will be accepted through November 30, 2026, subject to earlier closure due to applicant volume.

  • Drive engagement across area of responsibility and work with the team to foster a strong engage culture. Work with manager to review the peakon score and create action plans within the tool

Support committees and programs for safety, fire prevention, disaster recovery and so forth. Ensures the development of specific plans for inclusion in these programs.

At Erie Insurance, you're not just part of a Fortune 500 company; you're also a valued member of a diverse and inclusive team that includes more than 6,000 employees and over 13,000 independent agencies. Our Employees work in the Home Office complex located in Erie, PA, and in our Field Offices that span 12 states and the District of Columbia.

Benefits That Go Beyond The Basics

We strive to be Above all in Service® to our customers—and to our employees. That's why Erie Insurance offers you an exceptional benefits package, including:

  • Premier health, prescription, dental, and vision benefits for you and your dependents. Coverage begins your first day of work.
  • Low contributions to medical and prescription premiums. We currently pay up to 97% of employees' monthly premium costs.
  • Pension. We are among the 2% of Fortune 500 companies to offer a traditional pension plan. Full-time employees are vested after five years of services.
  • 401(k) with up to 4% contribution match. The 401(k) is offered in addition to the pension.
  • Paid time off. Paid vacation, personal days, sick days, bereavement days and parental leave.
  • Career development. Including a tuition reimbursement program for higher education and industry designations.

Additional benefits that include company-paid basic life insurance; short-and long-term disability insurance; orthodontic coverage for children and adults; adoption assistance; fertility and infertility coverage; well-being programs; paid volunteer hours for service to your community; and dollar-for-dollar matching of your charitable gifts each year.

Position Summary

Exercises independent discretion or judgment in handling property claims within designated level of authority. Also responsible for servicing assigned territory and may handle litigated claims.

• The selected candidate will ideally live in NW Westmoreland, NE Allegheny, Southern Armstrong, or Southern Butler County or the close surrounding areas.
• A company car and equipment to work from home will be provided
• Ability to drive/travel regularly within the assigned territory
• The hiring manager will consider candidates for Property Adjuster Trainee (F08), Property Adjuster I (F09) or Property Adjuster II (F10).
• Level of position offered will be based upon the depth and breadth of selected candidate's experience and qualifications.

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Contacts Policyholders regarding property claims within level of authority. Conducts investigations, interviews insureds and witnesses, inspects damage and prepares estimates. Evaluates and makes recommendations regarding coverage of claims.
  • Handles property claims within designated authority. Sets and maintains adequate reserves. Obtains and reviews reports, statements, records and related materials as required. Evaluates information to determine coverage and total value of claim. Determines payments and issues checks or declines payment as required.
  • Documents claim files and submits final report to file for closure.
  • Identifies subrogation situations and initiates appropriate action.
  • Services assigned territory and brings assigned claims to conclusion.
  • Interacts with Agents and district sales managers on matters of mutual concern.
  • Handles property claims involving damages or coverage. May handle litigated claims, including negotiating with plaintiff attorney, or coordinates litigation with defense counsel as required.
  • Develops and applies a working knowledge of estimating practices and procedures relating to the adjustment of property claims.
  • Attends industry-related training programs and attends other training sessions to stay current on policy changes, interpretation or new legislation.
  • Successfully completes Technical Learning Center Training within one year of hire date.
  • Participates on Catastrophe Team when required.

Duties and Responsibilities (cont'd if applicable)

The first five duties listed are the functions identified as essential to the job. Essential functions are those job duties that must be performed in order for the job to be accomplished.

Regular and predictable attendance is an essential job function. For certain positions at ERIE, including leadership roles, regular and predictable onsite presence may also be an essential job function based on business and operational needs.


This position description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the incumbent. Employees are required to follow any other job-related instruction and to perform any other duties as requested by their supervisor, or as become clear.

  • Optimizes Work Processes (IC)
  • Job-Specific Knowledge
  • Instills Trust
  • Ensures Accountability
  • Decision Quality

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Bachelor's degree preferred.

Property Adjuster I

  • High School Diploma or GED and two years of claims handling experience, or equivalent required; or
  • High School Diploma or GED and successful completion of ERIE sponsored formal education; or
  • Bachelor's Degree required.

Property Adjuster II

  • High School Diploma or GED and five years of claims handling experience, or equivalent required; or
  • Bachelor's Degree and two years of claims handling experience, or equivalent required.

About this job

Lead AI security strategy and organizational capability for W. R. Berkley Corporation, defining multi-year roadmaps and governance frameworks for secure AI adoption. Build a force-multiplier model that enables existing security teams to use approved AI and automation safely across the enterprise.

Good fit if you have executive leadership experience in information security, AI risk governance, and building organizational capability across large enterprises.

Full job description

Company Details

Company URL: https://www.berkleytechnologyservices.com/

Berkley Technology Services (BTS) is a dynamic company committed to providing world class IT services. We offer a unique culture, enabling our team members to be on the cutting edge of technology while delivering high quality solutions. We are looking for outstanding individuals who will bring unique perspectives, insight and innovation to our teams. BTS, a member company of W. R. Berkley Corporation, has facilities located in Des Moines, Iowa and Wilmington, Delaware.

Our functions include working with various third parties to develop, integrate, and support insurance systems of WRBC's operating units. BTS strives to provide these functions in a holistic manner including helpdesk support, system connectivity, and operational support. Additional responsibilities include coordinating communications regarding best practices in the use of our supported systems and researching new technology. At BTS, there are opportunities associated with being a part of an established and empowering corporation while maintaining a positive personal working environment.

Additionally, we provide a competitive compensation and benefits package including a casual dress code. BTS is constantly growing and expanding to meet the changing demands of one of the most successful insurance organizations in the world. Visit us at berkley-bts.com to learn more information.

The Company is an equal employment opportunity employer.

Responsibilities

The Vice President, AI Security & Automation Enablement leads the Information Security capability responsible for secure artificial intelligence adoption, AI security, and reusable automation across W. R. Berkley Corporation. The role sets strategy, establishes priorities and investment plans, leads people and partners, and remains accountable for measurable security and business outcomes.

This executive builds organizational capability rather than serving as the primary developer. The VP translates emerging AI risk and opportunity into a governed portfolio, equips existing security teams to adopt AI and automation safely, and ensures that architecture, engineering, governance, operations, and business stakeholders have clear standards, reusable patterns, and accountable decision paths.

Primary Responsibilities

  1. Strategy, Portfolio and Investment Leadership
  • Define and maintain the multi-year AI security and automation strategy, roadmap, operating model, and investment priorities for Information Security.
  • Convert enterprise objectives and emerging risks into a prioritized portfolio with clear owners, funding needs, delivery milestones, operational acceptance criteria, and measurable outcomes.
  • Advise the CISO and senior technology leadership on AI-related risk, capability gaps, investment tradeoffs, tool overlap, and opportunities to improve security delivery.
  1. People Leadership and Organizational Capability
  • Lead and develop a multidisciplinary team spanning AI security, automation, architecture, engineering, security data, and related enablement capabilities.
  • Establish clear accountability, role expectations, talent plans, succession coverage, performance objectives, and sustainable delivery practices.
  • Build a force-multiplier model that enables existing Information Security teams to use approved AI and automation rather than creating a centralized team that becomes the sole builder for every use case.
  1. AI Security Governance and Enterprise Partnership
  • Represent Information Security in enterprise AI governance and provide accountable security recommendations for AI use cases, platforms, vendors, and material changes.
  • Align AI review activities with existing architecture, third-party risk, legal, procurement, privacy, and Building Permit processes to reduce duplication while preserving required oversight.
  • Define escalation criteria for high-risk, restricted-data, autonomous, externally hosted, or materially changed AI use cases.
  1. Secure AI Adoption and Control Framework
  • Establish and govern security standards, reference architectures, and control patterns for generative AI, machine learning, AI agents, model and data pipelines, and AI-enabled applications.
  • Ensure appropriate controls for identity, access, data protection, secrets, logging, monitoring, human oversight, output validation, change control, resilience, and incident response.
  • Maintain a risk-based approach that enables approved experimentation and production use while identifying and reducing unmanaged or unsanctioned AI use.
  1. AI and Automation Delivery Enablement
  • Oversee delivery of reusable capabilities such as governed AI experimentation environments, security workflow automation, evidence generation, control validation, AI-assisted analysis, and security data integrations.
  • Set technical direction and challenge designs while assigning detailed architecture, prototyping, coding, integration, testing, and operational runbook development to qualified team members and partners.
  • Require production readiness, support ownership, measurable adoption, quality controls, rollback capability, and acceptance criteria before automated capabilities are operationalized.
  1. Visibility, Measurement and Risk Reduction
  • Establish reliable visibility into AI systems, AI usage, agents, integrations, and material data flows within the scope of Information Security oversight.
  • Define executive and operational measures for control coverage, review cycle time, automation reliability, adoption, realized capacity, risk reduction, and exceptions.
  • Use trusted data to identify gaps, prioritize remediation, and demonstrate whether investments are producing the intended outcomes.
  1. Vendor, Partner and Financial Management
  • Lead evaluation of AI security and automation vendors, strategic partners, and professional services based on risk, capability, interoperability, supportability, cost, and measurable value.
  • Own portfolio-level commercial and sourcing recommendations, including build-versus-buy decisions, statements of work, acceptance of partner deliverables, and avoidance of unnecessary tool overlap.
  • Manage the approved budget and communicate material cost, schedule, delivery, and residual-risk decisions to executive stakeholders.
  1. External and Industry Leadership
  • Maintain current knowledge of AI security threats, regulatory expectations, industry standards, and relevant technology developments.
  • Represent WRBC in selected industry, peer, and strategic-vendor forums and translate external developments into practical internal action.
  • Provide clear executive and board-ready communications on AI security posture, priorities, decisions, and progress.

Decision Authority and Accountability

  • Accountable for the AI security and automation enablement strategy, portfolio priorities, organizational capability, resource recommendations, and delivery outcomes within the assigned scope.
  • Approves technical standards, patterns, and acceptance criteria within delegated authority and escalates policy exceptions, material residual risk, and enterprise-level investment decisions through established governance.
  • Retains human accountability for risk decisions, production access, material changes, vendor commitments, and executive representations. AI and automation may support analysis and execution but do not replace accountable leadership judgment.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • 10 or more years of progressive experience across information security, technology, architecture, engineering, automation, data, or related disciplines, including significant leadership responsibility.
  • Demonstrated success setting strategy, building teams, managing a portfolio, and delivering cross-functional technology or security capabilities in a complex enterprise.
  • Strong working knowledge of AI and automation risks and controls, including data protection, identity and access, model and application security, agent authority, monitoring, human oversight, and operational resilience.
  • Ability to evaluate technical designs and make difficult tradeoffs without becoming the primary hands-on developer for the function.
  • Experience leading vendors and service partners, developing investment recommendations, and communicating with executive and business stakeholders.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex risk and technology decisions in plain language.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Leadership experience in insurance, financial services, or another regulated enterprise.
  • Experience with cloud platforms, enterprise security architecture, AI development platforms, workflow automation, security data and analytics, and modern software delivery practices.
  • Familiarity with recognized cybersecurity, AI risk, and AI management frameworks and with regulatory expectations relevant to WRBC.
  • Relevant security, architecture, cloud, risk, or AI credentials. Equivalent demonstrated experience should be considered.

Leadership Competencies

  • Enterprise strategy and prioritization
  • People leadership and talent development
  • Technical judgment and intellectual curiosity
  • Executive communication and influence
  • Financial and vendor stewardship
  • Cross-functional collaboration
  • Outcome ownership and operational discipline

Additional Company Details

The Company is an equal employment opportunity employer.

About this job

Carolina Casualty seeks a Claims Examiner to investigate, evaluate and settle bodily injury claims for commercial auto losses. You will handle pre-litigation claims up to $100k, manage coverage determinations, and negotiate settlements for trucking and public transportation industries.

Good fit if you have 3+ years commercial auto claims adjusting experience, an Adjuster License, a Bachelor's Degree, and strong written communication skills.

Full job description

Company Details

Carolina Casualty is a member company of W. R. Berkley Corporation, an insurance holding company that is among the largest commercial lines insurance writers in the United States. We specialize in liability, physical damage, cargo and other insurance solutions for the commercial auto markets including trucking, public transportation and others.

Join Carolina Casualty, where innovation meets purpose.

Carolina Casualty is a proud member of W. R. Berkley Corporation, one of the largest commercial lines insurers in the country. What sets us apart is not just our size, but how we work and who we are.

We specialize in liability, physical damage, cargo, and other insurance solutions for the commercial auto market, including trucking and public transportation industries that keep America moving. Our team tackles real, complex challenges for the people and businesses that make that possible every day.

At CCIC, we live by three simple truths:

Always do right. Integrity is not just a slogan. It guides every decision we make.

Everything counts; everyone matters. Every role, every voice, and every contribution help shape who we are as an organization.

Embrace innovation and act responsibly. We are willing to challenge the status quo while remaining thoughtful and committed to our people, customers, and partners.

If you are looking for a place where your work makes an impact, your ideas are valued, and doing the right thing is expected, we would love to meet you.

The company is an equal opportunity employer.

Responsibilities

Carolina Casualty is looking for a talented Claims professional who will be responsible for the investigation, evaluation, disposition and settlement of bodily injury claims involving commercial automobile losses. This includes the investigation, determination and evaluation of coverage, liability and damages, risk transfer, and the timely setting of proper reserves. In addition, the Claims professional will control the insured's exposures and losses, manage consultants, and achieve a prompt, fair and equitable settlement according to fair claims handling requirements.

Key Functions/Duties of Position:

  • Oversee and resolve truck, bus, commercial auto and/or public transportation bodily injury pre-litigation claims involving unrepresented and represented claimants.
  • Conduct a prompt, thorough and fair investigation by obtaining relevant facts to determine coverage, origin, and extent of loss losses.
  • Utilize critical thinking and solid judgment to solve problems, make decisions and resolve complex issues inherent in handling losses, as well as plan and organize activities throughout the claim's management process.
  • Able to write concise reports and effectively communicate contractual issues, technical legal concepts and coverage application in easy to understand terms.
  • Act timely upon emerging information to insure ongoing recognition of the financial exposure on losses within assigned exposure up to $100k as well as promptly communicate to management, if beyond the assigned level of exposure.
  • Interpret related claims documentation.
  • Initiate and oversee serious automobile accident investigations and rapid response
  • Develop strategies and effective plans that drive claims to better results
  • Accurately assess and resolve commercial auto insurance coverage issues, analyze facts and allegations in conjunction with all policy provisions, endorsements and amendments
  • Draft declination, Reservation of Rights and other coverage letters
  • Negotiate outstanding settlements
  • Present case statuses/summaries in a clear, concise and understandable manner
  • Documents and communicates all claim activities timely and effectively and in a manner, which supports the outcome of the claim file
  • Experience with Self-Insured Retention (SIR) is a plus
  • Experience with PIP claims is a plus.

Qualifications

  • Bachelors Degree
  • 3 + years commercial auto claims adjusting experience
  • Adjuster License required
  • Key Competencies
    • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
    • Excellent organizational and analytical skills with high attention to detail.
    • Ability to work independently, managing time and resources to accomplish multiple tasks in fast-paced, deadline-oriented environment.
    • Strong interpersonal and negotiation skills.

Additional Company Details

Any unsolicited resumes/candidate profiles are not subject to payment of the agency fees.

The company offers a competitive compensation plan and robust benefits package for full-time regular employees which for this role include:
• Base Salary Range: $70,000-$115,000
• Eligible to participate in annual discretionary bonus.
• Benefits: Health, Dental, Vision, Life, Disability, Wellness, Paid Time Off, 401(k) and Profit-Sharing plans.

Administer, configure, and develop Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM solutions for a Fortune 500 insurance company. Work across business units globally to deliver scalable enterprise solutions while supporting production systems and participating in Agile development.
