Full job description

Company Details

Berkley Technology Services (BTS) is the dynamic technology solution for W. R. Berkley Corporation, a Fortune 500 Commercial Lines Insurance Company. With key locations in Urbandale, IA and Wilmington, DE, BTS provides innovative and customer-focused IT solutions to the majority of WRBC's 60+ operating units across the globe. BTS's wide reach ensures that ideas and opinions are considered at every level of the organization to guarantee we find the best solutions possible.

Driven by a commitment to collaboration, BTS acts as consultants to our customers and Operating Units by providing comprehensive solutions that not only address the challenge at hand, but proactively plan for the “What's Next” in our industry and beyond.

With a culture centered on innovation and entrepreneurial spirit, BTS stands as a community of technology leaders with eyes toward the future -- leaders who truly care about growing not only their team members, but themselves, and take pride in their employees who shine. BTS offers endless ways to get involved and have the chance to grow your career into a wide range of roles you'd never known existed. Come join us as we push forward into the future of industry leading technological solutions.

Berkley Technology Services: Right Team, Right Technology, Simple and Secure.

Company URL: https://www.berkleytechnologyservices.com/

The Company is an equal employment opportunity employer.

Responsibilities

The Dynamics Administrator/Developer is responsible for the administration, configuration, development, support, and continuous improvement of the organization's Microsoft Dynamics 365 enterprise CRM capabilities. This role partners closely with Product Management, Engineering, business stakeholders, Operating Units (OUs), and other development team members to deliver scalable, secure, and efficient solutions that support business objectives.

The Dynamics Administrator/Developer combines technical expertise with business analysis capabilities to configure, develop, test, and support Dynamics solutions. The role contributes to solution design, integrations, releases, and production support while collaborating across the Business Systems team to ensure successful delivery of business value and a high-quality user experience.

  • Partner with Operating Units (OUs) and business stakeholders to gather, analyze, document, and validate business and technical requirements.
  • Translate business requirements into scalable Dynamics solutions.
  • Build strong relationships with business stakeholders and serve as a trusted advisor on Dynamics capabilities and best practices.
  • Create and maintain functional specifications, technical documentation, process flows, user stories, and acceptance criteria.
  • Support the administration, configuration, maintenance, and continuous improvement of Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Power Platform solutions.
  • Configure and maintain entities, tables, forms, views, dashboards, model-driven applications, business rules, workflows, and security roles.
  • Manage user access, role assignments, and security configurations while adhering to organizational standards and compliance requirements.
  • Assist with environment management, application lifecycle management (ALM), and release management processes.
  • Monitor system health, performance, and adoption and identify opportunities for optimization.
  • Design, develop, test, and deploy Dynamics and Power Platform solutions
  • Develop custom functionality to meet business requirements while following development standards and best practices.
  • Participate in solution design discussions and provide recommendations regarding platform capabilities, scalability, maintainability, and performance.
  • Collaborate with team members on code reviews, solution reviews, and technical design sessions.
  • Evaluate new Dynamics capabilities and recommend enhancements that improve business value.
  • Understand integration architecture, APIs, authentication methods, and data synchronization processes.
  • Create, refine, and manage test plans, test cases, test scripts, and testing documentation.
  • Perform and coordinate quality assurance (QA), regression testing, and user acceptance testing (UAT).
  • Prioritize features and functionality in collaboration with Product Management and business stakeholders.
  • Support sprint planning, backlog grooming, sprint reviews, retrospectives, and other Agile ceremonies.
  • Collaborate with developers, engineers, and product team members to ensure timely and high-quality delivery.
  • Support release planning, deployment validation, and post-production verification activities.
  • Identify risks, dependencies, and potential delivery challenges and assist in developing mitigation plans.
  • Provide Tier 1 off-hours support by participating in triage and application support rotations to ensure timely issue resolution.
  • Design, execute, and analyze A/B tests or similar experiments to optimize user experience and business outcomes.

Qualifications

Qualifications: Include necessary skills/experience and core competencies required

  • 3+ years of experience administering, configuring, and developing Microsoft Dynamics CE (Sales) applications.
  • Experience working with Microsoft Dataverse and the Power Platform.
  • Experience developing custom solutions using C#, JavaScript, Power Apps, and Power Automate.
  • Understanding of Dynamics 365 security models, business units, teams, roles, and solution management.
  • Experience gathering requirements and translating business needs into technical solutions.
  • Experience creating process documentation, technical documentation, data mappings, and workflow diagrams.
  • Knowledge of REST APIs, web services, integrations, and data synchronization concepts.
  • Experience troubleshooting application, integration, and data-related issues.
  • Experience with Agile methodologies and software development lifecycle practices.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to effectively collaborate with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

Preferred

  • Experience with Dynamics 365 Customer Service, and/or Marketing Customer Insights.
  • Experience with Azure services, integrations, and cloud technologies.
  • Experience with Power BI reporting and analytics.
  • Experience with DevOps, CI/CD pipelines, and Application Lifecycle Management (ALM).
  • Experience supporting enterprise CRM platforms within a multi-business-unit organization.
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365, Power Platform, or Azure certifications.
  • Insurance industry experience.

Education Requirement

  • Bachelor's Degree (open to all degrees and majors)
  • At least 3 years of job experience

Posting Description

  • Demonstrate strong business and technical acumen by making ROI-driven decisions to optimize technology investments and outcomes.

  • Demonstrated success managing M&A integrations or large-scale programs.

  • Proven ability to lead in a fast-moving, entrepreneurial environment.

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

The Director, Detection & Threat Response is the enterprises senior leader for intelligence-led detection and response. The role is accountable for how Allstate anticipates, finds, and stops adversaries before they affect customers, data, or operations. This leader sets the strategic direction for three global functions: D&R Engineering & Automation, Threat Intelligence, and Threat Hunting. The goal is to unite them into one system in which intelligence sets priorities, hunting tests those priorities against the environment, detections are engineered and shipped as code, and response runs at machine speed under clear governance.

As a Director, you wont just deliver results you drive our culture and shared purpose. You can work remotely and will commute to a nearby office and/or travel for meaningful connection opportunities.

Imagine this.

  • 7:02 a.m. A new intelligence report describes an MFA-bypass technique being used against financial services firms. Within two minutes it is scored against Allstates priority intelligence requirements and flagged as relevant, and an automated hunt launches across identity and email telemetry.
  • 7:09 a.m. The hunt gets a hit: one account shows the techniques pattern. An AI agent opens the investigation immediately, pulls identity and device context, runs the pivots a senior analyst would run, and reaches a high-confidence verdict with a full evidence trail.
  • 7:11 a.m. Contained. The verdict meets the bar for a pre-approved, reversible response, so the system acts on its own: active sessions revoked, credentials reset, account temporarily locked. Nine minutes from first intelligence to containment.
  • 7:16 a.m. An analyst reviews the evidence and the actions taken, confirms the call, and reaches out to the employee. Humans stay accountable for every automated action, without being the bottleneck for it.
  • 8:02 a.m. An AI-drafted detection for the technique is waiting in an engineers review queue. It uses the real attack telemetry from the hunt as its test case, and has been backtested against 30 days of history for false positives. It arrives linked to the intelligence that prompted it, the attack path it closes, and its expected alert volume. The engineer approves it and the pipeline promotes it. Next time, nobody has to go hunting. It fires on its own.

Now imagine you lead the teams that made that possible. Your intelligence team set the priority. Your hunters tested it against our environment. Your engineers built the automation that contained it in minutes and the pipeline that turned it into durable coverage within the hour. And you know it worked because you inspected the data, not because someone said so.

Thats the job, and its what were building at Allstate.

What were building

Allstate is building a Cyber Response organization designed for the speed of AI-enabled threats. The work underway is the kind most security teams are still only talking about:

  • An AI-assisted detection-as-code pipeline. Every detection version-controlled, peer-reviewed, tested, tied to the attack paths that matter most to Allstate, and promoted through CI/CD, with AI agents accelerating how detections are created and validated.
  • Agentic investigation and governed response. AI-driven triage and investigation paired with orchestrated response, with human decision gates where the business impact is real.
  • Automated threat intelligence. Pipelines that turn global threat reporting into fast, relevant action for exposure management, incident response, hunting, and leadership.
  • Intelligence-led threat hunting. Hypothesis-driven hunts, AI-assisted scoping, and findings that flow straight into durable detections.
  • Continuous adversarial validation. Breach-and-attack simulation and purple teaming that prove coverage against real attacker behavior.

We need a leader who can bring these together into one system and take it to enterprise scale.

Why this matters

Allstate exists to protect people from lifes uncertainties. In security, that promise now runs into a math problem: adversaries are using automation and AI to scale, and human hours do not. If analyst capacity decides what we detect, risk ends up in the alerts no one had time to look at. Our goal is to predict, detect, and disrupt threats before they reach our customers and our data, with coverage we can prove, detections we can trust, response at machine speed, and automation we can govern.

What Allstate can do for you

  • A charter, not a backlog. Youll lead three teams, D&R Engineering & Automation, Threat Intelligence, and Threat Hunting, and define how they work as one system. You report to the leader of Cyber Defense & Response and sit on that leadership team.
  • Scale and stakes. A Fortune 100 insurer, a global team across the US, Ireland, and India operating follow-the-sun, and an enterprise attack surface spanning identity, cloud, email, endpoint, and applications.
  • Real backing for the AI-era SOC. Executive sponsorship and active investment in agentic investigation, orchestration, and AI-assisted engineering, with a mandate to scale through intelligence and automation.
  • Room to build the culture. A mandate to build teams where candor is normal, I dont know is a respected answer, quality is inspected rather than assumed, and people improve the system instead of heroically working around it.

What you can do for Allstate

  • Build one loop, not three teams. Create the strategy and operating processes that connect intelligence, hunting, and D&R engineering. Priority intelligence requirements set the agenda, hunts test the hypotheses, and every finding ends in a detection, a control change, a telemetry requirement, or a documented decision.
  • Decouple coverage from analyst capacity. With AI handling first-pass investigation, stop tuning coverage to what humans can staff. Expand behavioral coverage across the attack paths that matter most to Allstate, with identity first in line, and measure coverage of those paths rather than rule counts.
  • Run detections like code, end to end. Git-backed content, unit tests, linting, peer review, staged CI/CD promotion, and a clear definition of done, applied to every detection in the library.
  • Make the queue work for the SOC. Partner with Security Operations so detections land in AI-assisted investigation at creation time. Look past medians to tail wait time and cycle time across every severity, because the risk sits in the tail, not the average.
  • Put humans where judgment changes the outcome. Let machines investigate and take pre-approved, reversible containment actions at machine speed, with every action reviewed by a human. Keep a human decision gate for business-impacting remediation. Earn trust in AI the statistical way, with parallel runs and measured agreement, and expand its autonomy as the data proves it out.
  • Inspect quality, then build it in. Stand up quality control across detections, hunts, and intelligence products: defined rubrics, meaningful sampling, and a feedback loop where every defect becomes training, automation, or a process fix.
  • Scale intelligence for speed and relevance. Lead automated intelligence pipelines that tell exposure management, incident response, hunting, and leadership, in minutes, when a threat actually matters to Allstate.
  • Show your work. Build capacity models, coverage baselines, and a quarterly scorecard that ties detection and response to outcomes and cost lines leaders already track. Ask the right questions and answer them with data.
  • Lead leaders and grow people. Develop the leaders of all three teams, hire for traits like curiosity, empathy, and candor, and teach the skills. Protect the team from burnout by fixing the system that causes it.

What you should bring with you

  • 12+ years across threat detection, incident response, threat intelligence, or security operations, in large enterprise, managed detection and response, incident response consulting, or security product teams.
  • Experience leading leaders, including teams distributed across time zones.
  • A track record of applying software engineering discipline to detection: you have run detections as code and know what it takes to keep a library healthy.
  • Experience taking AI or agentic capabilities in detection and response from pilot into production, and clear opinions about where humans must stay in the loop.
  • A data-driven management style: capacity modeling, queueing, quality control, and the habit of answering hard questions with data.
  • Deep understanding of attack surfaces and attacker behavior, especially identity, cloud, and email, and how to turn that into measurable coverage of the attack paths that matter rather than a color-coded matrix.
  • The ability to explain the math to a CFO and the TTP to an engineer, in the same afternoon.
  • Empathy and candor. You own the problem before you solve it, and you build teams where people can say I was wrong.

Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Chicago, IL

About this job

Director leading Allstate's supplier cyber incident response, overseeing incident investigation and supplier monitoring functions. The role owns technical inventory of supplier connections and leads assessments when incidents or intelligence signals emerge.

Good fit if you have incident response leadership experience, understand how suppliers integrate with large enterprises, and can build teams that perform under pressure.

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

The Director, Third-Party Cyber Defense is Allstates senior leader for supplier cyber incident response. The role is accountable for how quickly and appropriately Allstate understands and responds when a supplier is compromised. This leader sets direction for two functions: Supplier Incident Investigation & Response, and Supplier Monitoring & Intelligence. The Director also owns the technical inventory of supplier connections and leads targeted technical assessments when incidents, intelligence, or monitoring signals call for a closer look.

The role calls for an experienced incident response leader who understands how suppliers connect to large enterprises and can build a team that performs consistently under pressure. As a member of the Cyber Defense & Response leadership team, the Director partners with Enterprise TPRM, Procurement, Legal & Privacy, and Security Operations. Together they deliver fast, fact-based answers about Allstates exposure and a stronger supplier ecosystem after every event.

As a Director, you wont just deliver results you drive our culture and shared purpose. You can work remotely and will commute to a nearby office and/or travel for meaningful connection opportunities.

A supplier just told us theyve been breached.

It is now one of the most common ways a cyber incident reaches a large company: a claims vendor, a payroll provider, a SaaS platform, a file-transfer service. The notice is usually short and vague. From that moment, five questions decide whether Allstate handles it well:

  • Do they have our data? Which data, about which customers, in which states.
  • How do they reach us? Every network link, API, file transfer, and service account, and whether we can shut each one down safely.
  • What did we already know about them? Their risk tier, their last assessment, and the findings that are still open.
  • What do they owe us? The notification, cooperation, and audit terms in their contract, and whether they are living up to them.
  • What is the right response? Action that fits the facts: enough to protect our customers, without shutting down a business process when the facts dont call for it.


The best third-party programs answer all five within hours, every time. Not because someone heroic stays up all night, but because the assessments were done, the connections were mapped, the playbook was practiced, and the working relationships with Legal, Privacy, Procurement, and Security Operations were in place before the call came.

Building that capability is the job, and its what were building at Allstate.

What were building

Allstate is establishing Third-Party Cyber Defense as a dedicated pillar within Cyber Defense & Response, bringing supplier incident response, supplier monitoring and intelligence, and targeted technical assessment together into one mature, repeatable capability:

  • A supplier incident response practice. A dedicated team with clear intake, triage, and severity criteria, a standard way of engaging suppliers, playbooks for the most common supplier incidents, and agreed escalation into enterprise incident command.
  • Targeted supplier technical assessment. Deep technical reviews of specific suppliers when an incident, threat intelligence, a monitoring signal, or a TPRM referral calls for one, with findings handed to TPRM to record and govern. Onboarding, tiering, and scheduled reassessment remain with TPRM.
  • Shared supplier context. Response and monitoring built on the enterprise supplier inventory, the TPRM system of record, contract data, and business-service mapping, so every incident starts with a clear view of who the supplier is to Allstate.
  • Ongoing visibility into our suppliers. Security ratings, attack-surface signals, and supplier breach intelligence from Threat Intelligence, so we hear about trouble early.
  • A clear picture of how suppliers connect to us. A technical inventory of supplier connections and accounts, security review and recertification, and a tested way to cut off each critical connection if we ever need to.
  • Strong partnerships. Clear hand-offs with Enterprise TPRM and Procurement, Legal & Privacy, Security Operations, Threat Intelligence, and Exposure Management.


We need a leader who can bring these together and make them dependable at enterprise scale.


Why this matters

Allstate exists to protect people from lifes uncertainties, and a growing share of the data and services that let us do that sit with our suppliers. Attackers know it: the 2026 Verizon Data Breach Investigations Report found a third party involved in nearly half of all breaches, up sharply from the year before. Regulators have been clear that insurers remain accountable for the providers they rely on. When a supplier has an incident, what matters is how quickly we understand what it means for Allstate and whether our response fits the facts. Overreacting disrupts the business; underreacting puts customers at risk. Getting it right every time takes preparation, practice, and a team built for it.

What Allstate can do for you

  • A new function to build. Youll lead two teams, Supplier Incident Investigation & Response and Supplier Monitoring & Intelligence, and shape how they work together, including how targeted technical assessment is delivered. A dedicated assessment team is a planned decision as demand is demonstrated. You report to the leader of Cyber Defense & Response and sit on that leadership team.
  • Scale and stakes. A Fortune 100 insurer with a large, varied supplier ecosystem spanning claims, agency, cloud, SaaS, and data providers.
  • Strong partners from day one. Youll work alongside Security Operations, Threat Intelligence, Exposure Management, and Red Team within Cyber Defense & Response, and with Enterprise TPRM, Procurement, and Legal & Privacy across the company.
  • Support for doing it right. Leadership backing and a clear mandate to build a lasting capability, with room to shape how it grows.

What you can do for Allstate

  • Build the supplier incident response muscle. Define intake, triage, severity criteria, a standard supplier question set, and playbooks for the most common scenarios. Run tabletop exercises with Security Operations, Legal, Privacy, and business owners until the process is second nature.
  • Respond quickly and in proportion. When a supplier is hit, establish the facts, determine the impact on Allstate data, systems, customers, and access, and choose actions that fit those facts. Deliver an impact summary that lets Legal & Privacy make notification decisions within regulatory timelines.
  • Assess where it matters most. Lead targeted technical assessments of suppliers when an incident, threat intelligence, a monitoring signal, or a TPRM referral calls for one. Use TPRMs tiering to prioritize monitoring and response, contribute cyber input to how suppliers are tiered, and provide incident-response and technical-security requirements to TPRM, Legal, and Procurement.
  • Hand off findings cleanly. Own operational incident actions through to completion. TPRM records and governs enduring supplier-risk findings, and the team confirms technical closure of incident-related findings when asked.
  • Build on enterprise supplier data. Work from the enterprise supplier inventory, the TPRM system of record, contract data, and business-service mapping, and partner with TPRM on the access and integration that response and monitoring depend on.
  • Know how suppliers connect to us. Own the technical inventory of supplier connections and accounts, working with Identity & Access Management, and make sure each critical connection has a documented and tested cut-off procedure.
  • Hear about trouble early. Lead continuous monitoring of critical suppliers and work with Threat Intelligence so supplier breach news reaches the team quickly. Extend that view to fourth parties and concentration risk.
  • Draw clean lines with partners. Agree on who owns what with Enterprise TPRM and Procurement, Security Operations, Threat Intelligence, Exposure Management, and Legal & Privacy. This is a cyber function, not a second TPRM program.
  • Measure progress. Report on time from supplier signal to triage, time to confirm our exposure, targeted technical assessments completed and handed to TPRM, and the percentage of critical connections with a tested cut-off, for leadership, the board, and regulators.
  • Build and develop the team. Hire the leads for both teams, bring incident response, intelligence, and technical assessment skills together, and develop people who can move between them.

What you should bring with you

  • 12+ years in cybersecurity across incident response, third-party cyber risk, or security operations, including 5+ years leading teams.
  • Hands-on incident response experience, including incidents at suppliers or service providers where you had to get timely, accurate facts from an organization you do not control.
  • Hands-on experience performing or leading technical security assessments of suppliers, and working knowledge of the third-party risk management lifecycle.
  • Working knowledge of assessment frameworks and evidence, such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, SIG, and NIST CSF 2.0, and of continuous monitoring platforms.
  • A technical understanding of how suppliers connect to a large enterprise: SaaS integrations, API and service accounts, B2B network links, managed file transfer, and managed service provider access.
  • Experience in a regulated industry such as insurance, financial services, or healthcare, including working knowledge of obligations like NYDFS Part 500.
  • A record of building a new function and scaling it into a repeatable, measurable program.
  • Sound judgment under pressure and clear communication: telling Legal and business leaders what we know, what we dont, and what we recommend, and holding suppliers to what they owe us.

Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Chicago, IL

About this job

Principal Digital Product Manager at Allstate leading a Unified System of Controls platform focused on cybersecurity controls adoption, intelligence, and exception management across the enterprise. The role owns vision and implementation of this critical system while supervising digital product teams and driving digital transformation.

Good fit if you have 12+ years of experience, deep enterprise cybersecurity controls knowledge, and proven ability to build and lead high-performing teams.

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

Our Unified System of Controls will focus on three major areas, housing controls to ensure homogeneity of control adoption across Allstate and all subsidiaries, the buildout of an intelligence engine that can identify when controls are not being adopted at the required rate and what changes may be needed, and managing exceptions, risks and conclusions to controls. This system will be leveraged as threats occur against the Allstate landscape, and fast analysis is required to understand what changes or new controls may be needed and who will need to take ownership of the delivery of those controls. The Unified System of Controls is the nervous system of Cybersecurity and Controls as it houses all the information necessary for Allstate to take immediate action to safeguard the business. The Principal DPM will own the vision and implementation of the platform, including the adoption and measurement of controls and messaging, including in active event scenarios.

As a Director, you wont just deliver results you drive our culture and shared purpose. You can work remotely and will commute to a nearby office and/or travel for meaningful connection opportunities.

Job Summary

The Principal Product Management Director develops and guides the digital product teams and roadmaps for customer experience aligning with Allstates overall experience strategy. This role is critical for ensuring processes and experiences are ready for the digital future-state and partner with the respective stakeholders to drive the necessary elimination, optimization and reengineering solutions. This position owns the vision and roadmap for innovative digital solutions, ensuring alignment with business goals and customer needs. This role requires a deep understanding of technology, user experience, and data-driven decision-making to drive digital transformation and deliver exceptional user experiences.


Key Responsibilities

  • Enforce a digital mindset by pushing on service and experience optimization using the process of elimination, optimization, and reengineering
  • Define, drive, and own the product strategy, vision, and roadmap, ensuring partnership with Principal Engineers and Principal Platform Consultants
  • Manage the entire product lifecycle from ideation to launch, ensuring timely delivery and continuous iteration based on user feedback
  • Leverage data analytics and user research to identify opportunities for product enhancements and new feature development
  • Tirelessly advocate for simplification within and across consumer journeys
  • Drive delivery acceleration through reuse of capabilities and smarter, simpler ways to achieve outcomes on a consistent basis
  • Evangelize product capabilities and seek additional use cases for broader applicability across AORs and new business ventures
  • Collaborate with key stakeholders to define business requirements, success metrics, and key performance indicators (KPIs)
  • Advocate for a customer-centric approach by deeply understanding user needs, pain points, and behaviors
  • Influence digital product strategy & backlogs across AORs in support of strategic priorities
  • Cultivate strategic mindset within AOR Digital Product Managers, empowering product teams to independently make decisions through a strategic lens


SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • This job has supervisory duties


EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • 4-year Bachelors Degree (Preferred)
  • 12 or more years of experience (Preferred)
  • Deep understanding of enterprise cybersecurity controls across technology environments.
  • Experience building capabilities that measure control adoption, coverage, compliance, effectiveness, and gaps.
  • Strong understanding of risk acceptance, control exceptions, compensating controls, remediation plans, and risk disposition.
  • Experience designing security capabilities as enterprise products/platforms, rather than isolated processes.
  • Ability to establish consistent control adoption across different businesses, subsidiaries, technology environments, and engineering organizations.


Education & Experience (in lieu)

  • In lieu of the above education requirements, an equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.


Skills and Capabilities

  • People Leadership & Talent Development: Track record of building, developing, and leading highperforming large organizations; establishes clear decision rights, accountability, and operating cadence while developing future leaders and succession pipelines.
  • Operational Expertise: Brings strong operational expertise, with a proven ability to optimize processes, drive execution against strategic outcomes, and deliver consistent, high-quality results across complex environments.
  • Strategic Thinking & Innovation: Demonstrates strong strategic thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess complex business challenges, identify innovative solutions, and drive continuous improvement initiatives. Applies forward-looking insights and analytical rigor to optimize processes, enhance performance, and support long-term organizational objectives.
  • Business Acumen & Analytical Rigor: Advanced business acumen with strong analytical skills; uses data, insights, and technology fluency to inform decisions and foster a culture of disciplined execution.
  • Innovation & Process Orientation: Natural process innovator with strong learning agility and a continuousimprovement mindset.
  • Influence: Proven capability to successfully influence decision-makers and collaborators at all levels - upward, downward, and laterally. Able to build alignment, negotiate effectively, and drive outcomes without relying solely on positional authority.
  • Change Leadership: Proven ability to lead large, multilocation teams through significant changes, including business transformations, systems implementations, and organizational integrations.

Skills

Automatic Control System, Change Management, Executive Communications, Influencing Others, Product Management, Product Strategies, Security Risk, Strategic Management, Strategic Thinking, Strategy Development, Systems Thinking

Compensation offered for this role is 187,500.00 - 258,375.00 annually and is based on experience and qualifications.

Job.JobTitle: Obvious Total Loss Adjuster (Job Location EST)
Job.JobDescription:
At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

** This position supports the Eastern Standard Time (EST) Region

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.


Join Our Team as an Obvious Total Loss Adjuster Where Your Expertise Drives Real Impact
As an Obvious Total Loss Adjuster, you will play a critical role in our claims handling process, focusing on determining the repairability or total loss of vehicles. Working remotely, you will spend the majority of your time managing total loss claims. Your responsibilities will involve reviewing claim details, preparing total loss valuations, assessing vehicle conditions, determining salvage valuations, and engaging in negotiation and settlement processes with our valued customers and/or claimants.
This is more than just a jobits an opportunity to make a meaningful difference in peoples lives during challenging moments, all while leveraging your analytical skills and industry knowledge.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 12 months or more of Auto Collision estimating in CCC One, Audatex, or Mitchell preferred
  • Previous experience in total loss adjustment or a related field is highly desirable
  • Proficiency in using estimating software and valuation tools for virtual assessments
  • Strong analytical skills to evaluate moderate to complex vehicle damages effectively
  • Excellent negotiation and communication skills to interact with customers and stakeholders remotely
  • Ability to work independently and manage time efficiently in a virtual work environment
  • Detail-oriented and organized, with a commitment to delivering accurate and timely results

Youll wear a few hats to fill a few roles throughout your day that all require a level of experience:

The Customer Service Expert youll live into Allstates Claims Culture by caring, empowering, and restoring, and you will accomplish that by being compassionate, clear, and a committed partner in each auto claim. You lead with empathy, always.

The Investigator youll confidently and independently investigate auto claims by performing detailed reviews of damage and interpreting policies to determine coverage.

The Effective Communicator youll use phone, emails and sometimes even video chat with customers to help them through a fast, fair, and easy claims process. Youll also incorporate a specific approach to claim handling to offer the customer their preference of communication to efficiently discuss their claim needs and keep them updated on the claim progress.

The Negotiator You will evaluate and negotiate claims settlements with customers, vendors, third party carriers and claimants, in accordance with all legal and business standard methodologies. With negotiations, you will incorporate tactics in handling challenging and complex situations.

The Problem Solver youll utilize multiple tools to get the job done in a fast-paced environment, including estimate tools, job aids, and additional settlement platforms, all while using your sharp critical thinking skills.

The Recorder youll protect the company financially by executing policies along policy agreements, and you keep a clear record of your work in a claims system that you will be trained on. Youll accomplish this by ensuring timely and accurate documentation is completed as you work on each claim.

Work Location:

This position is a remote home-based role. Your home office does not need to be near an Allstate office, but it does need to be in the United States. This Position is not available for Washington, California, Alaska, and Hawaii residents.


When you work from home full time, youll need:

  • A dedicated workspace in your residence that is private and free from distractions.
  • A minimum internet bandwidth of 50 MB download speed and 5 MB upload speed.
  • Appropriate work surface and seating.

Work schedule:

Candidates are considered based on the time zone they live in. If you are selected for this position you need to be willing to work one of the following schedules to be determined by business needs.

Candidates in Central or Eastern Time Zone preferred

Standard business hours 8:00 am - 4:30 pm local time

What Allstate will provide:

  • A technology bundle that includes all equipment needed to perform your work from home (laptop, monitor, headset, keyboard, and mouse.)
  • Connectivity reimbursement of $80 per month to offset some of the cost of internet.

Notice of Licensing Requirement:

As a condition of employment, your office/area may require you to obtain an adjuster and/or an appraiser license which includes passing an additional background check with the Department of Labor. If applicable, you will be required to secure license(s) within 60 days of hire.

If required, the Hiring Manager will work with you along with the Centralized Licensing team to ensure that you are properly licensed.

Sign on Bonus:

You may be eligible for a $1000 Licensing Sign on Bonus if you have the applicable active licenses needed for this role. This could include Home Resident Property & Casualty License, Designated Home State (DHS) Florida or Texas License, and/or applicable Appraiser License.

**Candidates who have previously worked for and are seeking to be rehired at Allstate and its family of companies are not eligible for this sign-on bonus.


Benefits

Allstate cares about you and your wellbeing. We offer a comprehensive total rewards package that includes pay, benefits, and programs to help you balance work with the rest of your life. You can choose whatever benefits are most important you. Here are some of our offerings:

    • Competitive salary based on experience and qualifications
    • Medical, dental, and vision coverage
    • Allstate pension plan and 401(k) savings plan
    • Ayco financial coaching
    • Spring Health mental and emotional wellbeing resources
    • Paid parental leave
    • Adoption reimbursement
    • Paid time off
    • Tuition reimbursement
    • Wellness incentives
    • Learn more by visiting Allstategoodlife.com

Notes

The preceding description is not designed to be a complete list of all duties and responsibilities. May be required to perform other related duties as assigned. Regular, predictable attendance is an essential function of this job.

Job.JobTitle: Catastrophe Field Property Large Loss Adjuster
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Catastrophe (CAT) Adjuster, Claims, Property Claims Adjuster
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Chicago, IL

About this job

Catastrophe Field Property Large Loss Adjuster for Allstate in Chicago. Inspect fire, water, and weather damage at loss sites or virtually, write repair estimates, and settle complex homeowner claims while working a 10/4 schedule with 70% or more travel.

Good fit if you have 5+ years of property adjusting experience, construction or trades background, and can travel 70% or more.

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

A day in the life of a Catastrophe Field Large Loss Property Adjuster

  • Spend your day handling claims traveling to loss sites that have been damaged by fire, water, weather or other unexpected events as well as virtually from home
  • Conduct a detailed inspection of the property and write an estimate to capture the extent of the damages
  • Settle large homeowner claims involving complex structure losses as a result of, for example, fire, water, theft, etc.
  • When you are not in the field, use advanced video technology to collaborate with onsite vendors to identify damages and write a damage estimate from a virtual setting
  • Review the policy and decide how coverage applies and provide the customer with a detailed explanation of both the estimate and the policy
  • Communicate empathetically with customers and help them through their claim process in a fast, fair and easy manner
  • Negotiate claim settlements with customers in accordance with business unit standard methodologies
  • Use data and analytics to tell a story and influence decision making
  • Flexibility to work in a variety of environments - independently, within a team, face-to-face, and virtually
  • In our virtual environment, adjusters are required to engage and participate on camera during online meetings and training
  • Researches and responds to complex customer communications, concerns, conflicts or issues
  • Documents a claim file with notes, evaluations and decisions making process
  • Investigates, reviews, determines and verifies complex coverage/policy information
  • Handles complex contents inventories, complex pricing analysis, and mitigation bills, and prepares claims reports
  • Handles and occasionally negotiates complex claims that included Public Adjuster involvement
  • May serve as a committee team lead for medium-sized projects or as a committee team member on large projects
  • Proficient knowledge of all regional construction types and related repair methodologies
  • Assists in reviewing files and making recommendations to refer files to Home Office for escalation

Key Responsibilities

  • Assists Attorney Represented team in writing comparative estimates used to help with litigation strategy
  • Reinspects complex and occasionally highly complex damage estimates and provides quality evaluation coaching
  • Advanced knowledge of all regional construction types and related repair methodologies
  • May serve as a committee team lead for large projects or as a committee team member on very large projects
  • Acts as a resource to leadership or others on complex and occasionally highly complex claim/coverage matters and high severity claims
  • Handles inside investigation of complex and occasionally highly complex mortgagee claims
  • Review customer satisfaction results; recommends, designs, and implements personal and business unit action plans
  • Manages, researches, and resolves complex and occasionally highly complex customer communications, concerns, conflicts or issues

Preferred Qualifications

  • 5 or more years of property adjusting experience
  • Construction or trades experience
  • Written and verbal communication
  • This position is not available for those who reside in California, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and Washington

Supervisory Responsibilities

This job does not have supervisory duties

Schedule

  • This position follows a 10/4 schedule (10 days on, 4 days off) with hours of 7-7 and 70% or more travel

Notice of Licensing Requirements

  • As a condition of employment, your office/area may require you to obtain an adjuster and/or an appraiser license which includes passing an additional background check with the Department of Labor. If applicable, you will be required to secure license(s) within 60 days of hire.
  • If required, the Hiring Manager will work with you along with the Centralized Licensing team to ensure that you are properly licensed.

Sign on Bonus

  • You may be eligible for a $1,000 Licensing Sign on Bonus if you have the applicable active licenses needed for this role. This could include Home Resident Property & Casualty License, Designated Home State (DHS) Florida or Texas License, and/or applicable Appraiser License.

**Candidates who currently or have previously worked for and are seeking to be rehired at Allstate and its family of companies are not eligible for this sign-on bonus. **

Skills

Complex Claims, Empathy, Property Adjusting, Xactimate, Xactimate Estimating

Compensation

Compensation offered for this role is 56,000.00 - 92,000.00 annually and is based on experience and qualifications.

The candidate(s) offered this position will be required to submit to a background investigation.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Chicago, IL

About this job

Design and build full-stack AI-powered software products for risk and compliance decision-making at Allstate. Use Java Spring Boot, Python, modern front-end frameworks, and generative AI to create scalable, secure enterprise solutions.

Good fit if you have 3+ years full-stack development experience with Java Spring Boot or Python, hands-on experience with generative AI frameworks, and proficiency with Microsoft Azure.

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

Risk Data & AI designs, builds, and operates governed data products, analytics solutions, and AI-enabled capabilities that support risk and compliance decision-making. The team applies modern data, software, and AI engineering practices to deliver scalable data pipelines, trusted analytical products, intelligent automation, and responsible AI solutions that enable TORC to identify emerging risks, generate actionable insights, and make timely, evidence-based decisions.

We are looking for a Software Engineer with a passion for AI product development to join the team. Reporting to the Managing Engineer, Risk Data & AI, you will design, build, and run full-stack, AI-powered products that help TORC turn risk data into insight and action. This is a hands-on role where you will take ideas from concept to production, integrating Generative AI into enterprise-grade solutions that are scalable, secure, and responsibly implemented.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and develop full-stack applications using Java Spring Boot/Python, and modern front-end frameworks (React, Angular, or Vue.js).
  • Integrate Generative AI models and APIs into enterprise-grade solutions.
  • Build and maintain APIs, microservices, and data pipelines to support AI-driv
  • en features.
  • Implement CI/CD pipelines, containerization (Docker), and orchestration (Kubernetes).
  • Deploy and manage applications on cloud platforms, preferably Microsoft Azure.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including Digital Product Managers and risk stakeholders, to deliver high-quality, AI-powered software solutions.

Required Skills

  • 3+ years of full-stack development experience with Java Spring Boot and/or Python.
  • Proven experience with Generative AI frameworks (e.g., OpenAI, Hugging Face, LangChain) and APIs.
  • Strong understanding of CI/CD pipelines, DevOps practices, and infrastructure as code.
  • Hands-on experience with Microsoft Azure cloud services.
  • Proficiency in front-end development using JavaScript, TypeScript, and modern frameworks.
  • Familiarity with containerization (Docker) and orchestration (Kubernetes).
  • Experience in RAG technology
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and a passion for innovation.

Desirable Skills

  • Experience with vector databases, prompt engineering and fine-tuning LLMs.
  • Exposure to multi-modal AI systems and agentic AI frameworks.
  • Background in MLOps or AI model deployment on cloud platforms.

#LI-SM1

Skills

API Development, CI/CD, Full Stack Development, JavaScript, Microsoft Azure, Python (Programming Language), Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Software Development, Spring Boot

If you are ready to start working in a fun & exciting environment while making a difference, then apply to join our team today!

Job.JobTitle: Auto Claims Adjuster Trainee - National General
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Claims Adjuster, Claims, Training & Development Specialist
Job.JobDescription:
National General is a part of The Allstate Corporation, which means we have the same innovative drive that keeps us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. We offer home, auto and accident and health insurance, as well as other specialty niche insurance products, through a large network of independent insurance agents, as well as directly to consumers.

Job Description

Start building a career in claims through practical experience, increasing responsibility, and decisions that directly affect the customer experience. As a Material Damage Claims Trainee, youll learn how to investigate auto losses, determine coverage and liability, evaluate property damage, and negotiate claims within established authority. Youll also develop a broader understanding of insurance policies, claims technology, vehicle components, subrogation, and potential fraud. With each claim, youll strengthen the analytical, communication, and decision-making skills that are foundational to claims work.

National General Insurance is currently hiring for an Auto Claims Adjuster Trainee.


The Claims Auto Trainee is responsible for investigating and confirming the facts of loss for automobile accidents. This role determines coverage, liability, damages, and negotiates claims within authority.


Launch your claims career by learning how to investigate, analyze, and make meaningful decisions that help people when it matters most. This trainee role offers hands-on learning and a strong foundation in auto claims.


While this role offers flexibility, candidates located in certain areas may be expected to report to an office location in Winston-Salem, NC; Charlotte, NC; Ontario, CA; or Scottsdale, AZ.


Key Responsibilities

Handles basic investigation regarding most aspects of auto claims (coverage, liability and damages)

Identifies customer needs and works to meet those needs using appropriate customer service skills

Applies a basic understanding of systems and technology used within the company

Partners to determine subrogation or fraud potential and how to handle

Exhibits basic understanding of insurance policies written by the company, the industry, and organizational relationships within the company and department

Begins recognizing and identifying body parts of a vehicle and other potential property damage


As a requirement of employment, individuals who currently hold an active insurance license must terminate all existing appointments prior to onboarding and must not hold any outside appointments at any point during employment. Applicants seeking an adjuster role who also hold a resident producer license must formally surrender that license when instructed to by the licensing team. By proceeding with the application process, applicants acknowledge and accept these licensing requirements and agree to comply.


Supervisory Responsibilities

This job does not have supervisory duties.

Skills

Job Description

The Regulatory Compliance Analyst performs risk-based compliance testing and monitoring activities to evaluate whether business processes and controls effectively mitigate regulatory compliance risk. The role executes standardized testing procedures, evaluates control design and operating effectiveness, analyzes testing results and trends, identifies potential control deficiencies and root causes, and develops clear, evidence-based conclusions.

The Analyst partners with Compliance and business stakeholders to communicate testing results, identify emerging compliance risks and support remediation and continuous improvement. The role also contributes to the advancement of compliance testing through standardized methodologies, data analytics, automation and technology-enabled monitoring.

Succession and/or Development planning has identified a qualified candidate for this position.

Key Responsibilities

  • Execute risk-based compliance testing and monitoring activities in accordance with established compliance testing methodologies, standards and testing schedules.
  • Evaluate control design and operating effectiveness to determine whether controls appropriately address identified regulatory risks and are operating as intended.
  • Develop and execute test procedures, including reviewing populations, selecting or validating samples, evaluating evidence, documenting test results and reaching supportable testing conclusions.
  • Analyze testing results, operational data and historical performance to identify trends, recurring conditions, emerging risks and potential broader control weaknesses.
  • Clearly communicate testing results, risk implications and recommended actions to Compliance partners, business leaders and control owners.
  • Escalate potential compliance issues and control deficiencies in accordance with established governance and issue-management standards.
  • Support remediation activities by evaluating corrective actions and performing follow-up testing or validation, as appropriate, to determine whether identified deficiencies have been sustainably addressed.
  • Identify opportunities to improve testing effectiveness and efficiency through standardization, analytics, automation, AI-assisted analysis and continuous monitoring.
  • Collaborate with business, Quality Assurance, Compliance and other risk partners to leverage available data and monitoring results while avoiding unnecessary duplication of testing activity.

Experience

  • 2 or more years of experience in regulatory compliance, compliance testing, risk management, or a related discipline.
  • Experience evaluating processes, controls, transactions or operational data against defined requirements.
  • Familiarity with data analytics, automated testing, AI-enabled analysis or continuous monitoring tools is beneficial.

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Property Claims Adjuster, Claims, Claims Adjuster
Job.JobDescription:
At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

A day in the life of a Field Property Adjuster, and what it takes to do the job!

As a Field Property Adjuster, you will provide exceptional service to our policyholders. Your primary responsibility will involve traveling to our customers' homes to conduct on-site inspections, investigate coverage, prepare estimates, and settle claims promptly and efficiently. Additionally, you will handle virtual claims countrywide, leveraging various platforms and software such as Xactimate and ClaimsX Video Collaboration.

Candidates who live in Central, Mountain, Pacific Time Zones

You'll wear a few hats that will require a level of experience:

  • The Customer Service Expert youll live into Allstates Claims Culture by caring, empowering, and restoring, and you will accomplish that by being compassionate, clear, and a committed partner in each claim. You lead with empathy, always.
  • The Investigator youll confidently and independently investigate property claims by performing detailed reviews of damage and interpreting policies to determine coverage.
  • The Effective Communicator youll use phone, emails and sometimes even video chat with customers to help them through a fast, fair, and easy claims process. Youll also incorporate a specific approach to claim handling to offer the customer their preference of communication to efficiently discuss their claim needs and keep them updated on the claim progress.
  • The Negotiator You will evaluate and negotiate claims settlements with customers, vendors, third party carriers and claimants, in accordance with all legal and business standard methodologies. With negotiations, you will incorporate tactics in handling challenging and complex situations.
  • The Problem Solver youll utilize multiple tools to get the job done in a fast-paced environment, including estimate tools, job aids, and additional settlement platforms, all while using your sharp critical thinking skills.
  • The Recorder youll protect the company financially by executing policies along policy agreements, and you keep a clear record of your work in a claims system that you will be trained on. Youll accomplish this by ensuring timely and accurate documentation is completed as you work on each claim.

Youre provided with comprehensive training:

  • Training will be Monday Friday and you will be required to attend approximately 2 weeks of training that will take place in Dallas, TX
  • The training program is designed to help you build a claims foundation and understand the systems and processes in your day-to-day work
  • Ongoing training opportunities for continuous improvement happen regularly on the job

Schedule:

  • After training, Remote/Travel: 10 days on (include travel), 4 days off. Workdays range from 8 to 12 hours

Required Qualifications:

  • This field position requires up to 90% travel out of town
  • Valid driver's license
  • Are willing and able to carry a 50-pound ladder and access up to a 6/12 pitch on a one to two-story roof
  • Must reside within a reasonable distance of a major airport to support the travel requirements of this role.

Preferred Qualifications & Skills:

  • 2+ years of experience preparing property estimates
  • Prior experience as a Property Adjuster
  • Proficiency with estimating software, such as Xactimate
  • Strong commitment to delivering exceptional customer service
  • Ability to work independently while managing multiple priorities
  • Proactive problemsolving skills with a positive, solutionoriented mindset
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to multitask in a fastpaced environment
  • Clear, professional written and verbal communication skills

Notice of Licensing Requirement:

  • As a condition of employment, your office/area will require you to obtain an adjuster and/or an appraiser license which includes passing an additional background check with the Department of Labor. If applicable, you will be required to secure license(s) within 60 days of hire
  • If required, the Hiring Manager will work with you along with the Centralized Licensing team to ensure that you are properly licensed

Sign On Bonus:

  • You may be eligible for a $1,000 Licensing Sign on Bonus if you have the applicable active licenses needed for this role. This could include Home Resident Property & Casualty License, Designated Home State (DHS) Florida or Texas License, and/or applicable Appraiser License

*Current employees or candidates who have previously worked for Allstate, including its family of companies, are not eligible for this sign-on bonus

Job Description

We are seeking a Senior AI Engineer on the Enterprise Intelligence Factory team to play a foundational role in building the enterprise Semantic Ontology & Dimension Factory Platform. This platform enables AIready analytics by combining semantic ontologies, knowledge graphs, agentic AI, and data engineering to automatically generate businessready star schemas from heterogeneous enterprise data sources.

In this role, you will design and implement agentdriven pipelines that leverage RDF/OWL ontologies, SPARQL, and Large Language Models (LLMs) to perform semantic alignment, dimension mining, and AIassisted data modelling at scale. You will work at the intersection of AI, semantics, and modern data platforms, helping establish engineering patterns and best practices for the team.

This is a handson, senior individual-contributor role, ideal for engineers who enjoy building core platform capabilities rather than isolated experiments.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design, build, andmaintainagentic AI pipelines(usingGoogle ADK or similar frameworks) to automate semantic mapping, dimension mining, andontologydrivenreasoning.
  • Createand evolveenterprise ontologiesinRDF/OWL, including upper ontologies and domain extensions aligned to CIM (where applicable), to enable reusable enterprise semantics.
  • EngineerLLMpoweredservicesfor schema understanding, semantic alignment, ontology enrichment, andAIassistedmetadata generation, with a focus on accuracy, traceability, and scale.
  • ImplementSPARQL querying and reasoning layersover knowledge graphs to drive downstream transformations and ensure consistent interpretation of business concepts.
  • Architectand deliverPythonbasedmicroservicesand batch pipelines that integrate semantic reasoning with moderndataengineeringworkflows.
  • Buildandoptimizedimension and fact generation pipelinesonMicrosoft Fabric(Lakehouse, Spark, SQL, orchestration) to producebusinessreadystar schemas from heterogeneous sources.
  • Defineand enforceengineering standards, design patterns, and reusable components for semantic andAIdrivendata platforms (quality, observability, security, and performance).
  • Partnerwith data architects, domain SMEs, and governance teams tovalidatesemantic definitions, manage change, and ensure platform scalability and adoption.
  • Conductcode reviews, mentor engineers, and influence technical decisions across the platform to raise engineering quality and delivery velocity.

Required Skills & Qualifications:

  • 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, withstrongproficiencyin Pythonand GenAI.

  • Handsonexperience buildingLLMbasedsystemsusing commercial oropensourcemodels.
  • Solidunderstanding ofsemantic technologies: RDF, OWL, ontologies, knowledge graphs, andSPARQL.
  • Experiencedesigning or working withagentic AI frameworks(e.g., Google ADK,LangChainagents, or similar).
  • Strongbackground indata engineering concepts(ETL/ELT, star schemas,metadatadrivenpipelines).
  • Experiencebuilding and operating systems oncloud platforms, preferablyMicrosoft Azure / Microsoft Fabric.
  • Strongproblemsolvingskills and ability to work in ambiguous, greenfield platform initiatives.

Preferred Skills:

  • Experiencewithenterprise data models(e.g., CIM or canonical models).
  • Familiaritywithsemantic alignment, ontology mapping, or datacataloguingtools.
  • ExposuretoMLOps/LLMOps, model evaluation, and AI observability.
  • Knowledgeofdistributed systems, CI/CD pipelines, andcontainerisation.
  • ExperiencebuildingAIassistedanalytics or semantic layersfor BI or NLQ use cases.

The hiring manager has flexibility to hire across several levels of seniority. The level will be determined by the selected applicant's skills and competencies.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Chicago, IL

About this job

Director role leading P&C reserve estimation for Auto Injury and Business Insurance at Allstate. Reports to senior leadership with direct exposure to CFO, CAO, and CEO, managing complex reserving methodologies and an actuarial team.

Good fit if you have FCAS, 12+ years P&C actuarial experience with reserving depth, and proven leadership managing actuarial teams.

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

Why This Role

This is a signature seat within the enterprise P&C actuarial organization a role designed for a senior reserving leader who wants direct line-of-sight to the top of the house. You will own the estimation of loss and expense reserves across Auto Injury and Business Insurance, and you'll do it with a rare combination of technical depth, executive influence, and enterprise reach.

You'll have opportunities to regularly present to senior and executive level leadership up to and including the CEO, along with coordinating with and supporting the external appointed actuary, auditors, and state departments of insurance. In short: your work will be seen, challenged, and acted upon at the highest levels of the company.

As a Director, you won't just deliver results you'll shape culture, sharpen the craft, and set the standard for how modern reserving is done. We value in-person, connected experiences with your team and Allstaters across the enterprise, which will require travel within your local area or to one of our offices on a regular basis.

What You'll Do

  • Own the reserve estimate. Develop, execute, and continuously improve highly complex actuarial reserving methodologies across multiple lines of business, ensuring data quality, methodology appropriateness, and documentation standards are best-in-class.

  • Influence the enterprise. Present at Loss Reserve Committee meetings and translate complex actuarial results into clear, decision-ready insights for the CFO, Chief Accounting Officer, and CEO, as well as business unit presidents and finance leadership.

  • Benchmark and modernize. Continuously benchmark reserving techniques against industry practice and bring forward the next generation of methods from stochastic models to machine learning and AI-enabled reserving.

  • Engage external stakeholders. Serve as a primary point of contact for auditors, the external appointed actuary, and state departments of insurance; represent the company with credibility and command.

  • Lead reserving in dynamic environments. Review and challenge complex loss reserving techniques across multiple lines and provide expert consultation on the most difficult reserving questions.

  • Build the team. Own end-to-end talent management for an expanded team succession planning, compensation, development, bench strength, and organizational design and coach the next generation of reserving leaders.

  • Set strategy. Connect Allstate's vision and enterprise strategies to department initiatives; develop and lead multi-year plans that drive measurable corporate business results.

  • Ensure control and compliance. Develop and adhere to internal and external compliance requirements, including GAAP, Statutory, and evolving regulatory expectations around model governance and AI.

Executive Exposure & Impact

This role sits close to the decision-making core of the company.

Your voice will shape how the company communicates reserve adequacy to the Board, the Street, and regulators.

What You'll Bring

Education & Credentials

  • Bachelor's degree (preferred); equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered.

  • Fellow of the Casualty Actuarial Society (FCAS) or equivalent actuarial designation(required).

  • 12+ years of progressive P&C actuarial experience, with meaningful depth in reserving.

Technical & Analytical Skills

  • Deep expertise in loss reserving methodologies (chain-ladder, Bornhuetter-Ferguson, Cape Cod, stochastic reserving, individual claim-level models) and advanced actuarial/statistical techniques.

  • Strong knowledge of insurance reserving frameworks, ERM, capital, and regulatory requirements (GAAP, Statutory).

  • Ability to quickly master and apply a broad range of analytical tools, data sources, and software applications.z

AI & Advanced Analytics Proficiency

  • Working proficiency with AI, machine learning, and generative AI as applied to reserving and broader actuarial work including automated assumption selection and LLM-assisted documentation, analysis, and communication.

  • Familiarity with AI governance and model risk management frameworks (e.g.,CAS AI guidance) and the ability to responsibly deploy AI in a regulated environment.

  • Comfort using AI/GenAI tools (e.g., Copilot, Python/R ML libraries) to accelerate model development, benchmarking, exhibits, and executive-ready reporting.

Executive Communication & Influence

  • Exceptional communication skills able to craft and deliver clear, compelling, executive-ready messages, and to translate highly technical concepts for CFO/CAO/CEO-level audiences.

  • Proven ability to influence upward, downward, and laterally; builds alignment and drives outcomes without relying on positional authority.

  • Coaches others on the proper use of technical and analytical language and serves as a subject-matter expert to internal partners.

Leadership & Management

  • Proven leadership experience, including developing people leaders and building high-performing actuarial teams.

  • Leads with empathy and clarity through organizational changes; builds trust and sustains engagement in an evolving company environment.

Project & Program Management

  • Advanced program management capability, with a track record of independently leading multiple high-complexity, cross-functional initiatives on time and on quality.

Supervisory Responsibilities

This role has direct supervisory responsibility for a team of actuarial leaders and analysts across Auto Injury and Business Insurance.

Skills

Business Strategies, Data Analytics, Performance Management (PM), Strategic Leadership, Strategy Development

Compensation

About this job

Field Property Adjuster in Denver conducting on-site home inspections, investigating coverage, preparing estimates, and settling claims. Focus includes water loss claims and handling virtual claims using Xactimate and ClaimsX software.

Good fit if you have 2 years outside adjuster experience, valid driver's license, can carry 50-pound ladder and access roofs, and live in Denver area.

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection.

Job Description

A day in the life of a Field Property Adjuster, and what it takes to do the job!

As a Field Property Adjuster, you will provide exceptional service to our policyholders. Your primary responsibility will involve traveling to our customers' homes to conduct on-site inspections, investigate coverage, prepare estimates, and settle claims promptly and efficiently. Additionally, you will handle virtual claims countrywide, leveraging various platforms and software such as Xactimate and ClaimsX Video Collaboration. Your expertise will be particularly focused on water losses, ensuring our customers receive the highest level of support and resolution for these specific claims.

You'll wear a few hats that will require a level of experience:

The Customer Service Expert youll live into Allstates Claims Culture by caring, empowering, and restoring, and you will accomplish that by being compassionate, clear, and a committed partner in each claim. You lead with empathy, always.

The Investigator youll confidently and independently investigate property claims by performing detailed reviews of damage and interpreting policies to determine coverage.

The Effective Communicator youll use phone, emails and sometimes even video chat with customers to help them through a fast, fair, and easy claims process. Youll also incorporate a specific approach to claim handling to offer the customer their preference of communication to efficiently discuss their claim needs and keep them updated on the claim progress.

The Negotiator You will evaluate and negotiate claims settlements with customers, vendors, third party carriers and claimants, in accordance with all legal and business standard methodologies. With negotiations, you will incorporate tactics in handling challenging and complex situations.

The Problem Solver youll utilize multiple tools to get the job done in a fast-paced environment, including estimate tools, job aids, and additional settlement platforms, all while using your sharp critical thinking skills.

The Recorder youll protect the company financially by executing policies along policy agreements, and you keep a clear record of your work in a claims system that you will be trained in. Youll accomplish this by ensuring timely and accurate documentation is completed as you work on each claim.

Qualifications:

2 years' previous experience as an outside adjuster is highly desired.

Previous experience as an outside adjuster is highly desired.

Proficiency in using Xactimate and other relevant software for estimating.

Strong critical thinking and technical skills to assess damages accurately and expedite claims settlements.

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to provide exceptional customer service.

Ability to travel to customers' homes and handle virtual claims countrywide effectively.

Detail-oriented and organized, with a focus on delivering high-quality work.

This position is not available for California, Alaska, Hawaii or Puerto Rico residents.

Required Qualifications:

Residency within the posted location is mandatory for this role.

Are willing and able to carry a 50-pound ladder and access up to a 6/12 pitch on a one to two-story roof.

Valid driver's license and willingness to travel as part of the job requirements.

Youre provided with comprehensive training:

The training program is designed to help you build a claims foundation and understand the systems and processes in your day-to-day work.

Ongoing training opportunities for continuous improvement happen regularly on the job.

You will be required to attend approximately 2 weeks of training that will take place in Dallas, TX.

If required, the Hiring Manager will work with you along with the Centralized Licensing team to ensure that you are properly licensed.

*Current employees or candidates who have previously worked for Allstate, including its family of companies, are not eligible for this sign-on bonus.

Competitive pay with needed support for continuous development and career advancement.

Flexibility in scheduling and a time off policy that helps support your work/life balance.

Initial and ongoing training to get you proficient in your new role.

Full job description

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from lifes uncertainties.
